author: tommcclean
body:
This is liveplanner's second bug sweep, following #1455. It covers the leads that sweep left open and a wider read of the sheet function library, tab-scoped access, agent sheet reads and agent board building. Formula behaviour follows Google Sheets, and a link scoped to one tab follows the "no existence leak" rule: other tabs answer 404, as if they did not exist.

It fixes form and editor doors that answered 403 instead of 404, text functions that disagreed about positions after an emoji, two SUBSTITUTE edge cases, agent sheet reads that skipped columns, and agent boards that could lose a column.

**What was done** (spec first, and each fix has a test)

- **Form-link doors answer 404 to a link scoped to another tab.** `form-link`, `form-seen` and `form-preview` said 403 where every other tab read door says 404. They now use `deniedOnTab`.
- **Editor doors do the same.** A tab save, rename, agent form write, changeset, revert and tab delete all said 403, while item and sheet writes said 404. A new `deniedEdit` answers 404 for a grant confined to another tab, and keeps 403 for no grant or too low a level. A test covers each door, and a Viewer still gets 403.
- **Text functions count the same way.** `LEN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `MID` and `REPLACE` counted code points, while `FIND` and `SEARCH` gave UTF-16 positions, so `MID(t, FIND(x, t))` started one character late after an emoji. All of them now count UTF-16 code units, as Sheets does. Fractional positions and counts are truncated, and `FIND` refuses a start past the end, as `SEARCH` already did.
- **SUBSTITUTE.** A fractional instance number rounded up (2.7 meant the 3rd) and is now truncated. Matches overlapped (the 2nd "aa" in "aaaa" was found at character 2), which disagreed with replace-all. Matches no longer overlap.
- **Agent sheet reads continue from the right column.** When `read_sheet` hit its character cap mid-row, the note said "read on from C5", so an agent skipped columns A and B on every later row. The note now names the exact range to read next, for example `A5:D40`.
- **Agent boards keep every column.** Columns named "Phase 3", "Phase" and "Phase Ж" could end up sharing the id `phase-3`, and set-up dropped one. Ids now take the next free number.

**Performance**

- The text functions no longer copy the whole string into an array on each call. 20,000 `LEN` + `MID` calls on 10k-character text went from 7,808 ms to 0.6 ms (shared, loaded machine).
- `deniedEdit` runs only on requests already being refused.
- The column-id loop is bounded by the 12-column limit.
- No new dependencies and no client changes.
- No known risk.

**Screenshots:** none, since nothing visual changed.

Gate: typecheck, oxlint and prettier are clean. Vitest with coverage passes in api (1,487), sheets (1,384), items (1,276) and agent-verbs (555).

author: joaovitorsesma
ttimmahlax
body:
The encoder runs **1.37–1.63× faster on every preset**, with **byte-identical output**. It executes 31–43% fewer instructions at CIF and 48–59% fewer at 720p. It is 45 independent changes, three for each of 15 cost "veins" found by an exact instruction census. Each is its own commit, with its measured delta in the message.

## Results against 0.17.0 (`main`)

Exact instruction counts (callgrind, single thread, `encode --qp 26`):

| clip, preset | 0.17.0 | this branch | change | CPU time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| foreman CIF x30, `Fast` (CLI default) | 1,364,048,927 | 780,856,525 | **−42.75%** | **1.63× faster** |
| foreman CIF x30, `Balanced` (`Preset` default) | 2,573,724,283 | 1,785,491,533 | **−30.63%** | **1.37× faster** |
| foreman CIF x30, `Quality` | 5,835,366,013 | 3,992,943,047 | **−31.57%** | **1.41× faster** |
| FourPeople 720p x20, `Fast` | 5,058,945,802 | 2,077,420,435 | **−58.94%** | |
| FourPeople 720p x20, `Quality` | 6,919,016,470 | 3,594,289,756 | **−48.05%** | |

CPU time was measured on one pinned core, alternating 0.17.0 and this branch in ABBA pairs: 15 for `Fast`, 11 for `Balanced` and 9 for `Quality`. Output was the same in every pair, and the new encoder was faster in every pair.

## How each change was gated

- **Byte identity, every commit.** Nine encodes must produce the same md5 as before the change. They cover fast, balanced and quality presets, CABAC and CAVLC, B-frames on and off, all-intra, 1 and several references, and CIF and 720p. The merged branch was re-checked against current `main` on all nine.
- **Measured, not estimated.** Each change kept only if callgrind showed fewer instructions. Seven attempts that measured worse were reverted, and a note sits at each site.
- **Kernels.** Every new SIMD kernel has an x86 arm, a NEON twin and a scalar oracle with a differential test, and each oracle test was poisoned once to confirm it can fail. The aarch64 execution job here is the first run of the NEON twins on hardware; locally they were type-checked.
- **Recycling without re-zeroing.** The plane pools reuse retired reconstruction and half-pel planes without clearing them. A throwaway build filled every recycled plane with 0xA5, and all nine encodes stayed byte-identical. The pools are released when an encode finishes, so no thread keeps frame-sized buffers afterwards.

## What changed, by area

| vein | fast Δ Ir | quality Δ Ir |
|---|---:|---:|
| B-direct motion compensation | −154,579,427 | −182,360,221 |
| global-motion probes | −120,768,180 | −121,175,640 |
| motion-search glue | −59,289,922 | −107,353,613 |
| edge motion compensation | −65,759,398 | −26,172,817 |
| CABAC engine | −40,499,206 | −28,984,934 |
| SAD kernels | −6,433,021 | −305,798,612 |
| `me_wide` rescue grid | +105,902 | −391,237,119 |
| motion-compensation copies | −12,391,198 | −42,442,469 |
| residual emitter | −9,654,929 | −6,772,262 |
| SATD kernels | −30,577,681 | −447,364,288 |
| B-direct predicted twice | −26,439,915 | −12,196,096 |
| environment reads | −23,834,079 | −58,659,149 |
| allocation and zeroing | −23,940,805 | −17,829,112 |
| RD snapshot and trial | −7,735 | −56,684,414 |
| hand-rolled kernel twins | −9,453,859 | −38,200,453 |

These per-vein sums are against the campaign's starting point, a few commits before 0.17.0; main's own changes since then did not move encoder output. The per-commit ledger, the refuted attempts and three byte-changing findings left for a BD-rate gate are in section 7 of `docs/plans/ir-veins-encoder-2026-11-08.md`.

## API

Additive only:

- `rusty_h264-accel`: `ssd_16x16`, `ssd_8x8`, `ssd_scalar`, `sad_8x8`, `sad_avg`, `sad_avg_scalar`, `SatdGrid`, `sum_sq_16x16`, `sum_sq_16x16_scalar`. `satd_4x4` now dispatches to SIMD.
- `rusty_h264-common`: `inter::build_hpel_planes_reusing`.

Nothing was removed or changed in signature, so release-plz should cut a patch release.

## Test plan

- [x] Nine-encode byte identity against current `main`.
- [x] Local replica of the blocking CI gates: clippy `-D warnings`, the scalar build and tests, memprobe, SIMD suites, decoder fuzz, aarch64 checks, all-features, CLI smoke, the `no_std` targets and the overflow-checks suite.
- [x] `cargo test --release` for encoder, common and accel: 217 passed, 0 failed.
- [ ] GitHub CI on this PR, including the NEON execution job.

author: sdsleon
body:
# Summary

Collapsed reasoning rows in the chat now run to the row's right edge and end with the normal CSS ellipsis, instead of stopping at a fixed 120 characters mid-row. This covers the standalone "Thought" row, the live "Thinking" line, and Thought rows inside tool-call groups. The native iOS reasoning row gets the same fix.

# Why

`reasoningPreview.ts` cut every preview at 120 characters and appended its own "…", so the CSS `truncate` on the preview span never engaged on desktop-width rows. A reported row showed exactly 119 characters plus "…" in a row with room for about 165.

The bound is now 500. It remains a safety cap on DOM text: chat rows are capped at 920px, which holds roughly 220–265 characters at the smallest 8px chat font, so the CSS ellipsis at the row edge always decides the visible cut. iOS had the same pattern (a 90-character cap ahead of `.lineLimit(1)`, visible on iPad and in landscape) and now uses the same 500-character cap as a named constant. Android shows reasoning as a full-text card with no one-line preview, so it is unaffected.

# How verified

- Red → green: with the cap at 120, the new tests in `reasoningPreview.test.ts`, `Reasoning.test.tsx`, and `ReasoningInline.test.tsx` failed (preview cut to 119 characters plus "…"); with 500 they pass.
- `bun run checks --force`: format, lint, and typecheck (8,552 files) pass.
- `bun run vitest run` on `reasoningPreview.test.ts`, `Reasoning.test.tsx`, `ReasoningInline.test.tsx`, `ToolCallGroup.test.tsx`: 4 files, 74 tests pass.
- `xcrun swiftc -parse` on `RichChatTranscriptActivityComponents.swift`: OK.
- Manual QA in isolated mock sessions (`interactive-testing`): one built from the base commit `5306c09`, one from this branch, both at the default 1460×920 window, dark theme, opened "Fork smoke source" from the sidebar and appended the same reasoning, answer, and command items. Measured preview spans:
  - Before: standalone 120 chars ending in "…", no CSS truncation, 234px short of the row edge; inline 120 chars, 132px short.
  - After: standalone 279 chars and inline 245 chars, both CSS-truncated, 30px and 32px from the row edge (the chevron plus padding).
  - Expanding and collapsing both Thought rows with real clicks shows the full thought in the body, and collapsing restores identical preview geometry.
- CI scope (`scripts/ci-change-scope.mjs`): `core=true`, so CI runs the full sharded unit suite; `native_ios=true` (iOS build and AppTests); `native_android=false`.
- Not run locally: the full `bun run test` (CI runs it); the iOS build, AppTests, and simulator QA (local Xcode is 27.2, the project pins 26.6; native CI covers build and AppTests); mobile browser/PWA (same renderer components, and narrow rows were already CSS-truncated before this change); Android (no one-line reasoning preview).

# Before / After

Row crops from the two QA sessions above (same window size, theme, and data).

| | Standalone Thought row |
| --- | --- |
| Before | ![Before: standalone Thought row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b86d1ca1-a3a3-4d4f-9b90-f7b2ce51b182) |
| After | ![After: standalone Thought row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/990d85ec-0cbf-410b-8713-2c1ecfc7dfe0) |

| | Thought row inside a tool-call group |
| --- | --- |
| Before | ![Before: Thought row in a tool-call group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/624d989e-0b68-46a7-b9af-1c457968d21c) |
| After | ![After: Thought row in a tool-call group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fb1239c-42cc-4cbd-9c78-dd21cc38fd4f) |

# Risk & rollback

Display-only change: no persisted state, cache, protocol, or manifest is touched. Preview strings are now up to 500 characters on web (was 120) and iOS (was 88). Screen readers read the preview as part of the toggle's accessible name, so long thoughts announce more text than before. Roll back by reverting the merge commit.

Not in this PR: tool-call command rows have similar fixed caps in `commandSummary.ts` (120 characters for titles, 72 for git commands) and also stop short of the row edge.

body: This replaces the "prepared candidate" wording for `1.5.0` with the published state and adds the delivered-acceptance record (in the format of #95 and #102). Acceptance did **not** fully pass, so this PR records `published=true`, `accepted=false (partial)`, `deployed=false`. It does not claim acceptance. The requested title, "published and accepted", would have been inaccurate. **Published.** Release Automation run 42539192667 built tag `v1.5.0` from `81980d0` (tree `5d43fdf`). It published the PyPI wheel and sdist, the GitHub release, and the signed image `ghcr.io/consiliency/code-index-mcp@sha256:6ef6aa54…`. **Passed (dev0, Python 3.12.14, clean worktree at `81980d0`):** - **Downloads.** The PyPI wheel and sdist sha256 values match the recorded values and the GitHub release assets. `image-reference.txt` and `image-digest.txt` both name the published digest. - **Image signature.** Pulled anonymously by digest; the labels are `v1.5.0` and revision `81980d0`. cosign v2.5.2 (the workflow's version; its release checksum verified) verified the keyless signature with the workflow's identity (`release-automation.yml@refs/heads/main`), issuer and workflow SHA `81980d0`. - **Wheel and STDIO smoke.** `release_smoke.py --wheel-path --wheel-sha256 931f8ed7… --stdio --image-ref ` passed, using a fresh prefetched `TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_PACK_CACHE_DIR`. - **Container smoke.** dev0 can't reach bridge-published container ports (a plain `http.server` in the same image confirmed it). One deliberate rerun with `--docker-network host` passed: cosign, offline BAML, schema/prepare/Python as uid 999, HTTP queries before and after restart, log privacy, lifecycle and the safety probe. - **Co-install** of `index-it-mcp==1.5.0` with `phase-loop-runtime==0.7.30`: - `uv pip check` is clean, and the installed files match the wheel's RECORD. - Resolved: baml-bridge 0.23.0, tree-sitter 0.26.0, treesitter-chunker 6.0.0, language-pack 1.20.0. - `mcp-index --version` reports 1.5.0. `grammars prefetch` verified 47/47; `grammars check` found 47 offline, 0 missing. - With `MCP_BAML_TELEMETRY` unset or blank, a BAML import writes nothing under `~/.baml`. - **PMCP prepare.** Ran with the PyPI wheel: registry-origin manifest, PMCP 2.7.3. dev0's PMCP 2.7.3 tooling releases are archived symlinks that the binder refuses, so I installed PyPI `pmcp==2.7.3` as a private uv tool. The live dev0 gateway wasn't used. **Failed / not run:** - **Unconstrained PyPI install is broken.** The wheel declares `mcp>=1.0.0` with no upper bound, so `pip install index-it-mcp==1.5.0` (alone or co-installed) resolves `mcp` 2.3.0. `index-it-mcp stdio` then fails at import with `cannot import name 'McpError' from 'mcp.shared.exceptions'`. `1.4.1` has the same unbounded requirement. Release smoke and the pilot missed this because both install with lock constraints (`mcp` 1.27.0). Adding `"mcp<2"` resolves `mcp` 1.30.0 and STDIO passes, so the docs now pin it. A corrective release needs an owner decision. - **PMCP offline failed.** `reindex` returned `SandboxCallError`. The pilot fixture uses a fresh `XDG_CACHE_HOME` with no prefetched grammar cache, and network-denied sandbox workers can't download grammars. This is the #122 gap, still present in `scripts/v13_pmcp_pilot.py`. The same installed probe fails with a cold cache and passes with a warm one. - **PMCP rehearsal and browser not run.** Both use the same fixture. Rehearsal's Qdrant can't use bridge port publishing on dev0, and in host mode its gRPC port 6334 is held by dev0's live Qdrant. Browser also needs Inspector 2.6.0 and an operator session. **Deployed:** no. The dev0 code-index child still runs build `b79cc7c` and wasn't changed. **Changes** - README, GETTING_STARTED, MCP_CONFIGURATION and SUPPORT_MATRIX now say "published `1.5.0`" and add `"mcp<2"` to PyPI install guidance. - `v13-release.md`: Release Status and a new "1.5.0 Delivered Acceptance" record. - `V13_EXECUTION.md` and `public-package-identity.md` updated. - Version-pinned docs tests updated in lockstep: `test_release_metadata`, `test_pubname_public_docs`, `test_p8_customer_docs_alignment`, `test_p26_public_alpha_decision`. **Tests (dev0, one file per run, serial, under `nice`):** - All 66 `tests/docs` files, `tests/test_release_metadata.py`, `tests/test_v13_release_candidate.py` and `tests/smoke/test_release_smoke_contract.py` pass. - `tests/root_tests/test_readme_parsing.py` has 4 failures. That file only parses synthetic READMEs in `tmp_path` and reads no repo files, and this PR changes no code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? ## Summary
- Add `bbox_preservation="one_box"` and `"all_boxes"` to `RandomResizedCrop`. `None`, absent bbox fields, and empty bbox fields retain ordinary RRC sampling.
- `one_box` chooses uniformly from all active bbox fields and aliases. If the selected row has no visible geometry, the full frame is resized; no other box is selected.
- `all_boxes` protects the shared visible envelope. When constraints conflict, preserve geometry first, then choose the closest feasible ratio, then minimize scale deviation. Existing `BboxParams` filters remain active.
- Undersized `RandomCrop` and `CenterCrop` inputs are padded to their requested dimensions even when `pad_if_needed=False`. Batched images, masks, and mask3d targets preserve per-channel `fill` and `fill_mask` values.
- Non-finite OBB angles are filtered before normalization to avoid runtime warnings. `ReplayCompose` records exact crop coordinates; applied configs remain runnable but do not promise exact crop replay.

## Validation
- Full focused suite: **10,032 passed, 9 skipped** on Python 3.12.8. After the final target-alignment and volume-test refinements: **3 passed**.
- Ruff, mypy on changed implementation and focused RRC files, Pyrefly on implementation/focused tests, AX rules, and behavior-policy checks passed.
- Added docstrings for the complex new crop helpers and batched padding handlers flagged by coverage review.
- Full pre-commit could not complete locally: the project Python wrapper recurses, `uv` is unavailable, and the EOF hook cannot write readonly skill files. Direct checks were run; local commit hooks were bypassed.

## Performance
Paired public-Compose diagnostic comparing pre-review commit `21647a5` with the reviewed RRC implementation, on macOS ARM64 with Python 3.12.8, NumPy 2.5.4, OpenCV 5.0.0, PyTorch 2.15.0, Albucore 0.3.5, NumKong 7.8.7 (NEON enabled), and one CPU thread. Each workload used interleaved before/after pairs; each sample warmed up and timed seven batches of 201 calls.

| Workload | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RRC `None`, image only, 256×384 uint8 | 0.1006 ms | 0.1015 ms | +0.8% |
| RRC `None`, 32 HBB, 1080×1920 uint8 | 0.2434 ms | 0.2341 ms | −3.8% |
| `one_box`, 1 HBB, 256×384 uint8 | 0.2008 ms | 0.2041 ms | +1.6% |
| `all_boxes`, 1,000 HBB, 256×384 uint8 | 0.4234 ms | 0.4329 ms | +2.3% |
| `all_boxes`, 32 OBB, 256×384 uint8 | 0.4967 ms | 0.4905 ms | −1.3% |
| `all_boxes`, 1,000 OBB, 1080×1920 uint8 | 3.4063 ms | 3.4225 ms | +0.5% |

The OBB cells were rerun after the finite-angle guard; the later commits only changed fixed-crop padding and tests. Earlier Python 3.11.15/M4 Max acceptance comparing `fbba9b7` with the initial feature commit `6cb71ca` measured default Compose cells at 0.322→0.294 ms (256×384 uint8, no boxes), 0.415→0.413 ms (256×384 float32, 32 HBB), 0.463→0.466 ms (1080×1920 uint8, 32 HBB), and 0.543→0.542 ms (1080×1920 float32, no boxes). The current follow-up is diagnostic because this checkout has no Python 3.11 executable.

author: ryan-graves
body:
## Summary

Sign-in has never worked on Netlify deploy previews ("Sign-in failed: Sign-in timed out").

### Cause

`/auth/callback` was a route handler that redirected to `/auth/callback/exchange` using `new URL(path, request.url)`. On Netlify, `request.url` inside a function resolves to the deploy's **canonical** host, not the host the request came in on. Observed on the live deploys:

```
deploy-preview-92--eggo-web.netlify.app/auth/callback?code=…
  → 307 → 6af118617c1b58dc0e03ab85--eggo-web.netlify.app/auth/callback/exchange?code=…

eggo.fun/auth/callback?code=…
  → 307 → eggo.fun/auth/callback/exchange?code=…
```

On a preview the browser therefore arrived on the permalink host, a different origin from the `deploy-preview-N--` host it signed in on. The PKCE verifier lives in the originating origin's localStorage, so supabase-js's `_isPKCECallback` returned false, no exchange was attempted, and the page sat until its 10 s timeout. That is exactly the screenshot: the error is shown on the `<deploy-id>--eggo-web.netlify.app` host, which the user never navigated to. Production only worked because `eggo.fun` redirects to `eggo.fun`.

### Fix

- `/auth/callback` is now the client page itself (`src/app/auth/callback/page.tsx`); the route handler and nested `exchange` page are removed. No server hop, so the exchange runs on the origin that holds the verifier. The Supabase redirect-URL allowlist entries (`…/auth/callback`) are unchanged.
- When no session appears after init, the page calls `exchangeCodeForSession` explicitly and shows its error (e.g. the missing-verifier message, an expired or reused code) instead of a generic timeout.
- Provider errors (`?error=`, `?error_description=`) still bounce to the landing page, now client-side.
- CLAUDE.md notes the Netlify `request.url` constraint so the hop isn't reintroduced.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test`: 287 passing (5 new for the callback page: provider error bounce, already-exchanged session, explicit exchange, exchange error shown, missing code)
- [x] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run lint:css`, `npm run build` (`/auth/callback` prerenders as a static page)
- [ ] On this PR's deploy preview: `curl -sI https://deploy-preview-<n>--eggo-web.netlify.app/auth/callback?code=x` should return 200 with no `Location` header
- [ ] Sign in with Google on the deploy preview and land on `/home`
- [ ] Sign in on production still works after merge

## Summary

- A leak on **any** branch turned **every** open PR's `secret-scan` red. The job checks out with
  `fetch-depth: 0`, which fetches every branch, and `gitleaks git` scans every ref by default. The
  red-CI proofs for #17 showed it: #22, #23 and #24 failed on #25's fake key.
- CI now runs `just secret-scan --log-opts=HEAD`. On a PR, `HEAD` is the merge commit, so the scan
  covers main's full history plus that PR's own commits, and nothing else. Local
  `just secret-scan` still scans every local ref, which also catches unpushed branches.

## Related

Refs #17

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` is green, and the test count looks right (not zero, and up by the tests added)
- [ ] A red run was observed before the green, for each behaviour change
- [x] Dogfooded on real local transcripts (if the change affects output)
- [ ] Snapshot changes reviewed line by line (if any)

### Evidence

The sandbox repo was outside the project, with a clean `main` and a `leaky` branch holding a fake
generic `api_key`:

| Command | Checked out | Result |
| ------- | ----------- | ------ |
| `gitleaks git --redact .` (old CI behaviour) | `main` | **red**: `leaks found: 1` (from the other branch) |
| `just secret-scan --log-opts=HEAD` (before this change) | this repo | **red**: `justfile does not contain recipe --log-opts=HEAD` |
| `just secret-scan --log-opts=HEAD` | sandbox `main` | green: `no leaks found` |
| `just secret-scan --log-opts=HEAD` | sandbox `leaky` | **red**, exit 1: a branch's own leak is still caught |

`just ci` exit 0, with **0 tests**: there is no Cargo workspace yet (#3), so the Rust checks are
skipped. rumdl reports no issues and zizmor offline reports no findings.

## Notes for reviewers

Pull-request refs (`refs/pull/N/head`) aren't fetched by `actions/checkout`, so the closed red PRs'
commits never reach the scan either way.

author: knehari
body:
## Jira issue
TRUST- — no existing ticket is known for this change; none was invented. Stacked on knehari/trust-platform#192 (base `claude/console-redesign`).

## Change and rationale
The inventory showed only the issuance state (`SIGNED`), so a revoked certificate looked current in every management read.

- **Migration 0033** appends two columns to `management_certificate`, read from the core `revocation` table that an approved revocation writes (ADR-0018):
  - `revoked_at` (UTC);
  - `revocation_reason` (RFC 5280 CRLReason code).

  The issuance state is unchanged. A version marker `management_certificate_revocation_version()` is added.
- **API**: certificate list, by-request and by-serial routes return both fields. The startup view check and the isolation readiness check require 0033. OpenAPI is updated.
- **Console**:
  - inventory: a "Revoked" badge with reason and date, and a muted row;
  - detail panel: a revocation banner and a lifecycle fact;
  - dashboard: revoked certificates are counted apart and left out of upcoming expiries;
  - CSV and JSON exports carry both fields.
- **Plumbing**: migration runner, CI lists, ledger counts (21 → 22), retry, populated upgrade and restore scripts.

## Security impact / trust boundary
Read-only. The view keeps the 0021 reader filter: a principal sees revocations of granted authorities only, and nothing without a declared principal. `trust_api_reader` still cannot read the `revocation` table directly; the new SQL suite asserts it. Relying parties learn of a revocation from the next published CRL, not from this field; the console and docs say so.

## Tests and evidence
Run locally on PostgreSQL 16:
- `tests/management_certificate_revocation.sql` (new);
- the existing management SQL suites: read-only, reader isolation, SAN, revocation/CRL, CRL publication, applications, issuance;
- the populated 0011 → 0033 upgrade, the interrupted retry, the ledger with fault and untracked cases, the ledger restore and the dump restore.

API: unit tests (60) and Clippy with `-D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check` passes.

Frontend: 77 tests; one new test caught a numeric-cell bug in the CSV export, fixed here.

Fresh laboratory stack: the browser, profile-lifecycle, CA-proposal and certificate-application e2e suites pass. The certificate-application suite now checks `state`, `revoked_at` and `revocation_reason` through the inventory after an approved revocation.

CI has not yet run on this branch.

## Documentation / ADR updated
`docs/architecture/management-api-readonly.md` (migration range and the new fields), `docs/DEVELOPMENT_STATUS.md`. ADR-0018 already defines the revocation record; no new ADR.

## No secrets or employer IP
- [x] Verified

author: sangchul1011
body:
## Summary

Since #152, the web UI loads but stops working in dev mode (`./start.sh --dev`), because every API call returns `400 Invalid host header`.

Vite's string proxy shorthand (`'/api': 'http://backend:8000'`) implicitly sets `changeOrigin: true`, which rewrites `Host` to `backend:8000`. The backend's `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check then rejects it. The production stack was not affected, because nginx forwards the browser's `Host`.

## Changes

- `vite.config.ts`: the proxy now sets `changeOrigin: false`, matching nginx's `proxy_set_header Host $host`. The backend allowlist is unchanged.
- `docker-compose.override.yml`: removes the `5173` host port mapping. The dev server is already published on `FRONTEND_PORT`, and the extra mapping made `./start.sh --dev` fail with `port is already allocated` whenever another project used 5173.
- Adds a regression test for the proxy options.

## Test plan

- [x] Dev stack before the fix: `/api/v1/deployment` through Vite returns 400
- [x] Plain `./start.sh --dev` after the fix: starts with another container holding 5173, and `/api/v1/deployment` through Vite returns 200
- [x] `/api/v1/sources` and `/api/v1/mcp/status` return 200, and SSE returns `text/event-stream`
- [x] A foreign `Host` is still rejected
- [x] `viteProxy.spec.ts` fails without the fix; vitest (80 passed) and `vue-tsc` pass with it

author: graftrahula666
body:
## Production incident / diagnosis
The user reports no liquid on the main PIVNIK screen on Android. Current **Telegram and VK Railway production** runs `98b2c9176a28a275118a094c918f29aafb37d489` and loads the Mazut client assets (HTTP 200 for sampled assets). On main, `createRenderer()` throws on shader compile/link and no fallback runs after WebGL successfully opens; the outer home init catches and logs only, leaving the fluid canvas transparent. Unsupported `MediaQueryList.addEventListener` also aborts on legacy WebViews. **These are confirmed code failure paths, not yet proven root causes for the user's specific Android device.**

## Small isolated change
- Recover from WebGL init/shader and incomplete framebuffer errors to existing CPU canvas renderer; replace the canvas when it was already claimed by WebGL, rebind ink sampling, and preserve fluid settings and viscosity `1.265`.
- On GPU context loss, render with CPU instead of leaving a blank frame.
- Support legacy media-query listeners and absent observers.
- Last resort static dark liquid silhouette when *both* graphics contexts fail.
- Version frontend assets to avoid stale WebView cache.
- Extend existing Telegram/VK Android LOW smoke to force a broken GPU shader and old MediaQueryList API, assert 2D engine and actual painted ink pixels. HIGH keeps WebGL.
- Document new contract and real-device acceptance in ops/MODULE-MAP.md.

## Risk / release gate
Root branch from verified latest origin/main `98b2c9176a28a275118a094c918f29aafb37d489`. No new apply scripts, no server/API/auth/bonus/QR/POS/DB/kiosk changes. Draft only; no merge, no production deploy, no real kiosk flash. CI, VK bundle parity, double materialization and physical Android provider session tests required before release. No real hardware available in this ChatGPT session.

## 2026-11-09 WebView compatibility research and safe CPU optimization
External technical review: [MDN WebGL memory/performance](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API/WebGL_best_practices), [2026 Android WebView context-loss field report](https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/540886013), [Reddit WebGL compositor invisibility report](https://www.reddit.com/r/Devvit/comments/1w4sb9n/reddit_android_2026350_expanded_webview_no_longer/) and [Android in-app testing guidance](https://www.browserstack.com/support/faq/live/features-live/can-i-test-my-product-functionality-on-in-app-webview-with-live). These field reports are **not evidence of the user's phone model or exact failure**. Full source/decision/acceptance matrix: [ops/ANDROID-MAZUT-WEBVIEW-RESEARCH-20261109.md](https://github.com/GrafTrahula666/pivnik-bonus-app/blob/fix/android-mazut-webgl-fallback-20261109/ops/ANDROID-MAZUT-WEBVIEW-RESEARCH-20261109.md).

The Android-only **software** fallback now limits raster backbuffer to LOW/balanced/HIGH 260/300/340 pixels wide, can adapt lower on prolonged slow frames, and limits CPU raster cadence to 55 ms. Original iOS CPU budgets and all iOS/Android **WebGL** frame rates, shader code, physics and viscosity are untouched. Unit test proves the literal iOS original budgets. Existing Telegram/VK browser smoke now additionally forces context loss from HIGH and checks 2D visible pixels while continuing normal session/QR/navigation. No production flags or Android kiosk changes. The iPhone/device sign-off remains a separate release gate.

**Hold:** a WebGL canvas may be invisible to the compositor even when GPU calls succeed. That is not detectable reliably via `readPixels`. Do not claim real-device compatibility without actual in-app Android WebView testing; BrowserStack **App Live** or Firebase Test Lab physical devices are candidates, browser emulator is not equivalent.

author: kiran01bm
body:
The PR comment's progress summary now shows one rows-weighted percent across all running tables, instead of whichever running table happened to be listed last.

## Why

`writeProgressSummary` overwrote `runningPct` on every running table, so "2 running (X%)" showed the last one's percent. The same apply read 90% or 40% depending only on the order its tables were listed in, and neither figure described the two copies together.

## What

- A new `runningPercentText` covers three cases.
  - One running table still shows its own percent, unchanged.
  - Several running tables show rows copied over rows to copy across all of them, in the same two-decimal format.
  - When any running table has no row total yet, the rows cannot be weighed against each other, so no percent is shown rather than a made-up one.
- The "(finalizing copy)" label is unchanged.
- `presentation.PercentAcrossTargets` is not reused. It describes one table across its targets, returns a whole number capped at 99, and gives an unknown total an equal share, so it would render "40%" next to the single-table "90.00%".

## Before / after

Three tables: `audit_log` has completed, `orders` is running at 400,000 of 1,000,000 rows, and `events` is running at 9,000 of 10,000. Before, the summary shows whichever running table is listed last. After, it shows (400,000 + 9,000) / 1,010,000 in either order.

```
Before                                   After

orders  400,000 / 1,000,000  (40%)       orders  400,000 / 1,000,000  (40%)
events    9,000 /    10,000  (90%)       events    9,000 /    10,000  (90%)
     │                                        │
     ▼                                        ▼
keep the last running table's %          sum rows copied over rows to copy
 orders last → 40.00%                     409,000 / 1,010,000
 events last → 90.00%                     → 40.50% in either order
 ✗ depends on list order
```

<details>
<summary>Before</summary>

📊 1/3 complete · 2 running (90.00%)

(or 📊 1/3 complete · 2 running (40.00%) with the tables listed the other way round)

</details>

<details>
<summary>After</summary>

📊 1/3 complete · 2 running (40.50%)

</details>

author: tks98
body:
Fixes and features from using snoopy as different kinds of users would, start to finish, against local servers. They're the bug, rough edges and gaps that review found. Each commit is one item and can be reviewed on its own.

## Fixes

- **Ctrl-C during startup was lost** when snoopy started with SIGINT ignored, as a script's background job does. It asked for the signal only once tracing began, and kept running after that. It now exits at once, as Go's default would (`TestCtrlCWhileStarting`, which fails without the fix).
- **HAR kept a chunked body's framing.** A chunked body without compression was saved as `2\r\nok\r\n0\r\n\r\n` instead of `ok` (`TestHARChunked`).
- **Messages:**
  - The "permission denied inspecting" warning names the processes, `name[pid]`, and says "1 process".
  - Without root, the error starts with what to do.
  - A mistyped flag gets "did you mean --brief?".
  - An unknown address shows as `local:?` or `peer:?`, not `local` and `peer`.
  - A bare `snoopy` says once that it traces every process.
- **`--comm` takes names over 15 bytes,** matched on the program's file name, as `--help` already said (`TestLongComm`, with and without BTF).

## New

- **`--requests`:** one line per HTTP exchange once its response ends. Each line has the method, URL, version, status, type, size and decoded size, `grpc-status`, and the time from request to response, plus `served` when snoopy traces the server. It's HAR's pairing, which now says when an exchange ends, with nothing kept.
  ```
  curl[13221] GET https://127.0.0.1:37119/api/users HTTP/2 → 200, application/json, 61 bytes (gzip, 48 decoded), 811µs
  ```
- **`--brief` folds long bodies.** A 128 KiB download took 32 lines. Now it's the first call, then the last with `[+30 calls folded, 122880 bytes]`. `--verbose` shows every call.
- **JSON `http1` field.** HTTP/1.x requests, responses and body pieces are parsed, as HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 already were.
- **gRPC:**
  - Every message says which call it belongs to, and whether it's the request or the response.
  - `--proto FILE` takes descriptor sets from `protoc --descriptor_set_out` or `buf build -o` and decodes with field and enum names: `status: SERVING` instead of `1: 1`.
  - This adds `google.golang.org/protobuf`, and the binary grows from 9.2 to 11.2 MB.
- **`--har FILE` is written as it goes.** The file is created at once, then atomically rewritten while it changes, so `kill -9` keeps it. That was checked by hand.
- **`--grep REGEXP`** matches decoded headers, decompressed bodies and gRPC fields, after `--redact`.
- **`--duration TIME`** stops snoopy after that long.
- **`--java` with `go install`.** The agent's jars are embedded, 271 KB, built by `make jars` with the release's JDK, Temurin 21.0.13+9. A new CI job checks they match the sources, like the BPF objects check. `build.sh` now dates jar entries 2000-01-01, since jars committed in the same commit can't know that commit's time.
- **Packages:** `.deb`, `.rpm` and `.apk` for amd64 and arm64 in releases, covered by `checksums.txt` and so by the attestation. The release check installs them on Ubuntu, Fedora and Alpine. A Homebrew tap or Nixpkgs entry needs a repository of its own, so it isn't here.

## Docs

- **docs/usage.md:** the flags block is regenerated from `--help`. New examples for `--requests`, folding and gRPC with and without `--proto` come from real runs, and the JSON field table has the new fields.
- **README, HANDOFF.md and AGENTS.md:** the new features and how they work, and AGENTS.md has a "Changing the Java agent" rule.

| Unit tests, `-race` | Pass, both modules |

| Integration suite, Linux 6.18, uprobe_multi links | 50 pass, rustls and quinn included |

| By hand | `--requests` with curl, Python, Node and Go; `--proto` with grpc-go's health service; `--java` from a binary alone in a directory; the HAR file after `kill -9` |

author: cobular
body:
Closes #42.

**Cause:** the host fetched plugin manifests once at boot, then every `ManifestRefresh` (15 min). Sidecars start alongside Bindery, so the boot fetch often hit a plugin that wasn't listening yet — and it stayed unusable for 15 minutes or until someone pressed refresh. Same for a plugin restarting under a running host.

**Fix (no new dependency — a small loop, not Polly):**
- When any configured plugin is unusable, `PluginRefreshService` retries **only those** with exponential backoff: `Bindery:Plugins:ManifestRetry` (2s) doubling to `ManifestRetryMax` (1 min). Healthy plugins keep the 15-minute cadence.
- The registry signals when any refresh (background or the Plugins-page button) finds a plugin down, which restarts the backoff at the shortest delay.
- `RefreshAsync` now records any non-shutdown exception as the plugin's error; previously an unexpected exception type escaped and left the plugin with no descriptor at all.

**Tests:** new `A_plugin_that_goes_down_is_reconnected_without_anyone_pressing_refresh` (stub manifest 503 → recovers within the retry; fails on `main` after 10s). Core 140/140, Host 82/82.

- Allow Down+Right on the upright pipe landing tick and Up+Down while aligned. Allow grounded, right-facing contact to enter a sideways pipe after Right is released.
- Add regression coverage and update the architecture, testing, and backlog guides.

## Summary

This is the last O-05 PR. It completes Causalith's library API with:
- `intervention_test()`, the restricted CI test behind Causentra's trial T8, built on #213's blocks (05-causalith §3.7 steps 1–7: parents, baseline-only ridge fit, persistent robust z of the target and of the residual, explained fraction, block-conformal p-value, untestable reasons);
- `partial_corr_test()`, the CI ablation arm (§3.7);
- the **cross-engine checks** of the Observe lane (05 §7): Anomara's `onsets.entry_services` equals Causalith's entry nodes on every fixture, and Causalith's re-implemented robust scale floor equals Anomara's;
- a recorded per-service CI result on synth.

With the five stacked PRs below it, this completes O-05.

Closes #22 · stacked on #213 (base `observe/210-ci-test`)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lane** | observe (`packages/causalith`, `tests/integration/test_observe_entry.py`, an Observe-lane path). `cross-lane` because CI takes the lane from the PR author (the lead), and the stack carries `uv.lock` |
| **Type** | feat |
| **Agent used** | Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (session obs-detect) |
| **Contract / ADR** | none |

Drafted by the lead's agent (Claude Code) with the lane owner's agreement; the lane owner reviews and owns the engine afterwards.

### What is in it
- **`ci.partial_corr_test(x, y, z) -> (r, p)`**: x and y are residualised on z with the CI solver (no penalty); then Pearson r, Fisher `z = atanh(r)·sqrt(n − dim(z) − 3)`, and a two-sided `p = erfc(|z|/√2)`. No scipy is needed. The textbook check (r = 0.5, n = 28 → z = 2.7465, p = 0.00602) is a test.
- **`tests/integration/test_observe_entry.py`** (Observe lane path):
  - for all 13 fixture cases, `onsets.entry_services == sorted(node where is_entry)`. Today that is `[]` on the oracle cases and `[frontend]` on `synth-01@detected`, where both engines copy `alert.detector`;
  - hypothesis parity of the scale floor and of ε(family, unit) between `veyltrace_anomara.robust` and `veyltrace_causalith.ci`.
- **`fixtures/handmade/ci-synth.json`** records `intervention_test` for every synth service, as 05 §7 asks. Every result is `no_target` until Signalyth (O-02) fills `signal_cube.series`. The synth-01 check ("the CPU-hog service is not explained by its callees") is then written without naming the service: some service comes out `independent_of_parents = True`. It skips until O-02.

Met by #209's hand-made golden. It compares nodes and edges with `veyltrace_core.synth.layout` (`SERVICES`, `EXPECTED_EDGES`, `EXTERNAL_HOST`), and the synth topology is written as Signalyth will (O-02). On the synth fixtures themselves, the graph today has the nodes plus the two log edges, because `signal_cube.edges` is empty under the Signalyth stub. Once O-02 lands, the regenerated synth `graph.edges` should equal `EXPECTED_EDGES`, with log/topology provenance on two of them. Whoever merges second regenerates the cascade.

author: redmentos
body:
A positive skill rating could be re-applied after a later fact correction, recreating the success it had just retracted. A neutral rating could also leave an old positive or negative outcome in AG4.

This source-hash-bound candidate rechecks the routed skill, current explicit rating, FINAL answer, context sources and F5/F1 correction in the same SQLite transaction as the skill outcome and live marker. An active factual correction takes precedence over a conflicting positive rating; a neutral note retracts an earlier rating. A fact correction without an explicit nonneutral rating is recorded as pending without adding an AG4 use or success.

Before either existing skill fast path, the candidate checks current outcome sources and detects pending or undelivered rating/fact feedback. It falls back to normal routing if evidence is invalid or conflicting; it does not remove a blocked skill merely to make another conflicting skill look unambiguous. Tests include source revocation, concurrent rating/correction, a failed AGI hook, SQLite rollback and retry, restart, and the existing C5/replay flow.

The earlier FINAL-based parity expectation also remains separately RED on its candidate copy.

author: aschenbath
body:
With `ranker: 'longest-path'`, compound graphs could place children outside their cluster. The first upward ordering sweep skipped the bottom rank, leaving its initial order ungrouped by cluster. If that sweep had the best crossing count, the selected layout retained crossed border chains and computed incorrect cluster bounds.

Include the bottom rank in upward sweeps so its subgraphs are grouped before the crossing count is evaluated. Regression coverage checks child containment, non-overlapping sibling clusters, and finite edge routes across all three rankers, four directions, five alignments, and nested clusters.

Fixes #528.

Validation: four new test cases fail on the base revision; all 12 new cases pass with the fix. On Node 18 and 24, the complete suite has 355 passing tests and the same pre-existing Windows failure in the dist ESM test (it imports a drive-letter path rather than a file URL). Type checking, lint, and the normal build pass. A separate installed-package consumer checks CJS, ESM, and both browser bundles, including edge endpoints on node boundaries. The other two rankers retain exactly the same coordinates across the 80 control layouts.

The existing lock file pins graphlib 4.0.5 while the manifest requires 4.0.6; validation used `npm install --package-lock=false`. Generated dist files are left for the release build, avoiding unrelated existing version/dependency drift.

This change and its tests were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance.

author: derek-miller
body:
## What was wrong

The Hatch night light can't take a color without lighting: the account driver's `setColor` always sets the color with a brightness, which is 100 when the light is off. So a color sent to a Hatch Night Light while it was off, from programming, a scene or the color picker, turned the light on.

## What changes

The Hatch Night Light driver now follows Control4's reference smart bulb driver (DRIV-7274) for a color set while off:

- It's kept as the next on's color and not sent, so the light stays off. Control4 is told it at once as the light's color. A state report while the light is still off tells the kept color, not the dark one.
- The next On, Toggle or level from off carries it, in one command with the level.
- It clears once the light reports on, whether Control4 or the Hatch app turned it on.
- A color sent after an On but before the light reports on goes out as before. Hatch's state comes back through its cloud, and programming that turns a light on and then sets its color shouldn't lose the color. An On the account can't send, while it's disconnected, doesn't count.
- A Navigator tap is DYNAMIC_ON: the proxy sends the level, then 5 to 6 ms later the Color On Mode's own color naming its preset (measured on the dev controller, 2026-11-08). After an on in the color set while off, a color naming a preset within 250 ms isn't sent, and the proxy is told the color the light keeps. This driver takes no Color On Mode, so it can't match the preset's id; any preset-named color in that window is the follow-up. A color naming no preset is still a new pick, and a preset's color sent later goes out.
- A level of 0 still goes out as `setBrightness` 0, as before.

The driver's docs say what a color set while off does, and the changelog has a Fixed line.

Not in this PR: hatch_light's driver.xml declares the Color On Mode capabilities, but the driver has no UPDATE_COLOR_ON_MODE handler. That's a separate item.

## Tests

- New `test_hatch_light.lua`: a color while off sends nothing and is told at once; a report while off tells it; the next On, a level and Toggle from off each carry it in one command; once the light has reported on, the next on carries none; a color after an On, before the report, goes out; a color while on goes out; a level of 0 is unchanged; an on from elsewhere clears it; after an On the account couldn't send, a color while off is still kept; and the measured Navigator On, where the level carries the color and the follow-up isn't sent, while a color naming no preset and a preset's color 300 ms later still go out.
- Against main's driver, 10 of its 17 checks fail. With the follow-up guard turned off, 2 fail.
- `make fmt`, `make check`, `make test` and `make build` pass, and the build leaves a clean tree.

author: deciare
body:
A memory could not be found by when it changed. `memory_search` took a query, a mode, a type, a corpus and a limit, and nothing else, so dates existed only as text inside bodies and paths and "what did we decide yesterday" meant grepping the store by hand.

`since` and `until` now keep only entries whose modification date falls inside the window, both bounds inclusive. A memory is dated by `edited ?? created` — the schema already rejects an `edited` earlier than `created`, so that is whichever is later without comparing them — and a document by its file modification time. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` means that calendar day in the server's local timezone, because "yesterday" is the asker's yesterday; a value carrying a time means that instant. An impossible date, an unreadable one, or a window that runs backwards is an error naming what was wrong, never an empty result: an empty result is a claim about the store, and these are mistakes in the question.

Date filters apply to memories only, and imply `corpus: memory`. A document's date is a file timestamp, which a backlink or a `touch` moves without the content changing, so filtering documents by it would answer a different question than the one asked. Naming `corpus: all` or `corpus: documents` alongside a date is an error rather than a silent narrowing.

The window is applied before any content is compared. Keyword search filters as it walks the index; the embeddings path hands the window to the vector query, which is where item 40 made it possible to filter before the nearest-neighbour cutoff rather than after it. One predicate — kinds, type, status, dates — now serves both paths, replacing the copy the semantic path kept of the other three.

`query` stays required and this tool stays a search: listing the recent past is a different question with different parameters, and it gets its own tool rather than being a meaning that arrives when an argument is absent.

The result cap is still 25, and a request above it now says so instead of returning a shorter answer silently.

Not done here, deliberately: no ordering knob, no oldest-first, and no date filtering in automatic recall.

Tests cover the window (inclusive at both ends, an undated entry excluded by a bound and included without one), local-day resolution including an impossible date, inverted windows, the keyword path honouring the window, and the tool's rules — that a query is required, that dates narrow the corpus to memories and say so, that an explicit documents corpus is refused rather than narrowed, and that a clamped limit announces itself.

author: daun-gatal
body:
## Description

Found while testing #24 (its follow-up "B3"): two Flink CDC pipelines deployed to one Kubernetes runtime 12 s apart both passed preflight's capacity check, but the namespace's ResourceQuota couldn't hold both. The first one's pods didn't exist yet, so the measured quota usage didn't count them. The second pipeline then waited forever, and its status said only "Waiting for the pod to be created".

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- **Preflight counts pipelines still starting.** `runtime_capacity` adds what the other pipelines on the same runtime ask for when they should run but have no pods yet: never observed, last observed `missing`, or pending without a pod (`runtime.ReasonNoPod` / `runtime.ReasonRefusedPrefix`). The message names them; over the quota it blocks as before, and the fix says to wait for them, pause one, choose a smaller size, or raise the quota.
- **A pod Kubernetes won't create says why.** A Deployment without a pod reports Kubernetes' `ReplicaFailure` message, e.g. `Kubernetes won't create the pod: … exceeded quota: …`, instead of only "Waiting for the pod to be created". A Flink CDC cluster whose TaskManagers are refused says `TaskManagers: …`.
- Check catalog and reference, the guide (it already promised "the pipeline shows why"), contracts, changelog.

## Testing

author: codewesleylima
body:
## Objetivo
Ao abrir Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI ou Gemini CLI na raiz do projeto, a IA reconhece as instruções do IWDex e pode delegar tarefas não triviais a especialistas sem o usuário executar manualmente comandos ou abrir painéis.

## Mudanças
- `IWMESH_HOST.md`: contrato canônico compartilhado do host, com delegação proporcional, consulta a conhecimentos e revisão.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` e Copilot: instruções nativas para descoberta, impedindo delegação recursiva nos workers.
- `mesh_autopilot.py`: despachante consultivo assíncrono, sem trocar a IA principal, com painel Windows automático, status e espera.
- `mcp_iwdex.py`: mesmo comportamento via MCP, suporte a `windows=true` por padrão e status antes de o manifest ser escrito.
- `mesh2.py`: variável `IWMESH_WORKER` para delimitar o contexto dos trabalhadores.
- Instalador: copia arquivos v2.1 e anexa instruções com marcadores em projetos previamente configurados sem sobrescrever.
- Documentação de instalação e uso automático; CI Linux/Windows e testes.

## Segurança e limitações
A experiência acontece após uma demanda e autorização normal da CLI; instruções de repositório **não forçam** execução automática caso a ferramenta recuse processos. Os painéis mostram logs, não chats interativos. Os workers seguem read-only; saída `completed_unverified` ainda não comprova correção. O runtime não implementa edição paralela, consenso peer-to-peer ou sandbox forte. Testes com CLIs simuladas não validam login real de provedores nem GUI em desktop Windows.

## Revisão
Verificar CI do PR e branch atual antes do merge.

author: gonpassa
body:
Closes #86.

The mandatory-Link invariant of ADR 0014 holds at every moment, and the two deletion guards were the ones still missing: saving (#84) and removing the last Link (#85) were already in place, so since #84 landed, deleting a Literature note or a Source could quietly orphan a Permanent note. This closes that gap.

## The guard

One piece of logic in `backend/src/modules/notes/orphanGuard.ts`, asked by every delete path rather than reimplemented per path. It reads the Links a cascade would take (`listLinksTouchingNotes`, new, a batch form of the existing single-note read), takes the far ends of those Links, and asks the existing `findPermanentNotesLeftUnlinked` which of them would end at zero - the count taken in either direction, since a Permanent note reachable only from another note's Links is linked. Notes being deleted are left out of the question: a Permanent note cannot be orphaned by its own deletion.

A Source asks it once across the whole batch of Literature notes it cascades to, so the refusal names every idea that would have been left unlinked rather than stopping at the first.

Guard and cascade stay distinct (ADR 0012): the guard decides whether the deletion happens, and the delete statements behind it are untouched.

## Deleting a note is now kind-agnostic

`DELETE /api/notes/:noteId` took only the Literature kind; it now takes either, as the connections view at that same id already does. ADR 0014 names a Permanent note's deletion as one of the guard points, and the invariant holds of both kinds. `PATCH` still narrows to the Literature kind, since the fields a correction writes belong to that kind. `findLiteratureNoteOwnedByUser` had no caller left and is gone.

## The refusal

A 409 in the module's voice, naming the notes and what to do next. The shared message builder now takes the action it refused in front of it, so one shape serves all three guard points, and the link-removal path keeps its existing wording bar one correction (see below).

Both delete dialogs show the refusal where the deletion was asked for and stay open - the same shape `RemoveLinkDialog` already uses, because the notes it names were written elsewhere and are nowhere else on the page. Verified in the browser against a throwaway database, not just in tests:

| Source | Note |
| --- | --- |
| "Deleting this Source would leave ... with nothing connected to it." | "Deleting this note would leave ... with nothing connected to it." |

## Review follow-ups

Two changes came out of reviewing the first commit:

- **The second commit** gives the refusal its missing noun. "with none" leaned on a word the action happened to carry - "Removing this connection" supplied it, "Deleting this note" did not - so the sentence now says "with nothing connected to it" at all three guard points. That is a copy change to #85's refusal as well, since it is one builder.
- `client/src/modules/notes/components/TopicTags/TopicTags.test.tsx` had a formatting violation on `main`; `npm run format` corrected it in passing.

Two findings were left alone, deliberately:

- **Guard and delete are not one transaction.** Two concurrent deletions can each see the other's Link as surviving and both pass, leaving a Permanent note at zero. This is the shape the existing `deleteLink` guard already has, and closing it means threading a transaction through the db layer for every delete path - a change to the module's seams rather than to this ticket, so it is not made here.
- **A mutually-linked pair of Permanent notes cannot be escaped by deleting.** Each refuses because it is the other's only Link, and the Link between them refuses too, so the refusal's "or delete it" is unreachable in that one state; the way out is a new Link. That is ADR 0014's constraint behaving as written, not a defect in the guard.

## Acceptance criteria

All seven met: both note kinds and the Source refuse on the condition with the same message shape, the Source names every affected note across the batch, deletions that orphan nothing cascade as before (Answer history does not exist yet to cascade to - #89), the guard is one shared piece, the refusal reads in the module's voice and says what to do next, and backend lint, client lint, 533 backend tests and 400 client tests all pass.

author: juliantellez
body:
**What.** Terraform stops owning the code of the three deployed functions. The pipeline uploads it instead. Each function keeps the placeholder it is created from, and gains `ignore_changes` on its file name and its code hash. A new `functions` job builds one bundle for each function and loads every bundle through the runtime interface emulator. On a merge into `main` it uploads the authorizer, then the articles, then the vault, and waits after each one. Its last step reads the live api and requires a refusal.

**Why.** The vault service is written and the account runs placeholders. Terraform cannot take the zip as a file. The plan job builds no bundle, so a plan that needed one would refuse every pull request. This is the pattern the website already uses: a placeholder in Terraform, the code ignored as drift, and the pipeline as the only path from a merge into the account.

Second piece of `docs/design/deployed-functions.md`. The first piece is https://github.com/atlantic-blue/emi/pull/563.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LIST["tools/deploy/functions.ts: the name and the entry point of each function"] --> BUILD["Build one bundle for each function"]
  BUILD --> LOAD{"Does every bundle load through the runtime interface emulator?"}
  LOAD -->|"no"| RED["The job fails. Nothing is uploaded"]
  LOAD -->|"yes, on a pull request"| ENDS["The run ends. The account is untouched"]
  LOAD -->|"yes, on a merge into main"| UP["Upload: the authorizer, then the articles, then the vault"]
  APPLY["terraform apply, on a merge into main"] --> UP
  UP --> WAIT["Wait for each function to report itself updated"]
  WAIT --> LIVE{"Does every authorized route refuse an unsigned request, and does registration answer something other than 501?"}
  LIVE -->|"no"| RED
  LIVE -->|"yes"| DONE["The deploy is done"]
```

**The upload prints the version and nothing else.** An upload answers with the whole configuration of the function. That answer carries the environment variables of the function. A log of this repository is readable by anybody, so the call names `Version` and prints no other field. One case reads every run script of this workflow. It refuses an upload whose answer is left open.

**Three routes carry no authorizer, and the design named two.** The sign in with Telegram landed with its handler after that section was written. The reader in `tools/deploy/routes.ts` names all three, with the reason for each. A fourth route with `authorization_type = "NONE"` now fails the infrastructure test. The design document says three.

**What the mutations showed.** Each mutation was watched going red. Then the file was put back and the case was watched going green.

1. Remove `ignore_changes` from the vault function. The case `leaves the code of emi-vault out of the comparison` failed. The two other functions stayed green.
2. Remove `--query Version --output text` from the upload. The case `leaves the answer of no upload open, in any job of this workflow` failed. It printed the whole command.
3. Change `pull_records` to `authorization_type = "NONE"`. The case `puts the authorizer in front of every route but the ones named here` failed. It named that route.
4. Remove the guard from the upload step. The case `skips every step of the functions job that reaches the account` failed. It named that step.

**What is proved, and what is not.** The live read ran against a stub server on this machine. It refused on the three authorized routes, read 400 from the registration, and exited 1 when a route answered 200 and when it was given no address. So the command, the route reader and the path parameter filling are measured. `npm run check:bundles` needs Docker, and this machine has none, so the pipeline proves it rather than a local run. The first real upload needs a merge. Nothing here says what the account answers after that.

author: hdkshingala
body:
A local unary call has opened its own socket since the first commit of this repository (`6afe6b01b`). The socket closed with the response, so a cross-request leak was impossible by construction. This change trades that for isolation by contract.

## Contract

The host advertises `unary.persistentSession` on `openAck`. The client lists the same name on `open`. The session is used only when both sides name it. Otherwise, and against an older peer, each call still gets its own socket and the same result.

- One session per host, signed-in identity, and websocket URL. The key is the host id, the account's user id, and the URL. It is not the token string, the abort signal, or host status. A rotated token on the same identity reuses the session. A different identity opens a new session.
- The caller binds synchronously. Until the first `openAck`, a second call does not dial. When the ack advertises the session, that discovering socket is kept. Later calls do not open another. A host whose ack omits the capability is remembered as legacy for this process. `openAck` carries no host version and no instance identity, so the latch is not keyed on one, and an upgrade under the same URL is not re-probed. That host stays one socket per call until the client process restarts. The results stay the same.
- Each request carries its own bearer and cloud verdict, read when it is sent. Aborting one call cancels only that call. A call still in the queue sends nothing. A call already sent writes one `cancel` for its request id and leaves the others on the socket.
- A request that was sent is never written again, even when it carries an idempotency key. A close after send settles that call as uncertain (`HostTransportFailureError`, and it may have reached the host). A call still queued when the socket dies was never written, so it fails before send as `RetryableTransportError` with `replaySafetyFromKey` false, whether or not it carried a key. The session retires. The next public call discovers a new session. Nothing is written on another socket of the same session. That replacement dial is gone: nothing in ordinary production reached it, and the queue was not extended to make it reachable.
- `replayMustBeKeyed` refused before any frame of the attempt was written is a non-retryable `HostTransportFailureError` with `fatalDetails` set, so `mayHaveReachedHost` is false. The one-shot path and the remote session use the same shape. An earlier attempt of the episode stays the retry messenger's concern.
- A host `RPC_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` after send stays retryable and is not treated as having reached the host. Any other host fatal after send is uncertain, is not resent, and does not redial.
- There is no count cap and no byte admission cap. The remote unary session's `pendingUnary` is unbounded, and the interactive scheduler queue that carries unary is not credit-gated. This session follows that. The owner's ruling is that a local session does not invent a bound the remote session does not have. The real limit is the one trusted local client: each request runs in its own context, and nothing of it is retained after the response. A call is sent once the socket is up. The relay's 1 MiB mux frame is that relay's ciphertext cap, not a budget for this socket.
- A malformed frame closes the session. A per-call authorization failure does not.
- The host does not restart its post-open timer after the first session request. That timer is the handshake deadline from `openAck` to the first request, the same deadline a one-shot socket uses (`Timed out waiting for 'request' frame after openAck`). Clearing it on the first request leaves an idle session open until the client closes the socket or the connection fails. Restarting it would drop a quiet desktop and force a new handshake. The client closes its side when the queue and the in-flight calls are empty. A response timeout sends one `cancel` for that request id and still settles the call as uncertain.

This is stricter than the remote unary session. A sent local request is never retried automatically.

## Measurement

Eight unary calls, one identity, real client against the real host handler:

| path | socket opens | open frames |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before, the client does not name the session | 8 | 8 |
| after, both sides name the session | 1 | 1 |

The live before is 150 opens/min for 150 requests/min, 99.7% desktop, measured 2026-11-09. The live after is taken by the coordinator once a client carrying the session reaches staging.

## Tests that hold the contract

`clients/shared/host-transport/__tests__/local-unary-session.test.ts`

- two calls share the discovering socket, and nothing but the negotiated manifest and the identity
- a rotated token reuses the session; a different user id opens another
- a change in the reported host status does not rotate the session
- an ack that omits the capability is one socket per call, including a call that waited on the first handshake
- the bearer and cloud verdict are the values at send time; a one-shot request omits the token
- a close after send is uncertain and is not written again
- `replayMustBeKeyed` fails before send when the ack has no idempotency capability, and `mayHaveReachedHost` is false
- `RPC_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` after send stays retryable and does not open another socket; any other post-send fatal is uncertain and is not resent
- aborting a call before send sends no cancel; cancelling a sent call leaves the other call and the session going
- a per-call response timeout sends one `cancel` for that request id and leaves the session open
- forty calls are all written after one ack, none is refused, and they complete on the one socket
- a one-shot open omits `unary.persistentSession`; the discovering open names it
- a caller waiting on discovery can abort without aborting the shared dial
- a preflight failure, and an incompatible discovery, let the next call dial
- a throw from socket construction releases the unpublished dial, and the next call dials
- releasing an idle session closes it, and the next call dials again
- a socket that closes after `openAck` and before adoption is not published, and the next call dials
- a host fatal buffered behind `openAck` fails that call with the host's error, and the session is not published
- a malformed frame, a schema-invalid frame, a transport error, and an authority abort in that same gap each fail the discovering call with that outcome, write no request, publish nothing, and the next call dials
- a session released during an in-flight call closes once that call settles
- a release before the socket opens, and a release while `openAck` is still outstanding, each close the adopted socket once the discovering call settles
- a call that starts after a release and before the previous call settles keeps the socket
- a call that claims the session after publish of a released dial keeps the socket. Publish is that boundary
- two calls admitted before `openAck`, with a release during the dial, close the socket once both settle
- a caller already waiting when publish records that release still closes the socket after its call settles
- the owner's open-frame credential being refused does not reject a waiter that holds a valid bearer; that waiter dials its own handshake and is not a second credential recovery
- an incompatible discovery fails every waiter with its own error object, carrying that caller's request id and method
- a retryable `UNAUTHORIZED` on one session request does not refresh the bearer; a permanent one does

`clients/gui-app/src/lib/host/__tests__/host-messenger-release-during-dial.test.ts` drives `dispose` and `reset` through `buildRuntimeHostMessenger` while the socket is still dialing. The test awaits promises the fake socket settles from `send` and from `close`. The discovering call finishes, the socket then closes with `session-closed`, a later request after `dispose` is rejected, and a later request after `reset` dials a new socket

author: nishantsny
body:
Fixes #182.

## The problem

The **first navigation after every Chrome launch** stalled ~25 s. `dbus-monitor`
named the call: Chrome asks D-Bus to activate the freedesktop secret portal and
never gets a reply.

```
mc ...864357  22  chrome -> org.freedesktop.DBus  StartServiceByName  string "org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop"
sig ...864353     org.freedesktop.DBus -> systemd  Activator.ActivationRequest
   ... 25.023s with no bus traffic at all ...
mc ...889700  23  chrome -> RemoveMatch       <- gives up, tears down its match rules
```

Measured with plain Chrome over CDP using browden's own argv — no selenium, no
chromedriver, no browden in the path — against a page on **127.0.0.1**, fresh
profile per row, headless:

```
config                  launch    load#1    load#2
baseline (detect)       0.263s   25.091s    0.033s
gnome-libsecret         0.241s   25.075s    0.024s     <- naming libsecret does NOT help
basic                   0.273s    0.077s    0.036s
baseline again          0.264s   25.065s    0.028s     <- stable, not a warm-up artifact
```

`load#1` TTFB was 4 ms and `domInteractive` 25054 ms: the renderer was holding a
document it already had. Ruled out first, each with its own run: browden /
selenium / chromedriver, cold profile or HTTP cache, graphics init, the site and
page weight, any render-blocking resource, the sandbox, and
`--use-mock-keychain`. (My first diagnosis in the issue — "no secret-service
provider" — was wrong and is corrected there; this host's keyring is healthy.)

## Why the obvious fix is not the fix

`--password-store=basic` cures the stall, but the store holds the key that
encrypts the profile's **cookies**. One throwaway profile, three launches:

```
1. detect, set a cookie        load 25.040s   cookie PRESENT
2. --password-store=basic      load  0.138s   cookie GONE
3. detect again                load 25.101s   cookie GONE   <- does not come back
```

Permanent. On a logged-in profile that is a one-way logout from every site.

## What this PR does

Chrome's 25 s is not ours to shorten, so browden asks the same question first,
with a bound, and only acts where nothing is at risk:

| host | decision |
|---|---|
| `BROWDEN_PASSWORD_STORE` set | honour it (`detect` = Chrome's default) |
| no session bus (container, CI) | `--password-store=basic` — Chrome lands there anyway |
| portal owned, or activates within 1 s | change nothing |
| portal dead **but** a secret service works | change nothing, **warn** with the remedy |
| portal dead and no secret service | `--password-store=basic` — nothing to lose |

`NameHasOwner` is answered by the bus daemon itself and never triggers an
activation, so the healthy path costs one ~5 ms round trip; only an unowned name
pays the bounded probe (1.0 s — a healthy portal is a small service-activated
binary answering in tens to a few hundred ms, so this sits above that and 25×
below the stall). The result is host state, so it is cached per process rather
than paid per launch.

The probe is in `browden/common/secret_portal.py`, free of third-party imports so
`setup/onetime_setup.py` can run it before any dependency is installed:

```
[ok]   D-Bus secret portal reachable (no first-navigation stall)
```

so a new deployment hears about this on the machine being installed instead of
rediscovering it later as "browden is slow".

## Tests

- **Unit** (`test_password_store.py`, 26 cases): the decision table against an
  explicitly faked bus, the `dbus-send` argv — including that the probe never
  calls `StartServiceByName` where the cheap `NameHasOwner` will do, or it would
  hang exactly where it is meant to detect a hang — the 1 s bound, the env
  override, the per-process cache, and the install-time diagnosis. Deterministic:
  argv is the only thing assertable everywhere, since the stall is host state.
  Unit suite: 763 passed.
- **E2e** (`test_navigate_latency_budget.py`): times `new_blank_tab`, cold and
  warm `navigate`, and cached/uncached `query_selector_all` over the real SSE
  transport against a page on 127.0.0.1. Budgets sit ~5× above the observed
  median — a tripwire for order-of-magnitude regressions, not a benchmark, since
  a shared runner is far too noisy for tighter assertions.

On the affected host it caught this bug, with the diagnosis in the failure:

```
AssertionError: a fresh session's first navigation took 27.137s, budget 8.0s
  (new_blank_tab=2.643s  navigate_cold=24.494s  navigate_warm=0.109s
   read_uncached=0.032s  read_cached=0.032s)
```

and after repairing the host's portal config:

```
latency: new_blank_tab=1.152s  navigate_cold=0.061s  navigate_warm=0.054s
         read_uncached=0.044s  read_cached=0.019s
```

**Worth knowing for review:** CI cannot catch this class of fault. A GitHub
runner has no D-Bus session bus, so the policy names `basic`, the first navigate
is fast, and the test is green whether or not the bug exists. That is why the
deploy script now runs it as its own post-deploy stage (5b) on the target
machine, with the timings printed into the deploy log on every deploy, green or
not. `BROWDEN_SKIP_LATENCY=1` skips the gate so a known host problem can never
make a deploy unblockable.

body:
The last PR for the cold-start work, after #1230 and #1232. Stacked on #1232: until that merges, this diff includes its commit. The new commit is ec4519a.

In the e2e fake stack the sandbox came up instantly, so no test would notice if a conversation started waiting on pod startup again.

**What changes**
- **A cold fake pod, for one spec only.** With `FAKE_SANDBOX_COLD_MS` set, the noop provisioner holds `create()`/`resume()` that long, but only for conversations whose owner starts with `cold-pod-`. `fakeBackend.mjs` sets the hold to 8s. Every other spec on the shared server keeps an instant sandbox.
- **The noop provisioner reports `refFor`**, so the fake stack takes the same early-return path as the k8s provisioner.
- **`test/e2e/cold-sandbox.spec.ts`** (fast tier). As a `cold-pod-*` user:
  - creating a conversation returns in under 3s;
  - the first message shows in the transcript in under 3s, and the reply only arrives once the pod is up, which shows the hold really applied;
  - a message with a file attached also shows in under 3s, and the reply names `/workspace/uploads/notes.txt`.

**Testing**
- `just e2e test/e2e/cold-sandbox.spec.ts`: both tests pass, in about 32s including stack startup.
- With `refFor` removed, so that agent-host waits for `create()` again, both tests fail at the "message shows in under 3s" check.
- agent-host type-check and build pass.

In this stack the conversation-router writes the conversation row itself, and agent-host provisions the sandbox on the first prompt. So the create-time check is a guard, and the message checks are what catch a regression. The hold is a fake-sandbox setting, so the spec is `fastOnly` and does not cover the full (k3d) tier. I've added `full-ci` because the fast e2e suite only runs on the full tier.

e2e-target: before its pod is Ready|before its pod is back|is in the pod once it is up
