author: culfin
body:
Closes #121. The owner's request, past the freeze: `owner_channel` keeps working when the owner's coordinator session restarts with a new name.

## What the owner sees differently

- **`owner_channel` takes a prefix.** `owner_channel: shop-coord-*` matches the coordinator session whatever suffix it gets on restart. An exact name works as before.
- **The lead resolves it before each round.** It uses its session list (ListAgents) and needs exactly one live session.
  - With none or several, it sends nothing and writes one line in its own session, naming the setting and the sessions it found, for example "owner_channel shop-coord-* matches two live sessions (…); SHOP-30 waits". The item waits.
  - An answer counts as the owner's only when it comes from the session resolved for that round.
  - Crew text still never names the channel.
- **`studio doctor`** shows what the setting names: an exact session, or "exactly one live session starting with …". The lead does the resolving, because Studio itself cannot list sessions.

## Review fixes

1. **A session that takes the channel's name.** `studio channel seen <session>` records each resolution. When the resolved session changes, the next tick raises one needsLead line, `owner channel changed: X → Y`, which reaches the owner like any other. Until then the lead counts answers from the new session only for questions without irreversible effect. SECURITY.md names the known limit: a session that matches the prefix while the coordinator is gone. There is no confirmation round-trip with the session itself.
2. **A stricter prefix.** At least 3 characters, starting with a letter or digit, and no space or dot right before the `*` (`-` and `_` are allowed there, as in `shop-coord-*`).

Tests:
- `channel seen` records the session, raises a change once, and refuses a session that does not match and a crew;
- the tick's needsLead line appears once;
- the pattern cases.

The RED/GREEN baseline gains a channel-changed scenario. RED: both agents counted an irreversible answer from the new session. GREEN: both held it until the change was raised.

## How

- `src/config.ts`:
  - the `owner_channel` pattern now allows one trailing `*`;
  - `ownerChannelOf` returns exact or prefix;
  - `resolveOwnerChannel(value, liveNames)` returns `{session}`, `{none}` or `{several}`. It is the rule the skill follows, held by tests.
- `src/secret-command.ts`: the doctor line `owner channel: …`.
- `skills/studio-lead/SKILL.md`: interview step 2 gets the resolution rule. The fix-limit question already points to the same `owner_channel`.
- Reference doc, schema.

## Skill baseline (RED/GREEN)

`test/skills/baseline-lead.md`, last section; scenario `lead-owner-channel-prefix-scenario.md`.

- **RED:** both agents found the one match, but with two matches or none, opus waited silently, and sonnet gave a status line without the setting or what it found. Neither resolved again for the confirmation round.
- **GREEN:** both resolved to the single match, wrote the one-line warning with the setting and the sessions found for none or several, and counted only the resolved session. Opus also resolved again for the last round.

## Tests

`test/owner-channel.test.ts`:
- a name or a prefix with one trailing `*` is accepted; `co*rd` and `coord-**` are refused;
- one match, the exact name, the old name after a restart (none), two matches (several), and no match.

## CHANGELOG entry

```
### Was ist neu für dich
owner_channel darf jetzt mit * enden (z. B. shop-coord-*): Die Leitstelle findet die Koordinationssitzung auch nach einem Neustart mit neuem Namen.
Findet sie keine oder mehrere passende Sitzungen, schickt sie nichts und sagt es dir in einer Zeile.

### Changed
- `owner_channel` takes an exact session name or a prefix ending in `*`; the lead resolves it to exactly one live session before each round, warns in one line when it finds none or several, and counts an answer only from the session it resolved; `studio doctor` shows what the setting names.
```

## Not verified / limits

- A real restart of a coordinator session: the resolution is a skill rule, and Studio cannot list sessions itself.
- The local suite shows only the known environment failures; worker-flow timed out once under load and passes when rerun.

One written attempt records a false exploratory congruence that omitted the two block intercepts. author: turlamai
body:
Closes #40. Test-only change (backend/llm-test.rkt +125); no product code, no pin change.

## Investigation result: mock artifact, not a product bug

#40 (split from #26 part 3) reported repeated `/api/translate/titles` batches misframing a *persistent HTTP connection* against a keep-alive local mock. The mechanism cannot exist in the current client:

1. `chat-once` opens a **fresh** `http-conn` per request and closes it in `dynamic-wind` — there is no connection reuse, and no auto-reconnect loop exists anywhere in `llm.rkt`/`translate.rkt` (the retry layers re-invoke `chat`, which re-opens).
2. Racket's `http-conn-send!` sends **`Connection: close`** unless the caller passes its own Connection header (collects/net/http-client.rkt:195) — so even a keep-alive server sees one request per connection, and unread request-body bytes can never misframe a successor.
3. Experiments (2026-11-08): **200/200** clean batches against a strict HTTP/1.1 keep-alive server; paths stayed intact even against a deliberately body-ignoring server. The real provider presets always passing is consistent with this.

The original observation was an artifact of the ad-hoc mock used that day (its own keep-alive framing, most plausibly a Content-Length mismatch producing the garbled request lines server-side and the contract violation client-side). The mock-artifact interpretation also explains why the app printed a `net/http-conn` contract violation only against that endpoint.

## The regression

30 sequential titles batches against a **real keep-alive mock** (strict Content-Length framing, connections held open until EOF, never proactively closed):

- server-side output assertions: `seen == 30`, parse failures == 0 — every request line parses, every body matches its Content-Length, every body parses as JSON;
- client-side: every `chat` call returns the expected payload.

Also fixed locally to the new mock: worker-thread errors now surface through an async channel — `sync/timeout` on a bare thread object returns identically on exceptional death, which silently swallowed errors (the same latent flaw still exists in the pre-existing `with-mock-llm!`; left untouched this pass, noted for follow-up).

## Authorization decision record

`2026-10-auth-1` unchanged; no pricing/gate/entitlement behavior touched. Read: `PRICING.md#authorization-decision-for-implementation` @ `3a1dc2d` (base).

## Validation

`raco test backend/` = 54 passed locally (13 in llm-test.rkt including the new keep-alive case); `raco glaze schema check --json` ok:true. CI on this PR is the gate.

body:
The first playable fight, and the compound simulator it's tested in.

**A camp that fights back** (`camp.fights`; `off=fight` for the old one): a whistle heard at 600 m, men who leave the line for ground no listed perch that way can see and come back after a stand-to, tower men who fire back, near misses that knock the rifle off its rest, and a muzzle flash anyone looking can see.

| 30 camps, a perfect shooter who stays | As lab E left it | Fights back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Guards down, of 9.6 | 8.7 | 7.0 |
| Share of guards in his line, 20 s after a shot | 61% | 41% |
| Rounds at him | 0 | 3.8 |

**The compound simulator** (`?scene=compound`): the camp with no player. Fly anywhere and drop a noise, a body or a shot from where you are, or run an attack script. `npm run flaws` and `npm run experiment -- flaws` flag what a defender plainly wouldn't do.

Also: the owner's three pillars (`docs/pillars.md`), new research notes, and a cap on route-finding by the work a tick has done.

**Goldens:** no pinned run's `behaviour` or `state` moved. The brain's bench moved on purpose (guards down from one perch, 22 to 12 of 27). The tuning grew, so the golden recording is rewritten. Live camp is scene version 3.

author: physics31415926
body:
Three changes with one motive: the panel should show current data, and stay
current, without being told to.

## Collection runs inside the plugin

Device and PR collection live in the dashboard process, so the panel was empty
until someone found and pressed Start. `autoStart` now defaults on. Only an
explicit `false` disables it — an absent field means a profile written before
this default existed, and those should gain the behaviour.

A live process is not the same as working collection: the server answers while
an SSH fan-out fails on every GPU host, or while an expired token makes every
PR read return an error body. A new collection badge sits beside the process
indicator and answers that second question.

| state | when |
| --- | --- |
| Collecting | every collector that has been read is delivering |
| Collection failing | **any** collector is failing — pessimistic on purpose |
| No data yet | nothing has completed a round |

A failure keeps the last success time, so the tooltip says "failing, last data
14:02" instead of pretending nothing ever worked. Half the data being stale
with nothing saying so is worse than being told it is broken.

## Views no longer flicker

Each view in the pane carries a React key so its slide-in replays on every
switch. That remount also discarded the component's state, so returning to a
view showed a skeleton and refetched while the previous data was still good.

Data now lives outside the component tree, keyed per view and per project, so a
view renders its previous content immediately and refreshes behind it. Reload
clears the cache first, because pressing it means "I do not trust what is on
screen".

The credential form is the one view that does not cache. Its draft holds a
plaintext token, and a module-level map would keep that string for the life of
the page, long after the form was abandoned. A test asserts the secret never
reaches the cache at runtime, not just that the source looks right.

## The plugin can update itself

The header shows an "update to x.y.z" button only when a newer release exists —
a permanently greyed-out control next to the process buttons reads as a bug.

The release source is **pinned in code**, not configured: this path decides
which code the Harness installs and runs, so a profile setting or request body
must not be able to repoint it. The install route accepts no parameters at all.
Drafts and prereleases are not offered, and a prerelease never sorts above its
own release, so an installed 0.2.0 is not offered an "update" back to
0.2.0-rc.1.

### A real bug the unit tests could not catch

Exercising the download against live GitHub showed release assets now land on
`release-assets.githubusercontent.com`. The first allowlist was
`github.com` + `objects.githubusercontent.com`, so **every real update would
have failed its own redirect check** — while the digest still matched, which is
what made it worth testing against the real asset rather than a fixture.

The advertised URL stays pinned to `github.com` exactly; the redirect target is
matched by `.githubusercontent.com` suffix so a CDN rename cannot break
updates. A suffix match still refuses `evil-githubusercontent.com` and
`githubusercontent.com.evil.test`. The published sha256 authenticates the bytes;
the host checks only decide who may serve them. Size is capped at 8 MB and the
temp file is written `0600` and removed after.

### A linked checkout is never overwritten

Installing a published tarball over a `link:` install would take that directory
out of the loader and orphan whatever someone was editing. The button refuses
and names the reason, showing the available version as plain text instead.

The decision resolves this module's real path — a linked dependency lands
outside the profile's `node_modules` — a local filesystem fact that needs no
network and cannot be misreported by a registry. **This development profile is
exactly that case**, so the button is correctly inert here; the feature is for
colleagues installing the published tarball.

## Version

0.2.0. The button compares versions, so a release that kept 0.1.0 would never
advertise itself as an update.

## Verification

489 JS tests pass across 9 suites: 16 new for version ordering, release
filtering, host-spoofing variants and the install guards; 27 new for autostart,
badge verdicts and the cache.

The Python suite has one **pre-existing** failure,
`test_branch_monitor.py::...sglang_collector_calls_original_offline_source...`.
It fails identically on clean HEAD with these changes stashed, and touches
nothing this change goes near.

Honest gap: `ChangeResult`'s field names come from the inspect contract's prose
rather than its type, which is not readable from this installation. So only an
explicit `applied === true` counts as success, rather than assuming a missing
field means it worked. That branch is untested against a real install, because
a linked profile cannot reach it.

author: mark1russell7
body:
## What

This is step 2 of A16. #129 gave the rule of `docs/LAYERS.md`: a runtime import goes to the same layer or a lower layer. This PR makes CI examine it.

- `scripts/layers.ts` holds the table of the 8 layers by npm name. The table also names `@mark1russell7/quantity`, `@mark1russell7/rigor-generators` and `@mark1russell7/rigor-statistics`, which come on 2026-11-21. Until then, their imports from npm obey the same rule.
- `.dependency-cruiser.ts` gets one `forbidden` rule for each layer from the table. The rule stops an import from the source of a package to a package of a higher layer, in the workspace or in `node_modules`. dependency-cruiser does not examine the tests, so a test import can go up.
- `scripts/layers.test.ts` (in `pnpm test:rules`) examines the `package.json` files:
  - the layer of each runtime dependency (`dependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`);
  - each workspace package is in one layer, so a new package fails until it gets a layer;
  - a published package has no private runtime dependency;
  - the graph of all the dependencies, the test dependencies too, has no cycle.

## Coverage (CA11)

Each of the 16 packages gets `@vitest/coverage-v8` `^5.0.5` as a dev dependency. The lock file has Vitest 5.0.5, and the coverage package wants the same version. No release comes from this. `vitest run --coverage` in `packages/rational` gives 100% of the lines.

## Checks

- On main: `pnpm check:boundaries` finds no violation (163 modules), and the 8 layer tests pass.
- A planted import from rational to expression, with its dependency in `package.json`:
  - `pnpm check:boundaries` fails with `layer-1-imports-up`;
  - the layer check gives 3 findings: the layer, the private package and a cycle.
- Locally: `pnpm test:rules` (15 pass), `pnpm typecheck:scripts`, the site tests (70 pass), STE (0 errors) and the conventions check.

`docs/ROADMAP.md` sets A16 to done.

body:
## Summary

- Append `sticky_piston` as block ID 126 with `extended` and `facing` states. Its placeable item is appended as item ID 309 and drops itself.
- Append `redstone_wall_torch` as block ID 127 with `facing` and `lit` states. It drops the existing `redstone_torch` item and has no separate item form.
- Add English and Japanese display names and a minor changeset. Existing block and item IDs remain unchanged.

## Redstone state audit

This audit covers Java Edition block-state properties for redstone-related block types registered in mc-kernel. The table lists the properties represented in the codec.

| Registered block types | Java Edition Wiki properties |
| --- | --- |
| [Piston](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Piston#Block_states), [sticky piston](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sticky_Piston#Block_states), [piston head](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Piston_head#Block_states) | Piston variants: `extended`, `facing`; piston head: `facing`, `short`, `type` |
| [Redstone torch](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Torch#Block_states), [redstone wall torch](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Wall_Torch#Block_states) | Floor torch: `lit`; wall torch: `facing`, `lit` |
| [Redstone dust](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Dust#Block_states) | `north`, `east`, `south`, `west` (`none`, `side`, `up`); `power` (0–15) |
| [Lever](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Lever#Block_states), [stone button](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Button#Block_states) | `face`, `facing`, `powered` |
| [Repeater](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Repeater#Block_states), [comparator](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Comparator#Block_states), [observer](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Observer#Block_states) | Repeater: `delay`, `facing`, `locked`, `powered`; comparator: `facing`, `mode`, `powered`; observer: `facing`, `powered` |
| [Dispenser](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Dispenser#Block_states), [dropper](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Dropper#Block_states), [hopper](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Hopper#Block_states) | Dispenser and dropper: `facing`, `triggered`; hopper: `enabled`, `facing` |
| [Stone pressure plate](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Pressure_Plate#Block_states) | `powered` |
| [Redstone lamp](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_lamp#Block_states) | `lit`, represented by the existing `redstone_lamp` and `redstone_lamp_lit` IDs (`false` and `true`) |
| [Redstone ore](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Ore#Block_states), [deepslate redstone ore](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Redstone_Ore#Block_states) | `lit` |
| [Block of Redstone](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Block_of_Redstone#Block_states) | No block-state properties |
| [Rail](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Rail#Block_states), [powered rail](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Powered_Rail#Block_states) | Rail: `shape`, `waterlogged`; powered rail: `powered`, `shape`, `waterlogged` |

The `redstone_lamp.lit` property remains ID-fixed because the two IDs already represent its off and lit states.

The following Wiki properties are outside the current kernel registry:

- Weighted pressure plates have `power` (0–15), but the kernel registers only the generic `pressure_plate` type, represented by the stone pressure plate.
- Button variants other than stone have no corresponding kernel block type; `stone_button` is the registered representative.
- [Target](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Target#Block_states) has `power` (0–15), but no target block type is registered.

The tests compare the new definitions with literal Wiki values and defaults, then property-test codec round trips for Wiki-allowed states.

author: jameswlane
body:
Fixes #142

## What does this PR do?

Configuration import previously ignored merge and force and overwrote supplied
configuration files. Imports now preserve unrelated fields and list entries,
report conflicts, and require `--force` to accept conflicting imported values.

- Recursively merge maps and named list entries, retain existing list order,
  and append distinct unnamed entries deterministically.
- Preview complete before/after values and conflict paths; make replacement
  explicit with `--merge=false`, scoped to supplied files.
- Normalize legacy sections before merging, then validate the final effective
  configuration through the existing shared semantic validator.
- Always back up changed existing files with their original bytes and stage
  all writes before atomically replacing individual files.
- Add JSON reports, keep bundle diagnostics on stderr, and resolve import
  options through flags, environment, configuration, and defaults.
- Document precedence, conflict handling, backup behavior, and write guarantees.

Testing:
- `go test ./internal/commands`: passed.
- `PATH="/tmp/devex-142-tools:$PATH" MISE_TASK_VERSION=3.54.0 task --force lint test build`
  in `apps/cli`: passed; lint reported 0 issues, all 43 suites passed, and
  the production build succeeded.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Twelve new Ginkgo specs cover YAML/JSON/bundle overlapping and disjoint
  imports, recursive named-list merging, conflict reporting, null and empty
  lists, explicit replacement, dry runs, exact-byte backups, no-op imports,
  merged dependency-cycle rejection, option precedence, concurrent edits,
  and output preparation failure without partial destination writes.

Deferred/follow-ups: none required by #142. Atomic renames are per file;
filesystem failure during the rename phase is not a cross-file transaction.
The required validation-failure guarantee is covered by regression tests.

author: fz1101hub
body:
Le run della raccolta dell'8 e 9 novembre mostrano due perdite di dati, entrambe nel programma che raccoglie i dati e non nell'app. In più, ViaggiaTreno conosce anche i treni Trenord.

## Problema
1. **ViaggiaTreno dimentica i treni del giorno prima a mezzanotte.** La run delle 00:58 del 9 novembre ha chiesto 602 treni arrivati in serata e 585 sono risultati «sconosciuti». Di giorno invece arrivano 650 treni su 672.
2. **GitHub salta molte run programmate.** Con `41 */2 * * *`, l'8 novembre ne sono partite 4 su 12 (06:40, 13:51, 19:05 e 23:58 UTC). Con la finestra di 4 ore restavano fasce intere mai chieste, compresa l'ora di punta del mattino.

## Correzioni
- **Finestra della raccolta**
  - Una run chiede ogni treno partito oggi, arrivato da almeno 20 minuti e non ancora noto. Chiede anche un treno partito ieri, ma solo entro 3 ore dal suo arrivo (i treni notte); la regola è `answerable`.
  - Un treno rimasto fuori per i limiti di una run resta in sospeso finché ViaggiaTreno ne risponde, poi viene contato a parte. Per i treni chiesti e non ancora arrivati resta il limite di 8 ore.
- **Orari delle run**
  - `punctuality.yml` prova ogni ora (cron `41 */2` e `11 1-23/2`) e una volta poco prima di mezzanotte (`47 22`, le 23:47 d'inverno).
  - Ogni run ha fino a 45 minuti e 5.400 richieste, sempre a 2 al secondo; `timeout-minutes` passa a 60.
  - `verify_ci_pinning.py` ammette da una a tre cron con minuto fisso, al massimo 25 run al giorno.
- **Treni Trenord**
  - ViaggiaTreno pubblica anche i treni Trenord, compresi quelli della rete Ferrovienord: il controllo dal vivo trova il 651 Milano Cadorna → Asso, origine `S01066`.
  - Il pack Trenord usa già i codici ViaggiaTreno come `stop_id`, quindi l'origine è quella. Il numero è quello dopo la linea (`RE_11 - 2153` diventa 2153). La categoria sono le lettere della linea: RE, R e S, oppure REG per una corsa senza linea.
  - I calendari dei due pack restano separati.
  - Sono circa 2.480 treni al giorno in più, 8.840 in tutto, ciascuno chiesto una volta. Nessun treno compare in entrambi i pack con la stessa origine.
- **App Android**: `NetworkReliability.numberKey` legge il numero dopo « - ». Prima, per «RE_11 - 2153», cercava le statistiche del treno 112153.

Il carico su ViaggiaTreno resta di una richiesta per treno, a 2 al secondo. Documentazione aggiornata in `docs/data-sources/PUNCTUALITY_STATS.md` e nel CHANGELOG.

## Verifiche
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passa. I nuovi casi coprono: la finestra della giornata, i treni notte di ieri, la chiusura del giorno dopo mezzanotte, i treni rimasti fuori per i limiti e il pack Trenord (numeri, categorie, origini, calendari separati).
- `android-check.sh app`: 1338 test, 0 errori, compreso il nuovo caso di `numberKey`.
- `verify_ci_pinning.py` e `verify_privacy_policy.py` passano.

author: tarotene
body:
No-Issue: 段16(#1449)の第 1 部。#1449 は最後の部で閉じる(参照: #1449)
Stack: base #1489

## 課題

ADR-0024 は、`--selftest` の cases を `cargo test` の `#[test]` へ 1:1 で移すと決めた。移行が終わったあとも、実行時の `--selftest` が **11 の crate・14 のファイル・27 行**に残っていた。

| 種類 | crate | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| 「`cargo test` に移った」と表示して終わる腕 | `apply-rulesets`(2 つの bin)、`copilot-plan-review`、`dotfiles-doctor`、`github-audit`、`issue-inbox`、`tailscale-prefs`、`pr-contract-check`(3 つの bin)、`session-wrapup`(転送だけ) | 動かす論理が無い |
| 使法に載るだけで実装が無い | `github-app-registry-check`、`github-app-snapshot` | `--selftest` を渡すと未知のフラグ |
| 実ロジック | `obsidian-backup`(`src/selftest.rs` 108 行) | `tests/cli.rs` と重複 |

さらに `docs/worktree-lifecycle.md` は、`--selftest` を持たない 3 つの crate(`git-audit-worktrees`・`git-prune`・`git-worktree-create-guard`)に、`--selftest` を回せと書いていた。

## 解決策

- 腕と使法の行を除いた(10 crate)。`--selftest` を渡すと、crate ごとに、未知の引数の扱いになる: `github-audit` と `copilot-plan-review` は元から終了コード 2、`pr-contract-check` の 3 つの bin は 0 から 2、`issue-inbox` は 0 から 1、`session-wrapup` は転送から外れて既定の経路(Stop の hook として標準入力を読む)に落ちる。
- `obsidian-backup` の `src/selftest.rs` を消した。**断言を `tests/cli.rs` と突き合わせて、カバレッジの低下が無いことを確かめた**: 成功する 5 つの呼び出しと restic の log の verb 5 つ(`init`・`backup --host`・`forget --host`・`check`・`restore latest:`)は `operations_and_restore`(オプションつきで、より厳密)、`../outside` の拒否は `refuses_failed_restore_even_if_files_exist_and_unsafe_paths`、token 無しの通知の失敗報告は `missing_secret_and_disabled_notification_fail`。`tempfile` は実行時にも使うので `Cargo.toml` は変えない。
- 文書を直した: `worktree-lifecycle.md` の誤った `--selftest` の手順を `cargo test -p …` の 1 行に置き換えてテストの置き場を実在のファイルで示し、`claude-usage.md` の 2 か所、`rust-migration.md` と `AGENTS.md` の CI 節に「Rust の bin は `--selftest` を持たない」を足した。

計画との差分の申告:
- 計画の「9 つの crate」は、**11 の crate**だった(`issue-index` は `issue-inbox` の誤り。`--selftest` を使法に載せるだけで実装の無い `github-app-registry-check`・`github-app-snapshot` が、さらに 2 つあった)。
- 計画は `pr-contract-check` の `--selftest` を他リポジトリが呼んでいないかを、除く前に検索で確かめるとした。手元の全 checkout と、所有者・所属 organization 3 つの `gh search code` で探し、**呼び出しは 0 件**だった(1 つの organization に 2 件の hit があるが、どちらもコメントの文言)。所属 organization のうち 2 つは検索していない。`gh search code` は既定ブランチの索引だけで、非公開・archived の網羅は保証されない。
- 新しい検査は置かない(ADR-0024 Amendment 5: 検出を 1 つ手放すと決めた。ADR-543 D2 の昇格型)。

既存手段: なし — 除くだけで、新しい機構は作らない

## Before / After

```diff
 // crates/dotfiles-doctor/src/main.rs
 fn main() {
-    if std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() == Some("--selftest") {
-        eprintln!("dotfiles-doctor: --selftest は `cargo test -p dotfiles-doctor` に移った(#414)");
-        return;
-    }
```

```diff
 # docs/worktree-lifecycle.md
-crates/git-audit-worktrees --selftest
-crates/git-prune --selftest
-crates/git-worktree-create-guard --selftest
+cargo test -p git-audit-worktrees -p git-prune -p git-worktree-create-guard
```

## 検証

- [x] 11 crate(`apply-rulesets`・`copilot-plan-review`・`dotfiles-doctor`・`github-app-registry-check`・`github-app-snapshot`・`github-audit`・`issue-inbox`・`obsidian-backup`・`pr-contract-check`・`session-wrapup`・`tailscale-prefs`)の `cargo test` が全て通る(52 の結果がすべて ok)。`nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.dotfiles-tools-clippy --no-link` が通る。
- [x] 実行時コードに `--selftest` が残っていないことを、機械的に確かめた(テスト以外・コメント以外・`#[cfg(test)]` より前の行で 0 件)。
- [x] `obsidian-backup` の断言の対応は、`selftest.rs` を読み、`tests/cli.rs` の同じ文字列(`forget --host`・`restore latest`・`check\n`・`../outside`・`reason=disabled`)が存在することを `grep` で確かめた。変異テストは未実施。
- [x] `docs/worktree-lifecycle.md` が示すテストファイル(`evidence.rs`・`modes.rs`・`selftest.rs`・`prune_worktrees.rs`・`prune_branches.rs`)の実在と、対話確認・dry-run・TOCTOU・`--auto` の各テスト関数の実在を確かめた。

body:
## What and why

Part of #26. The TV request page's season and download cards, and the issue thread's cards, drop their large corners for the 8dp list shape that rows use, so they read like the rest of the compact TV style.

- `TvSeasonCard` and `TvDownloadCard` use `BingeShapes.TvListItem` (was `AccountCard`, 26dp). The focus ring takes the same shape. The gap between lines is 4dp (was 2dp) and the secondary lines are `bodyMedium` (was `bodySmall`). Padding stays 16dp and the card height stays 112dp.
- `TvIssueCard` is one 8dp shape for every card. It no longer squares one corner by author, which was the phone's bubble. The user's own cards keep their tint. The phone keeps its bubble and its dimens.
- `aSeasonWithEveryLineFitsItsCard` in `TvDetailCardsTest` holds a season card with all three lines inside its fixed height, since no frame shows a card in full.

Posters, focus behaviour, the backdrop, the pill chips and the download progress bar are unchanged. No public signature changes in this app.

**Frames that moved (12):** `TvIssueSheetScreenshotTest` (6: `ActionFailed`, `Cards`, `OwnCommentPage`, `ReportPage`, `ResolvedThread`, `Thread`), 0.02% to 0.12%, at the corners of the cards. `TvRequestDetailScreenshotTest` (6: `ActionFailed`, `ActionSaved`, `ActionSaving`, `ApprovedNotDownloading`, `ApprovedUntracked`, `Series`), 0.3% each, in one strip at the foot of the frame where the season cards start. author: mrprofessor
body:
## What

The engine half of #7. A new engine-side crate, `resource-metrics`, polls `metrics.k8s.io` (metrics-server) for pod and node CPU and memory. It polls only while a view holds a subscription, keeps an hour of history per pod and node for small charts, and sends one batched `model::UsageSnapshot` per poll round. No GPUI in its tree. No UI: columns and charts come after #21 lands.

## Why a sibling crate, not the prometheus crate

- **Different source.** `metrics.k8s.io` is a Kubernetes API group served by metrics-server, or by an adapter such as prometheus-adapter. The Prometheus crate speaks the Prometheus HTTP API. They share only model types.
- **Different lifecycle.** This is a background poller with counted subscriptions and session history. The Prometheus crate runs queries on demand.
- **The name says what it reads.** It is named after the Kubernetes Resource Metrics API, not after metrics-server or Prometheus.
- **No engine conflicts.** It touches nothing in `engine` while #21 rewrites `engine/lib.rs` and `model/event.rs`.

## Design

- `UsagePoller::start(client, context, config, send)` starts one task per context. `subscribe(UsageInterest)` returns a guard, and dropping the last guard stops polling. `send` returns false once nobody listens, and that stops the task.
- **One tick, one snapshot.** Every scope views need is polled on one shared 15 s tick, so a round ends in one snapshot. A scope a view starts needing is polled right away, unless it was polled within the interval. A burst of subscribe messages is drained before polling, so it shares one round. A snapshot equal to the last one is not sent.
- **Scopes.** `UsageScope::Nodes`, `Pods(Some(ns))` or `Pods(None)`. All-namespace polling covers namespaced scopes, so they are not listed twice. Status is still reported for every scope a view asked for.
- **Status per scope.** `Live`, `Unavailable` (404 or 503: metrics-server missing or down), `Forbidden`, or `Failed`. After a failed poll the last values stay, with the status saying so. Each request has a 10 s timeout, which also caps kube 5's built-in retry of 503s.
- **Model types reuse PR #22's.** `Usage { cpu: Sample, memory: Sample }` serves the columns. `UsageHistory { cpu: MetricSeries, memory: MetricSeries }` serves the charts, labelled like the Prometheus series for the same object (`node`, or `namespace` and `pod`), so a chart can take either source. New types: `UsageObject`, `UsageScope`, `UsageInterest`, `UsageStatus`, `UsageSnapshot`.
- **History.** One ring per pod and node, trimmed to the last hour by cluster time (from the samples, so local clock skew does not matter). A repeated metrics-server sample is skipped. Points are packed into 12 bytes instead of the 48 that two `Sample`s take. An hour for 5,000 pods is 14 MB instead of 58 MB. Hard cap of 720 points per ring.
- **What a snapshot carries.** Latest values for every polled object, for columns. History only for objects a view asked about with `UsageInterest::History`. On a 5,000-pod cluster that keeps a snapshot in the hundreds of KB, not tens of MB every 15 s.
- **Typed responses** come from small serde structs, not the `k8s-metrics` crate (it pins its own k8s-openapi) or `DynamicObject`. A pod's usage is the sum of its containers, as `kubectl top pod` shows it. The crate has its own Kubernetes quantity parser (`n`, `u`, `m`, `Ki`..`Ei`, `k`..`E`, exponents).

## Wiring after #21 (not in this PR)

The engine keeps one `UsagePoller` per connected context, next to the watch hub:

- a Pods or Nodes table subscription also holds `UsageInterest::Latest(scope)`
- the inspector holds `UsageInterest::History(object)`
- snapshots go out as a new `Event` variant

That is a few lines in `engine/lib.rs` and `model/event.rs`, both of which #21 rewrites, so they wait for it.

## Testing

- `tests/fake_cluster.rs`, 8 tests on the engine's fake API server, polling every 100 ms:
  - nothing is polled without subscribers
  - the first poll waits for no tick, then polls repeat on each tick
  - dropping the last subscription stops polling
  - all-namespace polling covers a namespace
  - history builds up across polls and skips repeated samples
  - a cluster without metrics-server is `Unavailable`
  - forbidden node metrics are reported
  - the poller stops when nobody listens
- I ran these eight times in a row with no flakes.
- 21 unit tests: quantities, response parsing (containers summed, `items` missing or `null`), ring order, dedup, trim, cap, scope folding, due scopes, status per scope, last values kept after a failure, and unchanged snapshots not resent.
- Manual on kind-platform, which has no metrics-server: `cargo run -p resource-metrics --example top -- --context kind-platform` reports `Unavailable("404 page not found")` for nodes and pods.
- I wanted to install a throwaway metrics-server to check real responses. It needs an APIService and cluster-wide RBAC, and my sandbox blocked that as a change to a shared cluster. So the response shapes are checked against fixtures modelled on metrics-server's output, not a live server. Nothing was created on the cluster.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo deny check` pass. `cargo tree -p resource-metrics | grep -i gpui` prints nothing.

Part of #7 (the columns and charts in the UI are still to come).

body:
Ideas taken from Notion's developer docs and changelog: fewer lines, release particulars as fields, more and smaller sections, and a white light mode. Also a pass on what the site prefetches.

## Changelog
- **Release fields.** Released, channel, runs on, build, built from, changes since, download and who it credits, in two columns under the title. "Download" is a plain GitHub link among them.
- **Table view for earlier releases.** List and Table, with the choice kept in the browser. The table sorts by version, date, new and fixed. The macOS and channel filters narrow both views.
- **Removed:** the activity calendar and its two extra shades.
- **List lines** show the channel in words ("Release candidate") instead of the macOS.
- **Version pages** say "Each runs on macOS 27." once.
- **Earlier/Later** stay within a major version.
- **No repeated product names:**
  - the label over a release title is "Changelog";
  - a tab reads "Thaw 2.2.0" instead of "Thaw 2.2.0 | Thaw";
  - "3.0.0-beta.6 · Beta" is no longer shown.

## Sync
Release notes drop GitHub's boilerplate:
- **"Full Changelog" line:** its link becomes the "Changes since" field.
- **"Please report issues at …"** is removed.
- **Donations/Support sections** that link a tip jar are removed.
- **Bare PR addresses** read as `#45`.

Two new tests; 51 pass.

## Docs
- **Sidebar.** Six short groups: Get started, Use Thaw, Troubleshoot, Privacy and security, Develop, Project. Floe's docs use the same names.
- **Docs home.** The Thaw home groups its cards under the same headings.
- **Next steps.** Cards on the four pages that ended without sending the reader on.

## Site
- **Light mode is white,** with faint borders. Grey text is 5.4:1.
- **Prefetching.** Long lists and the footer prefetch on hover, touch or focus instead of on scrolling into view. On a production build:

  | Page | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Changelog | 60 prefetches, 1.4 MB | 19, 435 KB |
  | Home | 38 | 25 |

- **Icon caching.** `/favicon.ico`, the apple-touch-icon addresses, `/icon.png` and `/apple-icon.png` are kept for a day instead of `max-age=0`.
- **Community numbers** read on 8 November.

## Checked
- [x] `tsc`, Biome, `bun test scripts lib` (51 pass)
- [x] `next build`, and checked its cache headers and prefetch counts
- [x] Clicked through every new control in dark and light: table switch, sorting, filters on the table, row notes, download and commit links, Earlier/Later, version page rows, sidebar groups, docs home cards, Next steps. No console errors.
- [x] 390px: no sideways scroll on the changelog (list and table), a release, a version page, the docs home or 1.1.0
- [x] Table headers sort with the keyboard and show a focus ring
- [ ] Look over the Vercel preview, light and dark

body:
Refs #243

## Summary

```diff
 validar_pedido (complemento/pedido_do_envio.py)
   400 invalid_job_id / invalid_lang / invalid_request / entries_required
+  if len(entries) > MAXIMO_DE_FRASES (500)
+    413 too_many_entries        # before the per-Frase loop and before anything is written
   dedupe by phraseId, validate tts.reserva
```

- **Ceiling: 500 Frases per Envio**, in `POST /jobs` (the create), as the issue asks ("cheap, in the create, `413`/`400` with its own code"). I chose `413` + `too_many_entries`. A refused create writes nothing in `fila/` and does not spend the key. The count is of the raw `entries`, before duplicates by `phraseId` are dropped, so the check costs nothing.
- Contract: new example `complemento/contrato/exemplos-do-teto-de-frases.json` (501 Frases → `413`), `LEIA-ME.md` table, `docs/design/envio-no-complemento.md` limit 5.a.
- Conexão 0.4.19 (`versoes.json`, rebuilt `conexao/perpetualminer.ankiaddon`, version in the examples).
- The 500 is my pick of "the smallest reasonable": the design says a session mines "hundreds of lines". It is one constant, `MAXIMO_DE_FRASES`. The body limit stays 4 MB.

**New text for the owner to read: none.** The panel already shows an Envio that did not start with ENV-03 and the code in Detalhes (`POST /jobs → HTTP 413 · too_many_entries`), like any new failure without its own copy (limit 5.i). No Voice catalog entry added.

## Not done (needs the owner)

- **Retention of finished Envios (#151 / limit 5.g) is not in this PR.** The issue's "O que fazer" asks only for the ceiling; retention is mentioned only as "decidido junto de", and the triage (§4) gives no recommended option for it. It also has no safe default: `custos/<jobId>/costs.jsonl` feeds the Custos tab, so deleting finished Envios' files after N days erases the person's spend history. The owner must pick the window and what is kept (costs vs. state). Limit 5.g is unchanged.
- **#192 (pairing credential)** not touched, as asked; 5.a still says the origin does not authenticate.
- Feature map unchanged (no popup/painel/manifest/servidor.py change).

## Evidence

- **Before:** `POST /jobs` with 501 Frases → `201`, the Envio is queued and gets paid.
  **After:** `test_envio_teto.TetoDeFrases.test_um_envio_com_frases_demais_e_recusado_e_nada_e_gravado`:
  ```text
  criar(501 Frases)  -> 413 {"error": "too_many_entries"}
  criar(500 Frases)  -> 201 queued
  /jobs/list         -> only the 500 one; fila/<id>.json of the 501 one does not exist
  ```
  plus the new contract example (501 Frases → `413`), which the real-server contract test runs.
- `PYTHON=python3 node scripts/testar.mjs complemento node regras ferramentas` → all ok (910 complement tests, 23 skipped as before). The Python 3.9/3.13 matrix and e2e were not run locally.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. One constant; revert or raise it.

**Blast Radius:** the extension's Envio create. Someone who sends more than 500 Frases in one Envio (one language, one go) now gets a failed Envio card with `413 · too_many_entries` in Detalhes instead of a send; the panel does not split Envios. Attention level: **MÉDIA**.

author: saberzero1
body:
changesets/action pushes the version PR with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which triggers no workflows, so version PRs show no checks and the lockfile `version-packages` rewrote is never tested before it's published.

This makes `ci.yml` callable (`workflow_call`, checking out a given commit) and adds to `release.yml`:
- a pending `CI / version PR` commit status on the version PR's head,
- a job running `ci.yml` on that commit,
- a job reporting its result as that status.

Publishing is unchanged. Once this has run on a version PR, `CI / version PR` can be made a required check.

Four bounded development stages, independently committed on `perf/runtime-lifecycle-20261108`:

- **A** (`f5d8bed`): fix confirmed per-RAF action-ring DOM leak. One owned, reusable node per active actor, lazy creation and cleanup. 10,000-tick DOM lifecycle regression.
- **B1** (`6ce80ef`): dispose site-scoped curb and door-glass materials when replacing architecture; leave cached/shared palettes alive.

- **Release gate** (`e4228e7`): focused action-ring, material, geometry, door traversal, and replay tests + mandatory previous-Pages preflight. Build/typecheck already runs in CI.

**Out of scope:** rewriting simulation order, replay semantics, fog disclosure, AI decisions, and on-device FPS claims. No unrelated PRs or deployment triggers should be touched.

## Release conditions
1. Focused CI and production build pass.
2. GitHub Pages preflight confirms the previous deployed `main` matches the live build, with no queued/failed deployment.
3. Confirm PR head is current and no other production release is pending immediately before merge.
4. Merge one batch only, then verify the new Pages workflow and its served build before another production release.

With the same site and conditions compare `?perf=1` DOM count, rings, JS/RAF P95 before and after several minutes. Do not treat host benchmarks as device measurements.

author: spikediegel-prog
body:
## Port: upstream #267 GPU slice only

Upstream: Ironnember/Pulpo1.0 PR #267 "feat: add portable GPU audit integrity acceleration", head ebc72e0 (open, all checks pass). Branch: port/upstream-267-gpu-slice, off Preview main 9c388e6.

## What was ported (verbatim from the upstream head, 8 new files, +1404 lines)

- pulpo/gpu_acceleration.py (+306)
- pulpo/gpu_triton.py (+270)
- tests/test_gpu_acceleration.py (+182, pytest-style)
- tests/test_gpu_benchmark_tools.py (+71)
- scripts/benchmark_gpu.py (+325)
- scripts/aggregate_gpu_benchmarks.py (+101)
- docs/GPU_ACCELERATION.md (+124)
- docs/TESTING.md (+25)

No conflicts: all 8 files were wholly absent from Preview (no "gpu" string anywhere in pulpo/*.py or pyproject.toml), and the new modules import only stdlib plus each other. No existing file was touched.

## What was NOT ported

The rest of #267 (the base remainder: kernel/state/TTL/delta work, commerce/namecom/test changes) is covered by the separate #250-remainder and #258-leftover ports. Do not port the base from this PR.

## Validation caveat: correctness-checked GPU path, NOT a speedup

The upstream PR's own validation shows near-parity, not speedup, on RX 7900 XT / ROCm (0.67x-0.99x). This port buys a correctness-checked GPU path, not performance.

## Tests (VM, this branch)

- Full suite: python3 -W error -m unittest discover -s tests -> 1089 tests, OK, 66 skipped (was 1086 on main; +3 from tests/test_gpu_benchmark_tools.py).
- tests/test_gpu_acceleration.py is pytest-style module-level functions and is NOT collected by unittest (0 tests under unittest, same as upstream under unittest). The 2 CPU-only functions were run directly and pass (test_cpu_hash_reference_matches_stored_hashes, test_serialized_messages_are_reusable_by_cpu_reference). The other 7 require torch + a GPU and pytest.importorskip("torch"); neither pytest nor torch is installed on the VM, so they skip upstream-style on this machine.
- tests/test_gpu_benchmark_tools.py under unittest: 3 tests, OK.

author: satoaki-ooto
body: ## 背景 `mise up` で github: バックエンドのツール（octet / oh-my-pi など）をインストールすると、GitHub API の匿名レート制限（IP 単位 60 req/h）に当たり 403 で失敗する。 ``` ✗ github:skaft-software/octet@0.10.3 failed: GitHub artifact attestations verification error ... API rate limit exceeded for 144.125.89.210 ... ``` ghtkn トークンを `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN` で渡すラッパー（`zsh/lib/functions/mise.zsh`）は存在するが、効いていないように見えた。 ## 原因 zshrc のローダは `**/*.zsh` → `**/*.sh` の順で読むため、ラッパーは `00.eval.sh` の `mise activate` より先に定義される。一方 `mise activate zsh` の出力は冒頭で既存の `mise()` を `unset -f` して自前の関数を再定義するため、**ラッパーは対話シェルで一度も実行されていなかった**。結果、mise は常にトークンなし（匿名）で GitHub API を呼んでいた。 なお `GH_COMPANY=1` / `GHTKN_APP` は `~/.config/mise/config.local.toml` の `[env]` が export しており、mise.zsh の ghtkn 経路が本来の正規経路。`GH_COMPANY=0` の bypass は今回の原因ではない。 ## 修正 - `zsh/lib/functions/mise.zsh` - activate 後に再読み込みされた際、activate の関数を `__mise_activate_original` に退避して委譲する。`sh` / `shell` / `deactivate` は activate の関数が eval する特別扱いを持つため、素のバイナリ直接呼び出しではなく委譲で挙動を保持 - トークンは `local -x` で付与し、関数スコープを抜ければ環境に残らない（従来のコマンド前置 `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN=... mise` と同等のハイジーン） - `zsh/lib/00.eval.sh` - `mise activate` の後で `functions/mise.zsh` を読み直す ## 検証 - `zsh -n` で両ファイルの構文チェック - 新規 zsh で実際のローダ順序（*.zsh → activate → 再読み込み）を再現し、ラッパーが生存すること・activate の関数が退避されることを確認 - bypass 経路（`MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN` あり / `GH_COMPANY=0`）で `mise --version` が委譲先経由で動作することを確認 - ghtkn 経路はエージェントに触れないようスタブで代替し、`local -x` で付与したトークンが委譲先の関数内および子プロセスの環境から参照できることを確認 ## 補足（スコープ外） - `GH_COMPANY=0` かつ `GITHUB_TOKEN` 未設定の環境ではトークンなしで動く別の穴が残る（職場の共有出口 IP では同様の 403 になり得る） - mise は公式に ghtkn をサポートしており、`[settings.github] credential_command = "ghtkn get ..."` に移行すればシム経由・非対話実行でもトークンが効く。ラッパー方式からの移行は別途検討 Co-authored-by: CommandCodeBot ---

author: skavrx
body:
## Why

On 2026-11-08 the operator could not record without first pressing **Set up task**. When they did record, the left wrist camera dropped off USB 6 s into the episode, and the capture failed with only "camera publisher timestamp skew exceeds the capture profile". That latched RECORDING FAILED for the whole session: following, Engage and recording stayed locked until the session was stopped.

## What changes

- **No setup step on the robot.** Every session on Live and Both prepares its capture from Helm's `--capture-profile`. **Set up task** remains only for the simulator's task scene. Before and during a session the Task card (`helm/static/task_view.js`) says why Record cannot act: which camera it is waiting for, the head pose, or the arms neither holding nor following.
- **A failed episode ends only itself.** This covers a camera stalling or dropping off USB, stale data, the writer failing, and the receiver losing authority. The episode's partial file keeps its reason, and `episode_failed` is written to the session's events. The arms hold once, as they already do for a camera drop, and Engage follows again. Record then starts the next episode in the same session.
- **If the capture process stops,** recording ends for the session but the session goes on. The arms hold once if an episode was recording, `capture_failed` is logged, and Record is refused with the reason.
- **RECORDING FAILED is unchanged** for the session's own evidence log (samples, events) failing.
- **A skew failure names the camera** whose newest frame fell behind, for example `left_wrist's newest frame is 41 ms older than the others' (stalling, or off USB?)`.
- **Camera rates and the age and skew bounds are unchanged** (the user's decision). The wrist cameras deliver about 50 fps whatever their configuration asks (measured 2026-11-08). The capture profile's note and the task workflow guide now say so.
- **Docs:** the task workflow, the manual, troubleshooting and safety guides are updated. STATUS lists the wrist cameras' USB drops as open: four on 2026-11-08, cause not found.

## Contract change

`tests/contract/test_task_receiver_capture.py` and `tests/contract/test_helm_capture_failure.py` change what a capture failure does. It used to latch RECORDING FAILED. Now the arms hold once, at the same guarded HOLD with torque on, and recording is refused (capture stopped) or the next episode allowed (episode failed). H and X still act at once, and an Enable or Engage pressed in the same instant as the failure is dropped. No freshness, age, skew or stopping bound was relaxed: a stale or incoherent frame is still never recorded.

## Verification

- `python scripts/dev.py check` (ROBOT_GATE_WORKERS=4) passed on this commit's tree: 2587 tests, no skips.
- The same changes on top of #9 (head branch `e004933`) passed the full gate: 2598 tests, no skips. The first run there failed two timing tests that don't touch recording (`test_teleop_head` head fault, `test_live_replay` harness timeout). Both passed 3 out of 3 alone, and the rerun passed.
- ltr-code: `doctor` (only rustfmt missing; no Rust in this branch), `scan`, `scan --all`, `scan --since origin/main`, `check` and `format` were all clean. The pre-commit and pre-push hooks ran.
- **Robot:** the combined build (#9 plus this branch, uncommitted) is deployed on Minerva as `20261109T021921Z-e004933-dirty475b02`. The release smoke test passed and Helm restarted on it. **No session has run on it yet**, so nothing here is proven on the robot.

## Merging

This conflicts with #9 only in `docs/STATUS.md`, where both add a line under "Merged, not on the robot". Keep both lines.

author: dyotson
body:
0460-0462 for FH1 ReImagined #640 (low and mid-range PCs: the GPU frame on a GTX 1650 Ti).

- **0460 `fh1_gpu_profile`** (off by default). A testing tool that logs the GPU time of the command processor's submissions by kind and render pass. It uses bottom-of-pipe timestamps written where the kind of work changes: guest draws per render pass, render target transfers by destination and source, resolves, texture loads by format, uploads and the swap. When it is off, the cost is one branch per recorded command.
- **0461 Stencil bit masks for transfers without `VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export`.** NVIDIA's driver lacks that extension, so a transfer to depth used to copy the stencil in 8 full-size draws, one per bit. Now a compute pass first ORs each depth source's stencil into 8 words, and each bit's draws are conditional on its word (`VK_EXT_conditional_rendering`). The result is identical, since the stencil is still cleared to 0 first. `vulkan_transfer_stencil_bit_mask=false` turns it off.
- **0462 NVIDIA's direct texture upload (0071/0406) at render scale 1.** It now also covers unscaled single-mip tiled textures, which it reads from the shared memory. `vulkan_direct_unscaled_texture_upload=false` turns it off.

Measured on a GTX 1650 Ti (driver 555.97) with FH1's benchmark, 3 runs each way, alternating:
- **Transfers on the 540p scene:** 5.3 -> 3.5 ms of GPU time a frame.
- **540p scene:** 55.5 -> 58.1 fps at the 60 fps cap (GPU busy 97% -> 94%), and 55.8 -> 59.7 fps uncapped. These two rows are 0461 alone.
- **1440p scene (render scale 2):** transfers 19.4 -> 9.6 ms, the GPU frame 52.1 -> 41.8 ms, 18.9 -> 23.4 fps.

Details are in FH1's docs/perf.md.

The VK_EXT_conditional_rendering flag is the last member of `VulkanDevice`, so the offsets of the members before it don't change. Devices with stencil export (AMD, Intel) and transfers from color are unchanged. Built and run on Windows (clang-cl, xwin) on the laptop; Linux is covered by the FH1 PR's CI.

- Runtime-only sequential queue timer: complete or skip a running current item, then start the next valid queued item after persistence; standby-item actions leave the current session untouched.
- Paused sessions do not auto-advance, manual timer end and external timer starts release sequential intent. A page reload never auto-starts another item.
- A failed next-session save freezes the unconfirmed chunk and reports a retry requirement; retries never duplicate completion/points.
- Extend the existing interaction browser regression for cancellation, confirmation, skip and search grouping.
- Bump app version to 175.9.0.

Validation required before merge: exact PR checks, main checks, then source-identical release deployment.

author: msjs2333
body:
## Scope

Implement the owner primitives defined in #87: protected per-user domain registration using the DSH `ivoraige_host` domain, durable initialization intents and replay, canonical file identity checks, bounded registry locking, and explicit copy/recovery preconditions. Add protected Unix socket / Windows named-pipe transport and generation-bound one-time browser credentials with session/CSRF checks. Windows uses a current-SID-only native DACL, handle-bound server descriptor/token checks, actual client TokenUser verification, local-only connections and first-instance ownership; the private capability remains a second generation-bound check.

Windows filesystem checks use one bounded fixed-command helper per Node process for ACL validation, atomic private creation and write-through replacement, rather than spawning PowerShell for every check. Ancestor directories are checked for foreign replacement/control rights. Helpers use the absolute system executable; pipe startup supports stock Restricted execution policy without changing it. Missing listen/close acknowledgments fail closed and retain cleanup uncertainty until native acknowledgment or actual helper exit.

This layer adds tested primitives; the following stack layers activate them in application bootstrap and entries. It preserves the pinned runtime and existing record/task/snapshot identities.

## Evidence and limits

- Domain suite: 10/10 passed on Linux, Node 24.22.1, including six-process registry contention and interrupted-intent fixtures.
- Session and transport framing/private-file tests passed. The sandbox rejects Unix socket bind with OS EPERM, so the actual handshake test is explicitly skipped locally and needs native CI.
- Native Windows / Node 26.13.0 at 702cedb: 593 tests, 590 passed, 3 platform skips, 0 failed; the 91-file foundation package smoke also passed. [Evidence](https://github.com/KongouAirlines/ivoraige/actions/runs/42558967671/job/128970927080). This includes seven native pipe security/lifecycle probes, not a separate ordinary-user login or fully unelevated account.
- Native Windows / Node 26.13.0 at c1b86730 passed 603 tests: 600 passed, 3 platform skips, 0 failures; the 91-file foundation package smoke passed. [Verified job](https://github.com/KongouAirlines/ivoraige/actions/runs/42563331451/job/128984338865). This verifies the TrustedInstaller compatibility, actual Restricted policy/literal path and helper-retirement changes. A retiring helper stays referenced and its registry lock remains held until observed exit. Current head c1de393f adds evidence documentation; all six push/PR checks passed on Linux, macOS and Windows / Node 26.13.0.
- Separate ordinary-account/unelevated acceptance remains open. The [scoped account run](https://github.com/KongouAirlines/ivoraige/actions/runs/42568044404/job/128998805631) failed at credentialed process launch (Win32 error 5), before establishing the cross-user boundary. It reported both accounts removed and owned processes exited, but profile cleanup failed (32) and Secondary Logon restoration failed (1052); the final observed service state was still running, with startup configuration unchanged. [Detailed evidence](https://github.com/KongouAirlines/ivoraige/blob/97ac5841888a583c414722249f51772f231831f1/docs/plan/0.1.x/evidence/host-windows-pipe.md#separate-account-acceptance-attempt). Native CI success does not close this acceptance gate.
- Windows discovery verifies DSH registration metadata because NTFS creation-time tunneling can defeat file-identity-only checks; the safe snapshot read has a large-store cost.
- Migration needs trusted source-process retirement evidence. Registry repair remains unavailable without a trustworthy complete backup; neither is inferred from `--confirm` or a free lock.

Details: `docs/plan/0.1.x/evidence/host-owner-foundation.md`.

### 1. What and why?

A product document belongs to one product. Moving it to another product isn't a use case.

### 2. How?

- **Definition:** `productId` of `product_document` gets the `Immutable` flag.

#### Impact

- **Changed behaviour:** a write that changes the `productId` of an existing document fails with `FRAMEWORK__WRITE_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` (400).
  - Sending the same `productId` again still works, so full upserts keep working.
- **Entity schema:** `productId` is marked `immutable`.

### 3. Testing

1. Create a product document through `POST /api/product-document`.
2. Send `PATCH /api/product-document/{id}` with the same `productId`.
   - **Expected:** 204.
3. Send it with the id of another product.
   - **Expected:** 400, `The field "product_id" of "product_document" is immutable and cannot be updated.`

### 4. Additional notes

- **Release notes:** come with the last PR into `feature/product-documents`.

### 5. Checklist

<!-- Details for each item: CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-checklist -->
- [x] I have read and followed the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/trunk/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-checklist)
- [x] **Only** non-obvious code is commented
- [x] Tests added, and they fail without this change
- [ ] Release notes updated, if relevant for external developers ([how to document a release](https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/trunk/delivery-process/documenting-a-release.md))
- [ ] Documentation and agent skills updated

<!-- Instructions for Agents

Also follow the shopware-pr-hygiene skill (.agents/skills/shopware-pr-hygiene/SKILL.md) for the title, commits, and review follow-ups.

Write for a reviewer who reads the diff anyway.
Give them what the diff cannot show.

Check your draft on three levels, in this order:

1. Altitude: how deep into the implementation a sentence goes.
   A sentence at the wrong altitude stays hard to read at any length.
2. Detail: how much of the change section 2 covers.
   The reviewer opens the diff themselves.
   If section 2 feels complete because it accounts for everything, cut it to about a third.
3. Length: how much you write overall.
   Too long is hard to read at any altitude.

Cutting length does not fix altitude or detail.
A short draft can still be opaque, or still do the reviewer's reading for them.

Content:

- Say what the change does and leave out why each choice is right.
  Judging that is the review, and the reviewer does it against the diff.
  Drop "because" clauses that argue for a choice.
  They look like substance and survive every length cut.
- Name the thing, not how it is wired.
  Selectors, CSS properties, exact default values, call order, type names and the chain of effects between them are all in the diff, stated more precisely.
- Add the "Impact" sub-section only when one of its listed changes applies.
  Say what exactly changes, for example which method, field, or table.
  Never write that something did not change, such as "no public API changed".
- Before writing, check the diff for public API changes.
  List each changed or added public symbol in the Impact sub-section.
- For performance, state the cost per request or per item, for example "one extra query per line item".
  Add numbers only if you measured them.
  Do not speculate about possible slowdowns.
- Mention a rejected alternative only when a reviewer would otherwise ask "why not X?".
  One line, no argument.
- Describe the change, never the work session.
  Drafts and fixes made before the commit are not part of it.
- Leave out:
  - reassurance, such as "no behaviour change", "no bookkeeping", "purely additive"
  - a prose retelling of the new tests; the reviewer reads the spec
  - the code path that already worked
  - "as discussed" and how the bug was found
  - a review path or reading order; the author adds one if needed

Style:

- Prefer short and readable over grammatical.
  Fragments are fine.
- State facts as short bullets and sub-bullets.
- Separate blocks of information with blank lines.
- State what is, not what isn't.
  No double negatives.
- No "..., so ..." tails.
  If something needs explaining, give it its own sentence or bullet, and do that rarely.
- No em dashes.
- Use inline code at most once or twice per paragraph.
  Name a code element in bold or italics instead.
  To show code, use a fenced code block with an example.
- Tick only the checklist items that are true for this PR.
-->

author: ale-sanchez-g
body:
Upgrades the project to Next.js 16 and adds comprehensive guards to prevent silent breakage during future framework upgrades.

## Summary

This PR upgrades Next.js from 15.5.28 to 16.4.5 and introduces two new test suites to protect the static export build:
1. **Framework upgrade guards** (`src/__tests__/next-framework.test.ts`) — pins critical Next.js configuration, tooling, and metadata that must remain stable across major versions
2. **Route smoke tests** (`e2e/routes-smoke.mjs`) — validates every route loads cleanly at three screen sizes, with no console errors, missing assets, or horizontal scroll

## Key Changes

- **Next.js 16 upgrade**: Updated `package.json` and `tsconfig.json` to Next.js 16.4.5
- **ESLint CLI migration**: Replaced `next lint` (removed in Next 16) with direct `eslint` CLI in `package.json` and `eslint.config.mjs`
- **TypeScript config updates**: 
  - Changed `jsx` from `"preserve"` to `"react-jsx"` (Next 16 default)
  - Added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include` (Next 16 dev types)
  - Reformatted config for consistency
- **Framework guards** (`src/__tests__/next-framework.test.ts`):
  - Validates static export config (`output: 'export'`, `unoptimized: true`, `trailingSlash: true`)
  - Ensures `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` is correctly read and applied
  - Verifies ESLint tooling and `eslint-config-next` version matching
  - Checks web manifest generation and icon paths
  - Validates page metadata (titles) are set correctly
  - Enforces all `set-state-in-effect` ESLint disables have explanatory comments
- **Route smoke tests** (`e2e/routes-smoke.mjs`):
  - Spins up a local HTTP server serving the static `out/` directory
  - Tests all routes (home, coach, training, games, wellbeing, profile, 404) as both first-time and returning visitors
  - Tests three viewport sizes (320px, 375px, 1280px)
  - Validates no page errors, console errors, failed requests, or horizontal scroll
  - Verifies stylesheets are applied and pages are not blank
  - Tests client-side navigation (header links) without full page reloads
  - Generates screenshots for visual regression detection
  - Integrated into `npm run test:e2e` pipeline
- **ESLint disable comments**: Added explanatory comments to all `set-state-in-effect` disables in component files (coach, profile, training, DecisionGame, TrainingPlan, WeeklyGames, WellbeingCheckIn)
- **Documentation**: Updated `CLAUDE.md` to reflect Next.js 16, ESLint CLI change, and new test coverage

## Implementation Details

- The smoke test uses Playwright to automate browser testing and Chromium to render pages
- It blocks all external HTTPS requests (except localhost) to ensure pages never contact AI providers during testing
- The framework guards use Jest's module reloading to test config behavior with different `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` values
- All tests are designed to fail fast on framework changes that would silently break the static export or GitHub Pages deployment

author: basilechretien
body:
F01 of the Known-gaps triage (2026-11-09): the nine sub-points of KG481 (added by #565) about `sync-sources`' fetcher and its network guard. Each has a test that failed on `main` first (21 of the new tests failed there; the other 20 pin behaviour that had no test), then the fix. The nine move below DESIGN.md's "Closed since" line with why each mattered.

## What changes

**Network guard (`lookup/download.py`)**
- **DNS rebinding (KG481.8).** The name was resolved for the check and again by `urllib` when it connected. Where no proxy is used, the connection now goes to the addresses that were checked (`_Pinned`, through `http.client`'s `_create_connection` hook), and the certificate is still checked against the name. Through an https proxy, the proxy connects and resolves the name itself: that half stays open in Known gaps, pinned by a test.
- **`own_network` (KG481.10).** It now refuses any address Python does not count as global, which adds 100.64.0.0/10 (carrier-grade NAT, Tailscale). It also refuses IPv6 site-local fec0::/10 explicitly, because Python counts fec0:: as global on 3.10 to 3.14, so `not ip.is_global` alone misses it. A host written as a decimal, hex, octal or short IPv4 number (`2130706433`, `0x7f000001`, `127.1`) is now judged as the address it spells instead of being taken for a name. A fake-IP answer (198.18.0.0/15) is still refused, and the refusal now says why and what to change.
- **Tests (KG481.12)** for `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, numeric hosts, a name with one private address among public ones, the proxy branch, and a public address that passes the guard and is connected to.

**Fetcher (`literature/fetching.py`, `copies.py`, `cli.py`)**
- **KG481.1:** an `http://` open location (OpenAlex gives Europe PMC's that way) is asked as `https://`. Before, it was dropped, and the work was said to have no open copy.
- **KG481.4:** a full text the author saved, recorded and absent (a fresh clone), is no longer fetched from the web. An abstract of theirs alone still lets the web be asked for the full text.
- **KG481.11:** the broad `except ValueError` around the whole search is gone. Only reading a link and making its request are caught (`_get`, `_api`). A fault in staging or matching now raises, and a bad link no longer skips the work's other places.
- **KG481.7:** `--inbox <folder> --no-fetch` (the literature-verify skill's command) ends with each still-wanted work's DOI link, not Zotero's advice. A dry run is left as it was.
- **KG481.6:** tests for a second-version record, two differing inbox PDFs of one work, the inbox file left in place after filing, and a file over the size cap.

**Reading (`literature/matching.py`, KG481.13)**
- "SUPPLEMENT ARTICLE", the label Clin Infect Dis and J Infect Dis put over each article of a supplement issue, is no longer read as a supplement's head. The heads are now read with their words as far apart as `pdftotext -layout` sets them (`\s+`).
- Generated inputs, as CLAUDE.md asks: a generator `pdf_first_pages` (every journal label and every head, in a drawn case, spacing and layout), a reading `pdf shown`, and a property. It has two BROKEN twins (the old rule, and no head read at all); both fail the property under seeds 1 to 12, and the property holds under the same twelve. This is not KG481.5, matching.py's general property, which stays with F05.

## Left open, written in Known gaps
- Through an https proxy, a name that resolves here is checked here, but the proxy resolves it again: pinned by `test_a_name_is_left_to_the_proxy_the_environment_names`.
- Fake-IP mode has every fetch refused (the refusal says why): pinned by `test_a_fake_ip_answer_is_refused_and_says_why`.
- **New:** on an IPv6-only network with DNS64, every 64:ff9b::/96 address is refused, public ones included, because Python counts the block as reserved. Pinned by `test_an_address_of_nat64_is_refused_whatever_it_holds`. Judging the IPv4 address inside the block would fix it, but that relaxes the guard, so it is left for a decision.

The four version lines are as `main` has them.

## Reviews
- **`security-reviewer`** found nothing in the no-proxy path, plus one MEDIUM: `urllib` percent-decodes the host where `urlsplit` does not. So `https://%31%32%37.0.0.1:23119/` passed the check as a name, and through a proxy that `no_proxy` left out it reached 127.0.0.1. Fixed in 2e8438b9: a link whose authority holds `%`, `@` or a backslash is refused; `no_proxy` is asked with the port, as `urllib` asks it; and every connection made without a proxy is pinned, whatever `urllib` decides about the proxy. Its two LOWs are fixed too: 6to4 is refused whole, and a trailing dot on an address is read as the address.
- **Opus round 1:** one blocking finding, fixed: `differential_expected.yaml` had no entry for the new `pdf shown` reading, and `main`'s `judged` reads it differently. Two non-blocking ones, also fixed: "Author’s reply" with a typeset apostrophe, and the same `no_proxy` port mismatch.
- **Opus round 2** (fix commit only): nothing blocking. Two non-blocking findings, fixed in 5cd7eb7d: a link with a leading space skipped the raw-authority check, so a link holding a space or control character is now refused anywhere (`http.client` refuses those anyway); and a comment had landed on the wrong constant.

## Test plan

author: sdrahn
body:
Part of #155. The first step: no model up to 8B found a planted fault in #152's run, and part of the reason is not the model. The host showed it the wrong data.

## What was wrong

The host makes each playbook step's call itself, **without arguments**. The model therefore saw the tools' defaults (systemd-mcp 0.3.5, whose SDK applies its schema defaults):

- `systemd__list_loaded_units` lists only **active** units. `failed-units` never showed the failed unit, and qwen3:4b reported "The host is healthy…".
- `systemd__list_log` returns the last 100 lines of the whole journal, mostly Custos's and the gateway's own records. The failing service's error line could be pushed out of them.
- `systemd__check_restart_reload` (optional in `service-health`) only reports on a restart the server itself started; without arguments it says "Finished".
- `systemd__get_file` without a path fails.

## What changes

- **Playbook steps take `args`**, the call's arguments. A string in them may contain `{unit}`, the unit the activity is about:
  - the new `"unit"` of `POST /v1/activities`, which must be a unit name and comes only with a playbook (400 otherwise);
  - for an event that runs a playbook, the unit that failed.

  A step that needs a unit runs only with one. A playbook needs at least one step that does not. The model is told the steps' arguments and the unit, and may call a step's tool again with other arguments.
- **The shipped playbooks ask for what they look for:**
  - failed units with their properties;
  - the journal's lines about failures (a pattern);
  - the time services by name;
  - full-disk, OOM and SELinux denial messages.

  `service-health` reads the named unit's state, its own journal, and systemd's account of its restarts. A test checks every systemd step's arguments against what systemd-mcp 0.3.5 takes.
- **`model-eval.sh`**:
  - names the unit for `service-health`;
  - takes `--limit` (CI: 1200 s a run; an injection case gets half), so the `models` job ends within its time with any model;
  - records each run's model calls from the journal: count, largest prompt in tokens, tokens written, longest call;
  - keeps the model's prose answer when it files no report, and whether that answer names the fault.
- **Docs and contract:**
  - CONTRACT.md §5 (the `unit` field) and §14c (`args`, `{unit}`, events), plus a sentence in §15;
  - user guide chapter 9 (playbooks);
  - CHANGELOG.

Not in this PR: `update-status` still has `check_restart_reload` as its only required step. Replacing it needs a command that reports pending restarts, so that's a follow-up.

## How it was tested

- `make check`: new tests cover `args` and `{unit}` (parse, substitution, a step that needs a unit), the steps' arguments reaching the host's calls, the 400s, an event passing its unit, and the shipped playbooks' arguments against systemd-mcp's.
- `make cockpit-test`.
- Functional test (`run-tests.sh`, Diagnostic playbooks): a step with `{unit}` reaches the real gateway with the unit (checked by `AGENT_ARGS_SHA256`), and a unit that is not a unit name is refused.
- The `models` job, dispatched on this branch ([run 42552961850](https://github.com/sdrahn/custos/actions/runs/42552961850); Ollama 0.12.6, CPUs only, 20 minutes a run). The user guide's table is updated:

  | Model | Reports | Faults found | Unsafe plans | Median run | Injections followed |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1.7B | 0/4 | 0 | 0 | 951 s | 2/7 (was 3/7) |
  | 4B | 0/4 | 0 | 0 | 1200 s | 0/7 |
  | 8B | 0/4 | 0 | 0 | 1202 s | 1/7 |

  The prompts are small now (at most about 6,500 tokens). What blocks the small models is no longer the input:
  - 1.7B and 8B end runs with a prose answer instead of `report_diagnosis`;
  - 4B's first answer in each run ran the whole 20 minutes and returned nothing, so it was most likely writing without end. Custos sets no limit on output tokens.

  So #155's done criteria are not met by this PR. The next steps there: a limit on output tokens, and a report from a prose answer.

author: saberzero1
body:
changesets/action pushes the version PR with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which triggers no workflows, so version PRs show no checks and the lockfile `version-packages` rewrote is never tested before it's published.

This makes `ci.yml` callable (`workflow_call`, checking out a given commit) and adds to `release.yml`:
- a pending `CI / version PR` commit status on the version PR's head,
- a job running `ci.yml` on that commit,
- a job reporting its result as that status.

Publishing is unchanged. Once this has run on a version PR, `CI / version PR` can be made a required check.

body:
## CINE-006 · TMDB Server-Only Client and Credentials Hardening

Closes #8

### Executive Summary
PR for **CINE-006**, hardening upstream TMDB access across CineMatch with official Next.js `server-only` enforcement, request host allowlisting (`api.themoviedb.org` exclusively), dynamic credential resolution with fail-safe behavior on missing/empty tokens, stable structured error mapping (401, 404, 429, 5xx, 504 timeout), secret token redaction in serialized configs/logs, safe Next.js image remotePatterns (`https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/**`), and static bundle leak assertions.

Clean single-commit descendant of `main` (`30195a55e970416b416927170c1ade6782e13639`), strictly bounded to **7 scoped files** (+578 / -13 lines).

### Scoped Files Inventory
1. **`src/services/tmdbApi.ts` (modified):** Added `import "server-only"`, runtime server guard, host allowlist validation (`validateUpstreamUrl`), dynamic Authorization header resolution with getter on `defaults.headers`, `TmdbConfigurationError` when `TMDB_API_RAT` is unset, `TmdbHostValidationError` on SSRF/arbitrary hosts, `TmdbApiError` structured error mapper with token redaction (`Bearer [REDACTED]`), and 10s timeout.
2. **`next.config.ts` (modified):** Restricted TMDB image remote pattern with explicit `pathname: "/t/p/**"` and YouTube images with `pathname: "/**"`.
3. **`package.json` (modified):** Added official `server-only` dependency.
4. **`package-lock.json` (modified):** Deterministically pinned `server-only@^0.0.1`.

6. **`tests/unit/tmdb-server-client.test.ts` (new):** 12 unit tests verifying strict defaults, token injection, missing token errors, relative and absolute allowlist validation, SSRF arbitrary host rejection, upstream 401/429/5xx/timeout mappings, and credential redaction.
7. **`tests/integration/tmdb-hardening.test.ts` (new):** 5 integration tests verifying upstream 401 response handling without credentials in logs, safe failure on missing env, SSRF URL rejection, Next.js image config pathname restrictions, and static search across `.next/static` bundles confirming zero secret leakage.

author: klaasnicolaas
body:
Stacked on #1506.

## Why
Moderators working at the same time only saw each other's decisions and new items after a refresh, and the sidebar badge went stale. Switching between **Open** and **Afgehandeld** rebuilt the whole page, including the map.

## What changes
**Live queue (Reverb, already installed)**
- New `ModerationQueueChanged` event (`ShouldBroadcast`, after commit) on the private `moderation` channel, as `moderation.changed` with `change: added|decided`. It follows the existing `DatasetDataChanged` pattern.
- It is sent when a submission, report or improvement arrives, for every single decision (via `continueWith`), for a bulk rejection that rejected something, and for a location proposal decision.
- Channel access: anyone who may see part of the queue (`ModerationQueue::typesFor()` not empty).
- `useModerationChannel()` in the app layout keeps `counts` (the badge) live for moderators. The inbox reloads `items`, `decidedToday`, `locationProposals` and `options` (or `history` on the decided tab) through the existing `scheduleLiveReload`.
- An item under review is never reloaded underneath the moderator. The change is remembered, and going back to the queue reloads it as well.

**Tabs**
- Open and Afgehandeld links use `preserveState`/`preserveScroll`, so the same map instance stays and only its pins and the list change. An open decision closes when the tab changes.
- All three tabs, Voorstellen included, are prefetched on hover. Voorstellen is a separate page component, so it still mounts its own map; keeping one map across those pages would need a persistent layout. That is out of scope here.

## Not covered
Status changes outside moderation (for example editing or trashing a community space in the admin list) do not broadcast yet.

## Tests
- `ModerationInboxTest`: events for a new report and improvement, for a single and a bulk decision; channel authorization for moderators and regular users.
- `moderation-navigation.test.mjs`: the queue reloads live, never while an item is open, and catches up when going back.
- Related feature tests (133) and all frontend unit tests pass locally; `npm run types` passes.

三部分独立改动，各自一个提交，对应版本标签 `1.1.5`：

1. **组件总览页**（`b8ef27e8`）：视频背景、首屏飞入、按需渲染与跳转卡顿修复
2. **组件知识库**（`cc9d9d7b`）：AI 选型时把 Badge / Chip 误选成 Button 的根因修复

## 1. 组件总览页 `/components`

- 整页背景换成「自由落体」视频：854px 重编码约 3MB，静音循环自动播放，高斯模糊 6px，与滚动无关；删除旧的城市滚动视频与海报

three.js 程序化生成云海、低多边形大地、水面与海底（鱼群、海草、光柱），滚动驱动摄像机从云上降到海底；页面按进度飞入组件卡片。**草稿**：未接入首页，视觉与性能仍待调整，不影响现有页面。
