author: uzieltzab
body:
Avanza: prueba manual S3-4 (M11)

## Causa
Fechas de negocio sacadas de un instante UTC sin convertir. Desde las 18:00 en México dan el día siguiente; el último día del mes, el mes siguiente.
- `Application/Comprobantes/Pdf/CfdiPdfModelBuilder.cs`:
  - la fecha de emisión era `FechaTimbrado ?? CreatedAt` en UTC (una factura de las 23:12 del 8-nov salía con 09/11/2026);
  - también estaban en UTC la fecha de timbrado, la fecha de pago del REPP y la de la cadena del TFD de respaldo.
- Periodo en UTC en:
  - `AplicarAnticipoAFacturaCommand.cs:97`;
  - `EmitirNotaCreditoDevolucionAnticipoCommand.cs:78`;
  - `Comprobante.AprobarAutorizacion` (`Comprobante.cs:239`, autorización de una NC de A+W).
- `DateOnly.FromDateTime(ahora.UtcDateTime)` como fecha de referencia del folio (series que reinician por periodo) en todas las `ReservarFolioCommand` de Facturación.
- `ProductoTerminado/Domain/SalidaPt.cs:47`: folio `HS-{ahora:yyyyMMdd}` sobre `UtcNow` (HS-20261109 a las 23:34 del 8-nov).

El atributo `Fecha` del XML ya iba en hora de México (`CfdiEmisionBuilder.FechaFiscal` → `FiscalApiTimbradoAdapter.cs:278`). El periodo de la factura de venta, anticipo, NC por bonificación, REPP y carta porte también.

## Cambio
- `CfdiEmisionBuilder.DiaFiscal(instante)`: día en la zona fiscal. Se usa en todas las reservas de folio de Facturación.
- `CfdiPdfModelBuilder` convierte todas las fechas del PDF con `FechaFiscal`.
- **Periodo en hora de México:**
  - en la aplicación y la devolución de anticipo, con `FechaFiscal`;
  - en `AprobarAutorizacion`, con `ZonaMillet.ALocal`.
- `SalidaPt.Crear(..., DateOnly? diaLocal)`: el handler pasa `HoraAw.FechaLocal(ahora)`. `CreadaAt` sigue en UTC.
- Sin migraciones. Los datos guardados siguen en UTC; solo cambia cómo se derivan las fechas de negocio.

## Pruebas
| Criterio | Prueba | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| Factura timbrada el 8-nov a las 23:12 (México) imprime 08/11/2026 y timbrado 2026-11-08T23:12:33, no 09/11 | `DocumentosFiscalesImpresosTests.M11_factura_timbrada_a_las_23_horas_de_Mexico_…` (modelo + texto del PDF) | ✅ |
| NC de A+W autorizada el 30-nov a las 23:30 (México) queda en el periodo 2026-11 | `NotaCreditoAwTests.M11_autorizada_la_noche_del_ultimo_dia_…` | ✅ |
| Hoja de salida armada el 8-nov a las 23:34 lleva folio HS-20261108 | `FolioSalidaDiaLocalTests.M11_hoja_armada_a_las_23_34_…` | ✅ |
| Regresión | `Facturacion.UnitTests` **1101/1101**; `ProductoTerminado.UnitTests` **137/137** | ✅ |

Rama al día con `origin/develop` (`1c9f5b654`, sin commits nuevos); HEAD `8e5eab8fa`.

## Fuera de alcance: el uso de UTC es general
Un inventario encontró unos 50 puntos más que sacan una fecha de negocio de `UtcNow`, y unos 25 helpers o zonas distintos. Ejemplos:
- folios de RQ, OC y nota de cargo;
- validación de periodo cerrado en CxP y Tesorería;
- vencimientos y antigüedad en CxC y CxP;
- PDF del acta de conciliación.

`Sucursal.ZonaHoraria` (America/Cancun en Cancún, UTC-5) solo la leen hoy cajas y terminal. Se propone una pieza común en SharedKernel, `IFechaNegocio`, que lea la zona de la sucursal, para migrar módulo por módulo en PRs propios. Eso incluye el atributo `Fecha` del CFDI de una sucursal en Cancún, que hoy queda una hora atrás.

# Pull Request

## Describe your changes

Dependabot now checks NuGet, GitHub Actions and the Ubuntu base image of the toolchain image daily, which GitHub runs Monday to Friday, instead of once a week on Monday. The `day` keys are removed because they only apply to the weekly interval.

Each ecosystem also excludes all of its dependencies from the cooldown (`cooldown: exclude: ["*"]`). author: houman44
body:
## What changed

The published Action failed in any calling repository whose `package.json` pins a pnpm other than 9.0.0. The error was `Multiple versions of pnpm specified`.

**Cause.** Both manifests ran `pnpm/action-setup` with `version: 9.0.0`. At the pinned SHA (`0ebf4713`), `pnpm/action-setup` reads `packageManager` from `package_json_file`, which it resolves under `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. That's the caller's repository, not this action's checkout. When the caller pins a different pnpm, the step throws (`src/install-pnpm/run.ts`, `readTargetVersion`). Callers that pin `pnpm@9.0.0`, or have no root `package.json`, were unaffected, and so was this repository's own CI.

**Fix.**
- `action.yml` and `action/action.yml`: Node is set up first. A step then computes this action's own `package.json` as a workspace-relative path. `pnpm/action-setup` gets that path as `package_json_file`, with no `version`, so this repository's `packageManager` (`pnpm@9.0.0`) decides. The caller's `package.json` is never read.
- `scripts/validate-distribution-metadata.mjs`: `requirePnpmVersionDerived`, already applied to workflows, now also applies to both manifests. It also requires their `package_json_file` to be the computed path.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a new job, `action-from-another-caller`, checks this repository out into `cejel/`, writes a workspace `package.json` pinning `pnpm@10.0.0`, and runs both manifests against it. The existing smoke steps run in this repository, whose `packageManager` matches, so they could not see this failure.

## Validation

- **Validator:** `pnpm run validate:distribution` passes. Against `origin/main`'s manifests it now fails with `action.yml hardcodes pnpm/action-setup version 9.0.0; remove the workflow version so pnpm@9.0.0 is derived from package.json packageManager.`
- **Path resolution, simulated locally:** a caller workspace whose `package.json` pins `pnpm@11.5.3`, with the action under `../../_actions/<owner>/cejel/<sha>`. Both the root and nested forms resolve `package_json_file` to this action's `package.json` (`pnpm@9.0.0`).
- **Tests reading the manifests:** `action-manifest-outputs`, `action-runner` and `public-claim-boundary` 35/0.
- **Tests reading `ci.yml`:** 23 files, 1566 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `maeve-lesson-delivery` on an existing stale seed, `PENDING_cejel_admit-the-safe-shape-…`, which this PR does not touch.
- **Not yet run:** the new CI job itself runs on this PR.

## Dual review

- [x] Pass A recorded with stable reviewer identity and human/AI disclosure: [behavioural correctness](https://github.com/BargLabs/cejel/pull/685#issuecomment-6735040181). AI subagent, APPROVE at `f2fb9762d`.
- [x] Pass B recorded with stable reviewer identity and human/AI disclosure: [security, supply chain, reproducibility](https://github.com/BargLabs/cejel/pull/685#issuecomment-6735040479). AI subagent in a separate context, APPROVE at `f2fb9762d`.
- [x] Both passes reviewed the complete base-to-head diff in isolation (`e53c4ca2a..f2fb9762d`).
- [x] All requested changes are fixed and rerun, or explicitly adjudicated. Neither pass requested changes. Their minor findings and nits are deferred to #686; nothing was changed after review.
- [x] Final review records or PR comments are linked here.

Both passes are AI reviews spawned from the authoring session. They are not independent human review.

Authored by an AI agent (Claude Code); both review passes are still owed.

body:
## Summary
Part of #614. The PR review plugin now posts a comment on the PR when a review stops early, so a review is never left stuck on "🔍 PR Review in Progress".

A new script, `scripts/report-failure.sh`, does the work. It:
- logs `[pr-review] <stage>: <reason>`
- removes secrets from the reason (tokens, credential URLs)
- **edits** the "In Progress" comment into ❌ / ⏭️, or posts a new comment if there isn't one
- works on GitHub and Azure DevOps
- posts only once per run, and always exits 0 so it never hides the original error

## Cases covered so far
| Unit | Case | Stage | PR comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PR merged, closed or abandoned | `pr-not-open` | ⏭️ PR Review skipped |
| 2 | Checkout fails (missing ref or branch, or a new commit pushed mid-review) | `checkout` | ❌ PR Review failed |
| 3 | Base branch missing, unrelated history, or out of date | `base` | ❌ PR Review failed |

## Changes
- `scripts/report-failure.sh`: new
- `scripts/gh-start-comment.sh`, `scripts/ado-start-comment.sh`: save the "In Progress" comment ID
- `scripts/verify-pr.sh`: reports PRs that aren't open
- `scripts/pr-setup.sh`: reports checkout and base-branch failures
- `commands/pr-review.md`, `skills/review-pr/SKILL.md`: step 2 checks the PR is open first, and failure comments are documented
- `scripts/tests/run.sh`: 62 new tests

## Behaviour change
The review now stops right away on a merged or closed PR. Before, it carried on.

## Testing
- **Unit tests:** `bash plugins/pr-reviewer/scripts/tests/run.sh` gives 79 passed, 0 failed (uses fake `gh`/`curl`, no network)
- **End to end (GitHub):**
  - Merged PR: [agent-studio#99](https://github.com/XiansAiPlatform/agent-studio/pull/99) got ⏭️ skipped ✅
  - New commit pushed mid-review: [#68](https://github.com/xianix-team/plugins-official/pull/68) "In Progress" edited into ❌ checkout ✅
  - Missing base branch (simulated): [#68](https://github.com/xianix-team/plugins-official/pull/68) "In Progress" edited into ❌ base ✅
- **Not yet tested end to end:** Azure DevOps

## Not covered by the plugin (needs a hook or the executor)
Plugin scripts missing, bad or invalid platform token, Claude API errors (credits, key, rate limit), container timeout.

## Still to do (follow-up units)
Previous review unreadable, analysis didn't finish, findings processing fails, review post fails, partial or warning issues, fix-mode push fails.

body:
Phase-548 W9. RISC-V ThreadX images need rust-lld and llvm-ar, and CMake now finds them in the pinned Rust toolchain. Before this change it looked in rustup's default toolchain, which outside the checkout may be a bare `nightly` with no llvm-ar. `nros setup` now also installs a "rustup default" need on the pinned toolchain.

- `nros_host_rustlib_bin` (`packages/api/nros-c/cmake/nros-rtos-helpers.cmake`) calls `nros_pin_default_rust_toolchain()` first and passes an explicit `-DRust_TOOLCHAIN` on to the rustup proxy.
- The refusals in `cmake/toolchain/riscv64-threadx.cmake` name the toolchain they searched and give two remedies: `nros setup rv-virt-threadx`, or `rustup component add llvm-tools --toolchain <tc>`.
- `setup.rs`: `also_on_the_pinned_build_toolchain()`, with the unit test `a_default_toolchain_need_is_also_installed_on_the_pinned_build_toolchain`.
- The phase-548 doc gets a W9 section. Draft #3293 also carries W9 text; whichever lands second keeps main's wording.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p nros-cli-core --lib setup::`: 103/103 passed, including the new test.

author: rjy1537-eng
body:
## 요약

세션이 끝났을 때 화면마다 빈 목록 · 화면 안 문구 · 오류 화면 · 폼 실패 띠로 제각각 보이던 것을 두 가지로 맞춘다 (C6).

- **화면을 옮기는 중에 알게 되면** 로그인 화면 LOGIN 버튼 위에 「로그인이 만료되었습니다. 다시 로그인해 주세요.」
- **쓰던 화면에서 요청하다 알게 되면** 「로그인 만료」 팝업([확인] 하나, 닫을 수 없음) → 로그인 화면 같은 문구. 여러 요청이 동시에 실패해도 하나만 뜬다.
- 로그아웃 실패는 브라우저 경고창 대신 「로그아웃 실패」 팝업([새로고침] 하나).

설계: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-session-expiry-design.md` · 계획: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-05-session-expiry.md`

## 구조

| 알게 되는 곳 | 처리 |
|---|---|
| `proxy.ts` | 세션 없음 · 갱신 401 → `/login?reason=expired`. `/login?reason=expired` 에 쿠키를 들고 오면 갱신으로 확인(401 삭제 · 200 홈 · 그 밖 유지) |
| `request()` (서버 화면) | proxy 가 화면 GET 에 붙인 내부 헤더 `x-whale-render` 를 보고, 401 이면 만료 로그인으로 이동 |
| `request()` (서버 액션) + 감싼 `window.fetch` | 세션 쿠키 삭제 + 30초 표시 쿠키 → 브라우저가 팝업 신호, 응답은 화면에 넘기지 않음 |
| BFF · 엑셀 · 첨부 | 그 자리에서 `notifySessionExpired()` |

겹치던 서버 액션 · 화면의 401 분기 약 30곳을 지웠다.

## 앞으로 화면을 만들 때 (okf/whale-erp-front.md)

- 서버 화면 · 라우트 핸들러에서 오류를 통째로 받는 catch 는 첫 줄에 `rethrowExpired(error)`
- 브라우저에서 `bff()` · `fetch` 를 직접 부르면 401 에 `notifySessionExpired()`

## 확인

- `pnpm test` 1064 통과 · `tsc --noEmit` 오류 없음 · `eslint src` 오류 없음
- 브라우저(BP 마스터 · 플랫폼 계정): 설계 5장 11가지(토큰 만료 · 메일 링크 · 맞추기 · 저장 · 중복 확인 · 폐점 선택 · 탭 두 개 · 탈퇴 최종 제출 · 로그아웃 · 동시 401 · 서버 화면 · [뒤로])
- 중앙 처리 뒤: 세션을 끊은 직후 점포 · 급여명세서 · 근로계약 · 운영 알림 · BP 공통코드 · 플랫폼 메뉴 · 알림 템플릿 → 로그인 화면 문구. 세션이 살아 있을 때 정상, 저장 401 팝업 유지

## 확인하지 못한 것 · 남은 것

- `pnpm build` 는 중앙 처리 전 커밋에서만 돌렸다.
- 강제 비밀번호 변경 401 은 메일로 받는 임시 비밀번호가 필요해 브라우저로 보지 못했다.
- 목록은 성공하고 상세만 401 인 경우의 패널은 브라우저로 만들지 못했다(같은 함수를 목록 화면에서 확인).
- 공지 · 문의 저장 401(`post-form.tsx`, `inquiry-form.tsx`)은 담당자 확인 대기 — 폼 문구 그대로.
- 코드로만 찾은 빈틈: `inquiry-detail.tsx` · `bp-select-dialog.tsx` · `current-bp-status.tsx` 의 `bff()` 401 신호 없음, 쿠키가 이미 지워진 뒤의 목록 엑셀 받기는 팝업 대신 실패 띠.
- 서버 액션이 `window.fetch` 로 나가는 것은 Next 16.3.3 내부 동작이다 — 업그레이드 때 다시 확인.
- Manyfast 반영은 레드마인 일감으로 따로 요청한다.

**main 과 충돌 있음(커밋 223개 뒤처짐).** 충돌 109개 중 103개는 `docs/demo` 빌드 해시, 나머지는 `docs/mockup/auth/login.html` · `okf/auth.md` · `okf/log.md` · `okf/whale-erp-front.md` · `src/app/stores/actions.ts` · `src/app/work-schedules/page.tsx`. main 에 새로 들어온 서버 화면도 위 규칙을 지키는지 병합 때 봐야 한다.

author: sarah367
body: ## This PR accomplishes the following: Adds accounts (steps 1 and 2 of 4). Accounts are **required for creators** and **optional for fans**: anyone can browse and enter contests without one. **Step 1: signing up, logging in, and what people see** - **Sign up and log in** with Firebase Authentication (email and password). At sign-up, people choose **Run contests** (creator) or **Enter contests** (fan), saved in a `users` collection. Firebase remembers the sign-in, so refreshing doesn't sign you out. - **A header that adapts:** creators see Episodes, Contests, and Entries; everyone else sees Browse contests, plus Log in and Sign up, or their name and Log out. - **Creator pages are guarded:** signed out, you're sent to log in, then back to the page you wanted (`?next=`). Signed in as a fan, you see "This page is for creators." - **A public Browse page** listing open contests, from a new public route that only returns fan-safe fields. **Step 2: the server checks who's asking** - The app sends each signed-in person's **Firebase ID token** with creator requests (`authFetch`). The server verifies it: not signed in → 401, not a creator → 403. - **Ownership:** contests and episodes now have an `ownerId`, and every creator action (viewing, funding, reviewing, closing, picking winners, paying, transcribing) checks the signed-in creator owns it. Someone else's contest gets the same "No contest with that ID" as one that doesn't exist, so contest IDs can't be discovered by guessing. - Creators only see **their own** contests and episodes, and a contest's searchable episodes are only its creator's. - **Creators can't enter their own contests,** signed in or using their account's email. - A one-time script, `scripts/assign-owner.mjs`, gives existing contests and episodes an owner. ## Problems Resolved/Encountered: - **Hiding pages isn't security.** Step 1 alone only changed what people see; anyone could still call the server directly. Step 2's token and ownership checks are what actually protect creators' contests. - **Signing up from a creator page bounced back to log in:** the page changed before the app had saved who was signed in. Sign-up and log-in now save the user immediately. - **An open redirect:** `?next=` could have sent people to another website after logging in. Only addresses on this site are allowed now. - **Creators who are also fans:** the creator role includes everything a fan can do, so creators can enter other creators' contests. - **Old data without owners:** contests and episodes made before accounts disappeared from creators' lists until the owner script assigned them. ## How I tested this PR - Signed up as a creator and as a fan, and checked that each sees the right header and pages. - Opened a creator page while signed out: sent to log in, then back to the page after logging in. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ada33c1-0919-4e63-be91-0ad93f5cff69 - Opened `/entries` as a fan: "This page is for creators." - Ran the owner script, and my existing contests and episodes came back. Refreshed page to confirm that episodes and contests came back. - With a second creator account, I couldn't see or open my contests from the first creator's account. ("No contest with that ID"). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c0aee0f-65c1-4a79-8f0e-2ef5371adb22 - Tried entering my own contest: "You can't enter your own contest." - In the Network tab, creator requests include an `Authorization` header.

## t-1kzwmo — Task journal type + task detail page

Three user-visible paths: a journal entry can be classified as a task journal and linked to a task; the Tasks page can open one task in a detail view (mirroring the project detail page); that view shows a table of the journal entries linked to the task.

- New `EntryType.TASK` + optional `task_id` (YAML frontmatter `task-id`), non-periodic, no migration, legacy files load with `task_id=None`.
- API: `task_id` on create/update (+ `clear_task_id`), `task_id` on out, `GET /productivity/journals?task_id=` exact-match filter before pagination; create/PATCH validate the task UID against CalDAV (400 on unknown); PATCH preserve-on-omit mirrors the `clear_project_id` pattern.
- UI: `/tasks?uid=<uid>` second state of the Tasks page (no new `st.Page`, no app.py change); Open action on the shared task table routes to the Tasks page (verified all 7 call sites; `st.switch_page` resets query params so no `uid` leaks onto Dashboard/Calendar/Projects/Onboarding); task detail mirrors the project detail layout; journal create/edit gains a task selector + `default_task_id`; the linked task survives deleted tasks (shown, not dropped); type pills pick up `task`.
- Project footer behaviour unchanged; no CalDAV schema/migration, no new dependency, no new endpoint, no ADR (plan decision 1/3/5-7, all in the plan journal).

Three commits on the branch:

- **ae95c28** — the feature (as above).
- **b3e7569** — review finding 1 fix: the create-dialog "Type" selectbox now resets on each open (the wrapper pops the type key too, mirroring the `task_edit_dialog` precedent); regression test `test_create_dialog_resets_the_type_default_on_each_open`.
- **b11cd31** — user-reported warning fix: "Calling st.rerun() within a callback is a no-op." The shared table's per-row Open action called `st.switch_page` inside a `ButtonColumn` `on_click` callback, where Streamlit drops the navigation and warns. The callback now only records the target (`request_page_switch` → session state); the table performs the switch in the script body after rendering (`run_pending_page_switch`, `_table.py:568` task table / `:776` journal table). Both the task-detail journal table and the task-list Open action (same defect) are fixed. Regression test captures the literal Streamlit warning in AppTest (fails on the pre-fix code, passes with the fix).

- **QA (re-run by coordinator, post-fixes):** 778 passed (99 deselected) / test-all 877 passed / ruff check clean / ruff format clean / pyright 0 errors.
- **Code review (fresh-eyes, cloud-strong, job s-26rpf):** APPROVE. The 1 low-severity recommended fix (b3e7569) and the user-reported warning fix (b11cd31) are in; the remaining notes are non-blocking (see below).

author: agentarclab
body:
## Change

`0.2.2-rc.1.20261109.1` could not be published: both installed-App acceptance
checks failed on the same onboarding assertion.

```
expect(locator('.agentkit-credential-onboarding-content')
  .locator('[data-onboarding-mode=model]')
  .getByLabel('模型名称', { exact: true })).not.toHaveValue('')
→ Error: element(s) not found
```

macOS `Verify native Studio first-use configuration` and Windows
`Verify the actually installed Windows App UI` both failed there, so the Windows
receipt carries `"uiVerified": false` and `publish-windows-candidate.mjs` refuses
to promote it.

`src/client/pages/model-settings.mjs` rendered the manual model field as

```js
'aria-label': catalogItems.length ? '自定义模型名称' : '模型名称',
```

So 读取模型 renamed the field. `manual` is a lazy locator, so the next assertion
re-resolved `getByLabel('模型名称', { exact: true })` against a field that no
longer had that name. Two acceptance scripts depend on the stable name:
`scripts/verify-studio-onboarding-ui.mjs` and
`scripts/verify-windows-online-update.mjs`.

Fix: keep the accessible name at `模型名称` regardless of catalog state. The
visual distinction survives through the placeholder (`输入目录外的模型名`), the
`选择模型` dropdown and its `__custom__` option. No `data-*` contract, step
title, layout or validation message changes.

`#102` already added the labels but shipped product and test disagreeing, and
the unit test only asserted the name before the catalog was read — which is why
CI stayed green while the real App check went red. The test now also covers the
catalog-loaded state.

## Validation

- `node --test tests/onboarding-ui-verification.test.mjs` → 2/2 pass.
- The new assertion is a real regression gate: reverting only
  `src/client/pages/model-settings.mjs` makes it fail with
  `reading the catalog must not rename the manual model input`.
- The full `node scripts/test-studio.mjs` suite cannot run in a bare worktree:
  it needs a built `dist/` and fails identically on unmodified `main` for that
  reason (missing `dist/native-mcp-client.mjs`). The public gate covers it.
- A green run here is necessary but not sufficient: the installed-App check only
  turns green after a macOS and a Windows rebuild.

## Release impact

The shipped client bundle changes by one attribute value, so
`0.2.2-rc.1.20261109.1` needs a fresh win + mac build before publication. No
runtime contract, patch, credential or packaging-name change.

author: mkpoli
body:
**Arithmetic composition.** The Korean 破字 converter now carries a second notation, CBETA's general arithmetic formula, and the finder reads both.

**ELI5**
Arithmetic composition writes a character by joining parts with signs, but the signs are not universal. The Korean History Database uses `+` for left-right and `*` for a combination with no fixed position. CBETA uses `*` for left-right, `@` for containment, and `-+` for removal plus replacement. The Composition page now has a notation switch; the finder reads either formula as a part clue.

**Motivation.** The Korean 破字 feature was one dialect. CBETA's general rules are a second documented arithmetic notation with different sign assignments. Reading one database's formula with the other's signs gives a different character; the switch makes the assignment explicit.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Arithmetic formula"] --> B["src/arithmetic.js"]
  B --> C["Korean notation"]
  B --> D["CBETA general notation"]
  C --> E["IDS"]
  D --> E
```

**What changed**
- `src/arithmetic.js` replaces `src/paja.js` with two profiles. Korean: `+ / * -`, `▼`, and implicit left-right. General: `* / @ - + ?`, `-+` replacement, `()` grouping and `[]` text separators.
- `app/pages/Composition.svelte` adds the notation switch, a sign palette per notation, and a rules table per notation. The notes name every sign whose position is not fixed.
- `app/lib/search.js` reads a formula under both profiles and searches the part index; `Find.svelte` gains a `日*月` example, and the intro says arithmetic composition.
- Messages in five languages, sources in `docs/materials.md`, and parser and clue tests.

**Trade-offs**
- `*` (Korean), `@` and `-+` say only that parts combine, contain or replace one another. IDS `⿻`, `⿴` and `⿻` are the closest standard readings; the page says so.
- Precedence is read from the arithmetic signs. The Korean help states only that `()` comes first, so a formula without parentheses could group differently in the database.
- Search matches characters that contain the parts. It does not require the exact arrangement.
- Two notations are implemented because both are documented. No arithmetic-sign description for Hong Kong or Vietnamese material was located: [SAT's gaiji work](https://21dzk.l.u-tokyo.ac.jp/SAT/ucs_encoded.pdf) uses CHISE and Unicode assignment, and [the Nôm Foundation's composition data](https://nomfoundation.org/Conf2006/NomNa_Csttc_dequy.pdf) uses IDS operators. A source would let the site add those dialects.
- No records are copied. Unencoded characters remain outside the site's Unicode scope.

**Verification**
`bun run verify` (tests, `svelte-check`, message check) and `bun run build` pass. Checked in Chromium at 1440×1500 light and dark, and 390×844 mobile. The finder query `日*月` returns 448 characters, including 明; `間-日+月` returns one; the Korean `氵+青` returns 25, including 清.

**Screenshots**

| state | light | dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before: Korean 破字 only | ![before light](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/before-light.png) | ![before dark](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/before-dark.png) |
| after: notation switch | ![after light](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/after-light.png) | ![after dark](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/after-dark.png) |

[The section, light](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/section-light.png) · [dark](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/section-dark.png) · [phone](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/phone.png) · [finder result for 日*月](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/search.png)

**References.** The Korean rule table: ![Korean rules](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/reference-korean.png) The CBETA rule table: ![CBETA rules](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/reference-cbeta.png)

The example that prompted the Korean side, `▼(乙*車)`, and the glyph the database renders for it: ![source text](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/tweet-text.png) ![rendered glyph](https://github.com/mkpoli/han-input/raw/pr-assets/pr-68/tweet-glyph.png)

Sources: [Korean History Database, 파자 검색 help](https://db.history.go.kr/resources/unicode/help/help07.jsp); [CBETA, 一般組字式基本規則](https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/doc/en/02-04_create_word.php); the Korean example is from [@sebansios, 2026-07-26](https://x.com/sebansios/status/2081348644020916467).

## Rejection alerts: no team ping when a moderator clears an ad we found online

**9 Nov 2026, 09:20–09:55 Kampala:** the shared **Moderator 1** account worked the found-online queue for the first time since moderator rejections began alerting the team (#659, 4 Nov). Six scraped ads were rejected — two weighing-scale adverts, three with no specific area, one with no price — and each pinged Arthur's UK number and the other alert number separately with *"The lister could not be messaged — tell them yourself."* Found-online listers are never messaged by design (`found_online_listing_never_messaged`): they never listed with makaug, so there is nobody to tell.

body:
## Root cause
PR #844 merged while `index.html` still held the pre-fix scheduler. The guarded production materializer subsequently rewrote `index.html` on `main` (commit `fea38d2f`), so the tests' assumptions that `patchRafStepCap(shipping) !== shipping` and that `shipping` must lose time became invalid. This is a test-fixture lifecycle defect, not a gameplay regression.

## Change
Use the current corrected shipping RAF as the authoritative source, reconstruct the precise pre-fix carry ordering *only as a negative control*, and keep the original timing, update-budget and composed-Game assertions. Tests now apply before and after materialization.

## Gate
Do not merge until exact-head CI, Android build, and relevant Chromium checks pass. Production gameplay HTML is untouched.

### 1. 비밀키 가드 수정 (`ac7270e`)
- **기존 결함**: 임시 키 허용 플래그의 기본값이 `True`였습니다. 그래서 `DEBUG=False`에서 키를 빠뜨려도 조용히 임시 키로 부팅했고, 워커마다 키가 달라 세션·CSRF가 서로 맞지 않았습니다.
- 이제 키가 없으면 `DEBUG=True`이거나 테스트 실행 중일 때만 임시 키를 만들고, 그 외에는 `ImproperlyConfigured`로 부팅을 거부합니다.
- 운영에서는 약한 키(50자 미만, `django-insecure-` 접두사)도 거부합니다.

### 2. HTTPS 보호를 기본으로 (`ac7270e`)
- `DEBUG=False`이면 SSL 리다이렉트, 보안 쿠키, HSTS가 자동으로 켜집니다. 예전에는 플래그를 직접 켜야 했고, 잊으면 세션 쿠키가 평문으로 전송됐습니다.
- HSTS 기본값은 **1시간**입니다. HTTPS 동작을 확인한 뒤 `DJANGO_HSTS_SECONDS`로 늘리면 됩니다.
- `DJANGO_BEHIND_PROXY`(`SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER`)와 `DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`를 추가했습니다.

### 3. 요청 제한 (`a36cb4f`)
`recommend/ratelimit.py`에 캐시 기반 고정 창 카운터를 새로 만들었습니다.

| 경로 | 한도 | 초과 시 |
|---|---|---|
| `/search/` | IP당 30회/분 | 429, 검색 로그 생략 |
| `/dashboard/` | 사용자당 10회/분 | 429 (Steam API 쿼터 보호) |
| `/click/` | IP당 60회/분 | 기록만 생략, 리다이렉트는 유지 |

`X-Forwarded-For`는 `DJANGO_BEHIND_PROXY`가 켜져 있을 때만 쓰고, 그때도 맨 오른쪽 값만 사용합니다. 왼쪽 값은 클라이언트가 위조할 수 있습니다.

### 4. 클릭 로그 오염 방지 (`a36cb4f`)
- 게임명을 요청 값이 아니라 카탈로그에서 가져오고, 카탈로그에 없는 `app_id`는 기록하지 않습니다.
- `source`와 `rank`는 허용 범위로 검증합니다.

### 5. 관리자 (`a36cb4f`)
- 경로를 `admin/`에서 `DJANGO_ADMIN_URL`(기본 `steamlens-admin/`)로 바꿨습니다.
- 로그인 **실패** 횟수를 IP 기준과 사용자명 기준으로 각각 셉니다(기본 5회/15분). 잠금 중에는 맞는 비밀번호도 거부합니다.

### 6. 오타 교정 비용 축소 (`a36cb4f`)
- 검색어를 100자로 제한하고(초과 시 400), 같은 검색어의 교정 결과를 1시간 캐싱합니다.
- 소문자 결과를 원래 표기로 되돌릴 때 매번 `list.index()`로 전체를 훑던 부분을 사전 조회로 바꿨습니다.

## ⚠️ 리뷰어가 알아야 할 동작 변화

- **`.env` 없이 실행하면 서버가 뜨지 않습니다.** 의도된 동작입니다. 로컬에서는 `.env.example`을 `.env`로 복사하면 됩니다(`DJANGO_DEBUG=True` 포함).
- 관리자 주소가 `/admin/`에서 `/steamlens-admin/`으로 바뀝니다.
- 요청 제한 카운터는 Django 캐시에 저장됩니다. 기본 `LocMemCache`에서는 **워커마다 따로 세므로** 워커가 N개면 한도도 N배가 됩니다. 운영에서는 `REDIS_URL`이 필요합니다.
- 사용자명 기준 잠금에는 트레이드오프가 있습니다. 공격자가 관리자 계정을 일부러 잠글 수 있고, 잠금은 15분 뒤 자동으로 풀립니다.

## 검증

- 유닛 테스트 **68개 → 100개**, 각 커밋 단독으로도 전부 통과합니다(75 / 100 / 100).
- 실서버(`runserver`)에서 확인한 결과:
  - 기본 `/admin/`은 404
  - 검색 4번째 요청은 429 (한도 3/m으로 설정)
  - 관리자 로그인 4번째 실패는 429 (한도 3/15m, CSRF 포함 실제 POST)
- 부팅 시나리오 4가지를 확인했습니다: `.env` 없음은 거부, DEBUG 모드는 임시 키로 동작, 운영 + 약한 키는 거부, 운영 + 정상 키는 통과.
- `manage.py check --deploy`의 남은 경고는 1개(HSTS preload, 선택 항목)입니다.

## 이 PR에 포함되지 않은 것

- **Django 업그레이드**: 개발 환경에 설치된 버전이 5.2.6이라 5.2.19까지의 보안 패치가 빠져 있습니다. `requirements.txt`의 `~=5.2.6`은 이미 5.2.19 설치를 허용하므로 `pip install --upgrade -r requirements.txt`만 하면 됩니다.
- 관리자 2FA, 로그의 SteamID 기록, `pickle` 기반 임베딩 로딩, 검색어의 외부 번역 전송.
- 과거 히스토리에 남은 개발용 `SECRET_KEY`와 ITAD API 키는 폐기 대상이며 현재 코드에서 사용하지 않습니다. 히스토리 재작성은 하지 않았습니다.
- `makemigrations --check`가 allauth openid 테이블 경고를 냅니다. `main`에도 있던 것으로 이번 변경과 무관합니다.

author: jsfrouws
body:
## What

**Homing guard.** Before this change, Start never checked for homing, so `G53 G0 Z0` (the usual CAM-post ending) could move Z to a random place on an un-homed machine. Now Start refuses any program that moves in machine coordinates until the machine is homed, and names the line, e.g. "Line 66293 moves in machine coordinates (G53/G28) - home first". That covers `G53` with an axis word, and `G28`/`G29`/`G30`. Simulate still runs. A tool-change macro that uses them is not run unhomed; the change falls back to by hand, with a message saying why.

**Tool setter (fixed tool-length sensor), off by default.** It works like bCNC, CNCjs and BitSetter-style setups:
1. At an `M6` it measures the tool in the spindle, unless that tool was already measured since the work Z was set.
2. You change the tool by hand.
3. Start measures the new tool and shifts every work Z (G54–G59) by the difference.

More details:
- **Measure ahead:** *Work › Probe › Tool length* measures the current tool on its own. So do Shift+Probe on Run and `POST /api/v1/probe/tool-length`.
- **Probe move:** works like homing: seek, brake, slow back-off to release, latch.
- **Safety:** it travels at least at the work's safe height. It is refused while the spindle runs, when the setter position is outside the soft or bench limits, when no probe input is set, and when *G43* is set to **Apply** (the length would be corrected twice).
- **Touch-off wins:** a Z touch-off during the change skips the setter for that tool.
- **Errors:** a failed measurement stays in TOOL CHANGE with the reason. Reset stops it.
- **Settings:** `probe.port`, `probe.level_high`, `setter.mode/x/y/z/travel/seek/latch`. Each has a hint.

The docs are updated: user manual §3.2, §3.7 and §1 load, the API reference, ethernet-api and the app README.

## Tests
- 1908 checks pass (`make test`). New tests cover the G53/G28 guard and the setter cycle: reference measurement, M6 with a valid or invalidated reference, too-short travel, touch-off skip, Pause fallback, probe already active, and the refusals.
- `make arm` builds clean.
- Rebased onto main (G41/G42, G68/G51, Fanuc dialect). The G28/G29/G30 detection now uses the new non-modal handling.

## To test on the machine before merging
1. Note the loaded program and resume line first, and restore them afterwards.
2. Load a program ending in `G53 G0 Z0` before homing and press Start. It should be refused with the line number.
3. Home, then press Start. It should be allowed. Run as TryCut or Simulate, or stop before cutting.
4. *Settings › Tool change › Tool setter* shows **Off**. An `M6` should behave exactly as before.
5. Optional, with a setter or touch plate on an input: set `probe.port` and the level, and set the setter X/Y/Z inside the limits. Then:
   - Run *Tool length* at a low seek speed and check that it stops and backs off correctly.
   - Repeat it a few times to check repeatability.
   - Try an M6 cycle.

body: ## Summary First **usable hardware-simulation prototype** on top of the C behavioral twin (PR #2). Clean-room SystemVerilog exercises the controller datapath against a cycle-approximate NAND model with a self-checking testbench and VCD dump. **Base:** `cursor/sim-prototype-vertical-slice-a49a` (PR #2). Does not overwrite #2. ## What’s included - `docs/hw-sim-prototype.md` — 简体中文 block diagram + runbook + install notes - RTL (`rtl/`): host cmd queue → decode → FDP RUH placement → L2P/GC suspend → NAND timing model → completion - `tb/tb_aissd_hw_sim.sv` — KV/checkpoint mix, pass/fail self-check, VCD - `scripts/run_hw_sim.sh` — Verilator preferred, Icarus fallback - `make hw-sim` / `make sim-hw`; existing `make smoke` / `make proto` unchanged ## How to run ```bash sudo apt-get install -y verilator iverilog # if needed make hw-sim # → hw_sim: PASS + build/hw_sim/aissd_hw_sim.vcd # aliases: make sim-hw # force engine: AISSD_HW_SIM_ENGINE=icarus make hw-sim ``` ## What the HW sim proves - Submit→complete path for seeded writes, KV-style `TC_LAT_READ`, and checkpoint writes - Read data matches prior writes - Checkpoint (RUH=2) completions report FDP **region 2** - GC suspends after latency reads and resumes on `gc_resume` - NAND busy-cycle / read / write counters advance (timing model active) ## Constraints - Apache-2.0 clean-room; **no** Cosmos+ GPL RTL vendored - Not an FPGA bitstream or ASIC-ready design — hardware **simulation** only

author: tjfontaine
body:
## ⚠️ Do not land until a runner carries `carrick-macos-queue`

Without one, every merge group's macOS jobs would wait for a runner that doesn't exist.

## What this is

Part of #1975 (I close the issue once a merge group's macOS jobs are shown starting within 5 minutes). Merge-group macOS jobs share the four self-hosted `carrick-macos-ci` runners with PR CI, and those runners don't pick jobs in order. Tonight, PR jobs created at 06:43 and 06:45 ran while merge-group jobs from 06:26 waited, and groups waited 24 to 50 minutes several times. The owner directed that the merge queue takes precedence (#231).

This changes `macos_runner` so `merge_group` jobs request a new label, `carrick-macos-queue`, which PR jobs never request. Same-repo PRs keep `carrick-macos-ci`; forks and the nightly stay on hosted `macos-15`.

## Rollout (needs the owner, since runner labels are a repository setting)

1. Add the `carrick-macos-queue` label to `cloudmac-ci-2`, keeping `carrick-macos-ci` for now.
2. Land this PR. Its own merge group then runs on that runner.
3. Remove `carrick-macos-ci` from `cloudmac-ci-2`, so PR jobs can't occupy it.

PR CI keeps three runners. Rollback: re-add the label to the runner and change `macos_runner` back in a forward commit.

## Acceptance

After step 3, one merge group's macOS jobs start within 5 minutes of queueing while PR runs are queued, shown by job timestamps posted here.

## What
Follow-up to the v0.17.0 feature-release review ([#59 comment](https://github.com/kaiserdrake/niu-heimar/pull/59#issuecomment-6734139880)), security LOW notes 1 and 2.

- **No redirects with a key** (`lib/niu_ollama.py`): `urllib` re-sends custom headers such as `Authorization` when it follows a redirect, even to another host. Requests that carry the bearer key now go through an opener whose redirect handler raises. The health check reports `redirect refused (bearer key attached)`. Requests without a key are unchanged.
- **Doc** (`lib/niu_ollama.py` docstring): a `url_env` override (`OLLAMA_*_BASE_URL`) receives the key too.
- **Test** (`tests/ollama_test.py`): the fake gateway can answer 302 to a second fake server. The test checks that the keyed health probe fails with the refusal and that the second server never sees the `Authorization` header. Without the fix, both checks fail and the second server receives the key.

Not changed: plain `http://` to a non-loopback gateway is still allowed (it may be a LAN or tailnet address). `/api/usage/*` still has no pairing check.

- Use one `BYTEPLUS_ACCESS_KEY` / `BYTEPLUS_SECRET_KEY` pair and optional `BYTEPLUS_SESSION_TOKEN` for both TOS and Ark/Virtual Portrait.

Existing installations must move the chosen IAM credentials and matching STS token to the `BYTEPLUS_*` fields before restarting the web server and worker. `TOS_ACCESS_KEY`, `TOS_SECRET_KEY`, and `TOS_SESSION_TOKEN` are no longer read. TOS bucket, region, and endpoint settings remain separate. `BYTEPLUS_API_KEY` remains the separate ModelArk bearer key. The private local `.env` is excluded from this PR.

flowchart LR

author: tobiedavid
body:
Tonight's piece, from the topic queue: **Unknown is not no**, on missing days in a self-test log.

Made-up Rosa tests a walk after dinner against evening bloating, with a coin each evening. In the made-up version the walk does nothing, but on walk evenings that end bloated anyway she's let down and skips the tap 4 times in 10. Her app reads no tap as fine, so it calls the walk "clearly better" 28 times in 100, against 6 with nothing missing. The coin can't help, because the gaps happen after it lands. Leaving the gaps out still gives 19 in 100. Filling them the hard way gives 1, but then a walk that really works is caught only 10 times in 100 instead of 32. Gaps at random (1 in 20) cost almost nothing. The piece ends with a three-mark log (fine / symptom / "?") and a check at both ends.

**Real anchors:** NRC 2010 on missing data in clinical trials, the EMA 2010 guideline, the Russell Standard (West 2005) and Jackson 2014, Stone 2003 on paper diaries (90% apparent compliance, 11% real), and the NHS bloating page for warning signs.

**What's in it**
- `posts/2026-11-09-unknown-is-not-no.html`: the piece, with an inline SVG figure and a table
- `code/unknown-is-not-no.js`: every number on the page. The rates are exact (every possible eight-week log, weighted by its chance); a seeded 50,000-log simulation checks them; `--svg` prints the figure
- `index.html`, `feed.xml`: the piece at the top
- `EDITORIAL.md`: queue item ticked, notes for the next night

**Checks run tonight**
- The page, `index.html` and `feed.xml` parse; the inline SVG parses as XML; internal links resolve.
- At 390 px wide (light and dark), there's no horizontal scroll, and the figure and table read fine.
- `node code/unknown-is-not-no.js` reproduces every number on the page; the figure in the page is byte-for-byte the script's `--svg` output.
- A second reader (a separate fetch) checked each claim against its source. Fixes made: the NRC quote is now a marked fragment (the sentence goes on past "randomization"); "never opened" became "wasn't opened" (Stone 2003); the NHS urgent signs were regrouped to match the page; "weight loss you can't explain" became "weight loss you weren't trying for", in the French too.
- French: five sentences, with non-breaking spaces before : ; ? and inside « ».

Branched from `main`: no Kerosene pull request was open.

body:
## Model packs

- **Furniture:** a pack is a folder in `~/Library/Application Support/Agent Office/packs` with a `pack.json` that names glTF models for furniture slots: chairs, sofas, armchairs, stools, plants and pendants. Each model fits the space of the piece it replaces, so seats and walkways don't move.
- **Characters:** a `character` slot swaps the robots for a rigged humanoid. The model's bones copy the hidden robot rig, so T-pose and A-pose rigs in any units work. Bones are found by name (Mixamo, Blender `.L`/`.R`, plain names), and `pack.json` can override them.
- **Where:** the bridge and the desktop app both list and serve packs. Customize has a **Model pack** picker.

## T3 Code sessions and stuck agents

- **Stuck agents:** a run that failed before its Stop hook left its agent "thinking" forever. When a Codex or Cursor log shows the turn ended after the last hook, the agent now finishes. A log from an earlier turn can't end a new one.
- **Labels:** sessions T3 Code runs (Claude, Codex, Cursor) show as "… in T3 Code". The button reads **Open in T3 Code** and brings T3 Code forward instead of the Claude or Codex app.
- **Cursor titles:** Cursor chats from T3 Code are titled with what the user typed, not T3's injected instructions.
- **Where:** the Node bridge, the Rust desktop server and `web/index.html`.

## Testing

- `npm test` (72) and `cargo test` (53) pass on the branch tip.
- The T3 Code changes were checked against real T3 Code runs, and in an isolated test office fed simulated hooks and a failed Codex log.
- A local desktop build of `b1e8448` is installed and running.
- T3 Code has no link to a single thread, so **Open in T3 Code** opens the app, not the thread.

_Requested by **randomboy** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VncajcXfgWeRUmc4TVqycg?thread=cmsg_01VncajcXfgWeRUmc4TVqycgUDNi7JiW79bqDdAEtm8W66)_

## Why

On Android (web build) sign text typed fine at first, but after the browser's tab was switched and back the keyboard came up and no letter reached the field. The engine's experimental virtual keyboard types through a hidden `<input>` that its own `blur` handler disables (`library_godot_display.js`, `GodotDisplayVK`); a tab switch blurs it, and the browser's focus/IME state around that box is what broke (a known class of Godot web VK problems on Android).

## What

- `src/client/ui/web_text.gd` (new, client UI): on the web with a touch screen, one text box of the page that is never disabled. The sign window arms its line fields (their rects in canvas pixels, text, max length); a touch that ends on one focuses the box **in the browser's own `touchend` handler** (a real user gesture), with the line's text and the caret at its end; every `input` is copied into the LineEdit; Enter goes to the next line or saves; the box's blur lets go of the field, so the next tap starts fresh. The JS is strict and touches no `arguments`.
- `sign_window.gd`: uses it when `on` (the LineEdits get `virtual_keyboard_enabled = false`), re-arms when the fields move (the keyboard shrinks the screen), disarms on close. Desktop and Android builds are unchanged.
- Docs: `systems/ui.md`, `systems/crafting.md`, generated code index.

## Checks

lint, doc_index --check, lang_check --strict en, parse_check (254 scripts), run_tests (5225 checks, 0 failed). Web export driven by Playwright as a touch phone (412×860, dpr 2, keyboard shrinking the viewport): three rounds of tap, type, save, reopen and append all went through the page's box (`ab0` → `ab0ab1` → `ab0ab1ab2`), including a round with the page's blur/focus fired in between as on a tab switch. A real tab switch on Android can only be checked on the phone.

author: izagood
body:
## Why

On first launch the app starts this machine's operator and auto-registers it, but both steps were swallowed: if the operator could not start (e.g. Node not found) or registration failed (code mint, list read, register), nothing appeared on screen, and the only retry was the next app launch. Settings showed "Registration status is unknown" with no reason. Also, a local "registered" record skipped auto-registration even when the server no longer knew that operator (fresh server DB at the same URL).

## What

| Part | Change |
|---|---|

author: nicoyogi
body:
## What the bundle reported

`anmerkung_ai_bundle_v3_2026-11-09-03-35-34.zip`, exported at engine 1.61.2: 345 rows scanned, 18 actionable on the six Nov-9 workbooks, 17 wrong and 1 overfired, 0 the engine already solved.

## What changed (1.62.0)

The Honold processor now reads the two cost groups it ignored, `MT` (Maut) and `TG` (Tauschgebühr).

| trigger | note |
| --- | --- |
| toll line billed below its tariff copy | `Mautdifferenz` joined to the freight verdict |
| toll charge with `MT Kosten lt. Tarif` blank or 0 | `Kein Maut Tarif für '<LAND>'`, terminal |
| `TG Differenz` over `T_DACHSER` | `Differenz Tauschgebühr, ok?` joined last |
| freight within `HONOLD_FR_FLOOR` (0.50) of its own tariff, claimed by no other arm | nothing |

Cascade order, each boundary pinned by a workbook row: locked tariff, stat gate, blank FR plus ZZ, FR `Kein Tarif` (20382640 r8, SI), `Kein Maut Tarif` (20384083 r6), Volumen gate, previous tariff (20379045 r4), both phrases (20382640 r5), fallback weight or silence (20382640 NEU r11), then `Mautdifferenz` (20384083 r4), then `Differenz Tauschgebühr, ok?` (20379045 r7).

## The 18 rows: 14 fixed, 4 not derivable

11 fixed by the rule change, 3 more once their cell was corrected. The four left are recorded in the not-derivable ledger, not forced into a rule:

- `84e2169c`, `4185cb39`, `ef059c12`: `Fremdnr <number> nur in PDF nicht in CSV`. The numbers are on no cell of their row; checked against `ReferenzNr`, `ReferenzNr DL`, `Beleg-Nr. DL` and `Beleg-Nr. LP`.
- `a88eb23d`: a 2x-freight claim citing an agreement with a named person, plus `Differenz star service`. 1575 equals `FR Differenz` but the freight ratio is 2.356x, not 2, and `EXP Differenz` has one positive in the whole corpus.

Next bundle should read 341/345, 4 `known_not_derivable`, 0 overfired.

## Workbooks corrected: 56 cells, 8 files

The Tauschgebühr note was missing on every audited row that had a TG difference, which the owner ruled a workbook error, so the engine writes it and the sheets were corrected to match: 20379045 28, 20381523 (Oct 19) 9, 20382640 (Oct 27) 6, 20382640 NEU 4, 20381521 NEU 3, 20384083 NEU 3, 20383038 NEU 2, 20380811 NEU 1. Backups in `D:\TESTER\_backup\`, every cell re-read after save, and the four human overlay rows (`Fremdnr`, `star service`, `2x abgerechnet`) kept verbatim.

After the correction 211 of 215 released rows agree with the engine. The four that do not are the ledger rows above.

## Fence

The three Honold fixtures grew the MT/TG columns and are regenerated from the workbooks by `scripts/honold/build_fixtures.py`, not hand-edited, so the replays exercise the new arms instead of silently passing. 20379045 124/124, 20381523 41/41, 20380293 7/7, 20382640 (Oct 27) 17/17.

`scripts/honold/validate_rule.py` mirrors all five arms and now compares blank-truth rows, so an overfire is a mismatch; it reported the engine-only note on 20382640 NEU r11 before the floor existed. `scripts/honold/fix_workbook.py` and `audit_workbook.mjs` are new, modelled on the Dachser pair: backup, refuse `Before\`, header-resolved column, re-read after save, and a refusal to drop a ` // ` segment unless `--force`.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 668 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped
- `npm run test:anmerkung`: 355 pass
- `py scripts/honold/validate_rule.py`: 124/124, 7/7, 41/41, 14/14, 0 mismatches
- `node scripts/honold/audit_workbook.mjs` on all ten workbooks: 215 released, 211 agree, exactly 4 differ (the ledger rows)
- `npm run verify:anmerkung`: ok, manifest 15/15

## Two business questions this PR cannot settle

1. The billed `Tauschgebühr` is the tariff times 1.11 on all 50 released CH rows that carry a TG tariff, and equals it on the 95 AT and CZ rows that carry one. So the new phrase lands on every CH row and carries no row-level signal. Either the TG tariff column is missing its CH clause or Honold systematically bills 11% over it. That is a contract or tariff-sheet question; flagged UNVERIFIED in `docs/anmerkung/honold-bundle-2026-11-09.md`.
2. `Mautdifferenz` is one-sided on purpose: undercharges only. Eight rows carry a toll overcharge and none is noted (20384083 NEU r22 at +2.46 is the witness, unflagged while four negatives in the same sheet are flagged). If an overcharge should also be a finding, the arm becomes `hasErr` and roughly eight cells change.

## Reviewer notes

- The terminal `Kein Maut Tarif` arm drops a freight note by design, and r6 proves it: its `FR Kosten DL` 83.77 is the LT rate of the 200 kg bracket its 183 kg falls in, so the previous-tariff note was derivable and the auditor wrote the toll phrase alone. Made additive, that row reads two phrases and the corpus goes to 5 differ.
- `HONOLD_FR_FLOOR` is a judgement constant, not a measurement. It sits above the only dust gap that reaches it (0.11) and far below the smallest difference the fallback arm reports (3.74). The 0.64 rows are claimed by the previous-tariff arm before the floor is consulted.
- `UID_EXCLUDED_INPUT_KEYS_BY_FW.honold` carries all four new keys, so no Honold `row_uid` was re-minted and the ledger survives.

## Not in this PR

- The current tariff matrix as a second asset, which is what would replace the divergence proxy.
- Pinning the four overlay rows in `validate_rule.py`'s `KNOWN_OUTLIERS` so its exit code separates a known overlay from a regression. Recommended follow-up.

author: manio
body:
`--prune` was a no-op for Email: `email::reconcile` always returned an empty plan, so emails deleted from the archive were never destroyed on the target. Also, emails already present on the target were matched by Message-ID and just counted as skipped, so a message moved locally (e.g. Junk -> Inbox) stayed in its old mailbox on the target.

With `--prune`:
- target emails with no counterpart in the archive become prune candidates (destroyed in the existing prune phase, before mailboxes)
- matched emails get `mailboxIds` and `keywords` aligned with the archive via Email/set update (keywords compared case-insensitively)

Without `--prune` behaviour is unchanged, so flags/folders changed on the target are not overwritten by a plain export. Dry-run reports the would-be updates without sending anything.

Closes #57

author: pooza
body:
Closes #334

オーナー決定（#334 のコメント）どおり、ヘッダで渡す口を置いてクエリからは外す。段階は分けない。**`8.0.0`（breaking）**。

## 何を変えたか

| | 7.1.0 まで | 8.0.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MastodonService#streaming_uri` | `…/api/v1/streaming?access_token=<token>&stream=user` | `…/api/v1/streaming?stream=user` |
| `MisskeyService#streaming_uri` | `wss://<host>/streaming?i=<token>` | `wss://<host>/streaming` |
| `streaming_headers`（新設・`create_streaming_headers` の別名） | — | `{'Authorization' => 'Bearer <token>'}`。トークンが無ければ `{}` |

- `PleromaService` は Mastodon を、`MeisskeyService` は Misskey を継承しているので同じ形。基底の `Service` は `ImplementError`（`streaming_uri` と同じ）
- ⚠ **Misskey も同じ版で外した**（#334 は Mastodon だけを挙げていた）。同じ漏れで、利用側（mulukhiya の常駐）は SNS を問わず同じコードで `streaming_uri` を呼んでいるので、片方だけヘッダにすると分岐が要る
- 両方ともヘッダを受けることはソースで確かめた: Mastodon `streaming/index.js`（`req.headers.authorization` を先に見る）／Misskey `StreamingApiServerService.ts`（`Bearer ` で始まる `authorization` を先に見て、無ければ `i`）

## ⚠⚠ 利用側への影響

**`streaming_uri` だけで接続している利用側は、`streaming_headers` を付けないと認証されなくなる。**

- mulukhiya-toot-proxy: `Mulukhiya::Listener#initialize` が `@sns.streaming_uri` を `Faye::WebSocket::Client.new(uri.to_s, [], {...})` に渡している（`main` / `develop` とも）。上げるときは options に `headers: @sns.streaming_headers` を足す
- makoto2: `streaming_uri` を自前で持っていて上流を呼んでいない（`ginseng-upstream: pooza/ginseng-fediverse#334`）。上げても変わらない。寄せるかは makoto2 の判断（SSE 用に `https://` へ読み替えている）
- ほかのアプリ側（cure-api / tomato-shrieker / loquat / shooby-do-bop / dqdai-anniv / chubo-core / kariyon）は `streaming_uri` を使っていない（既定ブランチと develop を grep）

## 確かめたこと

- `rake test` 211 tests・0 failures、rubocop clean
- 新しいテスト `test/streaming_test.rb`（4 クラス）。変異 3 通りが赤: Mastodon がクエリに戻す／Misskey がクエリに戻す／トークン無しで `Bearer ` を送る

body:
GitHub's Overview now draws its own **Resolve** beside "Write a reply". The digest's thread chat showed two, because Geld's picture, round field and Resolve stood beside GitHub's. **Composer** - **Overview:** the reply row is GitHub's own. `dressOverviewComposer` and its CSS are gone. GitHub draws nothing in Resolve's place once a thread is resolved, so Geld adds an "Unresolve" there in the same button, pressing GitHub's header control, only while the thread is resolved. - **Classic:** the reply area is drawn the same way. There's no picture, GitHub's "Reply…" is a plain 32px field with a 6px radius on the inset surface, and GitHub's Resolve form stands beside it as a 32px "Resolve", or "Unresolve" once resolved. **Head (both views)** - **Lines:** shown right after the path in short form, "203-205" or "8230", instead of the Overview's "Lines 203 - 205" or the classic "Comment on lines +203 to +205" (which the chat now hides). - **Jump to the comment in the diff:** uses the Overview's own link, or `/pull/N/files#r` on the classic page. - **Resolve:** the Overview's check. It's filled once resolved and then unresolves, with who resolved it in the tooltip. It presses GitHub's own control in both views, and follows the fresh thread GitHub swaps in after a classic Resolve. - **Shown without a path:** the head appears whenever it has lines, the jump link or the check to offer. Only copy needs a path. - **Path fitting:** the path is now sized to its text so the lines follow it. It's fitted to the room the head leaves it, because measuring against its own rounded box cut short paths that fitted. - **Path fix:** the head names the thread's own file. An item merging one finding from two files had labelled every thread with one path (on #516, a `settings-schema.ts` thread read `overview.ts`). Before (Overview, two Resolve buttons): [Overview before](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b429264d-bf03-54a0-aa5a-89c5443d88ca/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fchat-overview-before.png) After, Overview and classic: [Overview after](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b429264d-bf03-54a0-aa5a-89c5443d88ca/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fchat-overview-after.png) [Classic after](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b429264d-bf03-54a0-aa5a-89c5443d88ca/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fchat-classic-after.png) Resolved thread, Overview and classic, with Unresolve in the row: [Overview resolved](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b429264d-bf03-54a0-aa5a-89c5443d88ca/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fchat-overview-resolved.png) [Classic resolved](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b429264d-bf03-54a0-aa5a-89c5443d88ca/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fchat-classic-resolved.png) **Verified** signed in on #516 (8 open threads), #517 (open and resolved threads) and #509 (a resolved thread), in both views: - Every thread's range, path and jump link read correctly. - Open threads show only GitHub's Resolve in the row, and resolved ones only Unresolve. - The head's check sends GitHub's own resolve request (`page_data/resolve_thread` on the Overview, `threads//resolve` on the classic page). The requests were aborted, so nothing was resolved. - A jump link from a current thread lands on the comment in Files changed. - The open editor keeps working in both views. - `pnpm check` passes, with new tests for the line reader, the head's controls, both reply rows and a thread swapped in after Resolve. **Known limit:** for an outdated thread, the classic jump leads to Files changed, where the comment is no longer in the diff. GitHub's own Overview link for the same thread leads to a commit page saying the commits can't be found after a force-push. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Thread chats now show the file path and line or line range, with a link to the related diff comment when available. * Chat headings reflect whether a thread is resolved and provide controls to resolve or reopen it. Resolved Overview threads also include an Unresolve control beside GitHub’s reply row. * **Updates** * Overview comments use GitHub’s standard reply row. Classic reply controls have updated styling, and GitHub’s inline diff-range preview is hidden when the chat header shows the line information.

author: trissim
body:
## The restatement

Each `ReadAnswered` member named its answer type twice:

```python
class TranscriptAnswered(ReadAnswered, answers=TranscriptSnapshotUpdate):
    value: TranscriptSnapshotUpdate
```

Once as the `answers=` keyword the registry was keyed by, once as the `value` field the other side decodes. Seven members, fourteen statements of seven facts — and nothing stopped a new member being registered under one type while carrying another.

The member classes themselves stay: each is the tag that lets the other side decode an answer as itself, so seven answer types is seven classes. The duplication was inside them.

## The declaration

`ReadAnswered.answers()` builds the registry from each member's own `value` declaration. The keyword is deleted from all seven members, so a new answer is one member with one `value` line.

Resolution happens at the first lookup rather than in the class body, because this module declares its result types *after* the members and the annotation there is still a string. A member whose `value` stays the base's `object` is refused by name rather than silently answering every value, which the old keyword form could not catch.

## Evidence

- All seven resolve from their own declarations, checked on the installed interpreter: `NoneType→NothingAnswered`, `TranscriptSnapshotUpdate→TranscriptAnswered`, `TranscriptDraftUpdate→DraftAnswered`, `NotificationWindow→NotificationsAnswered`, `TeammateDetail→TeammateAnswered`, `GoalSnapshotReply→GoalAnswered`, `DeliveryOverview→DeliveryAnswered`; `of(None)` still answers `NothingAnswered`.
- Every test file naming these declarations: `test_observation_encoded.py`, `test_busy_history_loading.py`, `test_input_delivery_history.py` — **24 passed** in 75.8s. The encoded-transport file is included deliberately: both the local pipe and the encoded path reach these answers.

Found while tracing P101 (local reads answered in the asking interpreter). This is the restatement that P101's own first step has to stand on; the read-routing change is separate and still open.

body:
## v0.1.9 N1 step 2, part B: projects on screen and on the phone

Projects get a home. A New project dialog asks where the work happens, every project has its own page, the Chat Focus file pane follows the open chat's project, and the phone's chat list groups by project like the desktop panel. The daemon side is step 1 (#30) and the left panel is part A (#35), both already on main; this branch is two commits on top of `06dcc65`.

### What each point does
9. **New project dialog** (`apps/web/src/projects-view.mjs`, `styles/projects.css`):
   - It opens from the + on the Projects heading, or from the New project button shown when there is no project yet.
   - "Where does the work happen?" offers In P9, In a folder I already have, and In a new folder somewhere else.
   - The existing-folder choice uses the real folder picker (Browse…). If another project already uses the folder, a line names it; two projects may share one.
   - If chats were already started in the picked folder, a checkbox offers to add them. Nothing moves unless it is ticked.
   - A line under the folder says P9 keeps its own notes in its own folder and adds nothing to yours.
   - Name and folder errors show inside the dialog. Every control is reachable by keyboard.
10. **The project page:**
    - Chats come first, then Instructions, then Added files.
    - The name and the about line are edited in place: Enter or leaving the field saves, Escape puts it back.
    - Instructions show their first three lines, then "Show N more lines". Edit opens a text box that saves as you type.
    - Added files can be added (button or drop) and removed, and each row shows its size.
    - The work folder line has Open. If the folder has its own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, a note says agents read it on their own.
    - A folder that is gone shows "Folder not found" with Locate….
    - More has Show the work folder, Rename, Archive project and Delete project…. Archived projects get their own page, from which they can be brought back.
    - Delete asks once. It names what is removed, says the chats move to Chats, and never touches a folder the user chose.
    - Each chat row also gets Rename, Archive and Delete in its menu.
11. **MC-18** (`apps/web/src/files-view.mjs`): the Chat Focus file pane opens on the chat's project work folder. A chat in no project keeps today's behaviour. The second commit fixes a crash found while testing this: on the Archived page there is no project, and the pane's lookup threw, so the file tree stopped drawing there.
12. **Phone** (`apps/web/src/phone-projects.mjs`, `phone.ts`): the chat list groups by project, then Chats, the same way as the desktop panel. `phone.ts` stays at 1,909 lines; the grouping lives in the new module.

Line caps: `controller.mjs` 1,378 (cap 1,381) and `phone.ts` 1,909, both unchanged. No file is over 1,500 lines and `main.mjs` gains nothing. `scripts/gate.mjs` lists `projects-view.mjs` on the reviewed write list: it posts to the daemon's project routes and reads files the user drops.

### Tests (dev space)
- `test/projects-page.test.mjs`:
  - New project with each of the three kinds of work folder; the adopt offer moving only the ticked chats; the shared-folder line;
  - the page: in-place rename and about, instructions, added files, and Open;
  - MC-18: the file pane root follows the project, and the file tree still draws on the Archived page;
  - delete leaves the folder and moves the chats to Chats; Locate on a gone folder; archive and back; a chat's Rename, Archive and Delete.
- `test/phone-projects.test.mjs`: the phone list groups by project.
- A/B breaks, each failing its test: the adopt offer ignored; a rename not saved to the daemon; the file pane not following the project; the Archived page fix taken out; the phone list not grouped.

### Screenshots
They are kept with the sprint evidence, mock beside app: the project page In P9 and in a folder, the three dialog states, the delete dialog, no projects yet, Folder not found, 960 wide, and the light theme.

### Questions left open
Each point below keeps today's behaviour; the report asks how to go on:
- the In P9 work folder has no path to show;
- Open shows the Files pane, because a page can't open a folder elsewhere;
- the native picker's title still reads "Start the chat in";
- the adopt offer counts only chats with no project;
- in split view the pane header holds more buttons than fit in a half-width pane, so the last ones are cut off. Fixing it needs a choice of which actions move into a menu, so it is not changed here.

body:
## 问题

用户提问「查看下现在项目 github action 是怎么触发才能发布，为什么我推送了很多次都没有直接发布 npm」时，Router：

- 查到已关闭的 tk-3（PR #11 已合并）后，按「重复已经开过工单的请求」直接 `ignore`，没有开工单；
- 回复内容来自 tk-3 的历史 Worker 上报，没有核实当前仓库，却以现在时陈述为当前事实；

body:
Stacked on #84.

Specification 7.3 asks for two things at once - the workflow disappears **and** the records stay - so both are tested. A test that only proved the first would be satisfied by deleting the module, which is what the specification forbids.

**Suite: 701 passed, 2 skipped, 703 collected** (reconciled against `--collect-only`).

| Decision | Why |
|---|---|
| 404, not 403 | The resource does not exist for a hospital that never bought the module; 403 would disclose that it exists |
| Routers stay mounted, gate per request | Module state is data and changes while the server runs; omitting at startup means a restart after every switch |
| Unmigrated database degrades to core only | A missing `ModuleState` table is a broken install, not a hospital with no modules - and not a 500 on every request |

Three things the suite caught: the QA harness needed module rows (it builds schema with `create_all`), the unmigrated-database path, and two tests that asserted a source literal rather than an actual mount.

author: ascrivener
body:
Part of T1 (Vec/Option decoders): the allocator facts needed to run `realloc` again in `read_vec`'s chunk loop (3473) for payloads over 16384 octets.

New file `Services/Bootstrap/Decode/ReallocOk.lean`. It only adds results; nothing existing changes.

- `realloc_wrap_cases_hdata` is `Alloc.realloc_wrap_cases_data` with one more conclusion for each block `(r, s', _)` the model's `realloc` returns: `s'.base = s.base` and `s'.base + 32 · s'.allocated ≤ 4096 · h'`, where h' is the heap's page count afterwards. Every allocator theorem assumes this bound (`hHT`), so the next `alloc` or `realloc` can now be called.
  - In place, shrink, zero, and grow without new space: h' = ph, because these cases keep the allocated space.
  - Grow with `grow_heap`: the bound is the existing sub-theorem's conjunct.
  - Fallback: the bound comes from `alloc`, then passes through `free`.
  - The proof is a copy of `realloc_wrap_cases_data`'s case split that keeps each case's bound. Hypotheses are identical.
- Model lemmas:
  - `free`, `shrink` and `free`'s two merges keep the allocated space.
  - `realloc_inplace_state`: an in-place realloc keeps the base and the allocated space.
  - `growInplace_grows`: `growInplace_ok` without its "unchanged" disjunct, for a chunk that actually grows. Its proof is a copy of `growInplace_ok`'s.
  - `realloc_chunk`: for alignment one unit and a nonzero request, the returned block is an allocated chunk of exactly the request plus one unit, so its usable size is the request.

Docs: an entry under the `read_vec` item in `docs/whats-proven.md`. `Services.lean` imports the new file.

Checks: full `lake build` passes. `scripts/CheckAxioms.lean` passes. That script does not cover the `Picoalloc` namespace, so I ran `#print axioms` on `Picoalloc.realloc_chunk` separately: propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

Model/binary disagreements: none found.

author: teamleaderleo
body:
Leo, 2026-11-09: "the other thing is that for some reason the dot isn't disappearing in my case... but i guess the current nightly still hasn't fixed/restarted the service?"

The Mac fix (`lane/sticky-unread-read`, `TabReads`) keeps a read the person made while the daemon is down or restoring. The phone sent its reads once and only logged a failure, so a read made from the phone while the Mac's daemon was down, restarting or restoring was lost and the Mac kept the dot:

- Feed reads (`TerminalFeed.itemsChanged`): one `ack-tab-notifications`, error logged.
- Mark Workspace as Read (`setUnread`): a failed `set-workspace-metadata` rolled the row back with "Couldn't mark … as read", and the tab acks were `try?`.
- Mark All Notifications as Read: the first failed ack threw and the rest never went.

Now each of these goes through `StickyRead` (new, `CmuxMobileLive`): the write goes again, spaced 0.25 s doubling to 5 s, while the Mac is unanswered (no bound `daemon` channel, a closed one, or a reply past its deadline), on whichever connection to that Mac is bound at each try. Only the daemon's refusal (`DaemonReplyError`) ends it unsent. Every loop stops at its answer, a refusal, or once the read no longer stands:

- Feed: the Mac's ledger shows the row acknowledged, a newer notification arrives on that tab, the person marks the item unread, the Mac changes, or the feed is released. The ack goes to the tab's surface the ledger gives at that try, and a read in flight is never sent twice across a reconnect.
- Mark as Read: the Mac's tree shows the workspace read or gone, the person marks it again (Unread or Read), or the phone no longer links that Mac. Tabs showing a newer notification than the one read are left.
- Mark All: every tab settled, or the Mac is no longer linked. It now takes a linked Mac whose daemon channel is reconnecting, and its reads run in the background, so a down or silent Mac never holds another linked Mac's read.

The phone already shows each read at once without the Mac, so there's no new optimistic hold: a Feed item's read mark is the phone's own, and Mark as Read sets the row's `seenAt`, which keeps the row's dot hidden until newer activity even while the tree still says unread. The tab markers in the tree follow the Mac once the retry lands.

`DaemonClient` also now fails a request on a channel that already ended right away. Before, `request` and `resourceRequest` on an ended client waited forever (or until their deadline), which would have stalled a retry on a client the phone hadn't replaced yet.

Parity row added in `cmux-next-ios/verify/parity-mac.md`.

## Changelog

- Fixed: On iPhone, a notification or workspace you mark read while the Mac's cmux is restarting is now read on the Mac too once it is back.

## Tests

Red commit a0e4cbb9748e6e86cffe90b5a79bff3f5ce5dd92 (tests only), green head eee7416aecf0e7728fb028516d5ae00b7ca46428:

```
cmux-ci run --class simulator --script scripts/ci/cmux-next-ios-sim.sh --ref SHA --arg test \
  --arg only=CmuxMobileLiveTests/TerminalFeedTests,CmuxMobileLiveTests/PhoneReadsStickTests
```

- `TerminalFeedTests/aReadMadeWhileTheMacIsDownReachesItOnceItAnswers`: the daemon fails every request, the person reads a Feed item, the daemon comes back on a new connection; the ack must arrive once, on connection 2.
- `PhoneReadsStickTests`: Mark as Read and Mark All while the daemon goes quiet and its channel closes, then a new channel binds; the write must go again and reach it.

Red at a0e4cbb9748e6e86cffe90b5a79bff3f5ce5dd92 (tests only, base code), fleet step f05852b325d190933d1b2358 on an iOS 26.5 simulator: exit 65, passed 19, failed 3, the 3 new tests:
- `aReadMadeWhileTheMacIsDownReachesItOnceItAnswers`: `daemon.unanswered → 1` (the read went once), `daemon.acks → []`.
- `markAsReadMadeWhileTheDaemonRestartsReachesItOnceItIsBack` and `markAllAsReadMadeWhileTheDaemonRestartsReachesItOnceItIsBack`: `LiveWorkspaceCreationBackend` threw `LinkError(code: "closed")`.

Green at head 42ee5b1b8d17c7e00a48c6554645eee46d9b8c52 with `only=CmuxMobileLiveTests/TerminalFeedTests,CmuxMobileLiveTests/PhoneReadsStickTests,CmuxMobileLiveTests/AgentChatsLiveTests,CmuxMobileLiveTests/WorkspaceArrangementLiveTests,CmuxMobileTransportTests,CmuxMobileModelTests/WorkspaceArrangementTests`: exit 0, passed 61, failed 0, skipped 0. The step builds the Demo simulator app first, so the app target (ShellModel) compiled too.

### Observed / Not run

Ran: the red and green fleet steps above, and `prepush-gate.py` (no new violations). Review fixes added after the first review: a Feed retry waits for the new connection's ledger before it acks (`aReadOnItsWayEndsWhenANewerNotificationCameMeanwhile`), a marker the restarted daemon renumbered is matched by its post time (`aRenumberedMarkerIsStillTheNotificationRead`), Mark as Read goes even when a Mark as Unread on its way has not shown in the tree yet, and Mark All takes a Mac whose daemon channel is reconnecting and reads in the background (`markAllAsReadMadeWhileReconnectingReachesTheMacOnceItIsBack`; `markAllAsReadAcksOnlyTheUnreadTabs` now waits for its ack).

Not run: a real phone against a Mac whose daemon restarts (only the mock daemon above); the full CmuxMobileKit suite (only the suites listed). Mark All no longer shows the Mac's refusal of a tab in the Feed menu: it reads in the background, and a refusal is logged.

author: hanno-becker
body:
```
GEN_BIGSTEP_TAC simulates a call through the callee's ensures theorem.
Take a callee with frame MAYCHANGE [PC; X0; X1], called in state s29
and returning in state s30. After using the callee's precondition and
postcondition, the tactic has the goal

  MAYCHANGE [PC; X0; X1] s29 s30 ==> eventually arm R s30

It unfolds the frame into one nondeterministic write per component
(MAYCHANGE, ASSIGNS_SEQ, ASSIGNS_THM), which gives a nest of
beta-redexes with one level per component:

  (\s s'. ?y. (\s s'. ?y. (\s s'. ?y. write X1 y s = s')
                          (write X0 y s) s')
              (write PC y s) s') s29 s30
  ==> eventually arm R s30

REWRITE_TAC[LEFT_IMP_EXISTS_THM] reduces the redexes and moves the
existentials out, and REPEAT GEN_TAC strips them:

  !y y' y''. write X1 y'' (write X0 y' (write PC y s29)) = s30
             ==> eventually arm R s30

The state-update tactics then turn the equation into facts about s30,
such as `read X0 s30 = y'`.

Both of these steps get slow when the frame is large. The frame of an
ABI-conformant callee, MAYCHANGE_REGS_AND_FLAGS_PERMITTED_BY_ABI, has
58 components on AArch64, so the nest has 58 levels:

- REWRITE_TAC, with its basic rewrites, spends about 10 times as long
  on the unreduced nest as on the beta-reduced one: 2.7 s against
  0.27 s for one such call.
- GEN_TAC gives a stripped variable a primed name when the name is
  already free in the goal or its assumptions. That is most of them,
  since the names repeat across types: after y, y', ... of type int64
  come y, y', ... of type int128 for the Q registers. For each primed
  variable the justification alpha-converts the whole conclusion back
  to the bound name. In a safety proof that conclusion holds the
  instantiated event-list witness, which is large.

This commit beta-reduces the antecedent with TOP_DEPTH_CONV BETA_CONV
before the REWRITE_TAC, and replaces REPEAT GEN_TAC by
REPEAT_GEN_ALPHA_TAC. That tactic gives the same subgoal with the same
fresh names. Its justification generalizes all variables with one
GENL and gets back to the bound names with one ALPHA; if that fails it
falls back to the per-variable steps. The goal after a big step is
equal (`=`) to the old one, so no caller changes.```

## Summary

Add an experimental Auth0 agent tool for sign-in investigations. It exposes six tools for exact-email lookup, profiles, filtered authentication logs, brute-force block checks, and optional unblock. Reads and writes use separate OAuth credentials and token caches; writes default to disabled and require a distinct write application.

The node includes configuration validation, a read-only example pipeline, a curated credential catalog entry, and setup and operational documentation.

## Validation

- 99 Auth0 tests passed after rebasing onto develop.
- 13 credential generator tests passed; credential catalog check and node README validation passed.
- Gitleaks, Ruff, and Ruff formatting pre-commit hooks passed.
- Documentation build and docs export check passed.
- Read-only development-tenant tests exercised user lookup, profiles, user logs, individual log events, block checks, mixed-case lookup, and token reuse. An OpenRouter chat test returned the expected read-only result; individual agent tool calls were not independently traced.

## Limitations

Live unblock has not been verified against a real Auth0 tenant; no live writes were performed. It has not been confirmed through live testing that read:logs_users alone is sufficient for user-log reads. The full repository test suite was not run; focused Python tests used an isolated test configuration because optional local pytest plugins were unavailable. CI may identify additional integration issues, and these limitations may need resolution before merging.

Refs #3120

body: ## Summary Copter-4.6.3 plus the eRob CANopen servo driver. This pull request does not include ARINC429, AP_ARINC429, or the CS35 codec from PR #5. The base is the `Copter-4.6.3` branch on this fork, which is the official ArduPilot tag `Copter-4.6.3` (`92b0cd788ec29406f26c6f9c31d5ceedbd1cc538`). The tag is also pushed to this fork. The driver is the feature set from `0ac57cc5` (`feature/erob-canopen-can2` / `cursor/erob-rate-fault-backoff-84d6`): - `CAN_Dx_PROTOCOL` 15 owns the driver exclusively. It is not a `PROTOCOL2` option. - Parameters are `CAN_Dx_EROB_*`: NODE/BM fallback, SV/ID slots, MIN/MAX, GEAR, RES, CTR, and RATE/ACC/DEC. - Named-float telemetry and DataFlash ERB1/ERB2/ERB3. - Arming uses the cached CiA402 fault status. - `SRV_Channels::push()` writes the CSP targets. ZeroOneX6 and CUAV-X7 compile the driver in. Defaults do not select protocol 15. CAN1 stays DroneCAN. CAN2 uses eRob only after the user sets `CAN_P2_DRIVER 2` and `CAN_D2_PROTOCOL 15`. `AP_EROB_CANOPEN_ENABLED` defaults to 0. Other boards do not link the behaviour unless a hwdef or custom build turns it on. ## Porting notes - Copter-4.6.3 `AP_CANDriver::init` is `init(uint8_t driver_index, bool enable_filters)`. The driver ignores `enable_filters` and accepts only its own Node-IDs in software. - Arming uses `ARMING_CHECK_SYSTEM`, which is the 4.6.3 check id. - Protocol 15 was unused on this tag (`RadarCAN` is 14). - The unrelated RPLidar method rename that sits on the master eRob branch was not brought over. ## Testing - Toolchain: GNU Arm Embedded 10-2020-q4-major (`arm-none-eabi-gcc 10.2.1 20201103`). - `./waf configure --board ZeroOneX6 && ./waf heli` succeeded. - Firmware string: `ArduCopter V4.6.3 (0a197a57)`. - `.apj` `board_id` 5600, `summary` ZeroOneX6, `git_identity` `0a197a57` (tip `0a197a57ec80f990d8af5c18d9d55be4296455c5`). - Generated `hwdef.h` has `AP_EROB_CANOPEN_ENABLED 1` and `APJ_BOARD_ID 5600`. - `AP_eRobCANOpen` symbols are in `arducopter-heli`.
