author: sukardaddy
body:
## What this does

Roadmap PRs 7 and 14 of the saved-device desktop app. A technician can now **hand a support task to an agent that runs on the relay itself**, follow it, and leave it working. The agent acts as the technician, through the same tools, role checks and stops an MCP client has. It runs on any OpenAI or Claude model the team chooses, GPT-6.1 Terra by default, with the team's own key, and it stops at the caps the team set. Version **0.7.0**.

### Starting and following a task
- Three new MCP tools. `agent_start {device_id | session_id, instructions, keep_working?, model?}` starts a task on a saved PC or on a session the technician drives. `agent_status {task_id?, wait_s?}` shows the steps, notes, cost and summary, and can wait up to 25 seconds for a change. `agent_control {task_id, action: pause | resume | stop}` controls it. The tool count goes from 24 to 27.
- The same in the team API, under `/api/v1/w/<slug>/agent/tasks`.
- The agent tools are for members only, never open mode. Starting and controlling need `sessions.control`; reading needs `sessions.view`.
- The relay runs one step per Durable Object alarm, in a new `AgentTask` object, so a task keeps going after the technician disconnects. Without `keep_working`, it stops 2 minutes after the last status read.
- Every step checks again that the starter is still an active member with the role. A task also ends at 120 tool calls or 2 hours, when someone else takes over its session or commands its link session, when the session ends, and on a workspace or relay stop. It ends a saved-PC session it opened, and only while the starter still drives it, and it leaves a session it was given.
- An action already sent is never sent twice. After a crash, the model is told "outcome unknown; take a screenshot".
- The session log marks the agent's actions as the starter's, `via agent`.
- The next task on a PC starts with that PC's last three summaries, marked as untrusted.

### Settings, keys and caps (team API only)
- `GET` and `PATCH /api/v1/w/<slug>/agent` (`members.manage`) set the mode, the default model, whether a starter may pick a model, the two caps, and an OpenAI key and a Claude key.
- A key is sealed under `AUTH_SECRET` with the workspace as associated data. It is shown only as its last four characters and opened only inside an `AgentTask` object. A canary test checks that it never appears in an API answer, a tool result, a log or audit row, a step record or an error.
- **Nothing runs until an admin sets a per-task cap and a per-month cap.** Before every model call, its worst case is reserved in D1 against both caps with one guarded update, and the output limit shrinks to fit the room left (never under 4,000 tokens). So tasks running at once can't pass a cap together.
- **Mode.** A team picks MCP clients, the built-in agent, or both (the default). In agent mode, `/mcp` refuses the session tools but keeps the agent tools, `device_list`, `session_list` and `session_status`.

### Models
- The code has prices for five models: `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`.
- An admin adds the models a team may use with `POST .../agent/models`. That includes those five, and any other OpenAI or Anthropic model with its prices typed in. `DELETE .../agent/models/<provider>/<id>` removes one.
- Adding a model runs a two-turn check with the team's key: the model must call a tool, then read a word off a small screenshot.
  - Claude's settings (thinking, effort, output limit) come from Anthropic's model capabilities.
  - An OpenAI model that refuses reasoning is saved without it.
- A check costs under a cent and is shown in the answer.

### Privacy
- The relay now sends screenshots to the team's AI provider while a task runs. It stores no screenshot, typed text or model reply; only redacted step records are kept.
- OpenAI requests send `store: false`. The providers' own retention still applies, and the security model and README say what it is.
- Screen text, UI trees, command output, files, fields, notes and summaries go to the model wrapped as untrusted data.

## Tests
- `npm test`: 685 of 685 pass, 144 of them new. They drive the loop against fake providers built from real response bodies, and cover:
  - **Caps:** parallel tasks, output sizing, settlement, and charging a call that got no answer;
  - **Crash points:** before and after an action is sent, and around a connect;
  - **Takeovers:** with every way a task can end;
  - **Sessions:** pause and resume, and the 2-minute rule;
  - **Models:** the checks, the mode gate and membership;
  - **The key canary.**
- CI's Windows job builds the app and passes the native tests.

### Before the build, against the real APIs
- One-off calls to both providers with the real tool list confirmed:
  - a screenshot inside an OpenAI tool result works;
  - the strict schema conversion is accepted;
  - prompt caching works on both providers, with reads of 3,949 to 8,417 tokens on later turns;
  - the usage fields match the cost formulas.
- A throwaway free-plan Worker ran a Durable Object alarm with up to 34 MB of JSON work at 94 ms of CPU without being cut off. A realistic step uses about 9 ms.
- This PR's bundle deployed to a throwaway Worker (since deleted) at 699 KiB gzipped, with a 4 ms startup time.

### Live run (Windows 7, against `wrangler dev`, real keys)
- **Benchmark tasks:** all passed their verify scripts.
  - Printer, on GPT-6.1 Terra: 8 actions, $0.021.
  - Recycle Bin, on GPT-6.1 Terra: 5 actions, $0.014. The right file came back and no decoys.
  - Date format, on Claude Sonnet 5.5: 3 actions, $0.027.
- **Models added by id with typed prices:** both passed the check and finished a short task.
  - `gpt-4.1` was saved without reasoning after OpenAI refused that setting.
  - `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` was saved without thinking and effort, which its capabilities say it lacks.
- **Caps:** with a $0.10 task cap, a task on GPT-6.1 Sol stopped with "spending cap reached" at $0.021. It stops early by design, because every call first reserves its worst case.
- **Pause, resume and stop:** pause held for 30 seconds with no actions, and resume carried on. Stop ended a task after 6 actions with nothing sent after it, and the session it was given stayed attached.
- **The 2-minute rule:** a task started without `keep_working` stopped 121 seconds after its start, with "nobody asked for its status for 2 minutes".
- **Session log:** the agent's actions show as `[local-dev via agent] click 25,780`.
- **Cost:** the whole live run cost $0.48 across nine tasks.

Not run live:
- **Windows 11,** because that machine was in use for other work.
- **A task opening and ending a saved-PC session.** The Windows 7 PC lost its pairing during setup, so all nine tasks ran on a one-off link session. The saved-PC path is covered by tests.
- **Costs against each provider's console.** The cost formulas are tested against real usage fields, but not compared with the providers' own figures.

## Review
- Before the build, three blind Opus reviews of the plan found 16, 20 and 14 problems, all folded in. Two of them would have blocked the build:
  - the model check would have opened the key outside the task object;
  - replayed OpenAI reasoning items needed their encrypted content.
- A blind Opus review of the code scored 6.5/10 with one blocking finding: a task that was stopped could end a session another technician had taken over. All 15 findings are fixed, each with a regression test:
  - **Sessions:** a pause had no time limit, and a resume after a long pause tripped the 2-minute rule.
  - **Failures:** a failing step was never retried, and a timed-out call was never charged.
  - **Estimates:** the token estimate undercounted non-Latin text.
  - **Prompts:** the last note came back as trusted text.
  - **Smaller issues:** several more.

- The automatic review's first round (GPT and Opus, with a verifier) blocked on two cleanup bugs: a fa

author: akingundogdu
body:
## Summary
Adds recurring reminders with a menu bar alert, and makes the main window reliably appear at launch (full screen, with a minimum size).

## What changed and why

### Window never shows at launch
- **Problem:** the app (a login item) sometimes kept running with no window, so it had to be searched for and launched again. Observed directly: the running login-item instance had zero windows, and one fresh-build launch also created none. SwiftUI's `WindowGroup` offers no reliable way to reopen a window from AppKit (a reopen call and a self-sent reopen Apple event both failed).
- **Fix:** `MainWindowController` creates the window from AppKit in `applicationDidFinishLaunching`, so showing it is a direct call. `applicationShouldHandleReopen` and a new "Show World Clock" button in the menu bar popover bring it back after it is closed. The scene is now an empty `Settings` scene (Settings menu item removed). Trade-off agreed: ⌘N multiple windows are no longer available.
- The window opens in macOS full screen on the display it was last on; if that display is gone it is recentered on a connected one.
- Minimum content size 640×690 (measured with the calendar panel fully expanded). The Reminders/Timer/Add Clock tiles moved from an overlay into their own row, because the overlay covered the clocks at every size, even full screen. The date header scales down instead of truncating.

### Recurring reminders
- `Reminder` / `ReminderSchedule`: every N minutes on chosen weekdays between a start and end time (both inclusive), e.g. "Drink water" every 45 min on weekdays 09:00–18:00.
- `ReminderStore`: persistence in `UserDefaults`, due alerts, snoozes. After a long sleep only a fire time within the last interval is shown (no stale alerts).
- `ReminderMenuBarController`: bell icon in the menu bar (badge when an alert is active); click opens the list/editor popover; a due reminder slides a non-activating panel down under the icon with **Done** and **5m/10m/15m** snooze. Custom button style keeps colors in the inactive panel.
- `ReminderPanelLayout`: with several displays the status item window reports a frame ~74 pt away from the menu bar it is drawn in (measured), which pushed the panel off screen. Only the icon's x position is trusted; the panel goes under the matching display's menu bar.
- Main window: a "Reminders" tile opens the same list as a sheet.

### Tests
- New `world-clock-appTests` unit test target (Swift Testing) and a shared scheme with a test action.

## How it was tested
- `xcodebuild test` → 22 tests in 3 suites passed (schedule math, store tick/snooze/dismiss/persistence/stale-alert rules, panel layout with the real 4-display frames).
- Manual runs of the built app:
  - Main window present and on screen on 6/6 launches (5 direct, 1 via `open`); in full screen it covers the whole 1920×1080 display it was last on.
  - Window closed → app launched again → window back on screen.
  - Requested 500×500 → window stays at 640×690. In-process snapshots at 640×690 (calendar 80 and 300 px) and 1920×1018 show no overlap.
  - A test reminder (passed via launch argument, nothing written to disk) fired on time; panel measured at y=34 (right under the menu bar) instead of y=-40 before the layout fix.
- No e2e suite exists for this app.

body:
## What was red

Tip runs 42568653071 (ccf12d36) and 42575483067 (ca4bae15):

- `UpdatedCardScaleDownTests.swift:70/71/77/115/116/140/148`: held height and height are 0 pt.
- `UpdatedCardStreamingSteadyTests.swift:169`: "islands opened 1".
- `UpdatedCardHoverPreviewTests.swift:80` (x moved), `:115/:116` (resting glass frame, glass not first subview), `:296/:297` (hover does not end).

## Root cause

af041242c9c (Lawrence 2026-11-07, "i dont like how it expands upwards") changed the design on purpose. The Updated card's changes now open beside the sidebar in the hover card window (`SidebarUpdatedNotesPopover`). When the card shows, it also makes a second page (`.updatedNotes`). The in-card list that grows over the rows became the Debug look `UpdatedCardPreviewMode.above`.

- ScaleDown: the fakes appended the notes page to `islands`, so `islands.last` was the notes page. The tests reported heights to it, not to the card's page.
- StreamingSteady: the notes page, made when the card shows, counted as an island opened during the streaming turn.
- HoverPreview: the in-card preview tests ran the shipped beside look. In that look the notes page is parked as the host's first subview, and the card's page never grows.

Two more expectations followed earlier design commits:

- 8d5626228bc ("the hover preview reads whole: header first") puts the x on the header's title line at the open preview's top. `:80` still expected the x on the resting card's line.
- `:115` expected the resting glass to equal the host's bounds. The glass is the card's 48 pt on its bottom edge, and the view rounds to 49 pt on a half-point slot. This has been red since #38117 landed (fleet step 167377a4 at 3f277a1c, before af041242c9c).

## Change (test only)

- ScaleDown: the fakes keep the card's pages (`.updated`) and the notes pages apart.
- StreamingSteady: the island count starts after the card shows. A turn still must open no page.
- HoverPreview: the four in-card tests set `UpdatedCardPreviewMode.above` and put it back after. The open-x check now expects the header's title line at the view's top, and the x back on the card's line after the close. The resting glass check expects the card's height on its bottom edge.

No product change. No test was removed or skipped.

## Verify

Fleet step c30c48365dfa42699cabd254 (aws-m4pro-6) at 1e7f13c2a2761eedaf9506277474b8c20abf8bd0: UpdatedCardHoverPreviewTests, UpdatedCardScaleDownTests, UpdatedCardStreamingSteadyTests: All 3 suites passed.

author: edgar-fix-issues[bot]
body:
Closes #100

## Questions

- The issue does not define the quote request body; the client posts { network: 'mainnet' | 'testnet', sender }. Does /v1/sponsorship/quote expect that, or other fields such as the nonce or the fee tier?
- Error responses are read as { error, code, reason } at the top level of the body. If the sponsorship API nests them (for example { error: { code, reason } }), readLeatherApiErrorData needs adjusting.
- Ledger wallets are excluded along with Stacks policy accounts, following the issue's 'software account' scope. Should Ledger accounts also get the sBTC fee path?

## Why

- A user who holds sBTC but not enough STX for the network fee could not send their sBTC, and the old verify-based sponsor check never let them pay the fee in sBTC.

## How

- Added LeatherSponsorshipApiClient (quote and submit on the Leather API, X-Client-ID, HIGH priority, zod-parsed, SPONSORSHIP_API_URL override outside tests), React Query configs with an unpersisted quote, and sBTC transfer-many builder and decoder helpers in @leather.io/stacks.
- With an sBTC balance and STX below the lowest estimate, the SIP-10 form shows Low/Standard/High in sBTC with a Sponsored badge and no custom fee, validates and sends max against the balance minus the fee, and the review signs the sponsored transfer and posts { quoteId, transaction } to submit, re-quoting with a fresh nonce on expiry, quote_expired or stale_nonce.
- Removed the verify eligibility check, made both local broadcast paths refuse sponsored transactions, rendered the sent summary from the returned hex, and added the /playground/sbtc-sponsorship-flows exploration area.

## Tested

- Round 1: review found 1 critical, blocker or regression findings
- Round 2: checks passed and review found no critical, blocker or regression findings

author: abarbesgaard
body:
## Problem

A nightly kill-matrix shard took about 70 minutes: 121 mutants, each a 22s build plus 59s running the whole suite. A third of the suite's time is the 30 architecture tests, about 3s each. They read the source tree, which no mutant changes, so they never kill anything.

## Solution

- The sweep skips the architecture tests (`-E 'not binary_id(*::architecture)'`). They were already left out of the suspects. Locally, one file's sweep went from 2m34 to 1m22, with the same kills.
- 64 shards instead of 32, so each runner gets about 60 mutants. The repo is public, so runner time is free. The shard timeout drops from 180 to 90 minutes.

The nightly should take about 25 minutes instead of 75.

author: azrael417
body:
**Breaking:** samples for a given seed change, and models trained with the old noise (e.g. FourCastNet 3) see noise of another distribution.

Port of the fix in NVIDIA/torch-harmonics#351 to makani's own noise processes.

## Isotropy (`IsotropicGaussianRandomFieldS2`, `DiffusionNoiseS2`)
The real and imaginary parts of the SH coefficients were drawn alike at all orders. The real inverse SHT drops the imaginary part at `m = 0`, while an order `m > 0` also stands for its conjugate at `-m`. So the orders `m > 0` carried twice the power of `m = 0`, and the variance depended on the latitude: at the poles it was 0.5–0.87 of the equator's, 0.50–0.65 for the diffusion noise of the FourCastNet 3 configs.

The orders `m > 0` are now drawn with `1/sqrt(2)` of the amplitude, as in torch-harmonics, so the variance is `sigma^2` at every latitude. The complex-normal convention, half the variance in each of the real and imaginary parts (a `/ sqrt(2)` in the isotropic draw, a `0.5` in the diffusion normalization), is dropped: it used to make up for the doubled power of `m > 0`, and with the order weights it would halve the variance. As in torch-harmonics, the draws have unit variance in both parts. Compared to before, the mid-latitude variance is unchanged and the polar variance roughly doubles. The order weights are a non-persistent buffer (`m_weights`) of their own, split over `w`, so learnable spectra restored from a checkpoint get them too.

## Diffusion normalization
The normalization of the `DiffusionNoiseS2` spectrum (`F0norm`) left out the degree `l = 0`, which the field has, so the variance grew with `kT`: by 0.5% at the default, and by 14% and 74% for the two largest `kT` of the FourCastNet 3 configs. It now covers all degrees, and the variance is `sigma^2` for every `kT`.

## Noise truncation of FourCastNet 3
Without an explicit `lmax` the noise takes its truncation from torch-harmonics. Up to 0.8 that was `lmax = nlat`, so 721 on the 721×1440 grid FourCastNet 3 was trained on. From 0.9 on, equiangular grids truncate to `(nlat + 1) // 2 = 361`, which drops the finest scales of the noise. The `input_noise` blocks in `config/fourcastnet3.yaml` now set `lmax: 721`. The ICON benchmark configs inherit it, and that's enough for their `kT`.

## Tests
- `TestNoiseIsotropy` computes the exact pointwise variance by feeding an identity basis through the draw, in float64. It checks that the variance is flat over latitude and equal to `sigma^2`, for white, isotropic and diffusion noise over several grids and `kT`. Without the fix 10 of these tests fail; with the old diffusion normalization 5 fail.
- `test_spatial_variance_matches_sigma` expects `sigma^2`.
- `test_sampled_noise_has_unit_std` draws 512 fields with `sigma = 1` using the real draws and checks that the std is 1, over the sphere (±0.05) and in the polar caps (±0.15), with a fixed seed. Over several seeds it measures 0.96–1.01. It catches a stray factor in the draw convention, which the exact computation would miss: with the extra ½ the std is 0.71, and with the old noise the polar caps are at about 0.7.
- The compiled cases of `test_checkpointing_keeps_the_gradients_of_latent_noise` compare with a float32 tolerance (`rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6`). Inductor reorders the arithmetic, and the new noise values moved one element just past the old `rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-7`. The differences are at most 3e-7 on gradients of about 0.25. The eager cases keep the tight tolerance.
- Locally: the serial noise, noise-controller, model-input, interpolant and rollout tests pass. The distributed noise, rollout and interpolant tests pass on 2×2 and 2×1, and noise and rollout on 1×2.

author: motoki317
body:
## Motivation

The MVP translated the player's Japanese into English and other players' English into Japanese. A player who speaks another language could not use the app, and a first-time player had to read the page's text to set it up.

## Changes

Languages:
- Each flow has a spoken language and a target language, saved in `settings.yaml`. My voice is the self flow, and Others' voices is the world flow.
- Japanese uses Haas. English keeps Parakeet v2, which had a 3.12% word error rate on 200 SpeechBSD clips, against 4.65% for v3.
- 17 other European languages use the newly pinned Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3. The world flow can also detect the language (Detect, `auto`), which also uses v3.
- Targets are PLaMo 3 Translate's 53 languages plus Easy Japanese (`ja-easy`).
- PLaMo's language list lacks Portuguese, Swedish and Detect's mixed input, so the app sends those phrases to PLaMo with the source language omitted.
- A language change shows the downloads it needs. An enabled flow starts by itself when they finish.

Chatbox:
- The chatbox message is a Go `text/template`. The default is `[{{.SourceLang}}] {{.Original}}\n[{{.TargetLang}}] {{.Translation}}`, so existing players' chatbox text gains the language codes.
- `POST /api/chatbox/preview` renders a template into the pages that VRChat receives.
- A template that fails at send time marks only its phrase, and the flow keeps running.

Storage and settings:
- `DELETE /api/downloads/{id}` deletes a download. It refuses one that is downloading or that a starting or running flow needs.
- `POST /api/open/{data|settings}` opens the data folder or `settings.yaml`.
- The app reloads `settings.yaml` after another program edits it. While the file is invalid, the app keeps its last valid settings, and a stop still works.
- A page save that arrives before the app notices such an edit returns 409 with `settings_changed`. The app reloads the file first and writes nothing, and the page applies the change again to the reloaded settings. A license acceptance reloads the file first, then adds the acceptance to it.
- `settings.yaml` stores the page language.

Errors and events:
- Flow and download errors from known causes carry a stable `code`, so the page names the player's next action in either language.
- `speech` events mark when a flow hears speech begin and end.

Page:
- On first launch, the page opens on Setup. Setup stays until a flow can run and the player presses Next. After that, the page has Translation, with each flow's switch and the conversation like a chat app, and Settings, with Languages, Microphone, Chatbox, Downloads and About. While `settings.yaml` is invalid, one screen replaces them all and offers to open the file or replace it with the settings in use.
- The page is in English and Japanese, and it shows state with Lucide icons instead of explanatory text. It has no tooltips, and it is dark whatever the OS theme.
- Settings → About shows the app's version and commit, whether a newer release exists, and links to the source code, the releases and the licenses. Below, it lists the software that the app downloads, with "Built with PLaMo" on the PLaMo row, as the PLaMo Community License requires.
- `ui_test.go` fails when `index.html` holds text outside the string catalogs, when `app.js` names a key that a catalog lacks, when the English and Japanese catalogs disagree on keys or placeholders, when a string exceeds its length budget, when an error code has no message, or when an element has a `title` attribute.

Version and update check:
- `GET /api/state` reports the build's version and commit from Go's build information.
- At each launch, the app asks GitHub once for the latest release. This is the app's only internet request that the player does not start, so the README and the network rule in AGENTS.md now name it.

## Test plan

- [x] `just lint test`, `GOOS=windows go build ./...` and `go test -race ./...`
- [x] Parakeet v3 parity: Go tokens and transcripts are identical to onnx-asr 0.12 on one FLEURS clip each in English, German, French, Spanish and Russian.
- [x] The gated PLaMo test translates ja→ja-easy and a phrase with the source omitted.
- [x] Usability: in three rounds, a new AI agent that had not seen the code drove the page against a simulated backend. Each round had the same six tasks: first launch to a running My voice, German into Easy Japanese, a translation-only chatbox message, deleting an unused download, switching the page to Japanese, and recovering after VRChat exits. The page changed after each round, and round 3 finished every task with no wrong click.
- [x] The real app ran in a private PulseAudio sandbox, with test playback programs and a UDP listener in place of VRChat. The run covered both flows, the chatbox pages against the preview, German and Detect, and recovery after the VRChat stand-in exits. It also covered delete, external `settings.yaml` edits and keyboard-only use.

## Not in this PR

- Czech, Danish, Greek, Finnish, Maltese, Romanian and Ukrainian are not spoken-language choices. PLaMo's list lacks them, and in a one-sentence check with the source omitted, PLaMo changed each sentence's meaning. Detect still transcribes them and sends them to PLaMo the same way, and the README says so.
- Errors without a code show the server's English text in both page languages. Examples are a failed open of the data folder or `settings.yaml`, an ONNX Runtime load failure, a translation failure other than `llama-server` exiting, and the refused delete of ONNX Runtime on Windows after a flow loaded it.
- When a flow's audio source fails at once, the conversation shows an "On" pill right before "Stopped by an error". The app reports `running` after the models load and before it opens the source.
- An open of the data folder or `settings.yaml` reports success once the opener starts, even if the opener then fails.
- At window widths from 520 to 528 px, in English only, the "Others' voices" label wraps onto two lines. It overlaps nothing.

body:
desk-hubd now writes `[desk] machine = true` into the hub's config in machine mode and `machine = false` on this computer, so the hub is told which one it is instead of guessing.

Hub side: driftwerk/workforce#181 (SM5, session recall). The hub refuses a session's `recall` and `recall_read` unless `machine = false` is written and nothing else marks the hub as a machine's (`agents = false`, `restore = "auto"`). This fails closed: on a machine every session looks ungrouped, so a recall there could cross clients.

**Order:** until this PR ships, a Desk on this computer gets no session recall, because the hub sees no `machine = false`. Nothing breaks either way:
- an older hub ignores the new key, since `[desk]` isn't `deny_unknown_fields`;
- a newer hub with an older Desk simply refuses recall.

Test: the config render test checks `machine` in both modes, and still checks that nothing else differs between them.

author: ot-nemoto
body:
Closes #240

## 変えたこと
- 足止めで溜めが遅れた時間を、攻撃ごとに記録するようにした（`atkLag`）。画面のための記録で、戦いの計算には使わないので、戦いの結果は変わらない
- 盤面は、攻撃してからの経過から遅れた分を引いてコマを選ぶ。足止めされた信長の三段撃ちでも、撃つ×3のコマが弾の出る時刻に合い、銃口の火花と煙が出る
- 弾や煙を撃った武将を見つける時間の幅（`bigShooterOf`）も、遅れた分だけ待つ形にした。前は、足止めされたかどうかに関わらず、一律に2倍で待っていた
- 溜めのある通常攻撃（昌幸の火計・信玄の騎馬の突撃）のコマにも同じく効く
- `docs/design.md` の「スキル」に書き足した

## 確かめたこと
- 足止めされた守りの信長で、3発を撃った時刻から遅れを引くと、溜めと撃つ間のとおりになり、実際の経過は足止めの分だけ延びている（テスト）
- `npm run typecheck`・`npm run check`・`npm test`（600件）・`npm run build` の終了コードが 0
- 盤面での目視は、ユーザーと相談して省いた（足止めされたときだけの動きで、テストで確かめているため）

author: apejean
body:
## 요약
로그인 작업이 조건 없이 프로그램을 켜던 것을 환경설정 스위치로 끌 수 있게 합니다. 1.3.10 후보입니다. 사용자 요청(11-09): "Window 시작 시 자동실행버튼을 만들어서 Window 시작 시 자동실행 on/off 할수있게 해줘"(설계에 "응 진행하고"). 기존 "로그인할 때 공연 자동 시작"은 켜진 뒤 공연을 이어 갈지만 정합니다.

## 변경
- 환경설정에 "Windows 시작 시 자동 실행"(Windows만, 기본 켜짐)을 추가합니다. 끄면 "로그인할 때 공연 자동 시작"은 잠깁니다(`startup_settings.dart`, `preferences_modal.dart`).
- 끄면 앱 데이터 폴더에 표시 파일 `windows_autostart_off`를 만들고(`launch_mode.dart`), 로그인 작업이 띄운 감시(`--logon`)가 이 파일을 보면 앱을 띄우지 않고 끝납니다(`supervisor/src/run.rs`).
- 작업은 그대로 둡니다. 작업에 사용자 계정은 읽기 권한뿐이라(이 PC의 SDDL로 확인) 앱이 작업을 끄려면 UAC가 필요하고, 재설치가 작업을 다시 등록해도 표시 파일은 남습니다.
- 바로가기 실행과 충돌 뒤 재실행은 영향이 없습니다. `HANDOFF.md`·`WINDOWS_FIELD_CHECKLIST.md`도 갱신했습니다.
- Windows에서 실패하던 `test/credits_dialog_test.dart`의 macOS 경로 확인을 macOS·리눅스 호스트에서만 하도록 고쳤습니다(3437021, #77에서 들어온 시험, 시험만 변경, macOS 앱 코드 변경 없음).

## 검증 (Windows 증거, 이 PC, `D:/dev/logs/2026-11-09/`)
- T211: 시험을 먼저 써서 실패 확인(끈 상태에서 `--logon`이 앱을 띄움) → 구현 뒤 통과. supervisor 23개 통과, clippy 경고 없음, `flutter analyze` 0건, `flutter test` 240 전부 통과.
- T213: 로컬 release 빌드(Flutter 3.44.2)와 실제 앱 데이터 폴더로 확인, 소리 없음.
  - Off 저장 → 표시 파일 생성 → 감시 `--logon`이 종료 코드 0으로 끝나고 앱이 안 켜짐, 감시 기록 한 줄.
  - Off에서 바로가기 경로 → 앱 켜짐, Off 유지, 공연 자동 시작 잠김.
  - On 저장 → 표시 파일 삭제 → `--logon`이 앱을 `--supervised --logon`으로 띄움.
  - 시험 뒤 `shared_preferences.json`은 그대로, `config.json`은 저장으로 키 순서만 바뀜(내용 동일). 표시 파일 없음(켜짐 상태). 백업 `D:/dev/backups/20261109-141132-before-autostart-toggle-test`.
- **안 한 것:** 실제 로그아웃·로그인. 로그인 작업이 설치본 1.3.9 감시를 부르기 때문에 새 설치본이 있어야 합니다. 1.3.10 설치 뒤 확인합니다. 로컬 빌드는 Flutter 3.44.2이고 CI는 3.47.9입니다. CI 결과는 PR 체크로 확인합니다.

## macOS 영향
없음(스위치는 Windows에서만 보이고, `APPDATA`가 없으면 감시는 지금과 같음). Mac 세션 확인 요청 없음.

- CI 통과 확인 → 병합 → 버전 1.3.10 → 태그 v1.3.10 → 릴리스 빌드 확인(사용자 승인됨: "응 둘 다 진행해")

Proposes a warning of impending remote operation on board (SARUMS BPG Appendix A3.24), and holds a start until it has run. The design, the alternatives and the open questions are in #427.

Stacked on #332, because `SafetyState` exists only there.

**Draft on purpose.** The experimental channel takes every non-draft PR, and this should not reach a build before the shape is agreed.

## What changes

- `EMERGENCY_COMMAND_START_WARNING`, and two refusal outcomes.
- `StartWarning start_warning = 13` on `SafetyState`.
- `protocols/emergency_request.yaml`: the `ACTUATION_ALLOWED` term for a start, the actions, a flow, invariants, and the device named as deployment.

## Testing

`test_safety_state.py` pins the wire numbers, the states, the round trip, and the protocol's hold and expiry wording. 9 protocol mutants were killed, and `test_protocols.py` validates the new actions and flow. Nothing implements this yet: no supervisor, gate or station change is included.

Closes #427

body:
Amount is unsigned (u128), so `is_negative()` always returned `false` and `non_negative_checked()` / `negative_checked()` were vestigial.

- Removes `Amount::is_negative`, `non_negative_checked`, `negative_checked`.
- Drops the dead negative checks in engine (mint/recall), engine_types validation, walletd handlers, wallet crypto/sdk/storage, and the nft_faucet template.
- Removes the now-unreachable `NegativeAmount` error variants in wallet crypto/sdk.
- `partial_ord_impl!` compares against zero so it still serves the signed `PrecisionAmount`.
- Fixes stale doc comments referring to i64/negative results.

`is_positive()` is unchanged (false for zero). `PrecisionAmount` (signed) is untouched.

**Breaking:** public API of `tari_template_lib_types` (`Amount` methods) and of `tari_ootle_wallet_crypto` / `tari_ootle_wallet_sdk` error enums (`NegativeAmount` variants). Callers drop the calls; `is_negative()` was always `false`. Version bumps follow `crate_versioning.py impact tari_template_lib_types --breaking` at release.

## Summary

The post-merge publish run [42586005787](https://github.com/schubergphilis/claude-docker/actions/runs/42586005787) failed in CD, not CI: the publish pipeline (docker.yml -> mcvs-docker-action) runs dockle with `--exit-level warn --exit-code 1`, and DKL-DI-0003 ("Avoid apt-get dist-upgrade") fired on the main apt RUN. PR CI never runs dockle, so #259's green pipeline could not see this.

Root cause: dockle's `checkAptCommand` fires when a RUN's whitespace-split tokens contain any 2 of {apt-get, apt, dist-upgrade} (`containsThreshold`, exact token match). #259 names the `apt` package in the install list for CVE-2026-109518, so the tokens `apt-get` + `apt` met the threshold — a false positive with no `dist-upgrade` present.

Fix: spell it `'apt=*'`, which selects the same candidate version (3.2.1ubuntu0.1, the CVE fix) but whose token is never the bare `apt`. Verified by replaying dockle's `splitByCommands` + `containsThreshold` over all 16 RUN instructions in the Dockerfile: 0 fire (the old form fires, as expected). DKL-DI-0003 stays active for real dist-upgrade uses; no .dockleignore entry added.

## OpenSpec

- No spec change. Checked: `image-vulnerability-scan` (the CVE-2026-109518 layer-rebuild intent is unchanged — the RUN still names the packages, so the gha-cached layer still rebuilds and pulls 3.2.1ubuntu0.1), `image-distribution` (publish scan policy unchanged).

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` — 193 OK
- [x] `bats tests/bats` — 488 OK
- [x] dockle DKL-DI-0003 replayed over all RUN instructions (dockle source logic) — 0 fire
- [x] CI on this PR — all 9 checks pass (PR CI does not run dockle; the post-merge publish run will exercise it, see #261)

Refs #261 (the systemic CI/CD parity gap this PR's failure exposed).

### Summary

Closes #1430.

Under Watchdog 7.0.0's `full_match()` semantics (#1101), patterns like `*.json` or `logs/*.log` failed because event paths are absolute.

- **Relative matching**: `PatternMatchingEventHandler` now also evaluates event paths relative to the watched root directory using `PurePath.relative_to()`.
- **Standard glob semantics**: Non-recursive patterns (`*.json`) match top-level files without matching nested ones, while `**/*.json` and absolute paths continue to work as before.
- **Tests**: Extended `tests/test_patterns.py` to cover both relative and absolute path matching.

## Summary
Welle 9, Paket S21 (HOCH, Spec `restluecken-welle9.md`): Bisher prüfte nur der `LifecycleController` die Rollen der Workflow-YAML; jeder Fach-Controller, REST, MCP, Job oder Vorschlag, der `LifecycleService::transition()` direkt rief, hatte nur seine eigene `#[IsGranted]`. Beispiel: ROLE_USER konnte einen Auditbericht einreichen (YAML: ROLE_AUDITOR), ein Auditor ablehnen und ein Manager abschließen (YAML: ROLE_CISO).

- **`App\Lifecycle\TransitionAccess`** (neu), gerufen in `transition()` vor `apply()`: handelnde Person = Vier-Augen-Approver, sonst übergebener User, sonst angemeldeter User; Prüfung über `Security::isGrantedForUser()` gegen den `LifecycleVoter` (effektive Rollen inkl. Override, Rollenhierarchie, `responsible`). Wirft `TransitionAccessDeniedException` (AccessDeniedException → 403; Message = Übersetzungsschlüssel `lifecycle.errors.role_required`, damit gefangene RuntimeExceptions als lesbarer Flash erscheinen).
- Nicht geprüft: `automatic: true` (Listener, Cron, Zielwert erreicht), `approverAuthorityVerified: true` (Freigabekette-Schritt, Risikoakzeptanz-Stufe, freigegebene Akzeptanzkriterien, Re-Evaluierung), Transitionen ohne Rollen (dienstintern), keine Person.
- **`LifecycleVoter`** entscheidet Rollen/RECORD_RESPONSIBLE über den AccessDecisionManager auf dem gevoteten Token (sonst würde `isGrantedForUser` den angemeldeten User prüfen).
- **Interne Audits:** Berichtsschritte mit `#[IsGranted('lifecycle.internal_audit_lifecycle.<t>')]`; `reportedBy/At`, `approvedBy/At`, `closedBy/At`, Ablehnungsgrund stempelt der `LifecycleEvidenceStamper` erst nach erfolgreichem Schritt (vorher wurde vor der Transition geflusht). Anlegen/Kopieren ROLE_MANAGER, Bearbeiten Manager oder Leitender Auditor; REST/MCP `InternalAudit` → ROLE_MANAGER (`ApiTenantVoter::WRITE_ROLES`). Buttons auf der Audit-Seite und Befehlspalette folgen denselben Attributen.
- **DSR / Datenpanne:** `responsible: true` an den Schritten, die der Controller per `MANAGER_OR_RESPONSIBLE` für die zuständige Person öffnet (Fristen-Erinnerung bleibt erreichbar).
- `ISMSObjectiveService` (Ziel erreicht) `automatic: true`; `RiskAcceptanceWorkflowService` / `WorkflowService::rejectStep` `approverAuthorityVerified: true` mit Begründung.

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix / Security hardening (Verhalten wird strenger)

## How tested
- Neuer Dauertest `tests/Lifecycle/LifecycleServiceRoleContractTest` (findet jede Workflow-YAML selbst; >100 rollengeschützte Transitionen: ROLE_USER abgewiesen, Status unverändert; Rolleninhaber passiert die Rollenprüfung; automatic nicht geprüft). Mutation geprüft: `TransitionAccess` früh verlassen → Test rot.
- `TransitionAccessTest` (Approver vor User, Fallback auf angemeldeten User, Ausnahmen), `LifecycleEvidenceStamperTest` (Audit-Stempel), `InternalAuditApprovalWorkflowTest` (+ ROLE_USER einreichen 403 ohne Stempel, Manager abschließen 403, Auditor ablehnen 403), `AuditControllerTest` (Anlegen = Manager), `ApiWriteRoleParityTest`.
- Volle Suite lokal (PHP 8.5 + Postgres): alle roten Klassen auch auf main rot (Umgebung: MariaDB-SQL, Netz), keine neue Abweichung. Alle Python-Gates, `lint:container`, `lint:twig`, php-cs-fixer grün.

## Compliance / Security checklist
- [x] Rollen kommen aus der Workflow-YAML + Override (ISO 27001 5.3 Aufgabentrennung, 9.2.2 Audit-Unabhängigkeit)
- [x] Leitungsaktionen weiter nur mit explizitem ROLE_TOP_MGMT
- [x] Nachweise schreibt der Schritt (S12-Linie)
- [x] Operator-Hinweis in `UPGRADE.md` (Geändertes Verhalten), Doku `docs/user-guide/STATUS_LIFECYCLE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`

author: mchenziyi
body:
Retro follow-ups from #18（不关闭任何票；#19 的正文已追加它要接手的部分）。

## Summary

#18 两轮两轴 review 一共抓到 9 处「文档 vs 代码」漂移，全靠 reviewer 的注意力；其中两类是可机械判定的，现在变成检查。

```diff
 test/
+├── docs-contract.mjs   # 新增：契约 op 列表 / host 模块引用 / 已删 surface ↔ 代码
 ├── isolation.mjs       # + 每个顶层 test/*.mjs 必须被 package.json script 接线
 ├── modules.mjs
 └── host-contract.mjs
```

**`test/docs-contract.mjs`** 三条规则：

1. `docs/CONTRACT.md` §3 的 op 枚举 **逐项等于** `TASK_OPS`。
2. `CONTRACT` / `GLOSSARY` / `AGENTS` / `README` 里出现的 `host/<module>.js` 必须存在，**除非同一行标了「删除 / 历史 / deprecated」**（ADR 与历史段可以合法点名死文件）。
3. `executions` / `executionId` / `executionState` / `executorLost` / `conflicts` / `resolveConflict` 在契约里只能出现在历史行或 deprecated 记录块内。

**其余四条**：`test/isolation.mjs` 增加「顶层 harness 必须接线」（存在但没跑的检查等于不存在）；`AGENTS.md` 写明 `/code-review` 只对已提交 HEAD 跑；`CODING_STANDARDS.md` 把两条门禁时代的缺陷形状收窄到现存校验（claim CAS / executionApproval / complete/defer/archive）；spec 的「每张票的通用验收」加第 6 条：判据必须开工时就能跑。

## Evidence

- **Before:** 把新检查拿到 `aab88ae`（#18 之前）的干净导出上：

  ```text
  AssertionError: docs/CONTRACT.md §3 and TASK_OPS disagree
    doc-only: assign, dispatch, resolveConflict
  ```

  **After:** 在 `13b7e52`（#18 合并内容）与当前 HEAD 上：

  ```text
  docs contract ok
  ```

- 接线检查会红：加 `test/docs-contract.mjs` 但没写进 `package.json` 时：

  ```text
  test/docs-contract.mjs is not referenced by any package.json script
  ```

- `npm test` 全绿（isolation / modules / docs-contract / host-contract / host / tasks / client）；`npm run test:e2e` → `ALL 2 SCENARIO(S) PASSED`。
- 交给 #19 的两件后续已写进票面：把 #18 的 grep 判据兑现成可执行形式；`docs/implementation-status.md` 重写后把 `docs-contract.mjs` 的引用检查扩到它（它现在仍列着 6 个已删模块）。

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way —— 纯检查与文档；revert 即回到只有 `npm test` 的四套件。

**Blast radius:** 开发流程。用户可见行为无变化；唯一风险是新 docs 检查过严，后续改 CONTRACT 时必须同一 commit 同步 op 列表——这正是它存在的理由。

author: zzave
body:
Members and Admins can link an unmatched incoming payment to a member from the money pool. Part of #10. Uses the claim endpoint from #503; the alias editor is #511.

## Change

- **"That's mine"** (member) and **"Assign to…"** (Admin, with a member picker) on incoming payments without a member. Under act-as only the Admin variant shows.
- **Sheet** with the payment's name and "the IBAN of this payment", both on by default. The IBAN stays on the server. "On" is sent as the server default, so a payment with a blank or very long name still stores its IBAN (ADR-0046).
- **After a claim:** the pool and the member's aliases reload, a toast shows the alias, and focus moves to the payment row (visible focus ring).
- **Errors:** already linked (the pool reloads), name or IBAN taken, pool unavailable, invalid. Confirm explains why it is disabled. Cancel clears an error and is locked while saving.
- `Switch` accepts `aria-describedby`.

## Tests

- Vitest: `claimVariant` (member, admin, act-as, not claimable), `claimBody` (4 switch combinations), `failure` error mapping (6 cases).
- Stories: `ClaimPaymentView` (Data; Shells with admin picker, saving lock and each error; Interactions with `fn()` spies: member unticks IBAN → `onClaim({ userId: 'u-me', useName: true, useIban: false })`, admin picks a member → `onClaim({ userId: 'u-tom', … })`, focus on the row, Cancel clears the error, switches reset). `MoneyPoolView` Data asserts the control on unmatched incoming rows only.
- `tsc -b`, eslint and `make test-app` (1009 tests) green; pre-commit `make yolo test` passed.

PR gate: no new e2e. The claim is a tenant write by a team member through the existing auth path; `PaymentAliasControllerIT` and `MoneyPoolControllerIT` cover the endpoint against real Postgres.

Batch B of the CI wall-clock tuning (D-303): split the migration monolith.

- `LedgerDatabaseMigrationTest` (48 @Test methods, 251.5 class-seconds, the single heaviest class and therefore the shard wall-clock floor) is split into `LedgerMigrationV1ToV11Test` (12), `LedgerMigrationV11ToV19Test` (21) and `LedgerMigrationV20ToV36Test` (15). The two shared seeding helpers move into an abstract `MigrationTestSupport`; the file-level helpers (query/DDL readers, guard SQL, `VERSION_ONE_STATEMENTS`) move to the same support file as top-level `internal` declarations.
- The split is mechanical: a script cut the original class at member boundaries and re-assembled the files, and verified that the concatenated test text is byte-identical to the original (184082 bytes). No assertion, test name or fixture was edited.
- New `tests/python/test_migration_split_inventory.py` is the test-count guard D-195's residual asked for: the 48 test names must appear exactly once across the three classes, the 12/21/15 split is asserted, the original class must stay deleted, and all three classes must be registered in the shard manifest. Registered in python shard 1.
- Manifest repacked: 116 to 118 classes, five shards, the three new classes carrying a third of the old class's measured time until the next measured repack.
- D-303 gets the batch B landing record; the tuning spec records the split and the guard; the ci.yml class-count comment follows.

Verification: the inventory guard and the four CI-focused Python modules pass locally; project_docs clean; Python shard coverage 56/56; manifest 118 unique classes across ids 1..5. Kotlin compilation and the 48 tests themselves are CI-owned.

Task: EPC-029

## Summary

This records-only planning PR files TSK-1404 and amends TSK-1381, both in EPC-029, the guard parity epic. Both come from the cross-lineage review of TSK-326 (PR 718, Grok delta 6). That review found two things. When the guards cannot fill a command's program word, they do not refuse it in every case. And git-guard's command-builder name check peels fewer scheduling wrappers than exec-guard's deletion reader. Nothing open covered either.

- TSK-1404 makes both guards refuse a program word they cannot fill, and makes the deletion check report it as unproven.
- TSK-1381 AC-12 tracks the wrapper difference. Exec-guard's deletion floor still refuses such a builder, so this closes a coverage difference; it is not a bypass.
- Records only. Each build is a separate pull request with its own security review.

## Changes

| Record | Change |
|---|---|
| TSK-1404 (EPC-029), new, depends on TSK-326 | AC-1: both guards refuse an unfilled program word of each kind, whatever the evidence of git, naming the remedy "spell the program literally". AC-2: the deletion check reports it as unproven. AC-3: a literal assignment on the same line still passes. AC-4: an over-refusal count over this repository's scripts, docs code blocks and test corpus. AC-5: a sweep of other failed-fill early returns. AC-6: policy reference. AC-7: security review. |
| TSK-1381 (EPC-029), amended | AC-12: git-guard's command-builder name check peels each scheduling wrapper the deletion reader peels and it does not, with a fail-before test per wrapper; multi-call binaries stay with AC-11. One amendment line in the Execution contract. |

author: scylladbbot
body:
`run_repair_manager()` stops a repair task only when it reaches a non-DONE final status.

When the task is still running after the timeout,
the `wait_and_get_final_status()` raises `WaitForTimeoutError` and the stop gets skipped.

The task then keeps running for the rest of the test.

Later Manager repairs fail with `another task is running`,
and with tablets the busy topology blocks load-and-stream, so a later `nodetool refresh` hangs forever.

Fix it by stopping the task on the timeout
and re-raise the timeout error, also when the stop itself fails.

Also drop the `timeout is 24 hours` comment, the default timeout is 3 hours.

Google names 3.8 Flash-Lite as the replacement. - Flash-Lite keeps the same 30 voices and the same Interactions schema, and supports all 18 explicit app languages. - The app sends only single-speaker plain text, which 3.8 reads verbatim. - The request now declares `audio/l16`. - Saved 3.1 selections resolve to the replacement, and history keeps the retired price. - Cost estimates use the 2027 list price: $0.0003 per second of audio and $1 per million input tokens. - Sources: aistudio.google.com/docs/speech-generation.md, `models/gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts.md`, and the Gemini pricing page. **Soniox: adopt `stt-rt-v6` / `stt-async-v6`** - docs.soniox.com/stt/models (changelog dated 3 November 2026) says v6 is fully compatible with v5; only the model name changes. - v5 is removed on 2026-12-15, after which Soniox routes v5 requests to v6 automatically. The saved-selection migration (v3/v4/v5 → v6) therefore matches the provider's own behaviour. - Pricing is unchanged: $0.10/hr async and $0.12/hr realtime. v5 pricing is kept for history. - Custom IDs are preserved. - v6 changes formatting: - spoken commands such as "period" are written as words; - prices are written as spoken; - hyphens in codes appear only when spoken. - The app does not apply spoken dictation commands, so it does not rely on the old formatting. author: sotream
body:
Root cause of the flaky `enforces the overall grace deadline` test seen on CI (`events` was `['never-runs']` instead of `[]`).

**Cause.** In `Lifecycle.run` every hook was raced against `withTimeout(remaining)`, and the overall deadline was a separate `setTimeout(graceMs)`. With the test's 150 ms grace the hook timer (about 140 ms) and the deadline timer fire within a millisecond of each other. When the hook timer won, the loop caught the timeout, saw `deadline.signal.aborted === false` and started the next hook after the deadline. This is a real shutdown bug, not only a test problem: a hook could start after the grace period had run out.

**Fix.** Race each hook against the deadline signal itself (`Promise.race([hook, deadlineHit])`), so a timed-out hook always means the deadline has fired and the loop breaks.

**Evidence** (local M4):
- Reproduction on the old code, 300 shutdowns with 30 ms grace and a hanging hook followed by a late one: the late hook ran in 46, 36 and 35 of 300.
- Same probe after the fix: 0, 0, 0 of 300.
- New regression test (50 shutdowns per run): fails on the old code in 5 of 5 runs, passes on the new code in 100 of 100 runs of the whole `lifecycle.test.ts`.

author: alies-dev
body:
When a generator declared as `iterable`, `Iterator` or `Traversable` returns a value, Psalm reports a misleading `InvalidReturnStatement`. That value can only be read through `Generator::getReturn()`, which the declared type doesn't expose, so Psalm now reports the new `HiddenGeneratorReturn` issue (error level 4). For a `Generator<TKey, TValue, TSend, TReturn>` return type, the returned value is checked against `TReturn`.

**Before**
```php
<?php
/** @return iterable<int, string> */
function a(): iterable {
    yield "a";
    return 1; // InvalidReturnStatement
}
```

**After**
```php
    return 1; // HiddenGeneratorReturn
```

Fixes #11458

author: hwangtab
body:
## 배경
타임뱅크 점검(2026-11-09)에서 찾은 헛점 세 가지를 고친다. 원장·판정 로직은 건드리지 않는다.

## 바뀐 것
1. **이용규칙 판 변경 가드** — `PUT /api/admin/timebank/settings`가 `terms_version`을 바꿀 때 그 판의 본문(`TIMEBANK_TERMS`)이 없으면 400. 본문 없는 판으로 바뀌면 모든 참여자가 구판 동의가 되어 쓰기가 막히고, 동의 화면은 본문이 없어 단추를 숨기므로 아무도 다시 동의할 수 없었다(전원 잠금). `planTimebankSettingsChange`에 `termsExists` 주입점을 두어 테스트가 가상 판을 쓸 수 있게 했다.
2. **거절·취소 사유** — `POST /api/timebank/transfers/[id]/reject|cancel`이 본문 `{ memo? }`(선택, 500자)를 받는다. 사유는 행 memo 끝에 `거절 사유: …`/`취소 사유: …`로 붙고(원 memo는 지우지 않음, 관리자 취소와 같은 꼴), 다른 당사자의 알림 문구에 `사유: …`로 실린다. 대기 화면은 `window.prompt`로 사유를 받는다 — 비우면 사유 없이 진행, 취소하면 중단. 본문 없이 호출해도 그대로 된다(기존 E2E 호환).
3. **주석 정정** — 정지 회원은 `requireActiveMember`가 먼저 막아 거절·취소도 403인데 "정지도 거절할 수 있다"고 적힌 주석을 실제 동작대로 고쳤다. 동작 변경 없음.

## 검증
- 타임뱅크 단위 테스트 139건 통과(새 테스트: 판 본문 검사, 사유 memo 병합, 파서, 알림 문구)

- `lint:fix` · `format` · `type-check` · `build` 통과

## 남긴 것(이 PR 밖)
- 제19조 보존·폐기 절차(재가입 키 3년, 원장 5년)를 `scripts/turso/README.md`에 적는 일 — 문서 작업이라 따로 한다.

author: khaledsabae
body:
## «أسئلة يسألها الآباء والأمهات» + ترويسات الأمان

البندين ١ و٢ من الترتيب المعتمد.

### الأسئلة الشائعة (صفحة الهبوط بالعربي والإنجليزي)
ست أسئلة الأهل بيسألوها قبل ما ينزّلوا التطبيق:
- هل التطبيق مجاني؟
- منين بتيجي الإجابات؟
- هل بيغني عن الطبيب؟
- إيه البيانات اللي بتتعرف عن أطفالي، وأقدر أحذفها إزاي؟
- لأي سن، وبأي لغة؟
- بيشتغل على أنهي موبايل؟

كل إجابة بتقول بس اللي صفحة تانية بتثبته (المنهجية، أو سياسة الخصوصية، أو صفحة حذف الحساب)، ومعاها رابط للصفحة دي. الأسئلة معمولة بـ`<details>` عادي: من غير سكريبت، ومن غير أي تحميل من موقع خارجي. وملتزمة بقواعد النص اللي التستات بتفرضها: لا ادعاء إشراف أو اعتماد، ولا ذكر iOS، ولا كلمة «ألعاب»، وفصحى سهلة.

اتشافت في المتصفح على مقاس موبايل، عربي وإنجليزي.

### ترويسات الأمان
`tg-api.alsaba.cloud` كان بيرد من غير أي ترويسة أمان. الـmiddleware الجديد:
- **مكتوب ASGI صِرف**، عشان ستريم إجابات المساعد (SSE) يعدّي زي ما هو من غير ما يتلمس.
- **في أبعد طبقة**، فحتى ردود 401 و429 بتاخد الترويسات.
- **الترويسات:**
  - `nosniff` و`SAMEORIGIN` و`strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
  - HSTS لمدة سنة، على الـhost ده بس.
  - `Permissions-Policy` بيمنع الكاميرا والمايك والموقع والدفع.
  - CSP أساسي: `frame-ancestors` و`base-uri` و`object-src` و`form-action`.
- القيم هي نفس اللي nginx بيبعتها لـ`/seo` و`/methodology`.
- لو أي route حاطط ترويسة بنفسه، ترويسته هي اللي بتفضل.
- CSP يقيّد السكريبتات (`script-src`) محتاج nonces في كل الصفحات اللي فيها سكريبت inline، فده هيتعمل في تغيير لوحده.

### التحقق
- pre-commit عدّى كله، والسكراب طلع 0.
- pytest: 229 تست نجحوا، صفر فشل. التستات: ترويسات الأمان، وصفحة الهبوط، والإسناد، واللغة، وصدق سياسة الخصوصية، وclient_ip، وموثوقية الإجابات (فيها الستريم).

body:
New players currently receive only a four-step Home tour. This adds a complete optional introduction from AI connection to a prepared campaign and first scene, alongside independently accessible tutorials for the rest of Sylvia.

Sylvia speaks as a warm, playful guide who is excited to play with the user. Fifteen context-specific poses are extracted from all four approved transparent sheets. The complete originals, original filenames and hashes are retained, with reproducible masking that preserves irregular silhouettes and each pose's own effects.

### What changes

- Nine main lessons cover Home, AI connections, Ready campaigns, GM play, SRD Lite combat, campaign customization, Builder, workspace layout, and campaign management. ChatGPT subscription, API and local-server setup have their own direct guides.
- Home, the session header, Settings and contextual invitations reach the same lesson runner. First-run welcome offers guided play, connection help or independent exploration. Existing configured defaults skip setup.
- Back, Pause, Skip, Resume and Replay use local UI preferences. Legacy completed/skipped Home preferences survive; resumed setup returns to its exact branch. The Interview guide follows the actual active questions, including No Ruleset paths.
- Tutorials observe actual control interactions and selected-session results. They never authenticate, submit messages, create campaigns, execute mechanics, or spend resources themselves.
- Responsive guides and their expressions were inspected at desktop, 420px and 320px widths across the three themes. Attract mode and no-AI battles remain deferred.

### Validation

- 63 focused JavaScript/browser checks passed for the tutorial suite, Ready campaigns, shell, queued actions and game controls. After final copy/layout refinements, all 16 tutorial checks and the shell check passed again.
- 34 model/settings browser checks and both starter-character browser widths passed.
- 82 canonical frontend Python checks; 75 packaging/runner/selection checks; 46 final artwork/selection checks; nine actual Lite starter, No Ruleset and Builder-copy checks passed. Packaging tests admitted the new explicit asset inventory.
- Sprite extraction completed and all four originals and fifteen runtime crops match the recorded hashes. New/changed extraction and selection files pass Ruff; documentation-index and diff checks pass.

### Limits

- `tests/frontend_campaign_plan_browser.browser.cjs` has an unchanged baseline count mismatch: expected 19, actual 20. Its test, catalogue, widget and stylesheet are identical to main; no unrelated fix is included.
- Seven existing E501 line-length findings remain outside the edited frontend-contract test section; other checks on that file pass.
- Browser tests use synthetic owner/provider projections. No installed-app, native-input or genuine-account/provider acceptance is claimed. No installer or release was produced.

Subscription terminology was checked against [official OpenAI guidance](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart); the guide follows Sylvia's existing Codex-managed connection controls.

author: girlbossrush
body:
This rounds geometry coordinates to six decimal places in 32,880 of whosonfirst-data-admin-np's 80,727 GeoJSON files, and rewrites each changed record's `wof:geomhash` to match.

**Why.** Many coordinates carry more digits than the source data has. Some are six-place values printed with extra digits by an older exporter: `-90.18399100000001` and `-90.183991` are the same IEEE 754 double, so for those values the geometry is unchanged. Others carry 13 or 14 decimal places, a resolution of about 10 nanometers.

**Fidelity.** Rounding moves a coordinate by at most 0.0000005 degrees: at most 0.056 m north–south, and at most 0.079 m for a vertex moving on both axes at the equator.

**What is left as it is.** Every property, including `geom:area`, `geom:latitude`, `lbl:*`, `geom:bbox` and `wof:lastmodified`; records where rounding would make two neighboring vertices of a ring equal, so no ring loses a vertex; and superseded records, which are addressed separately.

**Hash.** `wof:geomhash` is recomputed as the MD5 of the geometry's compact JSON with `coordinates` before `type`, which matches the stored hash for 554 of 599 records sampled across the GB, US and FR admin repositories.

Only the geometry line and the `wof:geomhash` line of each changed file differ.

author: jm-opaas
body:
## What this is

One chat everywhere. The Copilot page, the dock, the My Work chat widget and the agent's new **Live** tab all render the same `Conversation`. The goal: you can work fully inside oc8's chat and don't need a separate ChatGPT.

This PR contains the whole oc8 Chat project, parts C1–C4 plus the core extension points for C5. The C5 features themselves (web search, canvas, data analysis, chat search, sharing, dictation, prompt templates) ship separately in `oc8-enterprise`.

### C1: one conversation
- Streaming over the realtime socket. No polling.
- Reasoning collapses into "Thinking…". Tool calls show as a compact step list with inline previews.
- Safe markdown: links, code highlighting, and click-to-load for external images. No external favicons are loaded.
- Model picker per chat, available before the first message. Admins choose which models are offered with the new **Models → "Available in chat"** switch, which applies org-wide.
- Regenerate with paging between variants, edit and resend, feedback, copy.

### C2: questions, decisions, suggestions
- `ask_user` can ask up to six structured questions (single choice, multiple choice, or free text). They appear as a "1 of N" card above the composer.
- The answer is stored as a turn of its own, so it survives a reload. The chat, messenger, inbox and admin doors can all answer.
- Decision approvals render inline in the chat.
- The new `suggest_replies` tool adds reply chips. Empty chats show prompt starters.

### C3: context
- Pin knowledge bases, data sources, single source files, attachments and oc8 objects to a chat. oc8 objects are agents, departments, runs, approvals, responsibilities and your own chats.
- **Projects** carry instructions and pins for a group of chats. Pinned chats and a date-grouped sidebar.
- `#` searches across every kind. A data-source file browser lets you pin a single file.
- "Discuss with Copilot" appears on agents, approvals, knowledge bases and responsibilities. "Continue" appears on finished runs.
- Every pin is re-authorised under the member's own rights when it is pinned and again when the agent reads it.
- Pinned content reaches the model fenced with a per-call nonce. Restricted or local-only content never goes to a cloud model.

### C4: Live
- Each agent gets a **Live** tab: its runs appear as chat turns.
- You can write to a running run ("steering") and stop it.
- What you see depends on whose run it is:
  - your own runs, and autonomous runs of agents you can reach: shown in full;
  - colleagues' runs, when "All runs" is on: redacted to labels and state.

### C5 core: extension points only
- Capabilities `enterprise.web_search|canvas|data_analysis|chat_search|chat_sharing|dictation|prompt_templates`.
- An `EditionTool` contract:
  - capability-gated;
  - offered per run and door;
  - checked again at call time;
  - audited;
  - its output is fenced and bounded through `ChatMessage.parts`.
- A read-only chat port with an extra-readers hook. Readers are strictly read-only and get a single redacted view.
- Frontend chat slots (`composerActions`, `messageParts`, `sidePanels`, …), capability-gated and wrapped in error boundaries.
- Community behaviour is unchanged.

### Removed
`ChatWindow`, `CopilotChatTab`, the run-activity strip and `ChatSessionPicker`. They are replaced by `Conversation` and `SessionPicker`.

## Migrations (additive): 0111, 0112, 0113

`0111_chat_c1`, `0112_chat_live`, `0113_chat_context`. They follow dev's `0110_trigger_access_fingerprint`: the first one has `down_revision="0110"`. Single head 0113. They were renumbered from 0107–0109 after dev took 0107–0110 for the connections work (#76/#80/#81). Tested: the migration chain test, a fresh upgrade to head, then a downgrade to 0110 and an upgrade back to head.

**Before rolling back**, stop runs that have unconsumed inputs.

Production runbook (lock behaviour, worker drain, rollback, renumbering against #71/#40): see "Production migration notes" below.

<details><summary>Production migration notes</summary>

# Production migration notes: 0111 → 0112 → 0113 (oc8 Chat)

Renumbered on 2026-11-09 from 0107/0108/0109 after dev took 0107–0110 for
the connections work (#76/#80/#81). The chain is now
`0110_trigger_access_fingerprint` → 0111 → 0112 → 0113.

## Order and transactions

- `alembic upgrade head` applies 0111, 0112 and 0113 in order. The env uses one
  transaction for the whole upgrade, but 0111 and 0112 each commit it midway:
  their large indexes are built `CONCURRENTLY` inside `autocommit_block()`.
  So the locks the early ALTERs take are released before each index build, not
  held until 0113 finishes.
- Every migration starts with `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'`. A DDL that can't
  get its lock within 5 seconds fails the deploy, and the app doesn't queue
  behind it. The fix is to retry, ideally after draining the workers (below).
- The Helm backend init container runs `alembic upgrade head` on pod start,
  while the old workers may still be running runs. An in-process run keeps one
  transaction open for the whole run, which is why these precautions exist.

## What each step locks

| Migration | Statement | Lock | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0111 | 4 × nullable `ADD COLUMN` on `chat_session` / `chat_message` | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, 5 s timeout | metadata only |
| 0111 | `model_config.chat_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, 5 s timeout | metadata only (PG ≥ 11) |
| 0111 | `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix_chat_message_reply_to_id` | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE (writes continue) | full scan, waits for older transactions |
| 0112 | `chat_session.kind text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'chat'` | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, 5 s timeout | metadata only |
| 0112 | `ck_chat_session_kind` CHECK, added `NOT VALID` | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, 5 s timeout | instant |
| 0112 | `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT ck_chat_session_kind` (own transaction) | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE | scan of `chat_session` |
| 0112 | `uq_chat_session_live` partial unique index | SHARE on `chat_session` | scan of `chat_session` (small) |
| 0112 | `CREATE TABLE run_input` | — | instant |
| 0112 | `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix_agent_run_agent_created` | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE (run writes continue) | full scan of `agent_run`, waits for older transactions |
| 0113 | 3 × `ADD COLUMN` on `chat_session` | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, 5 s timeout | metadata only |
| 0113 | `ix_chat_session_project_id`, `CREATE TABLE chat_project` | SHARE / — | small |

A `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` waits until every transaction older than it has
finished, including a long in-process run. It blocks nobody while it waits, but
the deploy waits with it. If an earlier attempt left an INVALID index, the
migration drops that index (`DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`) and builds it again
instead of keeping it.

Check table sizes first:

```sql
SELECT relname, n_live_tup, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid))
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
WHERE relname IN ('agent_run','chat_message','chat_session','model_config');
```

## Runbook

1. **Drain the workers.** Scale the worker deployment to 0 and wait until no run
   is `running`:
   `SELECT count(*) FROM agent_run WHERE state = 'running';`
   You can skip this, but then an upgrade may hit the 5 s lock timeout and need
   a retry, and the concurrent index builds wait for the longest open run.
2. Optional, for very large tenants: create the two indexes yourself first,
   outside alembic:
   `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS ix_agent_run_agent_created ON agent_run (agent_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);`
   `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS ix_chat_message_reply_to_id ON chat_message (reply_to_id);`
   Then confirm `indisvalid` is true for both in `pg_index`. The migrations
   then skip both builds.
3. Deploy. The init container runs `alembic upgrade head`. If it fails with
   `lock timeout`, retry once the blocking transaction has ended.
4. Scale the workers back up.
5. Check: `alembic current` shows `0113`, and both indexes are valid.

## Roll

body:
Account erasure, stage A, PR 1 of 2: the store contract's additions and the memory store's implementation of them. Everything is optional. No feature uses it yet; C onward will. The Redis implementation is PR 2.

Plan: `docs/work/release/0.20-erasure-stage-a.md` (2nd draft, read by auth-ca and Fable), on `docs/stage5/plans/account-erasure.md` §2.2, §3.3, §3.6 as folded on 2026-11-09.

## Commits (one module each: `store`, `store`, then the generated card list)

1. **store: the upkeep contracts, a declaration's erasure fields, reads of several keys and a batch's time**
   - New internal module `upkeep` with its own card. It holds the `storeControl` contract (a read of the control record) and the `storeUpkeep` contract: `mark`, `require`, `enterMaintenance`, `leaveMaintenance`, the ledger's `kept` and `retire`, `honours`, `sweep`. It also holds the shared contract test `upkeepContract`, exported through `./testing`.
   - `checkedUpkeep` checks upkeep input the way `checkedStore` checks store input. `require` refuses an empty set.
   - `Space` gains four optional fields: `subjectData`, `erasedBy`, `boundedMs` and `requiredOnceErasing`. They are erasure's vocabulary, carried on store's type. `checkedStore` checks only their shape, when the store is built. Store reads `subjectData` only as `none` or not, through `noSubjectData`.
   - `Store.getMany?` reads several keys, at one store time on a single-server store. `Committed.at?` is the store time a batch committed at; a resend gets the first commit's time. The memory store offers both, and the simulated store routes `getMany` to a confirmed read when any of its spaces confirms reads.
2. **store: the memory store offers its upkeep**
   - Shared data and processes: `memoryData` and `memoryProcess`. `memoryStore` keeps its signature.
   - Each process takes the control record's epoch when it starts. Once the record holds a different epoch, every change the process makes is unavailable. The check runs before the idempotency replay and before the expiry sweep.
   - The ledger is a name → `subjectDataEver` map. A space's entry turns true once it is declared with a category other than `none`, or with none at all, and never turns back.
   - `honours` answers durable and replicated as unmet.
   - The module provides `store`, `storeControl` and `storeUpkeep` from one process.
   - A new memory epoch only has to differ from the data's earlier ones, so memory counts them (G23: randomness comes from the kernel). Redis draws random epochs in PR 2, because a restore can bring an old one back there.

3. **docs: the card list with store's upkeep**: `docs/audit/cards.md`, regenerated (`pnpm --filter @mod/references run configuration`).

4. **store: retire only under the maintenance key; committed answers checked exactly** (auth-ca's P3s, raised to High by Codex). Taking a space off the ledger lets erasure's `done` pass over a removed module's data, so `retire` answers `not-in-maintenance` outside the key, as `require` does. The two committed answers loosened for `at` are compared exactly again, with `at: expect.any(Number)` where the store gives one.
5. **store: a cursor a store gives is taken back, however long** (Codex, Medium). `checkedStore` capped cursors at 512 characters, but the memory store's cursor names a whole key, which can reach three 512-character texts. So a scan or sweep over keys with the longest names refused its own cursor. Cursors now have a bound (16384) above any cursor a store gives. Redis's cursor is a number. The scan contract's paging test now uses keys with the longest names. The upkeep suite does the same for `sweep`, and it now includes Codex's reproduction for `retire`. Both regressions fail under the old bound.

## For review

- **Budget splits (G7, split rather than squeezed):**
  - The store card is at 44 lines against its 45-line narrow limit. The upkeep detail lives on `upkeep`'s card.
  - The package's test lines were near 2000, so the upkeep contract suite and the memory upkeep tests live in the `upkeep` unit.
  - The suite file (`src/upkeep/suite.ts`) counts as that unit's source lines, not its test lines. Guard counts only the exact `./testing` file as test code. Say if you'd rather see guard read files that `./testing` reaches as tests (a guard change, out of this PR).
- **Two exact comparisons loosened:** a committed batch answer is now compared with `toMatchObject`, because `at` is allowed on it (`storeContract`'s empty batch-across case and one simulated test).
- **Wiring only:** the store card does not promise that features may take `storeUpkeep` or `storeControl`. G adds the `takenBy` lists: upkeep for account-erasure-store and records, control for subject-revocation-store and account-erasure-store.
- **Left to G:** refusing to start under the maintenance key, or when a required space is missing. Nothing writes either one yet.

## Covered surface

- **Surface 3 (module contracts):** `@mod/store` gains optional members and two new contracts. All of it is additive.
- **Surfaces 2 and 6 (start-up, data at rest):** unchanged in this PR. The memory store keeps nothing across a restart, and its start-up ledger write cannot fail. Both surfaces change in PR 2 (Redis).

## Changelog lines (for the release cut)

- Added: `store` (`retire` under the maintenance key alone): the `storeControl` and `storeUpkeep` contracts (control record, ledger of spaces, `honours`, `sweep`), a declaration's erasure fields, `getMany`, and a batch's commit time `at`; the memory store offers them all.

No Deprecated notice and no U-0.20 text.

## Checks

- typecheck, lint, guard: ok
- workspace tests (whole `pnpm test`, under a heavy slot): 7196 passed, with 1 failure: the card list was not yet regenerated. Fixed in commit 3; its test (`audit-index`) and the store tests pass after the rebase onto develop.

author: braghettos
body:
Four low-risk CPU fixes from the run-23 CPU study (50K compositions × 1000 users, snowplow pinned at 4 cores). Each one gives the same output as before; the tests below compare the old and new code on real corpora. Shares are of total CPU in run 23. I re-read each one from the merged `n1-steady` profile before changing the code.

**This needs a paired run before it can be accepted.** These benchmarks are micro-benchmarks, run on a heavily loaded dev machine (load average around 79 on 8 cores). That is why CPU time per op (`cpu-ns/op`, from getrusage) is reported next to wall time. Allocation counts don't depend on load.

## 1. gojq cancellation check (~2.7%): `context.TODO()` → `context.Background()`

The gojq fork checks `env.ctx != context.Background()` (`execute.go:24`). On any other context it calls `select ctx.Done()` before **every opcode**. In run 23 `runtime.selectnbrecv` inside `gojq.(*env).Next` was 3.10% of all CPU, and `evalFilter` accounts for 80% of `Next`.

**Decision: switch to Background. This does not change behaviour.** Every one of these sites already passed a literal `context.TODO()`. `TODO().Done()` is nil, so none of these evaluations could ever be cancelled. Background keeps that and only removes the per-opcode check. I left the request context where it is wanted: the refilter's per-item `uafExpr.eval` runs on the request ctx on purpose (it fails closed) and is untouched.

Sites changed:
- `restactions.go:128`: the RESTAction filter. It is in-memory work over stages already fetched, and its result is the cell every requester of the key shares. #1054 had already kept it detached on purpose.
- `api/handler.go:286`: the stage filter, same pattern ("keeps its context.TODO").
- `api/setup.go:201` and `api/cluster_list.go:863`: path-template renders.
- `api/setup.go:542`: `evalJQE`.

Test `TestRun23_Filter_BackgroundAndTODOAgree` checks that both contexts give the same result on the corpus, and that a cancelled context still cancels.

| BenchmarkRun23_FilterContext (cpu=1, n=10) | todo | background | |
|---|---|---|---|
| compositions-list n=1000, cpu-sec/op | 32.65 ms | 28.41 ms | **−13.0%** (p=0.023) |
| dashboard-data n=1000, cpu-sec/op | 3.239 ms | 2.655 ms | **−18.0%** (p=0.001) |
| B/op, allocs/op | unchanged | unchanged | |

## 2. `normalizeParamKey` built a `strings.Replacer` per call (1.65%, 4.2% of bytes)

`call.go`: it now uses one package-level `strings.NewReplacer("_", "", "-", "")`, which is safe for concurrent use. On the customer path, every dispatched request goes through `hasCallOnlyParam → nearMissParam`.

| BenchmarkParamKey_HasCallOnlyParam (a widget-dispatch query) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| B/op | 140,641 | **192** |
| allocs/op | 100 | **16** |
| sec/op | 427.5 µs | 5.99 µs |

Tests:
- `TestParamKeyNormalize_IdenticalToPerCallReplacer`: every portal query key, the #443 near-miss spellings, non-ASCII keys and invalid UTF-8 normalize exactly as before, and `nearMissParam` gives the same answer.
- `_ConcurrentUse` runs under `-race`.

## 3. `LearnedClassKey` recomputed O(classes × units) times (2.4%, 6.2% of bytes, 9.1% of objects)

`prewarm_engine_boot.go`: `seedLearnedWidgetsFor` / `seedLearnedRAsFor` walked every seed's learned list for every admitted class. They called `learnedKey` on each unit every time, and that call was 93% of `learnedKey`'s CPU.

The new `learnedUnitsByClass` (`learned_identity_seed.go`) computes each unit's key once, after the seeds are sorted (they are never written afterwards). It groups the units by class, keeping seed order and then target order. Each class gets exactly the units, in exactly the order, that the old walk visited.

Test `TestLearnedUnitsByClass_IdenticalToPerClassWalk` compares the index with the old walk, `reflect.DeepEqual`, for every class key. The fixture includes reordered groups, `system:authenticated` added, duplicate units and empty seeds.

| BenchmarkLearnedUnits_SeedAllClasses | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 100 seeds × 20 classes | 34.3 ms, 5.07 MiB, 108k allocs | 6.96 ms, 0.71 MiB, 5.6k allocs |
| 300 seeds × 80 classes | 3.41 s, 238 MiB, 5.19M allocs | 54 ms, 6.7 MiB, 65.6k allocs |

## 4. Compiled-filter cache (Parse+Compile 0.91% in total; `evalFilter` alone ≈0.56%)

`jqsupport.Compile(query)` (`internal/support/jq/compiled.go`) returns the program `gojq.Parse` + `gojq.Compile(WithModuleLoader(ModuleLoader()))` would build, and reuses it. `evalFilter` now uses it and returns the same wrapped errors.

**Cache key: everything that affects compilation.** That is the query text, the compiler options and the source of every imported module:
- The option is always the process loader.
- Built-in modules are embedded in the binary and cannot change.
- Operator modules under `JQ_MODULES_PATH` (a ConfigMap mount the kubelet updates in place) are recorded with their exact bytes. Every lookup re-reads them and reuses the program only if every byte is unchanged.
- Errors are never cached.
- Authors' filters stay fully general: the cache only memoizes the compile.

**The bound (no knob):** a program stays cached while it is used at least once per GC cycle. A sweep after every GC drops the programs not used since the previous one; this is the primary/victim scheme `sync.Pool` uses. So the cache holds the filters of the RESTActions being resolved now. A filter that changed or was deleted, and an inline RESTAction's one-off filter, fall out within two cycles. A client sending new inline filters cannot grow it. Run 23 ran a GC every ~1.95 s (num_gc +158 over 307 s at a ~3.3 GB heap), so every hot filter stays compiled.

**Concurrent reuse:** a `*gojq.Code` is immutable (gojq: "safe … to reuse a compiled *Code"). The fork's `execute` only reads `bc.codes`, and its regexp cache is a `sync.Map`.

**Shared constants:** a cached program's folded constants are shared across runs, so its outputs must stay read-only. The filter's outputs only reach jqutil's encoder and `DecodedObjectOf`, which copies them into a fresh tree. `TestRun23_Filter_ConstantOutputsStayUnshared` modifies a resolved tree at every level and checks that the next resolve is unchanged; it goes red if `DecodedObjectOf` aliases its input.

**Not cached (left as residuals):**
- `api.CompileJQ`, the stage filter, ~0.18%. Its output goes into the stage dict, where a shared constant could be modified by later dict code. Proving it never is needs an audit of every dict consumer, so it stays uncached.
- **plumbing `jqutil.Eval`**, ~0.09% (the widget `widgetDataTemplate` path and evalFilter's per-output `"."` encode). The compile happens inside plumbing (`jqutil.go` v1.34.0: `gojq.Parse` at line 23, `gojq.Compile` at line 33). `Eval` takes only a query string and its encoder is unexported, so snowplow cannot cache at its own call site without touching plumbing. plumbing is not edited here.
- `pathtemplate.Compile` and `jqsupport.IterateValues` (~0.1% together).

| benchmark (steady state) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| CompileCache_PortalCorpus: get all 193 deployed portal programs | 159 ms, 27.1 MiB, 523k allocs | **167 µs, 0 B, 0 allocs** |
| Run23_FilterCompile corpus=portal (92 filters, extras dict; cpu=1) | 34.7 ms cpu, 25.4 MiB, 485k allocs | **2.12 ms cpu, 0.94 MiB, 8.0k allocs** |
| Run23_FilterCompile compositions-list n=1000 (cpu=1) | 22.37 ms cpu, 10.22 MiB, 104.9k | 22.35 ms cpu (~), 9.99 MiB (−2.2%), 100.7k (−4.0%) |

The restactions benchmarks give the process a 512 MiB live heap. That makes the GC pace like the pod's instead of running several times per resolve, a regime the pod never sees.

Tests:
- `TestRun23_Filter_PortalCorpusIdenticalToBefore`: all 92 deployed portal 1.8.84 RESTAction filters × 4 dict shapes. 368 results identical (250 with content), checked on values, text and errors.
- `TestRun23_Filter_Issue1079CorpusIdenticalToBefore`: the two composition RESTActions of portal 1.8.85 over 350 compositions, for every request the pages send. Both compare the old `evalFilter` on

## Summary

- Drop six runtime dependencies of `@kozou/svelte-ui` that nothing imports: `@internationalized/date`, `@lucide/svelte`, `@tanstack/table-core`, `bits-ui`, `formsnap`, `tailwind-variants`.
- Remove three `[[IgnoredVulns]]` entries that stop matching once `bits-ui` (and the `runed` it brought in) is gone.
- Make the README stack table match the code (Forms and Tables rows).

## Why the exceptions go

`runed` 0.35 declares an optional `@sveltejs/kit ^2.21.0` peer, which kept anyone installing `@kozou/svelte-ui` on kit 2.x, and with it on `cookie` 0.6.0. Without it, `scripts/derive-consumer-manifests.mjs` followed by `npm install --package-lock-only` resolves the `@kozou/svelte-ui` consumer tree to `@sveltejs/kit` 3.1.1 and `cookie` 2.0.2. GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x, GHSA-27mw-82g8-phjj and GHSA-pfhg-q3qv-9q6r then match nothing, and the gate would fail with `has unused ignores`. GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 (deepmerge, via kit -> vite-plugin-svelte) still matches and stays.

The built output still inlines the SvelteKit 2.x runtime. The gate scans dependency trees, not inlined code, so that is unchanged here. Moving the inlined kit to 2.70.4 follows in a separate PR.

## Supersedes

Dependabot #342 (`@tanstack/table-core` 9) and #344 (`tailwind-variants` 4) become moot once these dependencies are gone.

## Verification

- Local: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm -r run build`, `pnpm --filter @kozou/svelte-ui typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm --filter @kozou/svelte-ui test` (22 files, 199 tests) all pass.
- The lockfile diff is deletions only; regenerating it from a clean tree reproduces it byte for byte.
- The svelte-ui build output contains none of the removed package names.
- Not run locally: Playwright e2e, Docker-based tests, and osv-scanner itself. CI covers them.
