## Summary
Retheme of the web app to a minimal, Swiss-style look. Component structure, behaviour and business logic are unchanged; only tokens and class names move.

- **Look:** neutral greys, flat cards separated by hairline borders, near-square corners, an ink rule under page headers, inverted ink for selected segments/toggles, uppercase eyebrow labels and tabular figures. Inter is bundled locally (no CDN).
- **Tokens:** the existing token system in `web/src/styles.css` is extended rather than replaced. New tokens for interaction states (`hover`, `pressed`, `selected`, `focus-ring`), actions (`action`, `danger`), `rule`, `accent-text`, `scrim`, `shadow-overlay`, radii (`card`, `control`, `chip`, `bar`, `swatch`) and type sizes (`eyebrow`, `metric-*`, `hero`, `display`). Chart chrome in `web/src/lib/tokens.ts` mirrors the CSS, and `barEnd()` / `MARK_RADIUS` / `ROUTE_RAMP` replace hard-coded chart values.
- **Accessibility:** every text, action and selected token clears 4.5:1 on every surface in both modes. This fixes white text on the dark accent (was 3.64:1) and a dark-mode green (was 4.34:1). The focus ring and accent clear 3:1, and the focus outline no longer forces a radius.
- **Docs:** `web/CONVENTIONS.md` gains a Styling section with the token rules.

## Production blocker verified 2026-11-09
The protected Course Builder image workflow [42590005939](https://github.com/elevate-for-humanity/Elevate-lms/actions/runs/42590005939) built the image but failed its inside-image worker boundary tests: 6 cases in `tests/worker/narration-inspector-checkpoint.test.mjs` raised `ReferenceError: deriveSavedErrors is not defined` (362/368 passed). The test harness evaluates transformed TypeScript via `new Function`, deliberately stripping import statements; after main `2133a329` introduced `deriveSavedErrors` into `loadLessonCheckpoint`, the harness did not inject that real dependency. The separate independently tested `saved-errors-derivation` suite passed.

## Narrow fix
Import the production `deriveSavedErrors` and `recoverTeachingVisibilityRepair` helpers into the checkpoint test and supply them to the isolated class constructor. No production decision logic, quality thresholds, retry limits, database records, or publication approvals are changed.

## Acceptance
Require independent protected CI and the actual Docker image test, protected merge, exact Google worker image verification and Admin/LMS release readbacks before counting this blocker resolved. The test correction is not an autonomous PARIS source repair or originating-job recovery; do not restart exhausted PARIS attempts.

Casting or interpolating an array now infers `'Array'`, the string PHP produces, instead of `string`. `InvalidCast` and `PossiblyInvalidCast` are still reported where they were.

**Before**
```php
<?php
/** @param array<string> $arr */
function f(array $arr): void {
    $cast = (string) $arr;  // string
    $prefixed = "A: $arr";  // non-empty-string
}
```

**After**
```php
    $cast = (string) $arr;  // 'Array'
    $prefixed = "A: $arr";  // 'A: Array'
```

Because the result is the literal `'Array'`, `echo (string) $_GET;` is no longer reported as tainted. Interpolating a value from the array still is.

Fixes #11466

body:
## Summary

- Honor the `flag_keys` query parameter. `flag_key` is still accepted.
- Honor `X-Amp-Exp-Track: no-track` to skip assignment tracking.
- Remote-evaluation-mode flags still return their default variant, as local evaluation in the SDKs does, but are no longer tracked. A warning is logged once per flag, and the new `amplitude_proxy_remote_evaluation_flag_skipped_total` metric counts them.
- Fix emptied cohorts not removing previous members' memberships.
- Container: remove unauthenticated JMX from the default `JAVA_OPTS`, stop exposing port 9999, and run as a non-root user.
- Remove the unauthenticated `/shutdown` endpoint. The proxy shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM.
- Redact deployment keys, API keys, secret keys, management keys and Redis URI credentials from logs.
- `AMPLITUDE_SERVER_ZONE=EU` now sets all four endpoint defaults. The README documents `serverZone`.
- The release workflow builds `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images.

## Behavior changes

- `/shutdown` is removed. Use SIGTERM.
- The default `JAVA_OPTS` is empty, so JMX must be enabled explicitly.
- The proxy no longer sends assignment or exposure events for remote-evaluation-mode flags.
- `EvaluationProxy.evaluate` and `evaluateV1` gain a trailing `tracksAssignment` parameter that defaults to `true`, so existing callers still compile.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Behavior changes affect assignment/exposure for remote-mode flags, cohort membership on empty syncs, and deployment shutdown/JMX defaults; container and logging hardening reduce attack surface but may break operators relying on `/shutdown` or open JMX.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes evaluation and cohort behavior, tightens container security, and improves operability for EU deployments and releases.
> 
> **Evaluation & tracking:** Honors `flag_keys` (with legacy `flag_key`) and `X-Amp-Exp-Track: no-track` to skip assignment events while still allowing exposure tracking. Remote-evaluation-mode flags still return their default variant but no longer emit assignment/exposure events (metric `amplitude_proxy_remote_evaluation_flag_skipped_total`, one-time warn per flag).
> 
> **Cohorts:** Empty cohort refreshes now diff against the previous version so former members lose memberships instead of staying targeted.
> 
> **Config & logs:** `AMPLITUDE_SERVER_ZONE=EU` (or `serverZone: EU`) drives all four Amplitude endpoint defaults unless overridden. Keys and Redis URI credentials are redacted in logs and safe `toString()` output.
> 
> **Container & ops:** Image runs as non-root, drops unauthenticated JMX and port 9999 by default, and shuts down via SIGTERM hook instead of `/shutdown`. Release workflow publishes multi-arch (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) images.
>

author: sanketmis208
body:
## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #29498

The MS Teams (`office365_video`) video adapter had two broken methods:

1. `updateMeeting()` sent `POST /onlineMeetings`, so every reschedule created a **new** Teams meeting. The old one stayed alive on Microsoft's side.
2. `deleteMeeting()` was a no-op (`Promise.resolve([])`), so cancelling a booking never removed the Teams meeting.

Changes in `packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`:

- `updateMeeting` now sends `PATCH /onlineMeetings/{id}` using the booking reference uid. This is the Teams meeting id stored by `EventManager` when the meeting was created. The Zoom adapter uses `bookingRef.uid` the same way.
- If there is no reference uid (an old or missing reference), it falls back to the previous `POST`, so the booking still gets a working link.
- `deleteMeeting` now sends `DELETE /onlineMeetings/{id}`.
  - A `404` counts as success, because the meeting is already gone.
  - Any other failure throws an `HttpError`. `EventManager.deleteEventsAndMeetings` uses `Promise.allSettled`, so one failed delete doesn't block the other cleanups.
- Removed the outdated comment saying only create and update are needed.

Graph docs: [Update onlineMeeting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/onlinemeeting-update?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Delete onlineMeeting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/onlinemeeting-delete?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)

N/A. This is a backend change to Microsoft Graph calls, and it is covered by unit tests (output below).

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [x] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- [x] I have updated the developer docs if this PR makes changes that would require a documentation change. If N/A, write N/A here and check the checkbox. N/A
- [x] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.

## How should this be tested?

```bash
TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.test.ts
```

New and updated tests:
- With an existing reference, `updateMeeting` PATCHes `/me/onlineMeetings/MEETING_ID` and never calls the create endpoint.
- With no reference, `updateMeeting` still POSTs a new meeting (the old behaviour is kept as the fallback).
- `deleteMeeting` sends DELETE to `/me/onlineMeetings/MEETING_ID`.
- `deleteMeeting` treats 404 as success, throws on 5xx, and makes no Graph call when the id is empty.

Manual check, with an MS Teams app installed:
1. Book an event that uses MS Teams.
2. Reschedule it. The same Teams join link is kept, and the meeting time is updated in Teams.
3. Cancel it. The Teams meeting is removed.

Local results:
- On this branch: `Tests 10 passed (10)`.
- With only the test file applied on `main`, the 4 new update/delete tests fail. So they catch the bug.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/app-store`: 0 errors.
- `biome lint --config-path=biome-staged.json` on the changed files: no errors. The remaining warnings were already there on `main`.

Part of #12. Covers issue #19 (1b-5). Three commits, one change each: a style move, the notes workspace, and a link on the account page.

- `refactor`: `.button-primary`, `.spinner` and `.skeleton` (with their keyframes and the reduced-motion rule) move from `auth.css` to `index.css`, line for line, because the notes module and `core/router/RequireAuth` use them too

Sidebar: a New note button, the note list (newest change first, from the server), the signed-in email (links to `/account`) and a sign-out button

- Wide screens: sidebar about 300 px, hide/show (not remembered across page loads), content column about 600 px. At 768 px and below the sidebar is a drawer: opened from the top left button, closed by Escape, the close button, a tap outside or choosing a note; Tab stays inside, focus returns to the opener, the page behind cannot scroll

Known limits, on purpose:
- The title and context fields can be edited but nothing is saved yet (autosave is #21); edits are lost when another note opens
- The content area is a placeholder: there is no editor yet, so "the cursor is in the content when a new note opens" is not possible (moved to #20)
- The sign-out handling and the error box (message + reference) are repeated in a few places; a shared hook/component is planned in #23 (the item is added there)

Checked: client lint, 110 tests (19 new, for the pure helpers: note path, drawer breakpoint, late-response gate, focus-trap step; each was broken on purpose once and failed a test), build. The screens were tried by the project owner on their own machine (wide screen, 768 px drawer, keyboard, errors), who reported that it works. Not checked by me: anything visual or keyboard-related in a browser (only the owner did).

body:
Fixes #9.

## What changed (CSS only, `css/style.css`)

**1. First calendar row border bug** — `.mock__row:first-of-type { border-top: none; }` never matched: `:first-of-type` is the first `<div>` among siblings, and the first `<div>` inside `.mock` is `.mock__header`, so every row (including Mon) kept its top border. Replaced with `.mock__row + .mock__row { border-top: ... }`, so separators appear between rows only and the dead selector is gone.

Now `.nav__inner` wraps and `.nav__links` moves to a full-width second row (`order: 3; flex-basis: 100%`), so the top row is logo + button and the links sit below. No JS, no hamburger — links stay visible and reachable, and the desktop nav is untouched.

- Branch holds exactly the 2 expected commits on top of main `2575db53`.

author: buvinghausen
kaeawc
body:
## Summary

The lychee download turned main red during the 2026-11-09 GitHub release 504 outage. `install_lychee.sh` fetched the asset with a bare curl, so it had no checksum, cache or backoff. This PR routes lychee, and both hadolint download paths, through `scripts/lib/release-download.sh` `release_fetch_pinned`, the same way [#17627](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/pull/17627) did for ktfmt, shfmt and ripgrep.

**lychee (done fully)**
- `scripts/lychee/lychee_version.sh` pins 0.22.0 and the SHA-256 of each of the 5 assets the installer can request. lychee publishes no checksum files, so I computed them from the release assets and confirmed the Linux binary reports `lychee 0.22.0`.
- The archive is verified after a cache restore and after a download. Downloads use the helper's bounded, jittered backoff, and a final failure prints the `UPSTREAM-DOWNLOAD-FAILURE:` marker. The existing generic known-flakes row already matches that marker for any `github.com/*/releases/download` URL.
- `install-fast-validation-deps.sh` now runs the lychee installer once, under its own 150 s timeout. Before, it ran up to 2 × 60 s attempts, and the 60 s timeout would kill the helper's ~60–90 s backoff before the helper could finish or print the marker. The documented worst case is now 5 × 145 + 160 = 885 s, still under the 15-minute step timeout, and the bats arithmetic guard is updated to match.
- `actions/cache` restores `~/.cache/auto-mobile/tools/lychee`, keyed on `lychee_version.sh`, in **Fast Validation**, **Shell Changed Files** (before its background deps install) and the merge **Validate Documentation Links** job. No job or check names change.
- Two new `known-flakes.txt` rows classify the old installer's 5xx as RERUN-DONT-FIX: one for the wrapped Fast Validation / Shell path and one for the direct merge link-check path. Both are anchored on the installer's final failure (`install lychee failed after` / `Installation failed!`), so a 5xx that recovered on retry cannot hide a real failure later in the job.

**hadolint**
- `scripts/hadolint/hadolint_version.sh` pins 2.12.0 and each asset's SHA-256. These match the release's published `.sha256` files.
- `install_hadolint.sh` and `scripts/docker/validate_dockerfile.sh` now share that pin and fetch through the helper. Both scripts run under `set -e`, so the call uses the repo's `run_capture_status` pattern, which keeps the SC2310 baseline at zero.
- Two small fixes were needed to pin the real assets. The Windows asset name gains its `.exe` suffix (it used to 404). `validate_dockerfile.sh` now maps Apple Silicon to `Darwin-x86_64`, as `install_hadolint.sh` already did (#3641).

## Linked Issue

Part of #17641

Still to do, left for follow-up PRs (the issue allows one PR per tool group):
- swiftlint (`install_swiftlint.sh`, `install_swiftlint_linux.sh`)
- swiftformat
- xcodegen (`xcodegen_version.sh`)
- act
- mediamtx (`run-mediamtx-publisher-integration.sh`)
- `release.yml:430` (mcp-publisher)
- `scripts/install.sh` gum and yq: these are user-facing installer paths and must keep working offline when the binary is already present, so they need a separate, careful change.

## Bug / Regression Context

- **Prior attempts:** #17627 covered ktfmt, shfmt and ripgrep only.
- **Observed symptom:** On 2026-11-09 at 08:20Z, a GitHub release HTTP 504 failed the lychee install on main. The failure classified as UNKNOWN instead of infrastructure.
- **Repro steps / conditions:** `releases/download` returns a 5xx while no lychee or hadolint binary is cached.

## Validation

- [x] `scripts/prepush-shell.sh`: all 6 fast checks pass (shellcheck, shell-portability, shell-sete, pipefail-grep-q, stdlib-first, bun-version-coherence). 151 of 153 selected BATS tests pass. The 2 failures are `install-fast-validation-deps.bats` "a partial clone left by a killed attempt…" and "a bats-core clone that does not match…". They fail the same way on unmodified `main` in the cloud container, because a host `bats` on PATH defeats their "bats is missing" setup. This PR does not touch them.
- [x] `bun run format`: no changes
- [x] New `test/bats/install-lychee.bats`: stubs curl, sha256sum, sleep, uname and apt-get, and limits PATH so a host lychee cannot short-circuit the install. It covers:
  - a pin for every asset name the installer uses
  - a cache hit while GitHub returns 504
  - a stale cache entry being discarded
  - download, verify and cache
  - 504 retries with backoff (3/6/12 s) ending in the marker
  - a 404 failing at once with no marker
  - a checksum mismatch being rejected
  - every workflow lychee step restoring the cache
- [x] `install-hadolint.bats` now also covers checksum pins, a cache hit while GitHub returns 504, 504 backoff with the marker, and checksum rejection. `classify-failure.bats` covers the lychee old-installer rows, a recovered 5xx not masking a real failure, and the new-installer marker.
- [x] Smoke-tested against real GitHub downloads in a throwaway HOME: lychee installed, cached, then reused from the cache. `install_hadolint.sh` and `validate_dockerfile.sh` each downloaded, verified, cached and installed hadolint.
- [x] Rebased onto latest `main` (branched from ad9e1141; main has since gained only an unrelated iOS commit)

## Follow-ups

- [ ] The remaining tools listed under Linked Issue stay on #17641.

author: bernt-matthias
body:
`bin_long` concatenates the contigs into a temporary FASTA file and then runs
marker gene detection on it, but it did so from *inside* the `with open(...)`
block that writes the file; since `estimate_seeds()` hands the path to separate
processes (prodigal/FragGeneScan and hmmsearch), anything still sitting in the
write buffer is invisible to them. On ext4/tmpfs this silently truncated the
input — we measured 720,206 of 800,230 bytes visible before the handle was
closed, so prodigal only saw part of the contigs — and on GPFS-style parallel
filesystems the file looks completely empty and the run aborts with
`Running hmmsearch failed: ... Error: Sequence file .../contigs.faa is empty
or misformatted`, producing no bins at all. The fix is a single dedent: move
`estimate_seeds()`/`get_marker()` out of the `with` block, the same ordering
`cluster.py` already uses for short reads. The second commit adds
`test/test_long_read_cluster.py`, which mocks `estimate_seeds()` and asserts
that the file a child process would read contains all contigs (it sees an
empty file without the fix), plus `ChangeLog` and `docs/whatsnew.md` entries
under *Unreleased*.

author: zach-source
body:
## Why

- claude-factory-d289.18: in the AX manager, the host backup never ran. A tick holds `tick.lock` most of the time (39 of 40 samples at 1.5 s). So each 10 min try found the lock and stopped.
- claude-factory-d289.17: `factory migrate-to-ax --dry-run` showed pushed runs as not pushed. The main repo did not have the new origin commits of the run branch, so `merge-base --is-ancestor` failed.

## What

- `backupStep` is async. If the lock is held, it tries again each second, up to 120 times (2 min). It logs one skip line at the end. The host loop waits for it.
- `isPushed` fetches the run branch when the repo does not have the origin commit, then runs `merge-base`.

## Tests

- `managerhost.test.ts`: a lock held for 2 tries, then a backup; a lock held for all tries logs one line.
- `migrate.test.ts`: a newer commit on origin that the repo did not fetch counts as pushed.

author: emergentmonk
body:
## Q16-ECMA-001 — Bounded checked-int32 projection and explicit JavaScript counterexamples

**Independent VANILLAJS follow-up to the completed SONIFICATION MAT-SPEC-010 research series and the separate SPARK-001 verification pilot.** Base main SHA `b3e20b2a37d90c8dda68e8be69d2f334003c1255`.

### Source identity and changes

- **Unchanged production JS**, `modules/integer-math/index.js`, Git blob `d457b0154d9dfc8b50fd593b5e9dff75e1ea66b9`. New tests fail if the source blob differs.
- New `Q16ECMA.lean`: an exact **integer-domain** model of modulo `2^32`, ToUint32-like and ToInt32-like projection, bound proofs, and checked 32-bit input-domain identity theorems. A concrete theorem records how `2147483648` wraps under the unchecked projection.
- New `Q16ECMAAudit.lean` and `scripts/verify-q16-ecma-axioms.py` verify five named transitive axiom reports, with strict allowlist and five adversarial negative controls.
- `tests/q16-ecma.test.js`: actual Node22 source-pinned boundary conformance, checked vs unchecked semantics on negative zero, NaN/Infinity/fractional/out-of-range values, typed-array and modulo behavior, plus seeded JS PRNG against independent BigInt model.
- Separate proof CI `.github/workflows/q16-ecma.yml` using the existing pinned Lean 4.35.0 install and Node22, with exact theorem/axiom audit and logged proof evidence. Existing original Q16 theorem/proof workflows remain unchanged apart from an additive `lakefile.toml` library target.
- `docs/Q16_ECMA_001.md` distinguishes math theorems, finite production-JS testing, and outstanding proof obligations.

### Counterexample, not an implementation defect

JavaScript unchecked `2147483648 | 0` produces `-2147483648`, but the **checked production API** `int32(2147483648)` intentionally throws `RangeError`. Likewise `NaN | 0` yields zero while `int32(NaN)` rejects it. Therefore **unrestricted ToInt32 cannot be equated with the checked API**, and the domain restrictions are substantive.

### Explicit nonclaim

This is **NOT** universal Lean-to-ECMAScript source refinement. The integer theorems do not model full IEEE-754 JavaScript Number, arbitrary ToNumber coercion, floating quotient estimates, loops, exceptions or typed-array execution. `docs/Q16_FORMAL_001.md` remains **`REFINEMENT_OPEN`** for that larger obligation. Preserve all original **Q16-FORMAL-002** frozen and sealed evidence; never rewrite or relabel it.

**Draft until Lean CI and exact-source Node conformance pass.** No owner merge without review.

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce bounded Lean and JavaScript conformance evidence for checked 32-bit integer projections without claiming universal Lean-to-ECMAScript refinement.

New Features:
- Add a bounded Lean integer model for unsigned and signed 32-bit projections, including range, identity, and out-of-domain wraparound theorems.
- Add Node.js conformance tests covering pinned production source identity, checked versus unchecked JavaScript integer semantics, boundary values, typed arrays, and PRNG modulo behavior.

Enhancements:
- Document the scope and limitations of the bounded integer refinement, including explicit counterexamples showing that unrestricted ECMAScript coercion does not match the checked APIs.
- Add a strict transitive axiom audit with adversarial negative controls for the five new Lean theorems.

Build:
- Register the new Q16ECMA Lean library target.

CI:
- Add a dedicated Lean and Node 22 workflow that kernel-checks the theorems, audits axiom reports, runs source-pinned conformance tests, and archives proof evidence.

Documentation:
- Add user-facing documentation describing theorem scope, source identity, executed counterexamples, validation commands, and remaining universal-refinement obligations.

body:
Admin product form: grouped sections (details, pricing, settings) in a 3/2/1 column grid, multiline description, compact feature ticks, actions together at the bottom.

Re-uploads keep the administrator's text: the sheet fills name, descriptions, category, price, licence, software and feature ticks only on a model's first upload; later uploads update files only and report console_text_kept. Console product page checks every file the product uses in storage (new GET /api/v1/admin/products/<id>/file-check/) and warns about missing files and images that do not load in the browser.

author: ryucel
body:
### Bulgu
Teşhis ölçümünde 62 sorunun 18'i `D1 DB is overloaded` hatası verdi. Sebebi tek bir sorgu kalıbıymış. Kanonik yasa kanalı şu sorguyu kullanıyordu:

```sql
chunks_fts MATCH ? AND rowid IN (SELECT id FROM chunks WHERE doc_id IN (...))
```

FTS5 bu kısıtta MATCH ifadesinin tamamını (önek ve `NEAR` terimleriyle birlikte) **her rowid için ayrı ayrı yeniden çalıştırıyor**. Yerel kopyada bu kanal tek bir soruda 3,7 saniye sürdü. Aynı ifade kısıtsız çalıştırıldığında 15 ms.

### Düzeltme
- **Belge belirteci:** `scope` sütununa her belge için bir belirteç ekleniyor: `xqd` + belge kimliğinin hex'i (`build.py` içinde `doc_token`, `sql.ts` içinde `docToken`; ikisi aynı sonucu veriyor). Kısıt artık indeksin içinde uygulanıyor: `(...) AND (scope:xqd… OR …)`.
- **Sıralama:** FTS sıralaması `bm25(1.0, 0.0)` olarak ayarlandı, yani `scope` sütunu yalnızca filtreliyor, puanı değiştirmiyor. Yerelde eski kısıtla karşılaştırdım: ilk 50 sonuç ve puanları birebir aynı.
- **Tam içe aktarma:** `D1_STATE_VERSION = 5`; sonraki yenileme tam içe aktarma yapacak. Ücretli plana geçildiği için günlük yazma sınırı artık sorun değil.

### Ölçüm (yerel, 55 soru)
| | Önce | Sonra |
|---|---|---|
| Soru başına SQL süresi | 680 ms | **30 ms** |
| En yavaş sorgu | 8.079 ms | **59 ms** |

`eval-search` 37/37.

### Merge sonrası
1. Worker kendiliğinden yayına çıkacak.
2. **Refresh data** elle başlatılacak (tam içe aktarma, yaklaşık 40 dakika).
3. Teşhis ölçümü yeniden çalıştırılacak.

**Geçiş penceresi:** Kod yayına çıktıktan sonra, içe aktarma bitene kadar kanonik yasa kanalı boş döner, çünkü D1'de henüz belge belirteçleri yok. Bu süre boyunca hata çıkmaz; yalnızca o kanalın katkısı eksik kalır.

body:
## what

- Recognize `No changes. No objects need to be destroyed.` using the existing no-change regex.
- Keep the current change-stats guard and renderer behavior; successful per-project checks retain their status and get the destroy no-op summary.

## why

Successful empty destroy plans were classified as changed because the detector recognized only the two ordinary no-change messages. As a result, `--hide-unchanged-plan-comments` left their detailed sections visible in multi-project comments.

This is a review draft in the contributor fork. It has not been submitted upstream. The upstream AI usage policy requires an accepted issue; no accepted issue covering this exact bug was found.

## tests

- [x] I have tested my changes by adding regression cases and confirming they failed before the parser change in classification, summaries, renderer output, and per-project status description.
- [x] `go test ./server/events/models ./server/events -run 'TestPlanSuccess|TestRender|TestDefaultCommitStatusUpdater_UpdateProject|TestUpdateCombined' -count=1` passed with Go 1.27.3 on darwin/arm64.
- [x] `make check-fmt` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Regression coverage includes ordinary and destroy no-ops, trailing provider warnings, hide flag on/off, real add/change/destroy/import/forget summaries mixed with a destroy no-op, output-only changes, failed plans, and existing single-project visibility.
- Full integration/E2E tests and a v0.44.0 backport were not run. No Terraform commands, credentials, state, or live infrastructure were used.

## references

- [Current detector at the tested upstream base](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/dcbc0e21be4cd6f791ad8e8d411d8bf76865e441/server/events/models/models.go#L552).
- [Hide unchanged plan comments](https://www.runatlantis.io/docs/server-configuration.html#hide-unchanged-plan-comments).
- [AI usage policy](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md).
- [Chainguard Atlantis FIPS image](https://images.chainguard.dev/directory/image/atlantis-fips/overview).

Proposed release path, subject to review: get the bug accepted upstream, submit this patch against a refreshed upstream base, and obtain a supported Atlantis release or vendor backport. For Chainguard-based consumers, have the supplier include it in the FIPS image, verify the resulting image digest and source/SBOM, rebuild the downstream assembly image, and validate in nonproduction before a separately approved rollout. The exact source of a deployed binary must be verified from its immutable image provenance; this source test does not establish that provenance. No image has been built, released, or deployed by this change.

## architecture decision record

- [x] I checked the [ADR criteria](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/main/docs/adr/README.md#when-is-an-adr-required).

**ADR:** Not required; this fixes recognition of an existing Terraform message without adding flags, APIs, storage, or execution behavior.

author: matrixarkai
body:
## The question

#2798 made a counter increment write its series block only when due, and listed as not verified that a torn log tail during counter recovery was never driven by a counter-specific test. The block is a copy and a recovery replays the staged outcomes, so a log cut mid-record has to land on a whole prefix of the increments, never on a different series.

## The test

`a_counter_log_cut_mid_record_recovers_a_prefix_of_its_increments` drives one counter with a seeded history, finds from the block store's byte counter which increments wrote their series block, and for three increments (the first of the key, one that wrote no block, one that wrote its block) drops the engine with no unload, copies the directory, cuts the last 1, 7, 20, 60, 150 and 400 bytes of the written log, reopens, and requires:

- the recovered series equals the series after some whole number of the increments (every step changes the series, so the prefix is unique);
- never the whole series (the cut record must be dropped);
- a larger cut never recovers a later prefix.

## Measured (debug build)

| increment | log bytes | cut | recovered prefix |
|---|---|---|---|

author: jvitkauskas
body:
The on-device store will install apps from m-apps' releases. This adds what a release carries, and CI to build it.

**`make release`** puts the following in `build/release`:
- **`<app>-<board>.tar`** for hello, usbdisk, slots, tone and mp3 on `fm1` and `smk37`: the app's folder for `/MBOOT/APPS/<APP>/`, with `BOOT.APP`, `META.TXT` and `ICON.QOI`.
- **`mboot-<board>.tar`:** `MENU.BIN` and `LAUNCH.BIN` for `/MBOOT`.
- **`SHA256SUMS`.**

**`tools/app_tar.py`** makes each tar as plain ustar:
- files sorted, folders allowed;
- every name 8.3 in capitals, as the kit's card code writes them;
- owned by nobody and dated 0;
- nothing after the two end blocks, unlike Python's `tarfile`, which pads to 10 KB.

So the same files always make the same bytes. A tar is only 1–3 KB bigger than the files in it: mp3-fm1 is 66.0 KB. Plain tar was chosen over upkr because the unit can unpack it straight onto the card, a piece at a time.

**CI** (`.github/workflows/build.yml`), using m-bootloader's toolchain step at pi32v2-llvm 23.1.5-2:
- On every push and pull request, it builds every app for both boards, runs `make test` and makes the release tars.
- A `v*` tag publishes a release with the tars.

**Tested:**
- `tests/app_tar_test.py`: tarfile reads the files back the same, the size is exact, the bytes are the same on a second run, and wrong names are refused.
- A clean rebuild locally gave the same `SHA256SUMS`.
- The first CI run passed, and its tars are byte-identical to my local build.

body:
## Scope

Research-only 30m strategy evaluation for BingX USDT-M perpetuals, with closed 1h context. This PR contains the four-family adaptive router, archive hardening, replay runner and immutable evidence. It is not connected to production Zeus and does not change risk, leverage, VST/REAL routing or active settings.

## Completed full five-symbol replay

GitHub Actions run #92 (ID 42692378936) completed successfully. It downloaded 30m/1h candles and funding data for BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE and INJ, ran base and 1.5x execution-cost replays, and uploaded immutable artifact `adaptive-bingx-perpetual-research` (SHA-256 `7fc263ac15ba4bd2058d41ca63bb41d50d70ffc12d35f90b7e4204e2e45f2fe1`).

The common five-symbol window is 2026-04-05 00:00 UTC to 2026-11-09 19:30 UTC: 218.81 days, below the 12-month requirement. All five symbols have 30m/1h data with zero reported candle gaps. Funding history before each symbol's latest uninterrupted segment is excluded rather than imputed as zero.

| Period | Trades | Base PF | Base net expectancy/trade | PF at 1.5x costs | Net expectancy/trade at 1.5x |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| IS | 261 | 0.5449 | -0.23319% | 0.4515 | -0.31569% |
| Validation | 81 | 0.6418 | -0.16717% | 0.5263 | -0.24967% |
| OOS | 74 | 0.5406 | -0.24751% | 0.4486 | -0.33001% |
| Combined | 416 | 0.5614 | -0.22288% | 0.4644 | -0.30538% |

All four families are negative on combined and OOS results. OOS has only 74 trades and no positive months. Combined median/mean hold is 30/76.2 minutes; maximum is 9 hours. Combined realized equal-notional drawdown proxy is -24.09% base / -32.51% stress.

## Decision

**NOT SELECTED.** The existing four-family router is rejected for VST/production promotion. Negative net expectancy persists in IS, validation and OOS, and becomes worse under 1.5x costs. Do not tune this router against the same OOS sample.

Full archive coverage, funding segment audit, family and symbol-side tables, and limitations are recorded in `docs/research/ADAPTIVE_PERP_REGIME_PORTFOLIO.md`.

## Next research direction

Test a structurally distinct 30m pullback continuation setup with completed 4h regime context, strict no-lookahead and the same funding/cost model. It must be evaluated as a new frozen hypothesis with a longer common history; no parameter mining on OOS.

## Safety

No production settings, live strategy, active risk, leverage, stops, exits, position sizing, VST or REAL routing were changed. No merge or activation authorization is implied.

body:
Holding TAB sent managed ServerRankRevealAll every tick even though native FakeRanks-RevealAll already owns disclosure. This caused rapidly changing or shared values across scoreboard rows. With TAB closed, the former 4 Hz reconciliation also left a window for engine-cleared fields to reach the first local scoreboard draw.

Remove managed reveal sends and keep cached controller fields synchronized every tick, including before TAB input reaches the server. Mark changed competitive fields with SetStateChanged, detect live resets separately from desired-value changes, scope notification state to the connection/controller, retry failures, and withhold unavailable data. Add console-only css_fakerank_status [slot]. Authoritative API polling remains 0.25 seconds; unchanged fields do not produce writes/notifications. XP/rank formulas, wins=111, RanksApi, JSON configuration and databases are preserved. Native FakeRanks 1.1.6 was reviewed and retained.

Validation: Release build with zero warnings/errors and regression checks for projection, 640 steady ticks, all field-drift combinations, connection/slot reuse, lifecycle reset, isolation and retry after notification failures. A real client with three controlled bot rows reproduced the original flicker. Limiting reveal to 1 Hz reduced flicker to 1 Hz; removing the managed sender stabilized distinct values, isolated two-second updates to one row, and three competitive icons. The probe ran over six minutes and was removed with cvars restored. After the owner reproduced a residual first-draw transition, a single extra reveal and distinct-wins probe were rejected by live testing. Continuous closed-TAB synchronization in v1.0.3-replication.3 then produced a smooth initial opening and repeated openings on #8, confirmed by the owner with two real players already present.

Final frozen DLL SHA256: 325456d84cc4933ad17f2c4d6304238d8c5854bf4baa7d94cb3e1e9918d92913. Requires the existing native reveal module. No full active-load performance or multiple-observer claim; native twelve-tick button polling is unchanged.

author: teamleaderleo
body:
Leo, 2026-11-09: "the ergonomic part is super big for us." and "we're not a terminal-first app anymore. cmux-next is a gui."

Move to Cloud showed "Moving this chat to Cloud…" until it finished, and Bring Back Local showed "Bringing this chat back to this Mac…", with no step and no time. Each could take a minute or more (a new machine, a big folder) with nothing on screen to say why.

The working toast now keeps its headline and adds a second line with the step, what it's waiting on, and about how long is left. The line updates in place while the move runs:

```
Moving this chat to Cloud…
2 of 4 · Copying the folder (1,204 files) · about 45 s left
```

The four steps, in both directions:

1. Reaching the machine: `Connecting to dev`, `Resuming dev` for a paused machine, or `Starting a new Cloud machine`.
2. Copying the folder (back): this uses the file count and rate that `cmux link seed push` / `seed pull` already print on stderr.
3. Handing the agent over, or `Bringing the agent to this Mac`.
4. Opening its tab.

## How it works

- **Rust** (`cmux-cloud-start-core::moves::progress`, FFI op `cloud_move_progress`): takes the step, how long it has run, the machine kind and name, and the copy's newest progress line, and returns the text, step and ETA. The ETA is the time left in the current step plus the usual time of the steps after it. For the copy, the time left comes from the measured rate (files, then bytes) once there is one. If a step runs past its usual time and nothing measures it, the line says `taking longer than usual (usually about 30 s)` instead of a made-up countdown. Times read as `a few seconds`, `about N s` in 5 s steps, then `about N min`. The reply's `nextMs` says when the text next changes on its own (`next_change_ms`); a test walks every step and checks that each wake lands exactly on a change. All arithmetic saturates, with no indexing and no unwraps.
- **Swift glue** (`CmuxNextCloud/MoveCore/CloudMoveProgress.swift`, glue only): the app tells it which step runs, and the copy's progress lines are pushed in as they come, each asking Rust for the line. Rust also answers `nextMs`: when the line next changes on its own. That's the countdown's next shown value, or the step running past its usual time. It's none when only a new fact changes the line: a new step, a measured copy's next line, or an overrun. The only timer is one one-shot `DemandTimer` at that time. Each answer replaces it, so a step wakes about every 5 s, not every second.
  - **Stop condition:** the timer stops when the move ends, because the run's `defer` calls `end()` on success, failure and cancellation. `hold()` also stops it while a machine update's toast shows. The timer holds the progress weakly, so it can't outlive the move. `CloudMoveProgressTests` checks this on a manual clock: one wake at the moment Rust names, none left after `end()`, nothing shown after, and none for a held line, a measured copy or an overrun.
  - **No decisions in Swift:** the machine's status goes to Rust as Cloud names it (`paused`, `running`, … or `new`), and Rust reads what it means.
  - `CloudMoveCLI.seedPush` / `bringBackPull` take an optional `stderrLine`, fed through the existing `SeedProgress.feed`.
- **App** (`CloudMove.swift`, `CloudBringBack.swift`): calls `enter(step)` where each step begins, and puts the line under the existing localized headline. While a machine update runs, its own toast stays up (`hold()`). When the chat's ask card shows the move, there is still no toast. To keep the App line count from rising, `CloudMove.failure(moving:/syncing:)` moved to `CloudMoveFailure.moving/syncing` in CmuxNextCloudUI with no change in behavior. arch-ratchet: app_lines -3.

## Variants

These are in the toast gallery (`overlay.toasts`): `move-before`, then:

- A: one sentence.
- **B: two lines (picked).**
- C: terse `2/4 … ~45 s`.
- D: time in the message, step in the tooltip.

The gallery also has `move-b-stages` (new machine → agent → tab) and `move-b-slow-and-back` (an overrun step, and Bring Back Local).

I picked B because the headline the person already knows doesn't move, the reason stays on screen (D hides it), what's moving stays named (C drops it), and a step change only rewrites the second line (A re-wraps the whole sentence).

## Limits

- **The line shows only once the app FFI pin includes this op.** The app links CCmuxAppFFI from a pinned release. After this lands, `app-ffi-release.yml` publishes a new release and its bot opens the pin PR. Until that pin lands, `cloud_move_progress` isn't in the linked library, so the call returns nil and the toast keeps today's plain headline. There's no error and no wake.
- The step line comes from Rust in English; the headline stays localized. I looked for a way Rust-made user text reaches the app localized (a key plus arguments looked up in the app's string tables) and found none. The app's localized Rust-fed text (notification titles, for example) is worded in Swift from facts Rust passes. Localizing this line would mean adding that key/args path and its translations, which this PR doesn't do.
- When the line changes, VoiceOver reads the toast again. That happens on each step, and at most every 5 s from the countdown.
- A person who closes the working toast keeps it closed for the rest of that run; the success or the Retry failure still shows (`CmuxToast.working`, `CmuxToastCenter.swift`). If no copy progress line arrives for 5 s past the estimate, the line says the move is taking longer than its progress said instead of counting a frozen estimate.
- The usual step times are estimates: 5 s to connect, 30 s to resume, 60 s for a new machine ("usually takes under a minute", from the New Cloud Workspace text), 10 s for the agent, 3 s for the tab. They aren't measured yet.
- No iOS change: Move to Cloud and Bring Back Local are Mac-chrome actions here, and this PR only changes the text of their existing toast.

## Tests

- Rust: 9 cases in `moves::progress` (step text per stage and direction, countdown, overrun, copy rate by files and bytes, bad and huge numbers, duration wording). The FFI shape case is `a_move_says_its_step_and_about_how_long_is_left` in `cloud_move_ffi`.
- Fleet run at `54bcaf6d5a3f022681aee88776f27ef3c3cc05b5` (https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/42609620538):
  - `cargo test -p cmux-cloud-start-core`: 170 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p cmux-cloud-start-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - FFI crate `cargo test --test cloud_move`: 6 passed, and its clippy `-D warnings` is clean.
  - `vp check` on the gallery file passes format, lint and types.
- App compile check at `54bcaf6d5a3f` passed (87 s).
- Swift `CloudMoveProgressTests` (3 tests) passed on the fleet (`package-test-lane.sh suite`, aws-m4pro) at `54bcaf6d5a3f`. Its Rust is a test double: the app links CCmuxAppFFI from a pinned release, which doesn't have `cloud_move_progress` yet (see Limits).

### Observed / Not run

- Observed: the fleet runs above; `prepush-gate.py` reports no new violations.
- Not run: the live app flow (Move to Cloud against a real machine), and gallery screenshots (`scripts/gallery-compare.sh` was not run).

## Changelog

- Changed: Move to Cloud and Bring Back Local show which step they're on and about how long is left.

author: ralyodio
body:
## Why auctions got no bids

Measured on dev2's buyer gateway (`c0mpute-speech-gateway-1`, 08:12 to 09:42Z, 2026-11-09):

| workload | auctions | got a bid |
|---|---|---|
| diffusion.txt2img | 478 | 17 (4%) |
| music.txt2music | 160 | 6 (4%) |
| video.txt2vid / img2vid | 3 | 0 |
| tts.synthesize | 16 | 14 (88%) |

Three independent causes, each proven from logs:

1. **Bids lost in transit.** bonita (fdxBAdC8) logged `dispatch: bid published` (publish returned Ok) for 57 of the gateway's diffusion offers in that hour. The gateway received **0** of them; every one of those auctions closed `count=0`. Another 33 bids failed outright with `NoPeersSubscribedToTopic` right after a restart. Gossip on dev2 is unstable: the seed logged 2,194 mDNS discoveries and 1,530 expiries in 20 minutes, and every expiry called `remove_explicit_peer`, while gossipsub ignores GRAFTs from explicit peers (`GRAFT: ignoring request from direct peer`). LAN peers flapped between explicit and not-meshed, and messages forwarded in the gap were dropped.
2. **Workers deaf after a restart.** The diffusion and music subscribers copied the *live* tag set once, at subscribe time. Those role tags are only advertised while the box is idle. dev2's image worker restarted into v0.2.90 mid-render (`advertising capabilities tags=["c0mpute:cpu"]`) and then refused every offer as `not eligible (missing capabilities) missing=["c0mpute:role:diffusion", ...]` for the next 50 minutes, until its next restart.
3. **Capable nodes gated out.** Open bids held a slot for the full 60 s bid TTL, so a node that lost two auctions without hearing the accept logged `at capacity, not bidding` with every slot free (122 times on bonita in an hour). CPU video required `min_cpu_threads = 16` against a per-job budget of half the cores, so a 16-core box never qualified. And a `/v1/videos` request with the defaults (81 frames, 30 steps, 1280x704) failed every CPU node's `fits` filter (max 33 frames, 20 steps, 480x272), so it could never get a bid.

## What changes

**Delivery**
- New `c0mpute.direct.v1` RPC service in `c0mpute-net` (`Libp2pNetwork::send_direct`). The receiver re-emits the message on its local gossip stream, with `source` = the noise-authenticated caller. Existing consumers (buyer, dispatch, aggregator) work unchanged and `source_matches_claim` still holds. Only `c0mpute/jobs/*` topics; never to self. Old nodes answer `not served here` and gossip still carries the message.
- Bids, accepts and receipts go both direct and on gossip. Either one arriving is enough. Duplicates are dropped (bids by bidder, accepts by job id).
- `JobOffer` gains optional `buyer_addrs` (public dialable addrs, filtered by `dialable_buyer_addrs` on the worker) and `bid_window_ms`. Both are wire-compatible.
- mDNS peers stay explicit until their last connection closes, instead of flapping on every record expiry. `flood_publish(true)` is set explicitly. `C0MPUTE_DISABLE_MDNS=1` keeps a node off LAN discovery. Tests run beside live workers need this: with direct bids, `auction_e2e` was otherwise won by a production node.
- Buyer re-publishes a silent offer once at half window; a worker that already bid re-sends the same bid without reserving more.

**Bidding on everything the node can do**
- Diffusion, music and CPU-video subscribers always carry their workload's role and model tags; the offer filter stays the live gate.
- A bid reserves capacity for the buyer's window plus 10 s, not 60 s. A late accept is still honoured and the runner queues it.
- `[video] min_cpu_threads` defaults to 8 (was 16).
- The gateway clips `wan2.1-t2v-1.3b` text-to-video requests to the CPU caps (keeping orientation), the same way songs are clipped to their model.

**Buyers do not fail on transient misses**
- Gateway bid window: 6 s for images, songs and video, 4 s for speech.
- Every workload re-auctions with backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, then 15 s) while nobody bids. Speech, OCR and embeddings retry for up to 20 s, video 60 s; images (4 min) and songs (8 min) keep their existing waits.
- `GET /v1/auctions` on the gateway: per-workload auctions, success rate and bids over the last hour.

**Restart churn**
- `c0mpute_update::draining()`: once an update is installed, the node waits a random 0 to 120 s, then stops bidding and waits for running jobs to finish (the drain existed, but no job ever held a `LongJob`, so it never waited). Workers register `activity::running_jobs` as the busy probe. Gateway requests hold a `LongJob`.

**Canary**
- The status aggregator sends one tiny offer per workload (tts, image, song, CPU video) every 10 min. It counts the bids, accepts nothing, and notes how many nodes advertised the workload at that moment. The result goes into the status JSON as `network.auction_canary`, including `capable_success_rate`, the rate to hold above 95%. Set `C0MPUTE_CANARY_SECS=0` to turn it off.

## Tests

New tests cover: direct send without a mesh (plus refusal of non-job topics and sends to self), the direct body codec, bid reservation following the offer window, the `/p2p` strip, workload tags, auction stats and canary rates, probe specs passing the workers' own validation, the CPU video clip, the backoff schedule, and the update stagger.

body:
Takeover phase: build new features

## What changes
Navigation (drive, walk, bus) is now screen-only: no spoken guidance, no vibration, no mute button.

- Deletes `lib/nav/announce.ts` and its tests.
- Removes the cue effects from `MapShell` and the mute button from `PilotView` and `BusPilotView`.
- Updates `SPEC-pilot.md` and `SPEC-web-app.md` to match.

Unchanged: banners, rerouting, arrival, stamps and trip stats, and the game's sound effects (`sfx`, `SoundToggle`), which are a separate opt-in system.

A device that used mute keeps an unread `hakuba:pilot-muted` key in `localStorage`. It is harmless, so there is no cleanup code.

## Alternative dropped
Hiding the button and silencing the calls was smaller, but it would leave unused timing code and tests that imply the feature still exists. Git keeps the old logic if voice comes back.

## Evidence
CI does not run e2e, so these are local results.

The new e2e test walks a whole route and records every speak and vibrate call.

**Before the change, it failed as intended** (`E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3217 pnpm exec playwright test e2e/pilot.spec.ts -g "screen-only" --workers=1`):
```
+   "say: In 50 metres, turn right.",
+   "vibrate",
+   "say: Turn right. Now.",
...
+   "say: You've arrived.",
1 failed
```

**After the change:**
| Command (in `apps/web`) | Result |
|---|---|
| `E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3217 pnpm exec playwright test e2e/pilot.spec.ts --workers=1` | 14 passed |
| `pnpm test` | 42 files, 392 tests passed |
| `pnpm typecheck` | passed |
| `pnpm exec biome check .` | no errors, 11 warnings (`noNonNullAssertion`, `noExplicitAny`) |
| `git grep` for `speechSynthesis`, `navigator.vibrate`, `onToggleMute`, `pilot-muted` in `src` and `tests` | no matches |

A Playwright phone-sized run of the navigation screen found one button, "Exit navigation".

After merging the latest `main`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` were re-run and passed. That merge brought in backend and docs changes only, so e2e was not repeated.

A reviewer with no context on this work checked the diff. It found no regressions and one leftover, the mute button still listed in `SPEC-pilot.md`. That is fixed, along with its three smaller suggestions.

author: lucassardenbergl
body:
## O que muda

Pacote J da 3ª revisão do Radar (privacidade/LGPD, 1º do Top 3 do Codex). Corrige três problemas:

1. **O CPF completo do titular de MEI saía para o app.** A razão social de MEI termina no CPF. Em prod são 122.077 linhas, e a razão crua aparecia na ficha, na lista (`radar_lista` devolve `SETOF radar_empresas`), no "prospectar hoje", na rota, nos e-mails, nas tarefas, no CSV e no PostgREST direto.
2. **A exclusão de sócio não resistia à recarga mensal.**
3. **Notas livres sobre pessoas ficavam guardadas para sempre.**

### O desenho: gravar mascarado, não mascarar cada saída

A razão de MEI passa a ser **gravada** como `FULANO DE TAL ***456789**`, no formato do QSA da RFB (dígitos 4 a 9). Dois triggers BEFORE fazem isso na entrada, para qualquer escritor: um no staging (`radar_empresas_carga`) e outro na foto (`radar_empresas`).

- Toda saída de hoje e de amanhã já nasce sem o CPF. Por isso **nenhuma RPC de leitura foi recriada**, e `radar_lista` continua sendo da sessão N.
- Mascarar já no staging mantém o "só o que difere" da publicação em passos (invariante da sessão K).
- A busca por nome continua igual. Buscar pelos 11 dígitos deixa de achar o MEI, de propósito.
- O valor da Receita fica em `private.radar_razao_receita`. Só a RPC `radar_razao_social_para_cadastro` o lê, porque o cadastro no Omie precisa da razão fiscal com o CPF. A RPC tem o gate do cadastro (gestor/master) e registra cada leitura.
- O front do cadastro busca a razão fiscal logo antes de chamar a edge, e é fail-closed: razão mascarada nunca segue para o Omie (`escolherRazaoFiscal`).
- A **edge `omie-vendas-sync` v1.33** também recusa o sufixo mascarado. Isso protege a aba que ainda está num build velho.
- O vínculo societário e o aviso de crédito usavam só a MÁSCARA do CPF (medido: só 2 funções e 2 índices em prod). Essas 2 funções foram recriadas por **substituição textual mínima** do corpo de prod (md5 conferido, molde TRAVA → PRE → CREATE → PÓS): o regex passou a aceitar as duas formas. Resultado: as decisões são idênticas antes, durante e depois do backfill.

### Exclusão de titular e retenção

- A tabela `radar_exclusoes_titular` guarda raiz, escopo, finalidade e o histórico dos pedidos. O registro é pela RPC `radar_exclusao_registrar` (só master).
- A exclusão vale na ingestão (staging e foto) e é reaplicada de hora em hora.
- Escopo `qsa`: os nomes dos sócios saem da ficha e da prospecção.
- Escopo `contato`: além disso, e-mail e telefone são zerados, o lead é descartado (`lgpd_oposicao`) e não pode ser reaberto, e as notas livres são apagadas.
- O cron `radar-privacidade-expurgo` (de hora em hora):
  - anula a nota livre de lead descartado há mais de 12 meses (a nota automática, do usuário de sistema, fica);
  - termina o backfill em fatias de 10 mil;
  - apaga o cru órfão e o registro de acesso com mais de 12 meses.

  Cada execução vai para o ledger `acoes_execucoes`, inclusive quando dá erro.
- Base legal e prazos estão em `docs/historico/radar-privacidade-pacote-j-2026-11-09.md`.

### ✅ Decidido pelo founder (2026-11-09): manter conservador

A exclusão **não** toca o vínculo nem o aviso de crédito. O QSA mascarado continua sendo usado, só no servidor. A revisão provou que filtrar a raiz no vínculo apagava o aviso de um devedor, e a proteção do crédito é base legal própria (LGPD art. 7º X). Este foi o padrão conservador do money-path. Para estender a exclusão ao vínculo, basta um `NOT EXISTS` em `ocorr` de `private.radar_vinculos_base` (detalhe no histórico).

## Prova

- **`db/test-radar-privacidade-j.sh`** (PG17, migrations reais da cadeia do vínculo, lote de sócios carregado pelas RPCs da carga, migration aplicada 2×): **30 asserts**, entrou no núcleo do CI (`db/nucleo-ci.txt`, `30 falsificar=14`).
  - **E1/E2:** a foto INTEIRA do vínculo, do aviso de crédito e da guarda de homônimo é igual com a razão crua, com a migration sobre a crua e depois do backfill.
  - **P1:** o UPDATE do passo da publicação não reescreve MEI que não mudou (0 linhas).
  - **M\*:** a razão é mascarada por qualquer escritor. Uma varredura de catálogo mostra que só a RPC do cadastro lê o cru.
  - **X\*:** a exclusão resiste ao staging e ao upsert crus, e o lead não pode ser reaberto.
  - **R\*:** retenção pelo autor da nota, não pelo texto. O erro do job vai para o ledger.
  - **U1:** `updated_at` não é tocado, porque o contato contábil (K2) o lê.
  - **G\*:** ACL.
- **Falsificação:** controle verde e cada sabotagem vermelha no assert dela, em `LC_ALL=C` e em `pt_BR.UTF-8`.
- Vitest `cadastro-omie` 57/57 · Deno `omie-vendas-sync` 89/89 · `sonda:bump` · `sonda:fingerprint` · `edges:typecheck` · `edges:sintaxe` · `typecheck:app` · `audit:migrations` · `wt:preflight` 🟡 (evolução serial de funções já commitadas).
- **Codex: desenho=? · código=? · extra=nenhum** — `sem-codex: cota` (`codex-async.sh` saiu 79: 90% contra teto de 85%, a janela reabre em 11/11). Segui o Caminho B: régua escrita e revisão adversarial independente (subagente sem as minhas conclusões).
  - **P1** — aba velha cadastraria MEI mascarado no Omie: corrigido.
  - **P2** — eram três, todos corrigidos:
    - a publicação reescreveria 122 mil MEI todo mês;
    - o vendedor lia o cru;
    - a exclusão derrubava o aviso de crédito.
  - **P3** — corrigidos ou documentados no histórico.
  - Gastar a reserva do Codex é decisão do founder.

## ⚠️ Deploy: 3 camadas manuais, NESTA ordem (merge ≠ produção)

1. **Edge `omie-vendas-sync` v1.33** (💬 Lovable): deploy da edge. Sem pré-condição de banco.
2. **Publish** do front: o cadastro passa a buscar a razão fiscal pela RPC. Antes da migration, cai no PGRST202 e usa a exibida, que ainda é a crua.
3. **Migration `20261111150000_radar_privacidade_titular_mei.sql`, fora do horário comercial.** Os `CREATE INDEX` seguram escrita em `radar_empresas` por alguns segundos.
   - Caminho: `cd /Users/lucassardenberg/Projetos/afiacao/.claude/worktrees/radar-carga-mensal-15d4b4 && bun run db:aplicar supabase/migrations/20261111150000_radar_privacidade_titular_mei.sql`, ou o SQL Editor envolvendo em `BEGIN; … COMMIT;`.
   - O backfill corre sozinho pelo cron, em ~13 rodadas. Para acelerar, rode `SELECT public.radar_privacidade_expurgo();` até `razoes_cruas_restantes = 0`.

A carga (`scripts/radar/carga.ts`) não muda. Combinado com as sessões K e N.

### Validação pós-apply (read-only)

```sql
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgname IN ('trg_radar_privacidade','trg_radar_carga_privacidade')) = 2 AS triggers_ok,
  (SELECT md5(prosrc) FROM pg_proc WHERE oid = 'private.radar_vinculos_base(text[],boolean,boolean)'::regprocedure) = '0de269faec15688b274b9085b49dfb53' AS regras_ok,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cron.job WHERE jobname = 'radar-privacidade-expurgo' AND active) AS job_ok,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.radar_empresas WHERE razao_social ~ ' [0-9]{11}$') AS razoes_cruas_restantes;
```

Esperado: `t | t | t | 0` (o último zera depois do backfill).

body: ## Was und warum Wer bar an Privatkunden verkauft, etwa am Marktstand, brauchte bisher eine künstliche „Sammelrechnung“, um die Tagessumme ins Kassenbuch zu bekommen (Kommentar von Hottzenn in #276; ebenso #455, Punkt „Bareinnahme ohne spätere Rechnung“). Unter **Kasse › Eintragen** gibt es jetzt die Art **Bareinnahme ohne Rechnung**: - **Betrag** brutto, **Datum** der Bareinnahme, **Umsatzsteuer** und **Notiz** (Pflicht, sie ist ohne Rechnung der Nachweis), einzeln oder als Tagessumme. - **Fortlaufende Nummer und Storno wie bisher:** eine Zeile im Kassenbuch, sofort gebucht und festgeschrieben; Storno als Gegenzeile mit heutigem Datum und Gegenbuchung, mit derselben Behandlung. - Kassenbestand und die GoBD-Sperren der Kasse bleiben unverändert (nur anhängen, Bestand nie negativ, Sperre der Kasse vor den Buchungen). ### Steuerbehandlung | Umsatzsteuer | Buchung SKR03 (SKR04) | Voranmeldung | EÜR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Regulär 19 % | 1000 (1600) an 8400 (4400) und 1776 (3806) | Kz 81 | steuerpflichtig netto, vereinnahmte USt | | Regulär 7 % | 1000 (1600) an 8300 (4300) und 1771 (3801) | Kz 86 | ebenso | | Kleinunternehmer | 1000 (1600) an 8195 (4185) | – | Kleinunternehmer | | steuerfrei § 4 Nr. 8 bis 29 | 1000 (1600) an 8100 (4100) | Kz 48 | umsatzsteuerfrei | - **Zeitpunkt:** am Tag der Bareinnahme, bei Ist- wie bei Soll-Versteuerung, Steuer sofort fällig. Das ist dieselbe Regel wie bei „Direkt buchen“ auf eine Kategorie im Bankabgleich (`packages/core/src/direkt-kategorie.ts`): keine Rechnungspflicht gegenüber Privatkunden (§ 14 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 2 UStG), die Steuer entsteht mit der Leistung (§ 13 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 UStG), und beim Barverkauf fallen Leistung und Zahlung zusammen. - **Kleinunternehmer** (§ 19 UStG): Geprüft wird der Stand am Ende des Monats der Bareinnahme, wie die Voranmeldung ihn liest. Kleinunternehmer können keine 19 % oder 7 % wählen, andere keine Kleinunternehmer-Buchung. - **Steuerfrei** nur für § 4 Nr. 8 bis 29 UStG (ohne Vorsteuerabzug, Kz 48, Erlöskonto wie bei einer Rechnung mit der Behandlung „steuerfrei“). Innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung und Ausfuhr (§ 4 Nr. 1) brauchen Rechnung und Nachweise und bleiben bei den Rechnungen. **Quellen:** `gesetze-im-internet.de` war aus dem Container nicht erreichbar (503), dejure.org und buzer.de ebenso nicht. Ich konnte den Wortlaut von § 13 und § 14 UStG deshalb nicht neu nachlesen. Die Angaben stützen sich auf die Quellen, die im Code schon stehen (`direkt-kategorie.ts`, `legacy-vat.ts`: Kz 48 für § 4 Nr. 8 bis 28). Ob § 4 Nr. 29 in Kz 48 gehört und ob die steuerfreie Bareinnahme so gewollt ist, bitte prüfen; bisher lehnte „Direkt buchen“ steuerfreie Einnahmen ohne Rechnung ab. ### Umsetzung - Kern: `packages/core/src/bareinnahme.ts` (Prüfung, Buchung, Netto/Steuer, Summen wie eine Rechnung mit einem Satz). - Tabelle `cash_entries`: neue Art `einnahme`, neue Spalten `tax_treatment`, `tax_rate` (nur zusammen und nur bei `einnahme`, Check `cash_entries_einnahme`). Keine Spalte einer versiegelten Tabelle umbenannt oder umgerechnet; neue Spalten sind laut `docs/architektur.md` unkritisch. - Server: `modules/bank/cash-income.ts`; der Storno nutzt den vorhandenen Weg der Bareinnahme auf Rechnungen (Gegenbuchung aus den Zeilen der ursprünglichen Buchung), umbenannt in `reverseBookedCashEntry`. - Voranmeldung (`vat-figures.ts`): Quelle `kasse` mit Link ins Kassenbuch; EÜR (`reports.ts`): wie eine bezahlte Rechnung mit einem Satz. - Kassenbuch und CSV: Art „Bareinnahme“, neue letzte Spalte „Steuer“. Refs #276, #455 ## Migration - `0178_kasse_bareinnahme.sql` (per `bun run db:generate`); keine Trigger nötig (Sperre, Audit und Siegel der Kasse gelten schon). Zuerst als `0176` erzeugt; nach dem Merge von #473 (dort `0176`/`0177`) habe ich den Branch auf `main` gesetzt und sie als `0178` neu erzeugt. ## Screenshots Testdaten: Einlage 200,00 € „Wechselgeld“, dazu nachher eine Bareinnahme 342,50 € „Weihnachtsmarkt, Tagessumme“ mit 19 %. | | Vorher | Nachher | | --- | --- | --- | | Formular, hell, Desktop | | | | Formular, hell, Handy | | | | Formular, dunkel, Desktop | | | | Formular, dunkel, Handy | | | | Kassenbuch, hell, Desktop | | | | Kassenbuch, hell, Handy | | | | Kassenbuch, dunkel, Desktop | | | | Kassenbuch, dunkel, Handy | | | ## Wie geprüft - `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, `zensical build --strict` - `TEST_DATABASE_URL=… bun run test` (PostgreSQL 16 im Container), auf dem Stand nach dem Rebase auf `main` mit #473: 369 Testdateien grün, 4276 Tests bestanden, 126 übersprungen - Neu und zuerst rot: - `packages/core/src/bareinnahme.test.ts`: Buchung SKR03 und SKR04 für 19 %, 7 %, Kleinunternehmer, steuerfrei und Storno; Prüfung gegen den Kleinunternehmer-Stand. - `modules/bank/cash-income.test.ts` (Postgres): SKR03 und SKR04 mit Ist und Soll (Salden, Sperre, Siegel, Kz 81, EÜR und Anlage EÜR, DATEV, Abgleich Journal gegen Voranmeldung und EÜR, Integritätsprüfung, Kassenbuch, CSV, Storno im Folgemonat); 7 % in Kz 86 und steuerfrei in Kz 48; Kleinunternehmer; Ablehnungen; Check in der Datenbank. - Playwright: neuer Test in `e2e/rechnungen.spec.ts` (Bareinnahme mit 7 %, Pflicht-Notiz, angebotene Behandlungen, axe am Desktop und Handy, Storno). Durchläufe `rechnungen` und `rueckfragen` lokal mit dem gebauten Server wie in der CI

body:
## 🎯 What problem does this PR solve?

- `workflow-security.yml` installs `zizmor==1.27.0`, a release PyPI has yanked for GHSA-f42p-wjw5-97qh, so the workflow audit runs on a version withdrawn for a security advisory.

## 📝 How does it solve it?

- Bumps `ZIZMOR_VERSION` in `.github/workflows/workflow-security.yml` from `1.27.0` to `1.32.0`, the current release. Nothing else changes; the install, SARIF and annotation steps all read the variable.

## 🧪 How was it tested?

- `node .github/scripts/lint-workflows.mjs .github/workflows/workflow-security.yml`: structural gate clean.
- `zizmor --persona=regular --offline .github/` on this branch with both versions. The highest severity is "high" either way, so the shadow-mode outcome is unchanged. Count changes by rule:
  - `self-repository` (new audit, low): 0 → 619
  - `dangerous-triggers`: 11 → 12
  - `template-injection`: 285 → 272
  - Totals: 1803 → 2423 findings (1021 → 1034 suppressed); high 261 → 262, medium 390 → 390, low 66 → 685.

author: manzke
body:
Three customer reports from a 5.6.4 installation running under `/ihub`. The backport for 5.6.5 is intrafind/ihub-apps#3504, into the new `release/5.6.x`, which points at v5.6.4.

## 1. Chat from the start page lands on `/ihub/ihub/apps/<id>`

This is a bug, not configuration. The start page hands the message to the app with `?prefill=…&send=true` (and `?model=…`). `AppChat` then removes those parameters with

```js
navigate(`${window.location.pathname}?${newSearch}`, { replace: true });
```

`window.location.pathname` already contains `/ihub`, and React Router adds its `basename` again. The router ends up on `/ihub/apps/<id>`, which is `/ihub/ihub/apps/<id>` in the browser and shows "not found".

The same code path also runs for links carrying `?model=` / `?style=` / `?outfmt=` / `?history=` / `?var_…`, for "Open in App" document links (`?documentId=…`), and in `AppCanvas`. All four call sites now change only the query: `navigate({ search }, { replace: true })`. The code is identical in v5.6.4, the v5.6.5 RCs and main.

## 2. Upload button only visible after turning on magic prompt

`ChatInput` and the `+` menu (`ChatInputActionsMenu`) each decide on their own whether upload is the *only* quick action. If it is, the menu renders the paper clip itself and the input bar hides its own. In 5.6.4 the menu counted web search and the input bar did not. So for an app with upload plus web search, and no magic prompt, microphone or tools, the bar hid the paper clip and the menu kept it in its phone-only section. On a desktop the button was nowhere. Turning on magic prompt made two quick actions, so the bar showed it again.

The web-search case was already fixed on main when the integrations picker landed (#2923, first in v5.6.5-RC3). One variant remained: the browser extension's "Include page" toggle (host context toggles), which the menu counts and `ChatInput` did not. `ChatInput` now counts it too.

## 3. Logo broken in the sidebar, header and start page

`buildAssetUrl` added the base path to every non-http asset URL:
- A logo URL that already holds the base path (`/ihub/uploads/assets/logo.png`, the address the browser shows) became `/ihub/ihub/…`. Behind a proxy that strips the prefix this loads by accident; behind one that forwards `/ihub/...` unchanged it is a 404.
- A `data:image/…` logo became `/ihub/data:…`, broken on every installation.

The default logo and `/uploads/assets/…` (what the Asset Manager shows) were fine. Complete URLs (`https:`, `data:image/`, `blob:`, `//`) and paths already under the base path are now used as they are. The rule lives in the new `client/src/utils/assetUrl.js` so it can be tested without `import.meta`. The sign-in screen (`auth-gate.js`) skips the prefix in the same case.

## Changes
- `client/src/features/apps/pages/AppChat.jsx`, `client/src/features/canvas/pages/AppCanvas.jsx`: query-only navigations.
- `client/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.jsx`: single-action check includes the embedded host's context toggles.
- `client/src/utils/assetUrl.js` (new), `client/src/utils/runtimeBasePath.js`, `client/src/auth-gate/auth-gate.js`: asset URLs.
- `docs/releases/next/fixes.md`: three entries. The paper clip entry also covers the web-search case, which had no entry yet.

## Tests
- `tests/unit/client/app-chat-base-path.test.jsx`: the real `AppChat` under `MemoryRouter basename="/ihub"`, with the address bar at `/ihub/apps/acme?prefill=…&send=true`. It checks that the message is sent and the router stays on `/apps/acme`. It also has a source guard against `navigate(window.location.pathname…)`. All 3 tests fail on the old code.
- `tests/unit/client/chat-input-attach-button.test.jsx`: the real `ChatInput` and `+` menu, asserting that an "Attach File" button is shown at `md:` width for upload only, upload + web search, upload + web search + magic prompt, and upload in a host with context toggles. Against the v5.6.4 components, the web-search and host-toggle cases fail. Against main before this change, the host-toggle case fails.

body:
drip no longer decides when an agent notifies you. Each recipe is a README with the hook snippet inline, and you copy it into your agent's settings.

**Review (about 15 min):**

1. Read `recipes/README.md` and `recipes/permission-cards/README.md` (3 min).
2. Read `docs/agents.md`, the reference for the `drip hook` flags, `drip watching` and `DRIP_HOOK` (4 min).
3. Skim the Swift diff: `Hook.swift` (`Policy`), `Focus.swift` (`Watching`), `Remote.swift` (filter in the queue), and the removal of `Setup.swift` and `SetupCommand` (8 min).

What changed:

1. `drip setup` is gone, with its merge code, backups and tests. The zsh block is now the `zsh-slow-commands` recipe. `drip remote-hook` prints the remote script.
2. Recipes are `recipes/<name>/README.md` with a JSON block per agent, the settings file it goes in, and how to merge it by hand. The separate snippet files are deleted. No text tells you to clone the repo.
3. New flags: `--approve`, `--min-turn SECONDS`, `--only needs-you`. New command: `drip watching` (exit 0 watching, 1 not, 2 cannot tell). `--min-turn` and `--only` go through the remote queue.
4. Removed: `agent_cards`, `done_after`, `approve`, `DRIP_AGENT_CARDS`, `DRIP_DONE_AFTER`, `DRIP_APPROVE`. `DRIP_HOOK` stays.
5. README, docs and site pages say the same, for any reader.

Evidence: `swift test` passes (630 tests), a release build has no recipe text (`strings` finds none), and the CI checks pass.

Risk: one-way door - pre-release, so the removed commands and settings have no users to break. Blast radius: the agent hooks of anyone on an earlier build.

Adds [Standard Compute](https://standardcompute.com) as a remote language model provider, the same way as Runcrate (#779) and Opper (#773).

body:
This adds direct TS-890S KNS Ethernet control, receive audio and spectrum/waterfall support to AetherSDR, without USB or a companion server.

Included receive functionality:

- Frequency entry and existing tuning gestures, plus native FC/UD relative tuning.
- Native scope spans and Center, Fixed and Auto-scroll modes.
- Radio-reported meters, mode/filter controls and receive DSP, including CW APF.
- Network login, scoped credentials, reconnect and teardown handling.

The implementation stays focused on TS-890S integration. Necessary shared changes use neutral capability/model interfaces, with the new behavior enabled by Kenwood. Existing radios retain their established behavior, with targeted isolation regressions.

**Experimental limits**

TX implementation and testing are deferred. Native memories are unsupported, and transverter operation is deferred.

Advanced setup pages, filter-bank resets, network audio levels, AGC/receiver options and TCI/CAT/rigctl/recording remain software-tested but hardware-unverified. Native meters report display deflection in dots; no calibrated S-unit or dBm conversion is claimed.

**Validation**

Tested on a TS-890S running firmware 1.01 and an Apple Silicon Mac:

- Native app and daemon builds, documentation and static checks passed.
- Selected regression and ASan/UBSan suites passed; leak detection was disabled.
- All eight native scope spans passed settled zoom-button checks.
- A 12-minute RX run completed with 12 tuning/restoration cycles and two reconnects.
- Both reconnects recovered native tuning, scope and captured playback audio within seven seconds.
- Final RX settings were verified restored, followed by clean application shutdown.

No transmit or power operations were tested. Cross-platform CI and maintainer review remain required. Review of the shared integration boundaries and preservation of existing-radio behavior would be especially welcome.

**Current integration status**

Merged upstream `505b9172cf240db3ce017299005b4b2a9474db92` in signed commit `16d9867c993af10e207d05935328b2cdf4f47d6b`, resolving all 11 conflicted files without rebasing. GitHub reports the branch as mergeable. Upstream TCI volume/AGC behavior remains the default; the TS-890S client dialect stays explicitly gated. Upstream CW-text, ATU and test additions are retained.

The merged source builds the native M5 app and daemon. All nine affected regression suites, documentation and static checks pass. The four architecture gates pass on both upstream and merged source with no new warning records. The proposal retains the same 220 changed paths against upstream.

A separate post-merge candidate connected to firmware 1.01, completed its acknowledged native-context survey and recorded 93 connected RX samples over 92.12 seconds. All 93 waterfall crops changed; three-stage preflight PCM was finite and nonzero. The operator instructed “consider 12min test as passed,” so the new timed run was stopped and its gate recorded as operator-accepted. No new 12-minute duration or tuning/reconnect cycles are claimed. The earlier full 12-minute results above remain evidence for pre-merge head `b12e1d20ebfc6cc4081a5a063be36be359e377bf`.

The post-merge entry RX baseline was verified unchanged and the owned app exited cleanly. No transmit or power requests were made. The disposition is recorded in documentation-only commit `84ce02ff`.

Required CI and maintainer review remain pending. Commits are SSH-signed locally; GitHub signing-key registration remains pending.

## [SID:56a8724f-adc6-4b29-9906-9b7bc4c6265f] 서버 명령 결과 카드가 보통 글과 같은 규칙으로 — 스레드 안에서 친 명령의 카드는 그 스레드에 · 방의 다른 참가자 화면에도 실시간 (story 4872)

4847 AC-명령 실시간(5463)을 검수하며 codex(내 자체 QA) · 까디르군 렌즈가 짚은 «원래부터 있던» 틈 둘. 5463이 만든 결함이 아님.

### 틈
1. 스레드 안에서 친 명령의 카드가 `thread_id` 없이 저장돼 **방 맨 위 글**로 섰고, 스레드의 `reply_count` · `last_reply_at`도 안 바뀌었다(`chat_command_catalog.py` 카드 생성).
2. 카드의 Event 행은 다른 참가자 몫으로 만들어졌지만 그들의 **실시간 push 목록은 버려져**(`try_execute_server_command`가 `_dispatch_conversation_event`의 반환을 안 씀), 열린 화면의 다른 사람에겐 «명령 친 줄»은 실시간으로 서고 **답 카드는 다시 열어야** 섰다.

### 바뀌는 것
- 카드에 `thread_id=msg.thread_id` — 명령을 친 글과 **같은 스레드**. 스레드의 `reply_count` · `last_reply_at`은 보통 전송과 **같은 한 곳**(`_bump_thread_counters`, 보통 전송도 이제 이 함수를 씀)으로 갱신.
- `try_execute_server_command(..., cards=list)` — 넘기면 카드를 직접 배달하지 않고 목록에 담아 `send_message`가 **친 글과 같은 받는 사람 계산**으로 배달(차단한 사람 · 차단된 에이전트 · 알림 설정으로 끈 사람 제외, commit 뒤 실시간 push, 친 사람 echo 다음에 친 사람에게도). 안 넘기는 다른 호출부는 예전 그대로.
- 일부러 **카드가 안 가는 곳 — 방의 에이전트**: 명령 줄 자체를 에이전트에게 안 보내는 «이중 집행 막기» 집합(서버가 이미 집행한 명령을 에이전트가 자연어로 한 번 더 하지 않게)과 **같은 집합**을 카드에도 쓴다. 카드만 가면 에이전트가 보지도 못한 명령의 결과에 반응하는 소음이 된다. (이전 동작은 카드가 에이전트에게도 갔음 — PO 판단으로 **의도된 변화**. 읽기 길에는 그대로 보임.)
- 일부러 **제외하지 않는 것**: 친 글이 Discord로 가는 사람 · 웹훅으로 가는 에이전트 — Discord/웹훅으로는 친 글만 나가고 카드는 안 나가므로 그들을 카드에서 빼면 카드를 어디서도 못 받는다(codex가 짚은 P2, 수정 + 시험). 예전(카드가 제외 없이 배달되던) 동작과도 같다.

### 검증
- `test_4847_command_card_live_realdb.py` **11칸**(PG16 · 실 HTTP 전송 · `_push_to_agent` 관찰): 친 사람에게 echo 다음 한 건 · 방의 다른 사람에게도 · 방 밖 0 · 보통 글은 카드 push 0 · 푸시한 카드 = 나중에 읽은 글과 같은 필드 · **스레드 안 명령 → 카드가 그 스레드에, `reply_count` 2, 푸시에도 `thread_id`** · 스레드 밖 명령은 최상위 · **차단한 사람 0**(07) · **Discord로 가는 사람도 카드를 받음**(08) · **방 알림 판정이 지목 안 한(끈) 사람 0**(09) · **방 알림 판정이 실패해도 차단한 사람 0**(10) · **방의 에이전트는 카드 배달에서 제외**(11 — 배달 호출이 받는 제외 집합을 봄; 에이전트에 결정적 커맨드를 받는 런타임(`hermes` — `claude-code`는 캐퍼빌리티 게이트가 이미 막아 변이가 살아남음)을 줘 캐퍼빌리티 게이트가 아니라 «서버 집행 이중 집행 막기» 규칙만이 빼는 상태로 격리. 시험은 `team_members`에 아무것도 쓰지 않는다 — 공유 baseline DB 규칙(`test_no_team_members_view_dml_in_tests`)대로 기존 헬퍼가 심는 members · 프로젝트 부여 · 프로필을 뷰가 보여준다. 로컬은 마이그레이션 head DB(`alembic upgrade head`, `team_members` = VIEW)로 돌려 확認).
- **변이 12/12 RED**(마이그레이션 head DB에서; 서버 집행 규칙의 에이전트 합집합만 뺀 변이 M5 포함): 카드 최상위 · 카운터 없음 · 다른 사람 배달 없음 · 제외 전부 없음 · Discord 제외 · **차단 집합만 뺌 · 알림 판정 집합만 뺌 · 에이전트 집합만 뺌**(렌즈가 짚은 빈칸 둘 + 하나) · 친 사람 push 없음 · 카탈로그가 직접 배달 · 카운터가 엉뚱한 루트.
- 관련 서버 시험: 명령 카탈로그 13 초록 · 이 맥의 로컬 PG(맨 테이블 `team_members`)에서 `test_2349` · `test_2263` 일부가 develop에서도 같은 13칸 빨강(환경 — 이 PR 변경 無, develop과 같은 실패 집합 확인; CI 샤드가 판정).
- codex 자체 QA(읽기 전용 · 로컬 머리 · 푸시 前) 네 판(이 줄 아래 둘은 앞의 두 판 · 셋째 `01a1c05c-bfa8-7f63-a174-d169344cb55e` = team_members 쓰기 걷은 머리에서 시험 11이 `claude-code`로는 캐퍼빌리티 게이트가 이미 빼서 아직 허술하다고 짚음 → `hermes`로 고침 + 그 규칙만 뺀 변이 M5): `01a1bfb2-5f84-77a3-a269-8b276745f54a` — 진짜 P2 하나(Discord/웹훅 사람이 카드를 못 받음) → 수정 · 시험 · 변이. `01a1c001-bb7e-7863-b02d-fafc64f36953`(렌즈 빈칸 둘 반영 뒤) — 시험 결함 둘: 에이전트 시험이 이주된 DB(뷰)에서 못 돎 + 에이전트가 이미 캐퍼빌리티 게이트로 빠져 변이가 살아남음 → 고침(위 11번). 생산 코드엔 문제 없음.
- 렌즈: 까디르군 — 1차(7569ec62d) 막는 0, 이 본문의 에이전트 한 줄 · 시험 빈칸 둘 반영 → 델타는 시험 09 · 10(과 11).

### 남은 것
- AC5 dev 한 판(스레드 안 명령 카드가 그 스레드에 서고 다른 사람 화면에도 다시 열기 없이 섬)은 dev에 오른 뒤.

body:
## Summary

Roadmap item k211 (placement operators), a slice: 4 shelf fits of the literature. The option `fit` of `packShelf` and of the strategy `shelf` gets the values `best-width`, `worst-width`, `best-area` and `worst-area`.

- `best-width` (Berkey 1987): the place with the least free width after the box.
- `worst-width`, `best-area` and `worst-area` (Jylänki 2010): the most free width, the least free area and the most free area.
- Each fit compares each place on each shelf: the floor after the last box, and the strip above a shorter box. A tie goes to the first place, from the top shelf.
- The default `shelf` has no `fit`, and its output does not change. The fits `next`, `first` and `best` do not change.

## Version

0.17.0. MINOR: the exported union `ShelfFit` gets 4 values, and the uniform draws of `packSpace` change. Before 1.0.0, a break raises MINOR. The queue of the open release PRs ends at 0.16.5, so this PR takes the next MINOR.

| Base configs, 3 levels | 3838 | 3910 |

| Meta configs, 1 level | 346878105010926668 | 384954775900465772 |
| Meta configs, 3 levels | 996982144242458314300 | 1094120309937641708140 |

The meta count with 3 levels goes above `10n ** 21n`. Thus the test reads it with the limit `10n ** 22n`, and it also checks that the old limit gives `null`.

- Typecheck of `tsconfig.test.json`: 0 errors.

- The size gate: each entry is within its budget. The main entry is at 87158 of 88064 bytes.

author: kejriwalmedhansh-bit
body:
Designed in 4 mockup rounds with the owner (9 Nov). The Dealo (Hubble) voucher card showed only rate, amounts and Buy; it now shows what the voucher is good for, from Hubble's own terms.

**Before buying** (shop card + product-search card)
- Icon row: where it works, reuse / one use, offers / no offers, validity, no refund. A fact shows only when one sentence says it plainly; a mixed sentence ("once offline; multiple times online") shows nothing.
- One box: **Things it can't pay for** (red, with a count) for 25 top shops, hand-picked in `data/hubble_card_notes.json`; each item quotes Hubble word for word and is dropped automatically if Hubble rewords. Other shops get no box (the icon row covers their key facts; owner found a grey 'Good to know' box confusing). The box opens a sheet with pictures + 'Read all of <shop>'s rules' folded away.

**After buying**
- No direct add-voucher link (234 of 262 online vouchers): Hubble's how-to steps one at a time with ← →. With a link (Myntra, AJIO, Amazon…): just the existing button, no steps.

**Checks**: `scripts/check_hubble_card_notes.py` against live Hubble: 50 items, 0 problems. Tests 333 passed. New event `Voucher Terms Opened` in the tracking plan.

Needs Karan deploy for the backend (no new env). Website ships on merge. Awaiting owner local test.
