author: adamyoucef-muzi
body:
## Objet

Remplace les templates provisoires de gestion des ingrédients par une liste et un formulaire accessibles.

## Traçabilité

- Story : S-02 — Gestion des ingrédients (allergènes, nutrition, coût)
- Tâche(s) : T-12
- Sprint : 1

## Ce qui a été fait

- `app/templates/ingredients/liste.html` : tableau sémantique (`thead`/`tbody`, `scope="col"`), toutes les colonnes du contrat, unités pour 100 g, valeurs numériques alignées, lien de modification sur le nom, formulaire de suppression avec libellé accessible, message si aucun allergène ou liste vide, erreur affichée avec `role="alert"`.
- `app/templates/ingredients/formulaire.html` : champs et noms du contrat inchangés, labels reliés aux champs, `inputmode="decimal"` pour accepter la virgule, `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` sur les champs en erreur, valeurs de `saisie` conservées, fieldset des allergènes, bouton « Enregistrer » et lien « Annuler », titres création/modification.
- `app/static/style.css` : section `/* Ingrédients */` pour l'alignement numérique, le libellé « Aucun », les actions du formulaire et la liste vide. Aucune nouvelle couleur, uniquement les variables existantes.
- Aucune route, aucun modèle et aucun test modifié.

## Tests

- [ ] Tests automatisés ajoutés ou mis à jour — sans objet : les tests S-02 existants couvrent déjà les deux écrans.
- [x] `pytest` passe en local — **64 passed**, dont **19/19** sur `tests/test_ingredients.py`.
- [x] Cas d'erreur couvert — nom obligatoire, nom en double, coût négatif, valeur non numérique, allergène inconnu, suppression d'un ingrédient utilisé dans une recette (409).
- [ ] Rapport de tests mis à jour (`docs/tests/`) — à faire lors de la clôture de S-02.

Comment vérifier à la main :

1. Lancer l'application : `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload`, puis ouvrir <http://127.0.0.1:8000/ingredients> après connexion.
2. Vérifier la liste : nom, coût, calories, protéines, glucides, lipides, allergènes, liens et boutons de suppression.
3. Créer un ingrédient : les 14 allergènes sont proposés ; saisir une valeur invalide (par exemple un coût négatif) et vérifier que les valeurs restent affichées avec le message d'erreur.
4. Modifier un ingrédient puis vérifier que les champs et les allergènes sont préremplis.
5. Supprimer un ingrédient utilisé dans une recette et vérifier le message de refus en 409.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Le comportement correspond aux critères d'acceptation de la story — contrat T-12 de l'issue #35 respecté (variables, champs, endpoints et liens).
- [ ] PR relue et approuvée par Younes
- [x] Documentation impactée mise à jour — aucune documentation impactée par T-12.
- [ ] Heures réelles reportées sur le board en face de l'estimation — à faire après merge (estimation : 1,5 h).

## Points d'attention pour le relecteur

- `app/static/style.css` est aussi modifié par T-09, mais dans une section distincte (`/* Connexion */` contre `/* Ingrédients */`). Le merge devrait être automatique ; en cas de conflit, conserver les deux sections.
- Les attributs `required` et `inputmode` sont des aides côté navigateur. La validation serveur reste la référence, et les tests postent directement sur les routes.
- Les valeurs flottantes restent affichées telles quelles (`364.0`, par exemple). Un formatage plus fin (entiers sans `.0`, virgule française) pourra être une amélioration ultérieure si l'équipe le souhaite.
- La liste vide possède un message dédié mais n'est pas couverte par un test automatisé ; le comportement reste volontairement simple.

author: vinbaccelli
body:
Based on `main`, independent of the other PRs. Draft, not for merge.

## Coach request
With the data column box visible, every drawing that produced a measurement popped a "Name this measurement" question ("asked 1000 times"). Wanted workflow: click the **+** after a drawing, and only then be asked whether to add that last drawing to the column.

## Change (`app/analysis/page.tsx` + `lib/columnPrompt.ts`)
- `onMeasurementCommit` (angle, arrow angle, distance) and the ruler's `onMeasurement` no longer open the naming modal; they only **remember** the last measurement (one slot: a newer drawing replaces the older).
- The column's **+** (the HTML button under the column, and the canvas's `onMeasurementAdd`) first asks about the last drawing, using the existing naming prompt with the same default names and the Add / Skip buttons; with nothing waiting it opens the manual note prompts exactly as before.
- The **+** turns blue when a drawing is waiting, and its tooltip/label says "Add your last drawing to the column".
- Not changed: the Angle Differential flow (it captures the next two arrows on purpose, no modal, as before), the naming prompt itself, the column contents, the auto AI Detect measurements.

## Behaviour to know
The remembered drawing stays until you use the + or draw another; if the column is hidden and shown again, the last drawing is still waiting. Undoing the drawing does not clear it (the prompt would still offer its value); say if you want that tied to undo.

## Verification
`tsc` 0 errors; `npm test` 472 pass / 0 fail (+4 in `tests/columnPrompt.test.ts`: naming defaults, the + decision, and two source guards on the wiring). No existing test changed.

## NOT tested
In a browser or on a phone: the drawing flow needs the data column and a measuring tool, and I could not drive that in the phone emulation. The change is small and type-checked, but please try it.

## Manual test (iPhone, preview of this PR)
1. Metrics → show the data column.
2. Draw an angle or an arrow angle (several): no popup should appear; the column's **+** turns blue.
3. Tap **+**: the naming prompt for the **last** drawing appears; Add puts it in the column, Skip drops it.
4. With no drawing waiting, **+** opens the manual note as before.

author: oorabona
body:
Closes #905.

`lasterm session list` printed every session with an empty STATE column and the host's id under HOST. `cmdSessionList` read `state` and `host_label`, but `GET /api/sessions` answers `id`, `host_id`, `status`, `created_at` and `updated_at` (`rowToSession`), with no label.

## Change

- STATE reads `status`, as the hub sends it. Every session the hub returns is still listed, in its order.
- HOST shows the host's label, resolved with one `GET /api/hosts`, as `host remove` already does. A session whose host is not listed keeps its `host_id`.
- That request is made only for a non-empty table: `--json` prints the sessions answer unchanged and makes no second request, nor does an empty list.

The label is resolved, not dropped: the issue names the id as the defect, and a ULID (26 characters) does not fit the 20-wide column.

## Rest of the class

Every other `lasterm` command that reads `/api/*` was checked against its route: `status` (`/api/health`: `status`), `host add` (`label`, `id`), `host list` (fixed in #906), `host remove` (`label`, `id`), `pair` (`code`, `expires_at`; `token` on verify), `stop` (`others` on 409) and `quit` (`others`, `message`). None reads a field its route does not send.

## Tests

`packages/hub/src/cli.spec.ts`, `session list (#905)`: `main(["session", "list"])` against a TLS peer holding the pinned key that answers `/api/sessions` and `/api/hosts` by path (404 otherwise) with rows shaped as the hub builds them, and records the requests.

- The table: labels, the unmatched host's id, statuses, and the exact requests (sessions, then hosts). Red on `main` with the issue's output (STATE empty, host ids), green with the fix.
- `--json`: the answer unchanged, one request.
- An empty list: `No active sessions.`, one request.
- Fixture ids are 26-character ULIDs, so a change in a column width fails the table test.

## Reviews

Gate review (Claude) and codex-review: both CLEAN, no blocking finding. Taken: the fixture ids were 27 characters, so no data row was padded and a width mutation passed; they are now ULID-shaped.

Not taken, with the trigger that would make each real:
- **Closed sessions listed although the help says "active"; rows never deleted** (both reviews): older than this change, now visible because STATE shows `closed`. Filed as #911, which decides between a filter and pruning.
- **Labels from the SSH config import can hold control characters, printed raw** (both): only an authenticated client can import one, and it can already run terminals as the hub's user. `host list` prints them the same way.
- **All hosts fetched to resolve labels** (both): one loopback request per command, as `host remove` makes; it would matter with a host catalog large enough to slow that request.
- **A failing `GET /api/hosts` fails the command** (gate): as in `host remove`; it needs a hub that answers sessions but not hosts.
- **Long labels push STATE out of line; labels may contain spaces** (gate): the fixed widths predate this change, and `--json` is the format for scripts.

No Store news: the Store package exposes no `lasterm` command, and #906, the same fix for `host list`, had none.

author: darbymanning
body:
Replaces the name label above a hovered block, and the toolbar that moved with each block, with one floating bar in one place: top centre, below any site header and clear of the edit bar's panel.

**What the bar points at**
- Until a block is clicked, it offers the page's top-level block being read, once scrolling settles. The line that decides this runs down the window as the page scrolls, so short first and last blocks get a turn.
- A clicked block keeps the bar while it's in the window. If it scrolls right out, the bar goes back to the block being read, and the selection and settings stay as they are.
- Scrolling never changes the bar during a drag, a running action, with the add menu open, or with the pointer or keyboard focus on it.
- Using a button on an offered block selects it, as clicking would.

**Outlines**
- The label is gone. Hovering still shows the thin outline, so you can see what a click will pick, including nested blocks.
- The block the bar is offering gets the same thin outline. A clicked block keeps its own. Other people's coloured frames are unchanged.

**Tooltips**
The bar's icon buttons and drag handle use the edit bar's tooltip style instead of `title`. The name has a fixed width, so the buttons stay put as the block changes.

Checked by mounting the real bar and overlay on a test page: scrolling down and back, clicking a nested block, the selected block leaving and returning, deselecting, typing in text, hover holding the bar and releasing it, and the tooltips.

author: fametrano
body:
A hand-built `MiniscriptDescriptor` whose miniscript's text is a descriptor function's, such as `pk(K)`, `pkh(K)`, `multi(1,K,K2)` or `rawpkh(H)`, wrote a `wsh()` that `parse` read back as a `PkDescriptor`, `PkhDescriptor`, `MultiDescriptor` or `RawPkhDescriptor`: the same script, an unequal object. `MiniscriptDescriptor.__post_init__` now refuses such a miniscript, directly or through `dataclasses.replace`, with "parse reads pk() as a descriptor function, not a miniscript". The rule is `parse`'s own dispatch, so no list of functions is restated.

`parse` built that object itself from `wsh(c:pk_k(K))` and `wsh(c:pk_h(K))`, and their `sh(wsh())` forms, whose `str` writes `pk(K)` and `pkh(K)`. It now reads them as `PkDescriptor` and `PkhDescriptor`, built from the node's own key so a WIF of another network is still refused. The text and the script are unchanged; Bitcoin Core v32.1 writes the same text.

This breaks code that builds such a `MiniscriptDescriptor` by hand, which now gets a `BTClibValueError`, and code that expects a `MiniscriptDescriptor` from `parse` of those four shapes.

## Decision

The maintainer decided on #174 to refuse at build. He then accepted two extensions, recorded on the issue: `parse` reads the `c:pk_k`/`c:pk_h` shapes as the functions, since otherwise the new refusal would make `parse` refuse inputs Core accepts; and `rawpkh` is refused too, because `parse`'s dispatch reads it as a function.

## Evidence

body:
## Why
deja is published to npm as `dejactx`, but the command it installs is `deja`. The npm package named `deja` is an unrelated project with its own `deja` command, so a user who types `npx deja claude` or `npm i deja` runs someone else's code.

## What changed
- **README**: a note under the quick-start commands saying the package is `dejactx`, never to run `npx deja` or `npm i deja`, and that `npm i -g dejactx` provides the `deja` command.
- **README, Install**: one line explaining that every command works as `npx dejactx <command>` or `deja <command>` after a global install.
- **docs/troubleshooting.md**: a first check for anyone who installed the wrong `deja` package, with how to remove it.

Docs only. No code changes.

author: liuxie066
body:
## Design

- Reference: [docs/CODE_HEALTH_REVIEW.md](https://github.com/liuxie066/options-monitor/blob/2cdd8e4c29c3d698dd3ca7415be8e694a5e913e7/docs/CODE_HEALTH_REVIEW.md)
- Problem and scope: 代码巡检过去把确认缺陷直接送入修复队列，也没有独立的开放 PR 实测门禁或合并后的发布回执。此改动补上价值分诊、第三方服务产品边界、开放 PR 审查与实际验证，以及评论和发布交付。
- Constraints and authority: 用户明确授权实现这些能力，以及本次提交、推送、开 PR 和 CI 全绿后的 squash 合并；本次不运行真实 loop、不修改已安装配置或生产、不实际发版。
- Chosen design:

- Issue 分诊必须给出 worthwhile、not_worthwhile 或 needs_decision 及理由。只有值得处理、证据与归属成立且不涉及第三方服务接入的条目才能入修复队列；其他已处理条目保存解释和回复。
- 开放 PR 按创建时间处理，独立预算默认每轮最多 3 条、单条 900 秒。隔离 fetch 后绑定精确 head/base 和完整文件/hunk 清单，审查所有权及上下游，实际执行受影响测试与相关回归；缺陷修复还须通过真实断言失败到成功的同测试前后对照。模型结论不能代替宿主的测试、内容一致性、CI 和最终身份门禁。
- 只有完整通过审查和实测的精确修订可 squash 合并。第三方服务接入转产品裁决，changes_required/decline 回复具体原因，不改贡献者分支、不自动关闭 PR。
- 仅对实际处理过的 issue/PR 评论，持久化 outbox 并回读确认，响应丢失时先核对再重试。合入 main 的工作按现有 VERSION、CHANGELOG、release_delta、preflight、发布 PR 和 Guardrails 链准备 patch 版本；必须核对精确发布 SHA、工作流、tag、Release、资源和 runtime-ready 后才回复已发布版本，否则明确回复“已合并未发版”和下一步。

## Decision points

1. 默认启用 PR 审查、经门禁的合并、评论和发布能力，完成已授权的处理闭环；自动关闭 PR 保持禁用，逐条由用户决定。
2. 总预算默认 15000 秒，按提交巡检 6600、issue 3600、修复 1800、PR 1800、交付 1200 分配，超配直接拒绝。
3. 发布由实际处理的合并工作触发，同批可合并发布；没有待交付合并时不为每天调度空发版本。存在待发布批次时暂缓新的自动合并。

- Rejected alternatives: 不采用确认缺陷即入队、仅凭模型自报测试成功合并、直接创建 tag/Release 或失败即自动关闭 PR；这些路径分别缺少价值判断、宿主证据、既有发布合同或逐条授权。
- Risks and rollback boundary: 新能力须另行安装后才会生效，旧 12000 秒配置需要调整容量或关闭相应阶段。各写阶段有独立开关；已合并提交和已发布版本需按既有回滚流程处理，关开关不会撤销既有外部动作。

## Verification

- 修改前 code-health 套件：328 passed。
- 基线 3402161b96ba676c205bc2fe64b0686eaab1b253 上的最终 code-health 套件：434 passed in 78.89s，exit 0。
- 真实 CHANGELOG 格式与 canonical parser 回归已实际先红后绿。
- Ruff、生成依赖图检查、精确 staged wording/runtime-config/sensitive-artifact/public-surface guardrails、git diff whitespace 检查均通过；生产依赖环为 0。
- 实际执行 CLI --help。GitHub 和发布边界使用 mock，PR 实测用例执行真实临时 Git worktree 和 pytest 子进程。

本次只改 code_health 脚本、相关测试、维护文档，以及获准同步的生成依赖统计；没有修改业务代码、VERSION/CHANGELOG/发布元数据，没有运行真实 loop、安装本机脚本、修改已安装 config/state、访问生产或实际发版。后续部署须同时安装五个模块和 policy，并明确处理旧 12000 秒配置的预算容量。

author: lucasrtn
body:
## Ce qui change

Vécu : « Je dois pouvoir personnaliser le nom de domaine facilement depuis l'interface ».

Cloudflare tire au hasard l'adresse d'un Quick Tunnel : on ne peut pas la nommer. Pour une adresse choisie, il faut un **tunnel nommé**, dans un compte Cloudflare (gratuit) et sur un domaine ajouté à ce compte.

La carte « Accès depuis internet » propose maintenant deux types d'adresse :
- **Aléatoire** : les deux Quick Tunnels d'avant, inchangés.
- **Mon domaine** : un tunnel nommé.
  - On colle son jeton. La commande d'installation de Cloudflare se colle aussi telle quelle.
  - On saisit les deux adresses, panneau et applications.
  - Chez Cloudflare, ces deux adresses pointent vers `http://localhost:9011` et `http://localhost:9012` ; la carte rappelle ces étapes.
  - Un seul `cloudflared`, lancé par `tunnel run`.

## Le jeton est un secret
- Il est chiffré dans le coffre. Aucune réponse d'API ne le contient : elle dit seulement s'il est enregistré. La règle 16 de SECURITE.md le cite désormais.
- `cloudflared` le reçoit par `TUNNEL_TOKEN`, jamais par `--token` : la ligne de commande d'un processus se lit dans `/proc` par tout le conteneur.
- `cloudflared` tourne sous un uid à lui (`1002`), sans le groupe de `/workspace`.
  - Écarté : l'uid partagé des applications, qui aurait laissé un build lire l'environnement de `cloudflared`.

## Le reste
- Les adresses sont validées : deux noms de domaine distincts, jamais en `*.trycloudflare.com`.
- Le `PUT` vérifie tout avant d'écrire, pour qu'aucun réglage ne s'enregistre à moitié.
- Changer de mode ou de jeton relance `cloudflared`. Changer les adresses ne relance rien : elles se règlent chez Cloudflare.
- Le panneau ne demande aucune clé d'API Cloudflare : elle ouvrirait tout le compte.

## Vérifications
- `python3 -m pytest workspace/diagnostic/tests -q` : 923 réussis, 1 ignoré (6 nouveaux dans `test_tunnel.py`).
- Le test de lancement vérifie maintenant que `cloudflared` a son propre uid. C'est plus strict que l'ancienne vérification de `drop_privileges`.
- La carte rendue dans Chromium :
  - téléphone, tablette et ordinateur ;
  - thèmes clair et sombre ;
  - modes aléatoire, domaine complet et domaine incomplet.
- Aucun vrai tunnel nommé n'a été lancé ici : il faudrait un compte et un domaine.

author: imparsifal
body:
Tres cosas a raíz de las sugerencias de un usuario (09/11/2026). **Lleva migración: `sql/migra-183-comunidades-aura-cerrar-comentarios-premod.sql`** (idempotente; añade tres claves de config y `stories.comments_closed`).

## 1. Más comunidades para quien tiene más aura
- Config nuevas `comm_more_min_aura` = 20 (estricta: mayor que; 0 = desactivado) y `comm_max_per_user_more` = 6. Con aura > 20, y los moderadores, se pueden crear hasta 6 comunidades en vez de las 3 de `comm_max_per_user`. El admin sigue sin límite.
- `community_max($u)` en `lib/app.php`; `community_quota()` lo usa. `/comunidades` lo explica («Con aura mayor que 20, hasta 6.») y «Ya has creado tus N comunidades» usa el tope real de cada uno.

## 2. Cerrar los comentarios de un hilo (admin y moderadores)
- `stories.comments_closed`. Botón **Cerrar comentarios / Abrir comentarios** en la caja «Editar envío» del hilo (fila «Comentarios»), `public/cerrar-comentarios.php`, con registro en mod_log.
- El hilo se sigue viendo, votando y en su sitio; solo deja de admitir comentarios (la caja desaparece y sale «Comentarios cerrados.»; `comentar.php` rechaza el POST).

## 3. Premoderación de los anónimos
- Config `premod_anon` = 1. Lo que escribe quien no tiene cuenta —comentarios, mensajes del chat y hilos abiertos en los foros— entra como `pending_mod`, no cuenta en el hilo ni avisa a nadie, y `mod_premod()` (lib/moderacion.php) deja una fila en `mod_queue` como `hidden` con `reason = premod`. Sale en `/moderacion#ia` como **«pendiente de aprobar (premoderación)»** con botones **Aprobar** (se publica: `mod_unhide` suma el contador) y **Retirar**. Un hilo premoderado se lee entero en la propia pestaña y tiene enlace «ver»; los moderadores ya pueden abrir un hilo `pending_mod` (antes solo el admin), con un aviso arriba.
- No depende de `mod_enabled`: es moderación humana, la IA no pasa por ello.
- Aviso a quien escribe: «Como no estás registrado, tu comentario / tu mensaje / tu envío al foro tiene que ser aprobado por un moderador antes de publicarse.» (`?premod=1` en el hilo, el chat y el foro). Nueve traducciones.
- Los envíos de **enlaces** de anónimos (`/enviar`) siguen como estaban (posmoderados); solo cambia lo que Ángel pidió.

## Probado
MariaDB local + `php -S`: comentario, mensaje de chat e hilo de foro anónimos entran `pending_mod` con su fila en `mod_queue`; aprobar publica (comentario → `ok` y contador +1; hilo → `nuevas` y visible) y retirar el chat lo deja `gone`; avisos en las tres páginas; mod abre el hilo pendiente y un anónimo recibe 404. Cerrar comentarios: mod cierra/abre, usuario normal 403, el POST de comentar con cerrados se rechaza. Cuotas: aura 25 → 6 (crea 4, le quedan 2), aura 8 → 3 (la cuarta no entra), mod → 6. Migración aplicada dos veces sin efectos.

Nota: en pruebas con `mod_aura = 20` (valor de `schema.sql`) un usuario con aura 25 cuenta como moderador; en producción está a 0.

## 何が問題だったか（2026-11-09 に本番で確認） 1. **ほぼ全ページの canonical がホームを向いていた。** ルートの `app/layout.tsx` で `alternates.canonical: 'https://www.gatareview.com'` を設定していたため、`/lectures`・`/privacy`・`/terms`・`/reviews/new`・`/mypage`・404 などが「このページの正規 URL はホーム」と宣言していました。タイトルもホームと同じでした。自分の canonical を持っていたのは `/faq` と授業詳細だけです。 2. **授業の 404 が `

not found!

` だけだった。** さらに `robots` が2つ（`noindex` と `index, follow`）付き、canonical はホームを向いていました。 3. **`sitemap.xml` に授業ページが1件もなかった。** 固定ページ6件だけで、そのうち `/reviews` は 404 でした。授業一覧のページ送りはボタン（リンクではない）なので、Google が授業ページを見つける経路がほぼありませんでした。 4. **robots.txt が `/_next/` をブロックしていた。** このため Googlebot が CSS・JS・`/_next/image` を取得できませんでした。Google が無視する `Crawl-delay` と `Disallow: *.json$` もありました。 5. **全ページに FAQPage と固定のパンくず（ホーム > 授業レビュー > よくある質問）の構造化データが出ていた。** 6. **`` の不備。** `google-site-verification` が仮の値（`google-site-verification-code`）のまま、mask-icon の `/icon.svg` が 404、`og:image:width` などが重複していました。 ## 変更内容 ### canonical・robots・タイトル（問題1） - ルートの layout では canonical・robots・hreflang・og:url を**設定しない**ようにしました。ここで設定すると、設定し忘れたページや 404 にまで引き継がれるためです。 - `app/_helpers/seo.ts` を追加しました。 - `indexablePageMetadata`: 検索結果に出したいページ用。canonical・og:url・タイトル・説明・OGP・X カードをそのページの値にそろえます。 - `noindexPageMetadata`: `noindex, follow` を付け、canonical を消します。 - ページごとの設定は次のとおりです。 | ページ | canonical | robots | |---|---|---| | `/` | `https://www.gatareview.com` | なし（index） | | `/lectures` | 下記 | なし | | `/faq`・`/privacy`・`/terms` | 自分自身 | なし | | `/mypage/*`・`/auth/*`・`/admin/*`・`/offline`・`/reviews/new`・`/lectures/[id]/review` | なし | `noindex, follow` | | 404（どこでも） | なし | Next.js が付ける `noindex` の1つだけ | - noindex のページは robots.txt では止めていません。止めると Google が noindex を読めず、ヘッダーなどからのリンクだけで URL が検索結果に残ることがあるためです。 - 授業詳細の canonical は、もともと授業詳細の layout で設定済みなので変えていません。 #### `/lectures` の canonical の決め方 - **条件なしの1ページ目**（`/lectures`、`?page=1`、不正な `page`）→ `/lectures` - **条件なしの2ページ目以降**（`?page=N`）→ `/lectures?page=N`。Google はページ分割で1ページ目を canonical にしないよう求めているので、各ページ自身を canonical にしています。タイトルも「授業一覧（Nページ目）」にして重複を避けました。 - **検索語・学部・並び替え・詳細条件のどれかがある** → `/lectures`。組み合わせが無数にある検索結果ページを、検索結果に1つずつ出しても役に立たないためです。`sort=newest` は既定値なので条件として扱いません。`utm_*` などの無関係なパラメータも無視します。 - noindex ではなく canonical でまとめたのは、noindex と別 URL への canonical を同時に付けると Google への指示が矛盾するためです。 ### 404（問題2） - 404 のデザインを `app/_components/NotFoundContent.tsx` に切り出しました。サイト共通の 404 と授業の 404（`app/lectures/not-found.tsx`）の両方で使い、授業の 404 には「授業が見つかりません」と授業検索への案内を出します。 - ルートで robots と canonical を設定しなくなったので、404 の robots は Next.js が付ける `noindex` の1つだけになり、canonical もなくなりました。サイト共通の 404 のタイトルは「ページが見つかりません - ガタレビュ！」です。 ### サイトマップ（問題3） - 固定ページ5件（`/`・`/lectures`・`/faq`・`/privacy`・`/terms`）と、**レビューが1件以上ある授業ページ**を載せます。`/reviews` は外しました。 - 授業の ID は backend の新しい API（https://github.com/yu-yaba/gatareview-back/pull/71、`{ lecture_ids: [...] }`）を**1回だけ**呼んで取得します。公開一覧 API のページ送りはしません。 - **`lastmod` は付けません**（固定ページにも付けません）。授業ページの更新日はレビューの投稿・編集時刻から作るしかありません。レビュー・授業の作成・更新時刻は、日・月単位に丸めた値も含めて公開しない方針です。匿名レビューは編集できないため、時刻からログイン投稿かどうかや同じ人の投稿が推測できます。 - `changefreq` と `priority` は Google が使わないので外しました。 - キャッシュと失敗時の動き: - ビルド時には backend に問い合わせません（`dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`）。 - 検証に通った API の結果だけを `unstable_cache` に1時間保存します。backend への問い合わせは1時間に1回程度です。200 でも中身が壊れていれば保存しません。 - 期限切れのあとは古い内容を返しながら裏で取り直します。このため backend が一時的に落ちても直前のサイトマップが返ります。 - キャッシュが空のときに失敗した場合（5xx・429・タイムアウト 8 秒・壊れた応答）だけ、`sitemap.xml` を 5xx にします（Google は後で取り直します）。ID が1件でも不正な応答は、全体を捨てます。例外は backend にこの API がまだない 404 の場合で、固定ページだけを返します（デプロイ順を参照）。 - 1つのサイトマップの上限は 50,000 URL です。授業は約6,000件なので分割していません。上限を超えたら警告ログを出します。 - レビューのない授業を載せない理由: 「まだレビューがありません」だけの薄いページを大量に検索結果へ出すと、サイト全体の評価を下げるおそれがあるためです。ページ自体は index 可能なままです。載せたくなった場合は backend の API の条件を変えるだけで対応できます。 ### robots.txt（問題4） - `Disallow` は `/api/` と `/admin/` だけにしました。`/_next/` の行と、Google が無視する `Crawl-delay`・`*.json$` の行は削除しました。 ### 構造化データ（問題5） - **全ページ**: `WebSite` と `Organization` だけにしました。 - ロゴのサイズを実際の画像（500×500）に合わせました。 - `EducationalOrganization` は削除しました。このサイトは教育機関ではなく、`offers` なども実態と合わないためです。 - **パンくず**: ページごとに出します（`/lectures`・`/faq`・`/privacy`・`/terms`）。ホームにはありません。 - **FAQPage**: `/faq` だけに出します。画面と同じデータ（`app/faq/faqData.ts`）から全8問を作ります。以前は全ページに3問だけ出ていました。 - JSON-LD は `<` `>` `&` をエスケープして埋め込みます（`serializeJsonLd`）。 ### 授業の作成・更新時刻をページに入れない - 授業詳細・ホームの「人気の授業」「レビューのない授業」は、これまで backend の授業オブジェクトをそのままクライアントコンポーネントに渡していました。このため授業の `created_at` / `updated_at` が HTML と RSC payload に入っていました。 - `serverLectureApi.ts` で、公開する項目（`id`・`title`・`lecturer`・`faculty`・`avg_rating`・`review_count`）だけにしてから渡すようにしました。backend の PR でも公開 API から外しますが、デプロイ順に関係なくページには入りません。 - `LectureSchema` から `created_at` / `updated_at` を削除しました。どこからも読んでいません。JSON-LD に日付はありません。 ### Googlebot 向けの metadata を `` に出す - Next.js 15 は metadata（title・canonical・robots）を後から送るため、Googlebot には `` 側に出ることがありました（本番の `/lectures` もそうなっていました）。Google は `` 以外の canonical を使いません。 - `next.config.js` の `htmlLimitedBots` に Googlebot を加え、Googlebot には metadata を `` に出すようにしました。残りの bot は Next.js の既定の一覧と同じです。 ### `` の不備（問題6） - 仮の `google-site-verification` を削除しました。リポジトリ・ドキュメントに本物のコードはありませんでした。 - 存在しない `/icon.svg` の mask-icon を削除しました（いまの Safari は favicon・apple-touch-icon を使います）。 - `` に手書きしていた `og:image:width/height/type` を削除しました。metadata の `openGraph.images` が同じ値を出すため、重複していました。 ## Search Console の確認コードについて Search Console の所有権確認が必要な場合は、次のどちらかで行ってください。 - **（おすすめ）DNS の TXT レコード**: Search Console で「ドメイン」プロパティを追加し、表示された TXT レコードを DNS（Cloudflare）に追加します。コードの変更は不要です。 - **HTML タグ**: 「URL プレフィックス」プロパティで HTML タグを選び、表示された `content` の値を `app/layout.tsx` の `metadata` に `verification: { google: '<値>' }` として追加します。 ## テスト `tests/seo/seo-output.mjs`（`npm run test:seo`）を追加し、CI のビルド後の手順で実行するようにしました。本番ビルドを `next start` で起動し、ダミーの API を相手に次を確認します。 - **robots.txt**: `/_next/`・`Crawl-delay`・`*.json` がないこと。`/api/` と `/admin/` を止めていること。サイトマップの行があること。noindex のページを止めていないこと。 - **sitemap.xml** - キャッシュが空で API が失敗したら 5xx になること。 - 成功時の URL の一覧と順序、重複がないこと、`/reviews` がないこと、`lastmod` がないこと。不正な ID を含む応答と HTML の 200 は保存されないこと。API が 404 のときは固定ページだけを返すこと。 - 2回目の取得で API を呼ばない（キャッシュが効く）こと。 - **載せた URL がすべて 200 で、canonical がその URL 自身、noindex でないこと。** - **ページ**（Googlebot と通常ブラウザの2種類の User-Agent それぞれで確認） - index するページ15パターン（`/lectures` のクエリ違い9種を含む）: canonical の値、robots meta がないこと、og:url、タイトル（ホームのタイトルを使い回していないこと）、パンくずの中身、FAQPage が `/faq` だけで画面の質問・回答と一致すること。 - noindex のページ9つ: robots が `noindex, follow` の1つだけで、canonical がないこと。 - 404 の6パターン（存在しない URL、存在しない授業 ID、数字でない授業 ID、`/reviews`、本番の `/debug/session`、授業の下の存在しないパス）: ステータス 404、robots が `noindex` の1つだけ、canonical と og:url がないこと、共通の 404 デザインであること、`not found!` が出ないこと。 - 全ページ共通: 仮の確認コード・mask-icon・hreflang がないこと。canonical・robots・`og:image:width` が重複しないこと。`` が1つだけで googlebot meta がないこと。 - `tests/e2e/mock-backend.mjs` にサイトマップ API を追加しました（e2e と CI のビルド用）。 ローカルの結果（Node 24.22.2、`origin/main`（#131 まで）を取り込んだ最新コミットと同じツリー）: - `npm ci` → `npm run typecheck` → `npm run lint` → `npm run build` → `npm run test:seo`: 最新コミットですべて成功しました（32ルート × 2種類の User-Agent、最後のページより後ろ、robots.txt、sitemap.xml）。 - `test:seo` で追加した確認: - 授業・レビューの mock に時刻の目印の値を入れ、どのページ（HTML と RSC payload）にも `/api/public/lectures` にも出ないこと。授業詳細ではレビューが実際に表示されることも確認します。 - サイトマップに `lastmod` がないこと。 - #131 の不正な `page`（`0`・`abc`・`10001`）が `/lectures` にリダイレクトされること。 - `test:public-cache`・`test:search-cache`・`test:lecture-streaming`・`e2e`・`e2e:security`・`e2e:csp`: CI で確認します。 `origin/main` は強制 push ではなくマージで取り込みました。`app/lectures/page.tsx` の競合（#131 のリダイレクト）は、両方の動作を残して解消しています。 ## デプロイ順 **backend の PR（https://github.com/yu-yaba/gatareview-back/pull/71）を先にデプロイすることをおすすめします。** 逆の順でも壊れません。 - 新フロント × 旧 backend: サイトマップ API がまだない（404）間は、固定ページだけの `sitemap.xml` を 200 で返します。いまの本番と同じ内容から `/reviews` を除いたもので、この結果は保存しません。backend をデプロイすると、次のリクエストから授業が載ります。授業の時刻は、フロント側でも項目を絞るのでページに入りません。 - 旧フロント × 新 backend: 旧フロントは授業の `created_at` / `updated_at` を読んでいないので、影響はありません。 - デプロイ後に Search Console でサイトマップを再送信すると、授業ページが早く取り込まれます。 ## このPRでやっていないこと（別PR向け） - **授業詳細（`app/lectures/[id]/*`）**: 作業中は #129 が編集していたので触っていません。 - パンくずと、授業ごとの構造化データはまだあり

author: koic
body:
When `Style/HashSyntax` corrects a pair in the last hash argument of a call without parentheses, it adds the parentheses, since an omitted value would otherwise take what follows as its value. It did so also when the correction includes the omitted value (`EnforcedShorthandSyntax: never`, or `consistent` with a value that cannot be omitted), where nothing can be taken as the value. The closing parenthesis was only added when the corrected pair is the last one, so the result was invalid Ruby, and `Style/Semicolon` adds the same parentheses when it removes a semicolon after an omitted value, which doubled the closing one:

```ruby
# before
foo bar, baz:, qux: qux if condition

# after
foo(bar, baz: baz, qux: qux if condition
```

This adds the parentheses only when the correction omits the value.

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [ ] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/

author: marcel-bonifacio
body:
## Summary
A security and hardening pass over the server, web client and Android app, plus a dependency audit. Also adds what you asked for in this round: **in-app updates**, a **Light default with Dark and High contrast** options, and API 35.

### Dependencies
- **npm:** 0 advisories, registry signatures verified, no install scripts. `imapflow` 2.x and `pdfjs-dist` 6.x are available as optional major upgrades, not conflicts.
- **Android:** all 125 resolved artifacts are clean on OSV.
  - Conflict fixed: `kotlin-stdlib-jdk7/jdk8` resolved to 1.9.10 next to `kotlin-stdlib` 1.9.24. They are now aligned through `kotlin-bom`.
  - `targetSdk`/`compileSdk` raised to **35** (Play's target-API requirement).

### Server
- **IMAP SSRF / DNS rebinding:** the host check and the actual connection resolved DNS separately. The new `lib/netguard.js` resolves once, rejects private and reserved ranges (now including NAT64 and 6to4), and returns the address to connect to, preferring IPv4. ImapFlow connects to that address with TLS `servername` set to the host. This applies at sign-in **and on every later sync**, which previously had no check.
- **Spoofed bank mail:** alerts and statements whose sender fails authentication are dropped. A message is trusted when DMARC passes, or when SPF or DKIM passes for the From domain itself. Only the top `Authentication-Results` header counts, because it is added by the receiving server.
- **Attachments:** only PDFs up to 8 MB are downloaded. On IMAP, the message size is checked before it is downloaded.
- **`/api/unlock`:** accepts only the known password slots, with passwords up to 256 chars. The map is pruned, so the cookie can't grow past its limit.
- **`/api/yf`:** `Cache-Control: private`.
- **`/api/logout`:** sends `Clear-Site-Data: "cache"`.
- **Tests:** `app/test/security.test.js` (25 checks) runs with `npm test`.

### Web
- **Logout** asks first, then clears this device's Crumina data and caches. A *different* signed-in account never sees the previous person's data; local guest data still carries over on first sign-in.
- **Missing exchange rates** are no longer treated as 1:1:
  - the last good rates are kept
  - unconvertible amounts are left out of totals, with a notice under net worth
  - budgets and goals won't save without a rate
- **Dates** use the local calendar instead of UTC. This fixes the monthly projection on the 1st in WIB, statement and CSV dates being one day early, and default dates.
- **Duplicates:**
  - a purchase in both an alert and a statement now counts once
  - identical same-day statement rows are kept apart using their running balance
  - unreadable statement dates no longer count as today

### Android 0.4.0
- **In-app updates:**
  - checks GitHub Releases on launch, at most every 6 hours, and from Settings → Check for updates
  - downloads `crumina.apk` and verifies the package, a higher versionCode and the **same signing certificate** before opening the system installer
  - the check uses its own HTTP client, so the session token is never sent to GitHub
  - documented in `docs/ANDROID.md`, including the Play-policy caveat for `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES`
- **Appearance:** Light by default, whatever the system theme. Settings → Appearance switches to Dark or High contrast (web contrast colours, black lines).
- **Networking:** 45 s read timeout and no redirects. Refresh keeps previous data on failure, rethrows cancellation, and merges quotes by symbol. GBp, ZAc and ILA quotes are converted.
- **Exchange rates:** saved together with their base. Unknown rates are left out of totals with a notice, and rows fall back to the original IDR amount.
- **Amounts:** fields accept `42.500.000`, `1,000,000` and `50,5`, and reject NaN/Infinity. Share units and prices read `1.250` as 1.25.
- **PDF upload:** capped at 4 MB, and an unreadable file no longer crashes the app.
- **Shared phones:** a different Google account signing in starts clean, and a stray login callback no longer cancels a login in progress.
- **Startup:** encrypted prefs recover instead of crash-looping.
- **Manual credit cards** count as debt.

## Verification
- [x] `npm test`: 12 parser and 25 security checks pass. `node --check` on all JS. Self-host smoke test of `/api/unlock` (bad slot, `__proto__`, long password → 400) and the `/api/yf` header.
- [x] Web in the browser: local-date helper (1 Oct 03:00 stays 1 Oct), alert/statement dedupe, logout wipe keeps only preferences, page renders, rates are cached.
- [x] Android on an Android 14 emulator:
  - the release build runs (targetSdk 35)
  - Light, Dark and High contrast themes all render
  - a 0.2.9 build finds v0.3.0 on GitHub, downloads it and **refuses it because it was signed with a different key**, deleting the file
  - a build with an equal or higher versionCode is refused as "not newer"
- [x] Lint: 0 errors.
- [ ] A real update from a CI-signed 0.4.0 to the next CI-signed release. That needs two releases signed with the real key.

## Review
- **Code review:** 10 findings, all fixed in the second commit:
  - spoof check without alignment
  - IPv6 pinning on IPv4-only hosts
  - signer fallback for APK archives
  - 1969 dates in time zones west of UTC
  - leftover 1:1 conversion on web
  - $0.00 rows on Android
  - decimal share units
  - check timestamp recorded on failure
  - re-downloading the update
  - IMAP size checked too late
- **Security review:** this PR *is* the security pass. Covered threat model: mail and PDF content as attacker-controlled input, IMAP host as attacker-controlled, shared devices, update supply chain. Not changed and noted:
  - in-memory rate limits on serverless
  - the stateless 30-day session (no server-side revoke)
  - a free guest session reaches the PDF parser and quote proxy
  - session cookies without the `__Host-` prefix

author: serjtargarien
body:
R3.4 step 1 «Lists and limits», part 3 of 3 (completes the step).

- Every text box on the sheet, the creation form, the familiar sheet and the familiar editor carries its field's limit from the server's rules (`limitAttrs` / `maxLengthOf`, `src/components/LimitHint.tsx`); a paste over the limit stops at it.
- One `LimitHint` in the app watches the focused box: past 90% of its text limit, or of the list it adds to, a small counter appears under it («185 / 200», «28 / 30 entradas», «límite alcanzado»). The galleries show their counter in place («46 / 50 imágenes»).
- A unit test checks that every limited box names a field with a real limit.

Checked locally: type check, 53 unit tests, both builds, 47 browser tests (new: counter past 90%, paste stops at the limit, counter gone when the box is left). Looked at in the demo build at phone width.

author: gab-25
body:
## Summary
- The card recognition request to OpenRouter now sends `reasoning: {enabled: false}`: reading a card needs no reasoning.
- This makes reasoning models such as `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` usable through `OPENROUTER_MODEL`. With reasoning on by default, Qwen took 5–15 s per card (close to the client's 20 s timeout) and cost as much as or more than Gemini.
- The test of the request payload now checks the new parameter.

## Measurements
Two Scryfall card images (one Italian, one English) with the app's prompt and schema:

| Model | Time | Cost per scan | Set / number / language |
|---|---|---|---|
| `google/gemini-2.5-flash` | 1.1–1.8 s | ~$0.0003 | correct |
| `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, reasoning on | 5–15 s | ~$0.00016–0.0004 | correct |
| `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, reasoning off | 1.9–7.8 s | ~$0.0001 | correct |

Gemini accepts the parameter and behaves as before. These were clean scans, not phone photos.

Neither model gave the right English name for the Italian card (*Kona, Rescue Beastie*). Set and number are read correctly, so the number finds the printing, but the name mismatch makes `match()` return `ambiguous` and the owner confirms it.

When the Mac witness is offline, ordinary NAS Core writes must continue. Cached witness heads cannot establish the current source state after offline deletion or revocation.

Add an isolated, nonce-bound source observation signed in a separate domain and checked against the enrolled identity and current governance snapshot. The experimental witness requires that observation for every response and bounds its proof lifetime to the source observation. Production Core and deployment remain unchanged.

Validation: 119 scripts/tests pass locally, including 18 new real synthetic Core tests, current-tombstone restore, nonce/signature/expiry failures, source read-only hashes and persistent-reader trust checks. Network authentication, secure independent durable witness custody and activation are not implemented.

body: create_version() takes a read-only lvcreate --snapshot named <uuid>-<offset>-s<version_id> with -l 100%ORIGIN, so the preallocated COW area can hold every rewritten block and a version is never invalidated by overflow. The snapshot carries the live LV's rawstor.meta tag as of the version, since lvcreate does not copy tags. Adds remove_version(), list_versions(), version-aware list_chunks()/meta() and _open_version().

author: haryowaskito
body:
## Summary

Send a 4.9 MB image in chat → the server checks its base64 in milliseconds and keeps answering everyone else.

**Before:** `CANONICAL_BASE64_PATTERN` cost ~90 ms/MB, ran twice per chat image (0.5–0.85 s stall), and refused valid base64 past ~5.9 MB.
**After:** `normalizeAttachmentBase64` checks `length % 4 === 0` and a flat `/^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$/`: server stall ≤16 ms, and a 6 MB image gets the size error.

Why safe:
1. Same accept/reject result as the old regex on 21.4M strings
2. The `atob`/`btoa` round trip below still enforces canonical base64. Caps and statuses are unchanged
3. Same fix #1734 made for knowledge ZIPs (#1597)

Only revisit if a Bun upgrade makes the flat character class slow too.

Fixes #2486

author: homlo-bike
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"homlo-bike"} -->
_Requested by **Homlo** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01F1w55ANnnpLfXqB5CwyRpk?thread=cmsg_01F1w55ANnnpLfXqB5CwyRpk7yJi796sfo8wrxwuf7R6pq)_

## What

This replaces the interim rail pass-by model (a level per mode scaled with speed) with the CNOSSOS-EU railway source from Directive (EU) 2015/996 Annex II §2.3 and Appendix G, as amended by Delegated Directive (EU) 2021/1226.

### Tables from the official texts
- The tables in `crates/noise/data/cnossos-rail.json` are generated by `tools/noise/extract_cnossos_rail.py`. The script reads the 2015 OJ L 168 XHTML (Publications Office) and the 2021 OJ L 269 PDF, then applies amendment point (20): it swaps in the replaced rail roughness, contact filter, track transfer (including direct fastening on bridges), impact and bridge tables, and corrects the 2 200 kW diesel locomotive's 6 300 Hz value in Table G-5 (31.4 → 81.4 and 30.7 → 80.7). Running it with `--check` confirms that the file matches the texts. No value is typed by hand.
- Tables G-1 to G-7 have been checked against the texts. The 2015 wheel roughness table starts at 1 000 mm, so the bands from 1 250 to 2 000 mm that 2021 added use the 1 000 mm value.

### Model (`crates/noise/src/rail.rs`, estimate)
- Sound power per train in 1/3 octave bands. Roughness is converted with f = v/λ, using the minimum speed of 50 km/h (30 km/h for trams and light rail), then filtered by the contact filter. Track and wheel transfer functions are added with + 10 lg N_a. Impact noise covers 50 m either side of each placed switch. Squeal uses the 2021 table. Traction comes from Table G-5, per powered vehicle or locomotive. Aerodynamic noise is added above 200 km/h. Bridge noise is its own omnidirectional source (2.3.18 as replaced in 2021). The bands are then summed into octaves and A-weighted.
- There are two source heights, A at 0.5 m and B at 4 m. The horizontal dipole (2.3.15) and the vertical directivity (2.3.16 as replaced, and 2.3.17) are applied in the transfer tables. The band edge now starts at the first probe above the threshold, because source A radiates less steeply upwards.
- The bridge and switch checks now report the increase the model computes, not a fixed number.

### Parameters (noise plugin)
- New per-mode parameters for vehicle length, axles, powered share and locomotives. New enum parameters select the table entries: brake type, rail roughness E or M, contact filter, wheel and track transfer, traction and bridge type. The low and high variants use quieter and louder entries. `export_defaults.py` now exports enums.
- Removed: `rail_passby_db`, `rail_passby_ref_speed_kmh`, `rail_rolling_speed_exponent`, `rail_switch_db`, `rail_bridge_db` and `rail_source_height_m`, plus the interim rail spectrum shape. The squeal values are now read in the English text (`check: read`).

## Results to check
- Pass-by level at 7.5 m: a 30 m tram at 40 km/h gives about 73 dB, and a regional EMU at 80 km/h gives about 79 dB. Both fall within the range of ISO 3095 measurements and TSI NOI limits. CNOSSOS has no tram-specific vehicle data, so trams use small wheels and the EMU traction entry. At the 6/4/1 trains per hour the old tests used, a tram line no longer produces a 55 dB L_den band (about 52 dB at 7.5 m). Tests that check band widening now use busier flows.
- The GIS noise map with 6,300 buildings went from 1.4 s to 2.6 s natively, because rail now has two source heights.

## Not yet
- The +8 dB for switch turnouts with R ≤ 300 m (the diverging radius is not in the noise input), idling trains and freight.
- Per-project overrides for the enum choices: project preferences pass numbers only.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p noise -p noise-wasm` passes, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. New tests cover the 2021 amendments in the data, wavelength-to-frequency conversion, speed growth and aerodynamic noise, bridge and impact, directivity, and plausible pass-by levels.
- `export_defaults.py --check`, `tools/plugins/check.py --check-rendered`, `tools/assumptions/check.py --check-rendered` and ruff on `tools/noise` all pass.
- I did not run the web tests or the wasm32 build locally (no node_modules or wasm target here). CI covers both, and this PR changes no TypeScript.

author: callmetechie
body:
## Worum es geht

Bis 1.258.1 wurde das verschlüsselte Offsite-Archiv (`.gcbk`) als **ein Buffer** gebaut und so an WebDAV/S3/SMB/SFTP übergeben. Mit ~400 MB Plugin-Daten heißt das: das ganze Archiv (~400 MB) liegt im Arbeitsspeicher, die Spitze lag bei über 500 MB RSS – zu viel für einen kleinen VPS.

Jetzt wird das Archiv als Stream in eine Datei geschrieben und von dort hochgeladen. Der zusätzliche Speicher bleibt bei einigen zehn MB, egal wie groß das Archiv ist.

## Änderungen

**Archiv (`gcbk.writeBackupArchive`)**
- Backup-Datei → gzip → AES-256-GCM → Archivdatei, alles als Stream (Format GCBK1 unverändert).
- Größe und – nur wenn ein S3-Ziel aktiv ist – SHA-256 je S3-Teil werden beim Schreiben berechnet (kein zweites Lesen).
- Ablage in `<Backup-Ordner>/.incoming` (0700, Name zufällig vom Server, Pfad über `backupUpload.incomingPath` geprüft). Vorher Prüfung des freien Platzes (`backup.checkFreeSpace` aus #458), Löschen im `finally`, Reste eines Absturzes werden beim ersten Gebrauch entfernt.
- Zu wenig Platz → `NO_SPACE` (507) mit Hinweis `no_space`; die Oberfläche zeigt einen deutschen Text („Auf dem GateControl-Server ist zu wenig Speicherplatz frei …“).

**Transporte** (`services/offsite/source.js`: Archivdatei oder – für Schreibtests – Buffer)
- **WebDAV:** PUT als Stream mit `Content-Length` (nie chunked).
- **S3:** bis 64 MiB ein PUT als Stream, darüber Multipart in 64-MiB-Teilen, Teil für Teil aus der Datei gelesen. Jeder Teil ist mit seinem echten SHA-256 signiert (weiterhin kein `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`). Bei einem Fehler (auch bei „200 mit `<Error>`“ beim Abschließen) folgt `AbortMultipartUpload`.
- **SMB:** `put` direkt aus der Archivdatei (smbclient liest in Blöcken), keine Kopie in eine Temp-Datei mehr.
- **SFTP:** `put` direkt aus der Archivdatei.
- SMB/SFTP: Das harte Zeitlimit wächst mit der Größe (Basis + Größe bei 1 Mbit/s). Vorher endete die Übertragung nach festen 3 Minuten, was für einige hundert MB über eine langsame Leitung nicht reicht.
- Jeder Versuch öffnet einen frischen Lese-Stream: Die Wiederholung nach „Zertifikat beim ersten Kontakt gemerkt“ (`withTrust`) startet sauber von vorn.
- `via` (VPN-Gerät/Weiterleitung), `tls_ca`, Zertifikats-Pinning und SMB3-Verschlüsselung (#457) sind unverändert und laufen über dieselben Wege.

**Wiederherstellungstest**
- `downloadTo` statt `download`: Das Archiv wird Stück für Stück in eine Datei geladen (mit Größenlimit), das Entschlüsseln läuft wie seit #458 als Stream. Vorher lag es einmal ganz im Speicher.

Aufbewahrung, Status/SSE, Fehlertexte und der Ablauf des Wiederherstellungstests bleiben gleich.

## Speicher – vorher/nachher

`node scripts/offsite-memory-check.js --mb 400 [--legacy]`: 400 MB Plugin-Daten, Archiv 402 MB, Upload an WebDAV und S3 (Multipart, 16-MiB-Teile) in einem Prozess, RSS alle 10 ms gemessen.

| | zusätzlicher RSS | Spitze RSS |
|---|---|---|
| vorher (Archiv als Buffer) | +441 MB | 517 MB |
| jetzt (Datei + Streams) | +43 MB | 118 MB |

Mit 50 MB, 160 MB und 800 MB Archiv bleibt der Zusatz gleich bei ~43–45 MB (Arbeitsspeicher von V8 und zlib, nicht das Archiv).

## Tests
- Fake-S3 (prüft SigV4 inkl. Payload-Hash): Multipart mit abgesenkter Teilgröße, Hashes vom Schreiben und aus der Datei, falscher Hash wird abgelehnt, Abbruch bei fehlerhaftem Teil und bei spätem Fehler, Content-Length statt chunked.
- WebDAV, SMB, SFTP: Upload aus der Datei, `downloadTo`, unzulässige lokale Pfade werden abgelehnt (`"`, `;` …).
- API: Archivdatei nach Erfolg und nach Fehler entfernt, Reste-Bereinigung, `NO_SPACE`/507 mit Hinweis, auch in `last_error_hint`.
- `writeBackupArchive`: Größe, Teil-Hashes, Rechte 0600, kein Überschreiben, Aufräumen bei ENOSPC mitten im Schreiben.
- **Neu im CI-Job „storage targets (S3, WebDAV, SMB)“:** `tests/offsite_live.test.js` gegen moto, wsgidav und Samba. Ein echtes Archiv (~12 MB) geht hoch, kommt Byte für Byte zurück und wird entschlüsselt. S3 läuft als Multipart mit 5 MiB (drei Teile) mit und ohne vorberechnete Hashes und als einzelner PUT; SMB mit erzwungener SMB3-Verschlüsselung. Lokal gegen dieselben Server grün.
- `tests/offsite_memory.test.js`: Ein Archiv von 160 MB muss mit < 100 MB zusätzlichem RSS hochgehen.

Lokal (Node 22): volle Suite grün bis auf den bekannten lokalen Fehler `config_hash_stub_guard`. ESLint-Security und no-undef wie in der CI: keine neuen Befunde.

## Nicht getestet
- Gegen einen echten S3-Server, der Signaturen prüft (MinIO, Synology C2, Garage, AWS): Moto im CI prüft sie nicht. Die Signaturen je Teil sind gegen den signaturprüfenden Fake-S3 der Unit-Tests geprüft.
- SFTP gegen einen echten Server (wie bisher nur mit Shims).

body: ## Summary Fixes code scan finding sfind-3eb2c3931ae24bb78f00d1316a0542fa (high): `POST /api/seed` ran `User/Project/TestCase.deleteMany({})` and inserted demo fixtures with no auth, role or environment guard. Because it reads no body and needs no custom headers, a cross-site HTML form could also trigger it through a login proxy. - **Removed `server/api/seed.post.ts`**, so the route no longer exists in `nuxt build` output (`.output/server/chunks/routes/api/seed.post.mjs` is gone). - **Seeding is CLI-only now.** `scripts/seed.ts` has the route's fixtures (3 users, 2 projects, 10 test cases) and runs with the new `pnpm db:seed` (`tsx scripts/seed.ts`). The script never worked on main: `"type": "module"` means `require.main === module` throws `ReferenceError: require is not defined`. It now uses an `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` check and exits non-zero on failure. It loads `.env` (`process.loadEnvFile`, shell env still wins) so it seeds the same `MONGODB_URI` as the app instead of falling back to `localhost:27017/benchkit`. - README now documents `pnpm db:seed` and warns that it wipes the database at `MONGODB_URI`. No app code called `/api/seed`. Not in this PR: the finding also suggests a global `server/middleware/auth.ts` for `/api/**`. That is a larger design change that touches every route. The unmerged branch `devin/1789770123-users-idor-auth` already adds that middleware for the users routes. ### Verification I ran production builds (`nuxt build`) of main and of this branch with `node .output/server/index.mjs` against a disposable MongoDB. The DB held one "real" user, one project and five validated test cases. I sent a plain form POST with an empty body (`notes/bk-3eb2-harness/probe.sh`): ``` [main] POST /api/seed -> 200 {"success":true,"message":"Database seeded successfully",...} [main] after request: {"users":3,"projects":2,"testcases":10,"alice":0} # real data wiped [fix] POST /api/seed -> 404 "Page not found: /api/seed" [fix] after request: {"users":1,"projects":1,"testcases":5,"alice":1} # unchanged ``` CLI seeding: ``` fix : pnpm db:seed -> "Database seeded successfully: { users: 3, projects: 2, testCases: 10 }", exit 0 main: tsx scripts/seed.ts -> ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope, exit 1 fix : MONGODB_URI only in .env -> seeds that DB; shell MONGODB_URI overrides .env; no .env -> env/default, exit 0 ``` `eslint scripts/seed.ts` and `prettier --check` both pass. The repo has no test suite or CI. author: henryiii
body:
:robot: _AI text below_ :robot:

Stacked on #2. One commit per item:

- Hash compact values from their packed fields by mirroring `tuple_hash`, so no key tuple is built. Full values still hash the cached tuple; a new test checks equal hashes across both storages.
- Cache `str()` of full-storage values next to the cached key tuple. Component `__str__` errors still propagate on every call.
- Convert parsed digit runs of up to 18 digits into a `long long` instead of going through `PyLong_FromString`, and build the pre-release pair with `PyTuple_Pack`.
- Compare compact and full values in C when the full side's public components fit the compact key; a local label breaks ties. Epochs, wide numbers and int subclasses keep the tuple path.
- Publish freshly allocated objects without the critical section. Free-threaded builds only.
- Give plain subclasses the vectorcall constructor. A C `__init_subclass__` calls the next one in the MRO and installs `tp_vectorcall` on the new class; the fast path checks on every call that `tp_init` and `tp_new` are the inherited ones, so a subclass with its own `__init__` or `__new__` still goes through `tp_call`.
- Build compact version strings as ASCII directly instead of running the UTF-8 decoder over a buffer known to be ASCII.
- Last commit, four changes:
  - Compare in C whenever both sides' public components fit the compact key, full against full included. Full values pack that key at construction (the parser packs it from the parsed numbers), so the per-object lazy state and its lock are gone. Only two local labels on equal public versions still use tuple keys. A new test covers ordering of full-storage values.
  - Read the cached key and `str()` with an atomic load and install them with a compare-exchange. Free-threaded builds only.
  - Keep the pre-release letter strings in module state.
  - Read the first digit run once in the parser.

Release build, ns:

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First hash of a new compact value, above construction | 50 | 18 |
| `str()` of a full value | 103 | 11 |
| `str()` of a compact value | 22 | 20 |
| Construct `1.2.3+local` | 113 | 82 |
| Construct `2.0rc1.dev3+abc.9` | 160 | 100 |
| Compact vs local-labelled compare | 51 | 10 |
| Sort 1000 values, a quarter with local labels (µs) | 250 | 42 |
| Free-threaded compact construction | 39 | 36 |
| Plain subclass construction | 55 | 41 |
| `V("1.2.3") < V("1.3.0")` with `V` a plain subclass | 123 | 93 |

The last commit alone, against the commit before it:

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Local-labelled vs local-labelled compare, public parts differ | 22 | 9 |
| `.pre` of a compact value | 36 | 19 |
| Construct `1!2.0rc1` | 74 | 65 |
| Sort 1000 values, all with local labels (µs) | 292 | 100 |
| Sort 1000 values, a quarter with local labels (µs) | 67 | 42 |
| Sort 1000 compact values (µs) | 55 | 40 |

End to end, on the warm BigQuery/Soda resolve benchmark with the native-backed packaging checkout, this PR is neutral against #2 (about 4.05 s both); the resolver's own interval math dominates that workload. The same resolve takes about 5.16 s with the pure-Python fallback.

author: kume1a
body:
## Summary
R4c, the third part of v2.0 "Lessons and road trips": road trips, the Final drive, Jump ahead and Unit complete, built to the claude.ai boards R4-02, R4-12, R4-30 to R4-34, R4-40 and R4-61 (spec: `docs/specs/2026-11-09-r4c-road-trips-design.md`, plan: `docs/plans/2026-11-09-r4c-road-trips.md`).

- **Packs (format 3):** a road graph of the pack's named drivable streets. Junctions are OSM nodes the street ways share (or way ends); edges run between them, undirected. New tables `junction` and `road_edge`; `validate` checks references, ends and that at least 90 % of the edges connect (Tbilisi: 95 % of 16 311 edges). Same extract, no identity changes. The app installs format 3 and still opens a format 2 pack, without road trips.
- **Rules (`pindoro_core`):** `RoadGraph` with A*; `pickTrip` (B on the destination street, A on another street of the unit, a best drive at most 1.6 times the straight line); `RouteDraft` walks a drag along the streets junction by junction (backing up undoes, it stops at B); turn options and route legs for screen readers and the Miss sheet. `RouteScoring` (Perfect ≤ 3 %, Great ≤ 25 %, Close ≤ 60 % longer than the best drive, scaled by difficulty) is twinned in `@pindoro/geo` with `shared/fixtures/route_vectors.json`.
- **Lessons:** step 11 is a road trip (up to 670 XP). A Miss trip comes back once as the same trip; a Close one is no mistake. Trips never reach the Pit stop or known streets.
- **Final drive and Jump ahead:** 3 passed trips pass a unit and open the next; a unit is done when it or any later unit is driven, so passing a locked unit's Final drive (Jump ahead, from its signpost's sheet) marks every unit before it done. Each trip saves as its own result as soon as it is answered (no schema change: new enum values), so leaving keeps the trips passed. The third pass adds the +100 unit bonus and opens Unit complete; its Continue plays R4-61 on the Path (the trophy turns yellow, the next signpost flips open, its road fades up).
- **Road-trip view (`features/map`):** a drag that starts near the route's end draws (only then does it take the gesture from the map), with the next-junction ring, the rubber band and the off-road toast; Undo (hold: start over), Show the route, Check route; the car replay and the tier sheet; the first-trip ghost and coach bubble; a turn list when a screen reader is on.
- **Me:** the Road trips tile counts every road trip.
- **Design system:** `PinMark.endpoint`, `CarMark`, `glyphPng`, `LevelBadge.glyph`; golden `route_*` (existing goldens unchanged).

Left out on purpose (in `docs/TODO.md`): the "Choose turns from a list" setting, the detour sentence and its chip, the checking loader, one-way streets, B's ring pulse, unit titles, resuming a killed drive's trip in progress.

## Test plan
- Pipeline (synthetic OSM): shared nodes make junctions, a bridge crossing doesn't; edge lengths sum to the street; the fixture keeps only its streets' edges; Tbilisi and fixture packs validate.
- pindoro_core: A* against brute force, `pickTrip` limits and the detour cap, drawing (follow, back up, off road, stop at B), turns and legs, the route vectors (also in `@pindoro/geo`), lessons with a trip, the Final drive gate and Jump ahead.
- Mobile: trip answers in the DAO (no unit mistake, no known street, last distances untouched), `finishTrip` and the bonus, the lesson and drive controllers, the projection and camera fit, a lesson's trip through the screens, the turn list with a screen reader, Final drive → Unit complete → Path, Me.
- Emulator (debug build, local format 3 Tbilisi pack): a practice road trip (ghost, drawing, rubber band, Show the route, replay, sheet), Final drive trips (Perfect drives, a Miss with Try this trip again, the off-road toast), Unit complete, R4-61, the locked unit's sheet and Jump ahead, Me, dark theme. Fixes from it are their own commit: route maps fit the camera in Dart (MapLibre's bounds fit kept its padding on the camera, so drags from A missed), trips skip A or B that only a long loop reaches, a missed trip keeps its bar segment, the distance chip hides once B is reached.

author: shnicko
body:
Refactor stack 1 of 5: **enums instead of strings.** Merge after the regression-script fix, then the next PRs in order. Every PR in the stack targets `master`, so until the earlier ones are merged a PR also shows their commits.

## What changed
- **Fixed value sets are enums:**
  - `NodeType`, `OutcomeType`, `Side`, `EdgeStyle`, `LabelOrient`, `LabelPlace`, `FlowDirection` and `IpoSection` (in `Models/Catalogue/`).
  - `EmphasisLevel` (in `Models/Emphasis/`).
  - The string-constant classes `EdgeStyles`, `LabelOrients` and `FlowDirections` are gone.
- **The file format doesn't change.**
  - Each enum is saved by name (`"decision"`, `"rework"`, `"right"`) through `EnumNameConverter<T>` (new `Models/Serialization/`).
  - Optional ones (`Edge.FromSide` / `ToSide`, `Node.Outcome`, `ListItem.Section`) use `OptionalEnumNameConverter<T>`.
  - Normal emphasis is still left out of the file.
- **What a hand-edited file with an unknown name does:**
  - It still opens. The value reads as the enum's first member (Process, Pass, Elbow, …), or null for an optional one (an automatic side).
  - Before, an unknown type was drawn as a process but its text was kept in the file. Now it's saved back as `process`.
- **Outlines by reference, not by name:**
  - `NodeTypeInfo.Outline` / `OutcomeInfo.Outline` point at `ShapeOutlines.Diamond` and the other shared instances.
  - `INodeKind.OutlineOf` replaces `ShapeOf`.
  - The `"diamond"` keys, `IShapeOutline.Key` and `ShapeOutlines.Get` are gone.
- **Palette keys are typed:**
  - `"outcome:pass"` / `"round:decision"` become `PaletteItem` (type + outcome + round). `NodeFactory`, `QuickAdd`, `AddNodeAt` and the gestures all take it.
  - A palette drag keeps the drop action instead of a string that was switched on at drop time.
- **Showing an enum as text:** a dropdown's option values, Mermaid ids and toasts use `EnumNames.Of(value)`, which gives the same lowercase names as before, never `ToString()`.

CLAUDE.md gets a new design rule for this, and the README is updated.

## Testing
- **.NET 10:** compile-checked. **.NET 8:** click-tested.
- **One-type-per-file check:** OK.
- **Regression, against master** (gestures / keyboard / all-shapes):
  - Every saved diagram is byte-for-byte the same.
  - That run showed export differences, which turned out to be a flaky script step. It is fixed in its own PR.
- **The full four-suite run on the stack** (see the last PR) found one real difference: the toast after *Elbow* / *Straight* on a multi-selection said "Elbow" instead of "elbow". It's fixed here.

body:
## Summary

First step of the pivot from TimesFM price forecasting to a rule-based paper-trading system (see `TRADING_PLAN.md`). The TimesFM studies (`results/`, `results-broad/`, `src/timesfm_stock/`) are untouched.

- New `src/trader/` package: cached dividend-adjusted Yahoo data, 12-1 momentum + 200-day SMA trend signal, inverse-volatility weights targeting 10% volatility (max 25% per asset, no leverage), fills at the next session's open with 10 bps costs, SPY buy-and-hold and 60/40 benchmarks.
- Rules and pass bar fixed in `trader_policy_v1.json` / `trader_policy_v2.json` before each backtest ran; the CLI refuses to run if a frozen policy changes. Results are written per version to `trader-results/vN/`.
- `TRADING_PLAN.md`: the phased plan and the decision to keep LLMs out of the trading decision path.

## Results (2006-01-03 to 2026-11-06)

| | v1 weekly | v2 monthly | 60/40 | SPY |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 5.5% | 6.5% | 8.1% | 10.8% |
| Sharpe | 0.48 | 0.58 | 0.61 | 0.54 |
| Max drawdown | −15% | −12% | −33% | −55% |
| Cost drag/yr | 0.64% | 0.30% | 0.03% | 0% |
| Verdict | RETHINK | PROCEED | | |

v1 failed the cost bar because weekly signal flips drove 636%/yr turnover. v2 changes only the rebalance frequency and passes every check, including doubled costs. It still trails 60/40 on return and Sharpe; its value is drawdown protection. v2 was chosen after seeing v1 on the same period, so paper trading is the real test.

## Testing

- 19 new offline tests in `tests/test_trader.py` (look-ahead checks that shock future prices and confirm past decisions and equity are unchanged, next-open fills and costs, trade threshold, monthly scheduling, policy immutability, end-to-end run on synthetic data). The full suite passes locally: 43 tests.

author: andrewforester
body:
Removes the dark band with a hard edge between her upper lid and the brow when her eyes close. Refs #75.

## Cause

When the upper lid lowers, the inner side of the lid fold comes into view. It faces down, so the key light leaves it dark, and the brow skin above, facing up, overlaps it with a hard edge. The shader already lifted lid normals on blink, but it took its region from the blink wrinkle mask, which lies on the brow skin above and misses the fold.

Ruled out on GPU renders: the skin texture, the crease shading, wrinkle normals, the normal map, normals tracked vs computed from geometry, eyeshell, eyelashes, saliva, cartilage, eyeballs and back faces. A view-space normal render showed the band as down-facing skin.

## What changes

- `RigState` returns `lids`: how far each upper lid has closed, 0 to 1, from the rotation of `FACIAL_*_EyelidUpperB` (19 degrees when closed). It also covers a downward look, which lowers the lids without `eyeBlink`.
- The skin shader's lid term covers the fold around each eye: above the eye center, with a down-facing normal. It lifts those normals by that side's lid closure. The blink-mask term `lidA` and `WrinkleLayout.blink` are gone.
- Tests: lids at rest, one closed, one half closed; lids lower on a downward look and stay open looking up.

## Checks

- Close-ups, before and after: half closed, closed, looking down, a wink with one eye, open and wide. The band is gone when the lids are lowered; open eyes look the same as before.
- `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (2727 passed), `npm run build`.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 80 passed, 13 skipped, one failure in `coach.spec.ts` on phone. It fails the same way on `master` (#130).
- Contact sheets on phone and desktop: unchanged, since headless runs show the portrait.

Seen but not in scope: the cartilage mesh shows as a thin line through the closed lid.

author: dannyota
body:
### Description

WebGPU registers `SimplifiedLayerNormalization`, but `SimplifiedLayerNormFusion` only ran for CPU and CUDA, so decomposed RMSNorm (Pow/ReduceMean/Add/Sqrt/Div/Mul) in WebGPU-assigned graphs was never fused.

- Run the fusion for WebGPU, for the Cast-free pattern only. The WebGPU f16 kernel narrows `inv_std_dev` before the multiply, which can overflow, and removing a narrowing leading Cast would lose its rounding.
- For WebGPU nodes, fuse only when X and scale are both fp32 or both fp16, the scale covers the full last dimension, and the build is not a training build. The WebGPU kernel and the downstream MatMulNBits MLP/QKV fusions do not handle the other cases.
- Require `keepdims=1` (or absent) on the ReduceMean for every EP. With `keepdims=0` the normalized value broadcasts across the row, so fusing changes results; this was already wrong on CPU and CUDA.
- Fix scale selection for rank-one X on every EP. With `Mul(scale, normalized)` both operands are 1D, and the fusion could pick the normalized output as scale, leaving the fused node with an unresolved input. On main this makes a CPU session fail to initialize with `Invalid model. Node input ... is not a graph input`.

**Testing** (macOS arm64, Metal, `--use_webgpu`)

- `onnxruntime_test_all`: SimplifiedLayerNorm, LayerNorm, SkipLayerNorm, GQA pre-norm and MatMulNBits MLP/QKV fusion tests pass (94; 4 CUDA-only skipped). New tests cover WebGPU fp32/fp16, the rejected cases (including `keepdims=0` and promoted/narrowing Casts), rank-one X with both Mul operand orders on CPU and WebGPU, and the production transformer list.
- `onnxruntime_provider_test`: WebGPU layer norm tests pass (148), including new end-to-end fp32, fp16 and rank-one tests that check the fused node runs on WebGPU and matches CPU, and a promoted-fp16 Cast case that must stay unfused.
- The new tests fail without the change; `SimplifiedLayerNormFusionCpuRankOneScaleFirst` fails on main.

**Testing** (Linux x64, Intel Lunar Lake integrated GPU, Vulkan/Mesa ANV)

- All new tests pass; `onnxruntime_provider_test` WebGPU layer norm tests pass (148).
- `GraphTransformationTests.MatMulNBitsMlpFusionMatchesUnfusedSimplifiedQuickGeluWebGpuResults` fails on this GPU (2 elements just over tolerance), identically on main, so it is unrelated to this change.

### Motivation and Context

Fixes #29841. The other fusions listed there (Gelu, FastGelu, BiasGelu, LayerNorm, SkipLayerNorm) are already enabled for WebGPU on main.

author: sunrioa
body:
## Summary

Refs #6716.

The Rust Bot can arrange scheduled tasks, but scheduled investigations do not yet have a dedicated way to finish quietly or hand recorded findings back to the Bot.

Add a `discovery` effect to the existing Scheduler. Each fire creates a fresh read-only worker Session. The worker calls `DiscoveryComplete` to record either `no_report` or `report` and end its Turn. A `no_report` outcome settles without waking the Bot; a report enters the existing notification path, where the Bot decides whether to notify the user.

- Reuse once/interval/cron schedules and manual triggers. Model-created schedules remain paused proposals requiring human approval; discovery is opt-in.
- Use read-only workspace permissions without permission requests, with a restricted catalog of file-reading/search tools, enabled built-in Recall tools and `DiscoveryComplete`.
- Keep one investigation slot and persist the original fire, execution and result identities in the existing scheduler KV namespace. Track the investigation Turn independently of later user work in the same Session, including across restart and sealed Host handoff.
- Preserve cancellation when a plan is immediately resumed or the service is disabled and re-enabled. Recheck the captured source permissions at report admission; resuming a plan does not revive its cancelled fire.
- Update the generated SDK contracts and the native plugin's English/Chinese documentation.

Targets `rust-preview`. This is the initial manual/timed investigation and result-settlement slice of A1/A3 in #6716. Source-change intake, shared memory and feedback linkage remain follow-up work.

Local macOS verification for `96d87444c0dde0c1b4062da813df44645c562eeb`, using Rust 1.98.0 and Node 26.13.0 for SDK checks.

<summary>简体中文</summary>

## 概述

关联 #6716。

Rust Bot 已经能够安排定时任务，但定时调查还缺少一条明确支持静默结束和将已记录发现交回 Bot 的路径。

在现有 Scheduler 中增加 `discovery` 效果。每次触发新建一个只读 worker Session。worker 调用 `DiscoveryComplete`，记录 `no_report` 或 `report` 并结束本轮。没有值得报告的发现时静默结算，不唤醒 Bot；有报告时通过现有通知路径交给 Bot，由 Bot 判断是否通知用户。

- 复用 once／interval／cron 计划和手动触发。模型创建的计划仍是需要用户批准的暂停提议，主动发现默认不启用。
- 使用只读工作区权限，禁止申请额外权限；工具目录收敛为文件读取与搜索、已启用的内置 Recall 和 `DiscoveryComplete`。
- 保留一个调查位，在现有调度器 KV 命名空间中持久保存原触发、执行和结果身份。独立跟踪调查 Turn，不受同一 Session 中后续用户工作的影响，并处理重启及已封存的 Host 交接。
- 立即恢复计划，或停用后重新启用服务，都不会撤销已记录的取消。报告实际接纳前重新检查原来源权限；恢复计划不会复活已取消的那次触发。
- 同步更新生成的 SDK 契约，以及原生插件的中英文文档。

目标分支为 `rust-preview`。这是 #6716 中 A1/A3 的首个手动／定时调查与结果结算切片。来源变化事件接入、共享记忆和反馈关联留在后续阶段。

author: gthesheep-orchestra
body:
## Why
A week of Langfuse traces showed that most MCP tool "errors" were results too large for the Claude Agent SDK, not API failures. For example, 22% of `download_task_run_log` calls failed this way, as did 37% of `list_task_runs` and 48% of `list_assets`. Claude Code saves any text result over 50,000 characters (or 25k tokens) to a file, and the agent then spends Bash/jq calls reading it back.

## What
- Any tool returning the API's `{page, pageSize, total, results}` envelope never returns more than about 40,000 characters. That includes `list_task_runs`, `list_task_runs_for_pipeline_run`, `list_assets`, `list_incident_events`, `list_operations` and the other paged list tools. A page over that is cut to a smaller page size that divides the requested one. Its `page`/`pageSize` are rewritten to match, and a note names the next call, so following pages reaches every record exactly once.
- `download_task_run_log` and `download_task_run_artifact` read files in 30 KB chunks by default. `offset` sets the starting byte, and a negative offset reads the tail. Each result reports `total_bytes` and `next_offset`, so the whole file stays reachable.
- A new `chunk_bytes` setting on the downloads accepts up to 3 MiB per call. It's for saving a large file (such as a dbt manifest) to disk and processing it with a script, instead of hundreds of 30 KB calls.
- Downloads return UTF-8 content as plain text instead of base64. Text with a few invalid bytes stays readable: those bytes appear as `\xNN` escapes, and the original bytes can be recovered. Binary content is base64-encoded at 3/4 of the chunk size, so the encoded result stays within both the character and token limits. No bytes are lost at chunk edges, and an empty file returns empty content.

## Decisions & callouts
- **Breaking:** the downloads' `range_header` parameter is replaced by `offset` (plus the optional `chunk_bytes`). Agent prompts or skills that pass `range_header` need updating.
- Two caps, for two different limits:
  - **40k characters:** what an agent can read in line. The default download chunk is derived from it, as 3/4 of it to allow for base64.
  - **3 MiB per chunk:** what the Lambda response can carry; the existing 5 MB guard still backs up every other tool.
- Pages shrink to a divisor of the requested size rather than switching the tools to offset/limit. This keeps the API's own `page`/`page_size` contract, so continuation needs no state and no extra API call.
- Edge case: a single record over the budget on its own keeps only its top-level fields, with strings cut to 200 characters, and the note says so. I don't expect records that large in practice.
- No grep/filter for logs. Tail reads plus paging cover the traces seen so far.

- Not exercised against stage. Tests cover:
  - a server ignoring the Range header: offset 0 still reads, other offsets return an error
  - multi-byte characters split across chunk boundaries
  - binary artifacts
  - bulk 3 MiB reads
- After deploy: in Langfuse, check that the over-limit rejections for these seven tools drop to about zero, and that Bash read-backs of saved tool results fall.

body: ## Why In-app agents rebuild `diagnose` by hand. Over a week of traces, 208 sessions read operations or logs without ever calling `diagnose`, and 54 called it. The agents run Claude Code with deferred tools, so the model sees tool **names** and the MCP server's **instructions**, not descriptions. It loads tools by `select:` with names taken from its prompt. Nothing on this server's side pointed it at the composites: there were no server instructions, the low-level tools never mention `diagnose`, and the `diagnose` description doesn't say when to use it. Most of those sessions (153 of 208) come from the Incident Diagnosis managed agent, whose system prompt in pipeline-service spells out the low-level chain. That is the main fix, and it goes in a separate change there. This PR covers the part this server owns, for every client. ## What - **Server instructions** route triage to `whats_broken`, `diagnose(task_run_id)` and `pipeline_context`. They also name the low-level tools as the fallback for detail the composites don't return. - **A `prefer` hint on adaptations**, appended to the description of the tools agents load instead of the composites: `list_task_runs_for_pipeline_run`, `list_operations`, `list_task_run_logs`, `list_pipeline_runs`, `get_pipeline` and `get_pipeline_data`. `download_task_run_log` gets the same pointer. - **The `diagnose` description** now starts with when to use it and which calls it replaces. author: attackwave
body:
Tier 3 linked across language boundaries and to names no file defines.

- **Crate-scoped Rust names** (`name from ~dirs`) linked to the only definition of that name in any language inside the crates. With a crate at the tree root that is every file: on this repository 22 Rust functions called `deploy/kubernetes/core-smoke.yaml#args`, and `impact` on that YAML key listed them. Only Rust definitions count now, for the uniqueness test too.
- **A bare name** could link to a definition in a file of no language, such as a Markdown heading; a definition now needs a known language in the placeholder's set.
- **SCIP documents whose file no longer exists** minted their definitions; only their edges were dropped, so tier 3 linked calls to names nothing defines, and the phantom names made real ones ambiguous. Such a document is still reported stale and now defines nothing.
- **`is_test_path`** matches path components: `latest_x.rs` counted as a test file and a root-level `tests/` did not.

Not changed: a placeholder reached from two languages still links into one of them. Its callers share one node, so linking it nowhere is the only strictly correct answer without per-language placeholders, and that cost one structural set six points (8 callers of a Swift method shared the name with one call in another language). The comment states the trade-off.

`FORMAT_VERSION` 64.

Checks: `demo_imports` adds a YAML key inside a crate and a Python call named like a Markdown heading, neither linked; the SCIP self-check requires an index of another tree to mint no definitions; a unit test pins `is_test_path`. author: lotus015
body:
Benchmark on #247 (split run_app in main.rs) showed where a Baro run loses time against a single Claude Code session (15 min): stories merged at 27 min, then the final gate spent 20+ min on the untouched TypeScript suite and timed out.

**Shared cargo target per repository.** Each story worktree had its own empty `target/` (872 MB rebuilt per story). Story sandboxes (Claude and CLI lanes) now get `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` under the package cache, keyed by repository; it is already writable from the sandbox.

**Gates run only what the change touches.** `verifyBuild` takes `changedSince`; detected commands of ecosystems the diff never touched are not run (announced as `not run, the change touches none of their files`). Wired into the final run gate, the finalizer fallback and the per-story continuous gate. Fails open: an unclassifiable changed file, an unreadable diff, or a scope that would leave no suite runs everything; declared tests always run. `BARO_VERIFY_SCOPE=0` disables it.

**Pre-existing failures and test weakening.** Story sandboxes deny `ps`, so five process-group tests fail only there. The Critic rejected S1 for it, moved the criterion to a transfer story, and that story made the tests return early, which the Critic accepted. Now:
- Critic: a failure captured failing the same way at the base commit is pre-existing, never a violation or contract conflict (only a captured base run proves it).
- Critic: skipping, early-returning from, loosening or deleting an existing test is a violation unless a criterion asks for it.
- Stories are told to prove such failures at their base and never edit tests around the sandbox.

Tests: new `change-scope.test.ts`, sandbox/hook-bridge cargo target tests, prompt rule tests. Failures seen under heavy parallel load (Codex timeout, worktree integration) pass alone and on 0.130.0 alike.
