author: sh-agents
body:
Page side: https://github.com/simplex-chat/simplex.domains/pull/12. The `apps/simplex-domains` pin moves once that PR is merged.

Registration pauses when the sponsor allowance cannot cover the orders in flight, and checkout stops taking money while it is paused.

**Pause**
- The worker pauses registration on `InsufficientAllowance`, at start when the allowance cannot cover every active order, and when a queued order is not covered.
- A probe reads the allowance every 15 s and resumes once the whole queue is covered.
- The allowance is read at the sender's confirmation depth, so a mined register is not counted twice.

**Checkout and orders**
- Name invoices and balance spends answer 503 `registration_paused` while paused, before any chain read or provider call.
- Code orders, Try again and moves are taken and queued.
- Invoices opened before a pause stay payable; every registration view carries `paused`.

**Queue**
- A queued order (paid or by code) is committed only while the allowance covers all orders in committing to registering plus the queue up to it, oldest first.
- A committed order whose commitment lapses ends `failed`, paused or not, as on `names`; the buyer uses Try again after the resume, and the failure is logged by the order's commitment.
- A register that reverts once mined returns its order to `committed`; the commitment and the sponsor nonce are unspent by a reverted call.
- Queued views carry `queue: {position, of}`.

**Monitoring**
- One report line at start, hourly and at each pause change: queued count and oldest order, orders in flight, the pause, the registrar's address, ETH and allowance.
- Error level while paused, above `[names] queue_alert` (default 20), below 5 × `gas_limit_cap` × `max_fee_per_gas` of ETH, or below one 6-letter order's register cost; alerts and pause changes also go to the managed group, without order identifiers.
- Log lines name orders by their commitment, which grants no access.

**Docs**: README sections on the pause and the report; `docs/names.md` §3.2 and §3.5.

author: wingleeio
body: `lines = 2, truncate = true` was one line in Luau, though Rust's `.line_clamp(2).text_overflow(Ellipsis)` gives two lines ending in "…", and so does UILabel with `numberOfLines = 2`. `docs/reference/text.md` read as if it worked and `properties.md` said one line, so a script had no way to ask for it. `truncate` now sets only the ellipsis. Text with an ellipsis and no clamp already keeps one line (`clamp` in zgx-gpu, `fallback_measure` in zgx), so `lines` wins whichever order they're set in, either of them literal or changing. **What changes:** - `lines = N, truncate = true` is N lines ending in "…". - `truncate` alone is still one line. - **A `lines` inherited from a parent now counts as set**, where `truncate` used to override it. A truncating child under `lines = 3` now gets up to three lines. Stated in the docs and changelog. **Tests:** `truncate_means_one_line_only_where_lines_does_not_say` covers both orders, literal and state-driven `truncate` and `lines`, and one line being half the height of two. Without the fix it fails at `both`, reading `(1, Ellipsis)`. Full `zgx-script` tests, clippy and fmt pass on the code; after a test-only change since, the `ui` area, clippy on the tests and fmt pass. **Perf:** arm64 gate against 50dd4c37f exits 1 on four rows. | row | change | zgx's own instructions | | --- | --- | --- | | fx-passes | +0.43% | +0 | | fx-reader | +0.09% | -45 | | mount | +0.03% | -4 | | video | +0.02% | not attributed (known noisy) | Nothing else in the 44 rows is above +0.01%. author: paws-helper[bot]
body:
Fixes PAS-1442

Fixes PAS-1442.

## Why

Runner-backed agent turns ended with `turn_aborted reason=interrupted`, and the item failed with "Run failed during agent: Error." Nothing in the control-plane journal showed who asked for it.

## What changed

**Interrupts are journaled where they are sent** (`src/runner-worker/index.ts`), with the item and run: `source=follow_up`, `handover`, `stop_checkpoint` and `unsolicited_agent`.

**An interrupt Paws didn't ask for no longer fails the item.**
- The worker treats a turn as unsolicited when it ended as cancelled, interrupted or a bare `Error`, and no signal, halt, handover, question end or timeout explains it. It saves the WIP through the existing stop checkpoint and reports `interrupted: true` (new optional field in `RunnerResultSchema`).
- If that checkpoint can't be saved, the worker sets `dropped` on the stop checkpoint and reports an error, because a restart would lose work.
- A stop checkpoint with no sha means the worktree equals the base. The snapshot skips files the index marks `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree`, so when any such file could hold an edit, the worker reports the stop as `dropped` instead.
- The backend (`src/runner-backend/index.ts`) restarts the turn once through the existing `RetryableRunnerError` path. It does so only if this generation's stop checkpoint was delivered, was not dropped, and matches the item's recorded WIP commit. A refused push, a failed save or missing stop evidence fails closed, as before.
- The retry needs a runner at `INTERRUPT_RECOVERY_RUNNER_VERSION` (0.1.75, the next release after the latest tag `v0.1.74`). Older runners report a failed save the same way as nothing to save, so they keep today's behaviour.
- The one retry belongs to each agent turn: a later turn after a restart or an answer gets its own, and the restarted attempt within a turn doesn't.
- Intentional stops, cancels and handovers are unchanged.

## Not established

- **Original interrupter:** this change doesn't identify what interrupted the turns at 04:35 and 04:59. The new journal lines will name the source next time.
- **The 05:12 failures:** I didn't confirm that the Paws restart caused them, so there is no new test for that case. The existing probe "a Paws restart leaves a runner's work running…" passes.

## Verification

- `test/local/runner-backend.ts`: an unsolicited interruption isn't failed, the WIP checkpoint is saved and the turn restarts only once, and a later turn through the same closure gets its own single restart. A refused, failed or missing stop checkpoint, or a runner older than 0.1.75, prevents the retry.
- `test/runner-checkpoint-worker.test.ts`: worker checkpoint and interruption paths, including `dropped` on a failed save, untracked, edited and deleted files at the base each publishing a commit, and edits hidden by `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` preventing the restart.
- `test/proofs/agent-interrupted.ts`: new proof scenario, run by `verify:proof`.

author: goreecloud
body:
## Scope
Advance GoreeCloud Headless Browser acceptance from `about:blank`/arithmetic to a **real local HTML document**, without browsing any third-party website or authorizing production private-network access.

## Implementation
- Launch a disposable stdlib HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port, serving only fixed inert HTML with an explicit deny-all Content Security Policy, a deterministic title and a single heading. No remote images, scripts, fonts or redirects.
- Add optional `allow_private_network` to the owned CDP test helper, defaulting to **false**. Only this owned-fixture smoke launches `goreecloud-headless-browser --allow-private-network serve` on an ephemeral loopback CDP port, as required to reach the test server; existing private-address protections and other tests retain their secure defaults.
- Validate the entire test URL structurally (exact `http` scheme, numeric `127.0.0.1` authority, actual bounded port, fixed path, **no username, password, query or fragment**), including regression tests against a prefix-camouflage external host.
- Over an authenticated native CDP WebSocket protocol path, create and attach to `about:blank`, perform `Page.navigate` to the owned HTML fixture, poll bounded `Runtime.evaluate` reads for exact document title and heading text, close the page, and stop the fixture.
- Add 10 stdlib tests for CSP/inert fixture, raw bytes, forbidden routes, URL security, network URL serialization, bounded retry and cleanup even on failure.
- Run the real browser/fixture test in read-only, nonpublishing GitHub Actions behind a 90-second execution timeout after earlier build, SSRF, CDP and trusted-V8 gates.

## Local evidence
83 Python regression tests passed, four import/provenance/workflow gates passed, the Cargo.lock inventory verified 490 packages and `git diff --check` passed. Actual HTML navigation/DOM execution on the built Rust binary is **pending Actions verification**.

## Release caveat
This does not establish arbitrary external site navigation, rendering pixel accuracy, Puppeteer/Playwright integration, production egress isolation, license/asset clearance, distributable builds or deployment. The explicit private-network opt-in is restricted to the controlled fixture and must not be treated as a production default.

author: damrianeelesh
body:
## Description

Fix the six reported UAT Location regressions. Retired accounts are excluded before picker search and pagination. Location writes keep the database erasure fence and return a safe conflict if retirement races the action. Nearby check-in surfaces its existing phone requirement and resumes through the normal verification flow. Entrance editing normalizes renderer coordinates, bounds recovery and keeps the pin usable when address lookup fails. Active shares headings and controls align at responsive widths.

## Impact Map (Required)

- Routes touched: `/one/location`, `/one/location/check-in`, `/register-phone`, and the existing Location grant, access request, Circle-member and reverse-geocode APIs.
- API / schema / type changes: `LOCATION_PEER_UNAVAILABLE` is a safe HTTP 409 for the named erasure guards. The request and success response schemas are unchanged.
- Cache keys touched: none.
- Runtime DB data-plane changes: exclude tombstones from eligible reads before pagination. Acquire existing deletion locks before domain locks in Location writes. The existing migration and guard retain write authority. No new migration.
- World-model domain summary effects: none.
- Live Memory source impact (every feature):
  - [x] No durable owner data is created, changed, or deleted by this patch.
  - Live Memory evidence (source kind and test, or no-impact reason): The patch changes validation, recipient visibility, error handling and editor recovery. Existing owner-scoped saves and Location records keep their storage, source and consent contracts.
- Mobile parity impacts: shared Capacitor map and web UI code. Native bridge tests ran locally. Physical iOS and Android QA is separate.
- Docs updated: none.
- Top-level / devex / config / generated / ignore files touched: regenerated the existing UI Back and Search review receipts and runtime topology fingerprint with the repository UI contract builder.
- Trust boundary touched: existing account lifecycle, phone eligibility, encrypted Location grants, and private-agent action authority. Location writes still require the existing auth and relationship checks. No credentials, provider error details or raw DB payloads cross the response boundary.
- Caller / proxy / backend pairing: the existing One proxy preserves the typed backend response. Browser phone recovery returns to Nearby. The pin normalizes renderer longitude before calling the existing bounded geocoder.
- Rollback or safe-failure behavior: compatible application rollback. A retired recipient cannot receive a new grant, request or Circle membership. Existing approved access and manual address entry continue under their current authority.
- UI browser or Playwright proof: `playwright test e2e/active-share-actions.layout.spec.ts e2e/save-location-sheet.layout.spec.ts --project=chromium --project=webkit --workers=2` passed 186 layout cases before UAT intake.
- Verification commands executed: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:ui-contracts`, `npm run verify:ui-contracts`, focused Location and Circle Vitest, focused Python API/service pytest, and disposable PostgreSQL picker/deletion-race checks. Signed-in acceptance follows deployment.

## Review-Ready Contract

The existing Location app routes and private-agent Ask tool call the changed services. Tests exercise the production components, API error handling and SQL contracts. No dependent PR is required. The commits carry DCO signoff. Destination is protected UAT and current-head hosted validation is required.

## Tri-Flow Architecture Check

- Web: existing Next.js Location app and API proxy.
- iOS: shared Capacitor picker and existing native camera bridge. No Swift API change.
- Android: shared Capacitor picker and existing native camera bridge. No Kotlin API change.

## Privacy & Consent

The erasure fence and existing vault and consent checks remain authoritative. Nearby phone verification is eligibility only. Rejected accounts and providers yield sanitized user-facing errors.

## Licensing

No dependency or licensing changes.

## What

The marshal graph can now be limited to a time range, so individual RSSI peaks can be inspected in detail on long races.

Controls below the graph:
- **Graph from / to (s)**: show only that range across the full graph width
- **+ / −**: zoom in/out by a factor of 2 around the centre
- **Full Race**: reset to the whole race
- **⇤ / ← / → / ⇥**: at the current zoom level, jump to the start, move 25% of the visible range left/right, jump to the end (disabled at the respective edge)

Also:
- Marking a lap in the table that lies outside the zoomed range moves the view to it.
- The zoom resets when another race/pilot is loaded.
- Tap-to-time mapping on the graph now takes the visible range into account.

## Reviewer notes

- Smoothie drops data that has scrolled off the left edge on every render. The graph now sets `maxDataSetLength: Infinity`, otherwise the data before the zoom window would be lost after the first zoom-in.
- The zoom API (`setViewRange`, `zoomViewRange`, `panViewRange`, `resetViewRange`, optional `viewRange` callback) lives in `RHMarshal`; `run.html` also uses `RHMarshal` but doesn't pass the callback and is unaffected.

Tested in a browser with a standalone page that loads the real `marshal.js`/CSS and the controls from `marshal.html` with synthetic RSSI data: range input, zoom buttons, Ctrl/Shift+wheel, edge clamping, start/end/±25% navigation and button disabled states, and that no history data is lost after zooming. author: mason-x
body:
## What
DEV (T8) showed that the host sends `turn_ended` before `archived`/`closed` (force archive, cascade archive) and on a graceful daemon stop, so the T4a/T4b "no turn_ended" settlement never fired: the engine read the ended turn as a normal end, could not read the reply (`incomplete:dispatch-not-found`) and only kept a warning.

The settlement trigger is widened, reusing the decision kinds and constants already approved in T4a/T4b (`member-lost`, `host-lost`, `LOST_TURN_SETTLE_DELAY_MS` = 30 s). In one commit, when all of these hold, the engine opens the decision and removes the exhausted alert (no engine receipt, no release, no send, no timer):
1. the assignment still awaits its report, dispatch confirmed, no sending/outcome-unknown delivery for the agent;
2. the turn has provably ended, with the same evidence `planCancelFinish` accepts (extracted into the shared pure function `provenEndedTurn`; cancel behaviour unchanged, all its old tests unchanged);
3. the reply is lost: retries exhausted with exactly `incomplete:dispatch-not-found`, a re-read in this pass still says so, and 30 s have passed since the last failure.
`member-lost` (cancel only) when a closed/archived receipt after creation exists or the seat reads closed; otherwise `host-lost` (D1 actions). After the decision opens, a later readable reply of that attempt is not credited (T9a's gate). The exhausted-alert hint now covers idle, closed and archived.

## Contract
None: no schema, receipt kind, reducer event kind, ledger field, RPC or prompt template change.

## Tests
213 files / 3920 tests pass on the branch (before merging main); ledger v1/v2 x the three real receipt orders (L1, L2, R), 29 s / 31 s boundary with a fake clock, non-triggering causes, late reply not credited, cancel releases, host-lost retry sends exactly one message. 26 mutations, all caught.

## Not done / residual
An archived seat that the host reports as absent does not trigger (cancel completes as before); re-checked in the DEV re-verification. Rolling back to 0.7.0 leaves unanswered new decisions that show "retry" but do nothing (not drilled; derived from the 0.7.0 source). README keeps "do not roll back an active Run".

## Rollback
Revert the merge commit.

author: siketyan
body:
## Summary

The IntelliJ Platform LSP API no longer requires a paid subscription. It is available in the free IntelliJ IDEA, and is provided as the `com.intellij.modules.lsp` module rather than as part of `com.intellij.modules.ultimate`. This PR switches the required dependency so that the plugin can be installed on free IDEs too.

## Changes

- `plugin.xml`: `<depends>com.intellij.modules.ultimate</depends>` → `<depends>com.intellij.modules.lsp</depends>`.
- `build.gradle.kts`: add IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 to the Plugin Verifier IDEs (previously WebStorm only via `recommended()`), so installability on a non-WebStorm IDE is checked in CI.
- `README.md`: drop the "cannot be installed on Community IDEs" note; mention that the free IntelliJ IDEA works and that the JavaScript / Node.js plugins and `@typespec/compiler` are required.

The `JavaScript` and `NodeJS` plugin dependencies are intentionally kept as required. IDEs without them (e.g. Android Studio, CLion, DataGrip) remain unsupported.

## Background

- In the IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 and PyCharm 2026.3 distributions (`product-info.json`), `com.intellij.modules.lsp` is a module alias backed by `lib/intellij.platform.lsp.jar`, while `com.intellij.modules.ultimate` is a separate plugin (`plugins/ultimate-plugin`). `JavaScript` and `NodeJS` are bundled in both.
- Core JavaScript/TypeScript features (incl. running npm scripts) are free in IntelliJ IDEA since 2026.1, and this plugin already requires 2026.1.4+.

author: lophius-srl
body:
## Résumé
Le moteur rend désormais n'importe quel `AudioProgram` (durée + événements datés : sons nommés et annonces vocales). VAMEVAL / Luc Léger et Cooper / demi-Cooper passent par ce moteur et produisent **exactement** les mêmes pistes qu'avant.

Closes #48

## Changements
- `audio/audio_program.dart` : `Cue` (repère, changement, décompte, pip, départ, fin), `ProgramEvent` (son ou annonce), `AudioProgram` (ordre = ordre de mixage, textes dédoublonnés, clé de cache, temps de l'activité)
- `audio/test_programs.dart` : programmes des tests par paliers et chronométrés
- `audio/program_renderer.dart` : un seul rendu, sons définis à un seul endroit
- `audio/program_builder.dart` : synthèse vocale une fois par texte distinct, rendu en isolate
- `TrackService.prepare(AudioProgram)` : un seul cache (clé = contenu du programme, `trackFormatVersion = 2`)
- Supprimés : `track_renderer`, `track_builder`, `timed_track`, `track_cache_key`

## Non-régression
- Empreintes FNV des pistes relevées **avant** le refactoring (commit séparé), identiques après : VAMEVAL 3 min à 23,77 m (`3938f2080b0b5ab2`) et demi-Cooper (`6da9e6d292498249`), avec voix synthétiques
- Tous les tests des écrans VMA inchangés et verts

## Mesures
- 45 min, un bip toutes les 0,35 s (7715 événements) : rendu ≈ 0,1 s sur Mac, **119 Mo** de WAV. Pour le métronome (#51), une courte boucle répétée sera préférable à une piste de 45 min.

## Comment tester
1. `make lint test build`
2. iPhone : un VAMEVAL et un demi-Cooper (première génération à nouveau, cache invalidé)

## Checklist
- [x] Les critères d'acceptation de l'issue sont remplis
- [x] `make lint test build` passe en local
- [x] Tests ajoutés ou mis à jour
- [ ] Docs, `.env.example` ou ADR mis à jour si nécessaire
- [x] Titre de PR au format conventionnel

author: rowan-hyeho-song
body:
Closes #222

## 무엇을, 왜

사용자가 직접 써 보며 불편하다고 한 두 가지를 고칩니다.
1. 결재함 · 서재 옆 패널의 오른쪽 여백이 왼쪽보다 좁거나 줄 끝 요소가 잘림
2. 처리된 결재는 눌러 볼 수 없음

사양은 이슈의 디자이너 댓글을 따랐습니다.

## 바뀐 것

- **여백**
  - 패널 머리 오른쪽을 12 → 16 px로 맞췄습니다. 탭 · 스크롤 영역 · 아래 버튼 줄 · 서재 · 문서는 이미 16 px였습니다.
  - 스크롤 영역 세 곳(결재 · 서재 목록 · 문서)에 `scrollbar-gutter: stable`과 얇은 어두운 스크롤바를 줬습니다. 스크롤바가 생겨도 내용 오른쪽 끝이 그대로입니다.
  - 방문자 목록의 여백이 이중으로 들어가 32 px이던 것을 바로잡았습니다.
  - 줄 끝 요소(날짜 · 뱃지 · 결과 · 이슈 번호)는 `flex: none`, 글 쪽은 `min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere`입니다. 요청 본문과 문서 종이에도 `overflow-wrap: anywhere`를 줬습니다(긴 영어 낱말에서 실제로 넘쳤습니다).
- **처리된 결재 상세(주인)**: 대기 상세의 클래스를 재사용했습니다. 위에서부터:
  - `← 처리됨`
  - 에이전트 · 종류 칩 · 정지한 결과 도장(`승인` / `반려` / `안 N`)
  - 제목
  - `요청 … · 결재 … · 걸린 시간 …`
  - 본문
  - 읽기 전용 선택지: 고른 것은 빨강 테두리 + `✓ 고름`, 나머지는 55%
  - 의견: 반려인데 의견이 없으면 `의견 없음`
  - 원문 링크 둘
  - 버튼 줄은 없습니다. Esc나 `← 처리됨`을 누르면 목록으로 돌아가고, 초점은 연 줄로 돌아갑니다.
- **처리된 결재(방문자)**: 머리 줄 + `결재 서류 1건` + 결재 시각 + SECRET 표지(`주인만 볼 수 있어요` · `누가 · 언제 · 결과만 보입니다`)만 보입니다.
- **방문자 데이터**: `supabase/approvals.sql`에 `approvals_decided_cover` 뷰를 더했습니다.
  - 싣는 것: id · kind · requester_seat · result · decided_at
  - result는 `승인` · `반려` · `선택지 N` 꼴만 그대로 내보내고, 나머지는 `결정`으로 바꿉니다(자유 글이 새지 않게).
  - 앱(`supabaseSource.decidedCovers`)은 뷰가 없으면 빈 목록으로 처리합니다. 그래서 SQL을 적용하기 전에는 지금과 같습니다.
- 처리됨 목록 줄은 이제 button입니다. 읽어 주는 이름은 `메모 결재: 5인 책상 배치 — 승인, 11월 9일 23시 58분` 형식입니다.
- 테스트
  - `view.test.ts`: 도장 글자 · 걸린 시간 · 읽어 주는 문장
  - `fakeSource.test.ts`
  - `coverSql.test.ts`: 두 방문자 뷰에 제목 · 내용 · 선택지 · 의견 · 링크가 없는지
- `scripts/a11y.mjs`: 주인 처리됨 목록 · 처리된 상세 · 방문자 표지 상태를 더했습니다.

### ⚠️ 적용할 SQL (사용자)

`supabase/approvals.sql`을 다시 실행해 주세요. 새 뷰 하나와 grant만 더해지고, 여러 번 실행해도 안전합니다. 적용 전에는 방문자에게 처리된 결재 구획이 나오지 않습니다(지금과 같음). 주인 화면은 SQL 없이 동작합니다.

### 사양과 다른 점

- 스크롤바 폭: Windows Chrome의 `scrollbar-width: thin`이 10 px로 그립니다(사양 8 px).
- 종류 칩 글자: `선택` · `승인·반려` · `공개`. `공개`는 코더가 정했습니다.
- 읽어 주는 이름: `aria-label` 대신 화면 밖 글로 줬습니다. axe `label-content-name-mismatch`(serious)를 피하기 위해서이고, 읽히는 문장은 사양과 같습니다.
- 방문자 SECRET 도장 색: 어두운 패널에서 대비가 부족해서 `--stamp-red`를 썼습니다.
- 브라우저 뒤로 가기는 대기 상세처럼 쓰지 않습니다(Esc · `← 처리됨`만).
- 760 px 문서 보기: 종이 `max-width`(읽는 줄 길이) 때문에 종이 오른쪽이 비어 내용 기준 오른쪽 여백이 46 px입니다. 패널 안쪽 여백은 16 px 그대로입니다.

## 확인한 것

| 확인 | 방법 | 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| 여백 측정 | Playwright `getBoundingClientRect`, 패널 380 · 480 · 760 · 휴대폰 390 × 11개 화면(대기 목록 · 대기 상세 · 처리됨 목록 · 처리된 상세 주인 3종 · 방문자 · 방문자 목록 · 서재 폴더 · 파일철 · 문서) | 모든 칸에서 좌 / 우 16 / 16 px, 가로 넘침 0. 예외는 760 문서 보기의 종이 오른쪽 하나(위에 적음). 측정은 서브에이전트가 했음 |
| 화면(제가 직접 봄) | 380 처리된 상세(안 2 + 의견 + 링크), 480 방문자 처리된 상세 | 사양 순서 · 도장 · ✓ 고름 · 55% 흐림 · 추천 칩 · 링크 / 방문자는 SECRET 표지만 |
| 방문자 뷰 안전 | `coverSql.test.ts` | 두 뷰 모두 비공개 열 없음, result는 정해진 꼴만 |
| 전체 | `npx vitest run` (dev 병합 뒤) | 69파일 1127 통과 |
| 타입 · 빌드 · API · 8조합 | `pnpm typecheck` · `build` · `api:check` · `smoke` | 통과 |
| 접근성 | `pnpm a11y` | serious · critical 0 (moderate는 새 상태 3개가 더해져 늘어남, 랜드마크 종류) |

못 한 것: 실제 Supabase 데이터로 방문자 처리된 구획을 보지 못했습니다(SQL 적용 전이라). `?debug=1` 가짜 소스로만 확인했습니다.

## 스크린샷

| 처리된 상세(주인, 380) | 처리된 상세(방문자, 480) | 처리됨 목록(380, 긴 제목 · #10000) |
|---|---|---|
| ![a](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets/222-w380-04-decided-detail-20-20261110-001255.png) | ![b](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets/222-w480-08-visitor-decided-detail-20261110-001255.png) | ![c](https://github.com/Rowan-Hyeho-Song/agent-office/releases/download/image-assets/222-w380-03-decided-list-20261110-001255.png) |

## 위험·되돌리기

- 새 방문자 뷰는 처리된 결재의 종류 · 자리 · 결과 · 시각을 공개합니다. 사양("누가 · 언제 · 결과만")과 같습니다.
- 되돌리려면 PR을 revert하고 `drop view public.approvals_decided_cover;`를 실행하면 됩니다.

## 체크

- [ ] 이슈의 완료 기준을 모두 채웠다 (디자이너 확인이 남음)
- [x] 민감 정보(키·토큰·회사 이름·내부 주소·개인 경로)가 코드·문서·이미지에 없다
- [x] 설계가 바뀌었으면 `docs/`를 같이 고쳤다 (사양은 이슈 댓글 그대로. 다른 점은 위에 적음)
- [x] 대상 브랜치가 맞다 (작업 → `dev`, 배포 → `main`)

## AI 작성

코더 세션이 서브에이전트(Sonnet)에 구현과 측정을 맡겼습니다. 리뷰하면서 방문자 뷰 SQL과 그 안전 검사 테스트를 더했고, 위에 적은 화면은 직접 확인했습니다.

author: bdevloed
body:
Improvements on OP-3947 (#754) from ticket OP-3962. No backend changes needed.

Status: a relation whose start date is in the future is not active; it becomes active on that day. Both tables derive the status the same way, so nothing changes in the data.

Repeated relations: a new row with the same relation type and organization as a stored row, or as an earlier new row, shows the warning "Je maakt een relatie aan die reeds bestaat, deze nieuwe relatie zal niet worden opgeslagen" under the organization as soon as both are picked. Saving drops such a row, as it silently did before, and now also unloads it from the store. For "Heeft een relatie met" the sides may be swapped: a repeat picked from the other organization's page used to pass the filter and ended up stored twice.

A repeat is allowed when the two relations cannot be active at the same time: both organizations active and no overlap between the periods. A missing start date counts as "since always", a missing end date as "still running", and on its end date a relation is still active. So a repeat of an ended relation needs a start date after that end date; without dates it is a duplicate. This covers the ticket's case (first relation Niet actief) and also allows a relation in the past next to a running one.

Fixed along the way: removing a relation and adding it again in the same session no longer loses it, and the "Heeft een relatie met" double above.

Tests: the status and overlap logic, the duplicate rule and the save behaviour, plus tests for code that had none: the index and parent routes, the edit route query, the controller's direction and confirmation flows, the role-label filter and both tables.

TO TEST
- Add a relation with a start date in the future: Status relatie is Niet actief in the edit table and in the overview.
- Add a relation that already exists, same type and organization, without dates: the warning appears at once; after saving the row is gone and nothing else changed.
- Give an existing relation a past end date and save. Add the same relation again with a start date after that end date: no warning, and both are in the overview, the old one Niet actief, the new one Actief. With a start date inside the old period, or without dates, the warning is back.
- Repeat a relation with an organization that is not active, with non-overlapping dates: the warning stays, since such relations are never active.
- Remove an existing relation and add the same one again before saving: after saving it is still there.

The 780-line static `Geometry` is gone. Each member moved, unchanged, to a class with one job:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `Models/Routing/EdgeRouter` | `Route`, `EdgeGeometry`, `SidePoint`, `AutoSides`, `PointAt`, `RoundedPathD` |

author: adrianstrugala
body:
From the 4.x list of the release plan: `decimal` on `fixed` in classes.

## The problem

Java, Apache.Avro and Confluent schemas often hold money as a decimal on a fixed:

```json
{"type": "fixed", "name": "Money", "size": 16, "logicalType": "decimal", "precision": 20, "scale": 2}
```

AvroConvert already read such data, and its writer already wrote it when the schema was given. But a class could not have it:
- `decimal` was always `decimal` on `bytes`;
- `[AvroFixed]` was allowed only on `byte[]`.

So `GenerateModel` turned it into `decimal` on `bytes`. That is another schema with other bytes: headless data and a registry with that schema did not match the class.

## Now

`[AvroFixed]` on a `decimal` (or `decimal?`) member is a decimal on that fixed. Precision and scale come from `[AvroDecimal]`:

```csharp
[AvroFixed(16, "Money", "shop")]
[AvroDecimal(Precision = 20, Scale = 2)]
public decimal amount { get; set; }
```

- **`GenerateModel`** writes this for a decimal on a fixed. That covers a fixed defined in place and a fixed referred to by name in another field (`["null", "Money"]` → `decimal?`). A fixed without a logical type stays `byte[]`.
- **Unions.** In a union, `[AvroFixed]` names the `byte[]` branch, or else the `decimal` one. `GenerateModel` drops the attribute when that would be ambiguous: a decimal on a fixed next to a `byte[]`.
- **Too-large values.** A value that needs more bytes than the fixed has now throws `Decimal [1000000] needs 3 bytes; the decimal is on the fixed [Small] of 2 bytes`. Before, it was an `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `Span.Slice`. This also applies to schemas given as text.

Not covered: a decimal on a fixed in the items of an array or the values of a map. `[AvroFixed]` on the member cannot say that, so it stays `decimal` on `bytes`, listed in the exceptions in `Documentation.Schema.md`.

## Tests

- `DecimalOnFixedTests`:
  - the schema of the class has the same canonical form as the parsed schema;
  - round trip in `Formats.Core` (negative, zero, 20 digits, `null`);
  - headless bytes from the class equal those from the parsed schema;
  - error for a value that does not fit;
  - error for `[AvroFixed]` on another type.
- `GenerateModel`:
  - output for a fixed in place, by name, and without a logical type;
  - the generated class gives back the same canonical form and full JSON.
- Component 3816/3816, interop 132/132, unit 105/105.

Docs: `Documentation.Schema.md` (the attribute table, logical types, Generate model), CHANGELOG, and the XML doc of `AvroFixedAttribute`.

author: nopitch
body:
## Why

A running host blocked every removal of the microphone: a driver update, the device disabled,
`devcon remove`. The host interface refuses a query-remove while a handle is open (it must: the
host writes into a mapping that lasts until its handle closes), so removals waited for a
reboot. M5's design asks the crate to follow the microphone instead: let it go when Windows
asks, attach again when it comes back.

## What

- **`Player::follow(formats, callback)`** (`host/src/player.rs`): the player's thread attaches
  by itself and registers with `CM_Register_Notification` for interface arrivals and for the
  device behind its handle, as Microsoft's "Registering for Notification of Device Interface
  Arrival and Device Removal" describes.
  - **Removal request** (`DEVICEQUERYREMOVE`): the handle must be closed before the callback
    returns, but the player's thread writes into the mapping. The callback (a system thread)
    signals the thread and waits, up to 2 s, while it detaches and closes its handle.
  - **No reattach while the removal is being decided**: until it is cancelled
    (`QUERYREMOVEFAILED`, then attach again) or pending/complete (then wait for the interface
    to come back). The first version reattached at once, before the driver's query-remove, and
    its new handle made the driver refuse the removal: seen in the VM and found by the review.
  - **One registration per device**, kept across reattachments (it stays valid after its
    handle closes), dropped from the player's thread once the device is gone: unregistering
    waits for callbacks in flight, so it never happens while one waits for that thread. A
    request pending at exit is answered with the handle closed first; later ones don't wait.
- **`Player::stop`** returns `Result<Option<Host>, Error>`; **`PlayerStats`** gains `attached`,
  `attachments`, `releases`. `Player::start(host, callback)` is unchanged otherwise.
- **`tools/test-host`** and **`examples/tone.rs`** follow the microphone; test-host no longer
  keeps a read-only handle, which would hold a removal back.
- **docs/test-vm.md** (the removal scenario) and **PLAN.md**'s note.

A kernel change first planned with this one (enable the interface only after marking the device
started) was dropped: the PnP manager neither announces an interface nor lets it open before
`IRP_MN_START_DEVICE` completes (`IoSetDeviceInterfaceState`'s remarks).

## Checks

- clippy, rustfmt, unit tests, docs.
- In the VM, while `test-host` plays: `devcon remove` removes the device and unloads the driver
  (`STOPPED`); after the reinstall the host attaches again and `capture-check` passes;
  disabling and enabling the host interface makes it let go and attach again (`PASS`); 3
  attachments, 2 releases, no packet skipped, no request refused.
- Independent review, then two reviews of the fixes. Remaining, accepted: with two hostmic
  adapters, replacing a registration can stall 2 s and release the new attachment once.

  - [x] Linted (`make lint`)

    1. Clone / pull the latest [CLI](https://github.com/snyk/cli) main.
    2. Run `go get github.com/snyk/go-application-framework@YOUR_LATEST_GAF_COMMIT` in the `cliv2` directory.
        - Tip: for local testing, you can uncomment the line near the bottom of the CLI's
  [`go.mod`](https://github.com/snyk/cli/blob/main/cliv2/go.mod) to point to your local GAF code.
    3. Run `go mod tidy` in the `cliv2` directory.
    4. Run the CLI tests and do any required manual testing.
    5. Open a PR in the CLI repo **now** with the `go.mod` and `go.sum` changes.
    - Once this PR is merged, repeat these steps, but pointing to the latest GAF commit on main and update your CLI PR.

author: bobjoylove
body:
**Fix accessibility type (panel lock) mask**

The panel lock lives in status byte 9 bits 4–5 (`0x30`), but it was masked with `0x48`, which can never equal 16, 32 or 48, so `_accessibility_type` always fell through to `ALL`. As discussed in #118.

**Change:** `flag & 0x48` → `flag & 0x30` in `SpaClient._parse_status_update`.

## Testing

New parametrised test `tests/test_client.py::test_accessibility_type`. It takes the status message from the existing `bfbp20s` fixture, sets byte 9, parses it, and checks `_accessibility_type`:

| byte 9 | meaning | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | no lock | `ALL` |
| `0x10` | lock bits = 1 | `PUMP_LIGHT` |
| `0x20` | lock bits = 2 | `NONE` |
| `0x30` | lock bits = 3 | `NONE` |
| `0x0F` | no lock, with temp-unit / 24 h / filter-cycle bits set | `ALL` |
| `0x1F` | lock bits = 1, with those bits set | `PUMP_LIGHT` |
| `0x2F` | lock bits = 2, with those bits set | `NONE` |

- With the old `0x48` mask, the 5 locked cases (`0x10`, `0x20`, `0x30`, `0x1F`, `0x2F`) fail. With `0x30`, all 7 pass.
- Full suite, run as in CI: `uv run pytest --timeout=10 --cov=pybalboa --asyncio-mode=auto`: 32 passed.
- `uv run ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- `uv run ruff format . --check`: 15 files already formatted.
- `uv run mypy pybalboa tests`: no issues found in 14 source files.

author: lwille
body:
Fixes https://wearezeta.atlassian.net/browse/WPB-26631

### Change type

* [x] Fix
* [ ] Feature
* [ ] Documentation
* [x] Security / Upgrade

### Basic information

* [x] THIS CHANGE REQUIRES A DEPLOYMENT PACKAGE RELEASE
* [ ] THIS CHANGE REQUIRES A WIRE-DOCS RELEASE

### Testing

* [ ] I ran/applied the changes myself, in a test environment.
* [x] The CI job attached to this repo will test it for me.

Locally verified: running `pre_chart_process_0.sh` against the 5.25.0 `ingress-nginx-controller` chart vendors ingress-nginx 4.13.9; `helm template` with the prod and demo values renders `controller:v1.13.9`, `kube-webhook-certgen:v1.6.9` (tags, no digests) and `annotations-risk-level: "Critical"`; `helm lint` and `shellcheck` pass.

#### Offline Build CI (label-based)
`build-default`: builds the bundle and deploys it to Hetzner via `offline/cd.sh`. The deployment uses the prod example values, so it exercises the `server-snippet` annotation on the minio ingress of `nginx-ingress-services`.

### Tracking

* [x] I added a new entry in an appropriate subdirectory of `changelog.d`
* [x] I mentioned this PR in Jira, OR I mentioned the Jira ticket in this PR.
* [ ] I mentioned this PR in one of the issues attached to one of our repositories.

### Knowledge Transfer
~~* [ ] An Asciinema session is attached to the Jira ticket.~~

### Motivation

A customer on 5.25 reported CVEs in the bundled ingress-nginx controller image (`v1.10.6`, pinned in `values/ingress-nginx-controller`). Bumping the image tag to `v1.12.1` broke `nginx-ingress-services` with:

```
admission webhook "validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io" denied the request: annotation group ServerSnippet contains risky annotation based on ingress configuration
```

This branch provides a patched 5.25 bundle for that customer. It is not an official release.

### Objective

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ingress-nginx subchart of `ingress-nginx-controller` | 4.11.5 | 4.13.9 |
| controller image | v1.10.6 | v1.13.9 |
| kube-webhook-certgen image | v20220916-gd32f8c343 | v1.6.9 |
| `controller.config.annotations-risk-level` | unset (High since controller v1.12) | Critical |

Nothing else changes; wire-server stays on 5.25.0.

### Reason

- 4.13.x is the last ingress-nginx line that supports Kubernetes 1.29 (`kube_version: v1.29.10` in this bundle). 4.14 needs 1.30, 4.15 needs 1.31.
- The subchart is swapped in `pre_chart_process_0.sh` instead of changing wire-builds, so only this bundle is affected.
- Controller >= v1.12 lowered the default `annotations-risk-level` to `High`. `server-snippet` and `configuration-snippet` (minio, nginz and federator ingresses) are `Critical`, so the setting has to be `Critical`. It belongs to the ingress-nginx-controller release, not to `nginx-ingress-services`.
- `enableAnnotationValidations: false` (used in wireapp/wire-server#5623) is not needed: it works around kubernetes/ingress-nginx#12709 (redirect annotations), which the 5.25.0 charts don't use.
- Includes the CO-38 fixes (#946) so the Hetzner CD pipeline works again.
- Includes WPB-29054 (#943): the upstream `quay.io/minio/mc` image is no longer pullable, which breaks the bundle build. Uses the Wire mirror for the minio images and drops `fake-aws-s3` from the default build (prod uses an external minio).

### Use case

Existing installations must update their own `values/ingress-nginx-controller/values.yaml` (image tags and `annotations-risk-level: Critical`) and upgrade `ingress-nginx-controller` before `nginx-ingress-services`. Step-by-step guide: `offline/upgrades/ingress-nginx-controller-v1.13.md`.

author: projectdev-hq
body:
The 0.1.3 Release run ([run 17](https://github.com/ProjectDEV-git/Polyph/actions/runs/42640690807)) failed only on Windows. The step "Build polyph and polyph-relay" stopped with `cannot update the lock file Cargo.lock because --locked was passed`.

**Cause:** the Windows checkout has CRLF line endings, and `version.mjs` matched `Cargo.lock` entries on LF only. So `Cargo.toml` said 0.1.3 while the lock files kept 0.1.2. I reproduced this on a CRLF copy of the repo, where the lock files show `mixed ()`.

**Fix:**
- `version.mjs` reads lock files with either line ending and writes them back with the one they had.
- Each "Set the version" step in `release.yml` runs `--check` right after setting the version. A file that was left behind now fails at that step, with its name, instead of later in the build.
- New test in `scripts/release/release.test.mjs` covering both line endings; 6/6 tests pass.
- On the CRLF copy, every file now updates to 0.1.3 and keeps its CRLF line endings. `--check 0.1.2` still passes on the repo as it is.

After merging, Release will be run again with 0.1.3.

body:
## Problem

Voice input (#1228) shipped in 0.4.0-nightly.8, but on macOS every dictation shows "Microphone access is blocked" without macOS ever prompting. `tccd` logs `kTCCServiceMicrophone requires entitlement com.apple.security.device.audio-input but it is missing … Policy disallows prompt`. The spec listed the private release pipeline's handling of the entitlement as unverified.

## Approach

Root cause is outside this repo: the private signing pipeline re-signs every Mach-O with its own fixed entitlement plist, so `build.mac.entitlements` from `electrobun.config.ts` never reaches release builds (`Info.plist` still gets `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`). The fix lands in JetBrains/thinkrail-signing#20; this PR records the finding in the owning spec so the next entitlement change knows both places must move.

## Changes

- `apps/desktop/SPEC.md` § Microphone: replace the "unverified" release-pipeline note with a **Release signing** bullet — the pipeline's plist and its verification must carry `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` or TCC denies the microphone without prompting, and how to check a release (`codesign -d --entitlements -`). Linux stays unverified.

## Screenshots

Not applicable — no frontend changes.

None. Companion fix: JetBrains/thinkrail-signing#20.

author: roni-altshuler
body:
Completed-event numbering advanced only when a Grand Prix classification existed, while the full calendar retained every scheduled event. After the cancelled Australian Grand Prix, Malaysia and Qatar results were published against the preceding event's round.

This change binds ingestion to stable event identifiers and withholds the affected current-season MotoGP publication. Existing race/rider links show the exact mismatch and official references. No missing result is filled in and no saved forecast is relabeled. The raw snapshot is unchanged; hashes of all 69 quarantined public numerical artifacts retain their original commit identity.

## Scope

- [x] Several projects: MotoGP implementation; F1 inventory regression test; deterministic NASCAR test maintenance
- [x] Ecosystem hub and registry: truthful MotoGP hold status
- [x] CI / cron: validate the actual hold contract before bot commits

The ordinary shared continuity and baseline checks remain unchanged. Sparse completed IDs are explicitly held because existing numerical consumers still use count-based round bounds. A prior hold can clear only after a complete export bound to the current source snapshot, followed by successful evaluation. The completion record is not evidence of pre-race forecast publication.

The NASCAR test-only change fixes a failure reproduced on pristine main: the 2026 season is now complete, so an incomplete-season test must use explicit empty/missing-finale fixtures rather than assume the current year is incomplete. NASCAR production code and data are unchanged.

## Validation

- Full local suites on the final tree: 2,502 Python tests passed / 7 skipped; 3,175 Jest tests passed / 14 conditional skips across 200 suites.
- All 11 sites: lint, type checks, production builds with Pages prefixes, and post-build type checks. Python lint uses CI's Ruff versions; Python 3.11 and Node 20; dependencies installed from existing lockfiles.
- Registry, shared UI drift, evidence freshness, palette, circuit inventory/types and published-data validation: 78 commands passed. Published integrity reports 350 checks; MotoGP has no numerical publication and its source-bound hold is validated separately.
- Actual Chromium QA: 110 cases, widths 320/360/390/1440; 66 MotoGP HTML and 257 RSC/text files checked for numerical payload leakage; all 22 race and 33 rider deep links retained; quarantined numerical URLs return 404.
- Independent exact-diff review: no blocking findings. Final local checks and responsive QA repeated before commit and before push.

Existing conditional skips remain visible: unavailable F1 held/optional artifacts, a completed NASCAR season with no upcoming round, and numerical/evidence assertions where the hub or held MotoGP corpus has none. Healthy MotoGP numeric schema/sanity invariants still run on a verified contiguous source prefix; the actual published hold has dedicated regression coverage.

## Recovery limit

The official results API read was blocked by a proxy 403; it was not retried. Authoritative missing session inputs and supported sparse-round accounting are still required before numerical publication returns. The cancellation and event identities are supported by the preserved snapshot and official MotoGP calendar/news sources. F1 holds, other sports data, dependency locks and security settings are untouched.

body:
## Summary

Three CI/identity hardening changes:

- **Native auto-merge** — the promote job validates the manifest-only commit and calls GraphQL `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` for that exact SHA, then exits. GitHub merges once the required CodeQL checks pass, so the job token no longer lives through a 10-minute polling loop. Removes the old `merge-promotion-pr.sh` and the `checks`/`statuses` read permissions.
- **Deploy-key Argo access** — `argocd/apply.sh` now prefers a read-only SSH deploy key (`ARGO_DEPLOY_KEY_FILE`) over the runner-registration App. `debug.sh` flags unexpected runner registrations. The App now has only `Administration: write` + `Metadata: read`.
- **Init-container runner registration** — the App private key is used only by a short-lived init container that mints a one-hour registration token into an emptyDir. The runner container reads and deletes it, then starts the entrypoint with no `APP_*` credentials.

Focused map-development continuation after merged PR #756. **No real Aden DEM has been supplied or verified**, and this PR does NOT claim geographically accurate city coverage or native UE5 World Partition execution.

**Domain 1 / Importable public civilian terrain:** `src/aden-citywide-tiles.js` imports *local-only, nongeoreferenced* 512m tiles from a bounded 4MiB JSON file (max 49 tiles, 17/33/65 squared grid), requires declared provider, observed date, license and public-terrain source grade, rejects extra operational/geospatial fields, duplicate tiles, mixed adjacent resolutions and >15cm edge-height mismatch. Data is always explicitly `source-declared-unverified`; declaring a source is not proof of legal rights or actual Aden survey quality. On failure, existing registry remains intact. Imported terrain hides all 105 made-up civilian building shells to avoid misrepresentation. No server/network access and no external asset download.

**Domain 2 / Actually rendered geography:** `src/aden-map-relief.js` computes triangle-space surface normals, directional hillshade, height-based original material coloring, true interpolated 25m elevation contours, and optional oblique 2.5D relief projection at metre scale. `src/aden-city-explorer.js` and `terrain.html` show these on the real Canvas tile mesh, with keyboard H/C toggles, local import, reset to 25 fictional tiles, clear source and unresolved-tile reporting. Original 512m streaming, client 25-tile cache and LOD remain intact; BR/CH01/BR96 gameplay/physics/saves unchanged.

Regression tests assert local imported two-tile visualisation, malicious/invalid formats, source metadata, missing terrain, seam gaps, transactional reject/reset, 691 original contour line strokes on the default fixture, geometry and projection math, offline HTML dependency closure, source syntax, plus full Linux Node, actual Chromium geometry, ZIP/SHA256 and Windows WebView2-host CI.

author: maraudeurx-arch
body:
## NE PAS FUSIONNER sans revue d'Yves + GO de Popol

Règle de Popol (09/11/2026, 10 h 05) : comme Know Yourself et Clé en main, **OPC commence par un mur d'installation obligatoire**. Aucune entrée tant que l'app n'est pas installée sur l'écran d'accueil (PWA). Raison : pas encore de budget App Store / Play Store. PR **séparée** de la banque voix/image (#244).

### Comportement
- `InstallWall` enveloppe toute l'app dans `providers.tsx`. Il est rendu **par défaut**, y compris dans l'export statique. Le reste de l'app n'est **pas monté** derrière : aucun son du guide, aucun appel réseau, pas de fiche de consentement.
- Le mur se lève **seulement en mode installé** : `navigator.standalone` (iOS), `display-mode: standalone` ou `fullscreen`.
- Contenu FR/EN/ES avec sélecteur de langue :
  - titre et explication ;
  - **emplacement vidéo** (`INSTALL_WALL_VIDEO_URL`, vide pour l'instant) ;
  - guide **iPhone/iPad (Safari)** et guide **Android (Chrome)**, ordonnés selon l'appareil ;
  - avertissement pour les navigateurs intégrés (Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram…) ;
  - bouton **« Installer l'app maintenant »**, affiché seulement si le navigateur offre `beforeinstallprompt`. Il lance la vraie installation.
- **Conditions, vie privée et sécurité** restent lisibles sans installation : obligation de transparence (LPRPDE).

### E2E sans contournement en production
- `scripts/serve-e2e.mjs` (serveur e2e uniquement) injecte une émulation `navigator.standalone = true`. Toutes les specs existantes voient donc l'app « installée », sans rien changer à leur code.
- La spec `e2e/install-wall.spec.ts` pose le cookie `xsnow_e2e_install_wall=on` pour voir le vrai comportement navigateur. Aucun drapeau ni contournement n'existe dans le code de production.

### Vérifications (Node 22)
- Unitaires et fonctionnels : 482/482 (5 nouveaux : décision, mode installé, pages légales, détection iPhone/Android/in-app, guides dans les 3 langues).
- Build statique OK.
- e2e `install-wall` : **4/4**.
- Suite complète : 73 réussis, 3 ignorés. **6 échecs, tous dans les specs d'arbitrage.** Ce sont les mêmes 6 échecs préexistants sur `main`, aucune régression.

### Points d'attention
- Une fois fusionné, **toute personne doit installer OPC**, y compris les testeurs du Jumeau sur `/jumeau-banque` (#244) et les arbitres.
- iOS : Safari seulement (Chrome iOS : « Ajouter à l'écran d'accueil » dans les versions récentes).
- La vidéo d'installation reste à produire.

## Regression test
`tools/live-check/a11y.test.mjs` runs `browser.mjs`'s own `checkPage` axe pass (the same tags and serious/critical filter as the cold pass) on `connectors.html` and `ops.html`. The pages are served from `ui/` against a stub API that draws every state: online and offline nodes; pending, ignored and connected devices; a factory-login flag; OK and failing connectors; ok, quiet, degraded, down and off cards; alerts; process errors; and the no-data-yet CTA. It runs as operator (light, light with no data, dark) and as admin (light). Against origin/main's `ui/` all four cases fail with exactly the reported rules; on this branch they pass.

The test needs `npm ci` (playwright-core and axe-core; no browser download) and Chrome. Locally it skips without them. CI's live-check step now runs `npm ci` and sets `LIVE_CHECK_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1`, so a missing browser fails instead of skipping.

- `node --test` in tools/live-check: 51 passed.
- `pytest -m "not integration"`: 1883 passed, 30 skipped.

In dark mode only, the admin `Delete` button (`button.danger`) is `--color-critical` (#f56565) on Chrome's native dark button face (#6b6b6b), 1.75:1. This was already the case before this PR, and the cold pass doesn't see it (it runs as operator in light mode). author: middt
body:
## Summary
- **Same-key `updateData` takeover ran the chain N times.** When several `updateData` requests found an instance parked in Busy (an interaction wait with no live owner), every one of them took the parked pipeline over: the automatic chain ran again per request — duplicate parent notifications and finalize calls, and a late copy wrote a stale `Status=B` over the settled state. The handoff now claims the continuation first with one set-based UPDATE on a new nullable column `Instances.ContinuationClaimedAt` (`Status='B' AND CurrentState=@state AND` no claim younger than 60 s). The winner runs the chain and clears the claim; a loser drops its continuation and logs `10182`.
- **Less work per request on the hot paths** (behaviour-preserving; each change pinned against the old code):
  - Representation ETag: one pass over pooled UTF-8 instead of string → hand-written parser → string (~95% less allocation). Also fixes two parser bugs: the character after `\\` / `\"` / `\/` was swallowed, and a top-level array never parsed.
  - `JsonData.NormalizeJson`: one writer pass instead of re-serializing every subtree; output byte-identical (it feeds the persisted `DataHash`).
  - Tasks: local invokers get the typed binding (no JSON round trip); no journal serialization without a persistence strategy (`history: none`); boundary chain, post-commit binding and script cache key memoized; hot-path logs moved to `WorkflowLogs`.
  - Reads: read-only instance load 3 → 2 queries; state-function cache miss 6+R → 4+R; caller-scope hash once per request; no DI scope per extension reference.
  - Role grants: dynamic-grant context built once per evaluator instead of copying all instance data per transition; subflow override map read once.
- **Hosts name their Postgres connections** (`Application Name` from `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` / `DAPR_APP_ID` / host name, only when missing). Nothing else in the connection string changes; pool sizing stays with PgBouncer.
- `run-docker.sh restart` keeps the database an earlier `up --db` chose.

## vNext scope
- **Transition pipeline / locking (behaviour change):** `TransitionPipeline.RunChainAsync` parked-Busy handoff — claim before `TakeOverAsync`, release in a `finally`. A reserve from Active is unchanged. The claim does not stamp `ModifiedAt` (bookkeeping only).
- **Data model:** migration `20261109120000_AddInstanceContinuationClaim` adds one nullable `timestamptz` column (shadow property).
- **State function / reads, task engine, authorization:** performance only — same bodies, ETags (except bodies with the escapes above), authorization decisions, persisted hashes, downstream HTTP requests and log scope keys.
- **Hosts:** startup normalisation of `ConnectionStrings:Default` / `ConnectionStrings:Domains:*` (application name only).

author: leciric
body:
## What changed
In the native app, Ctrl+T (and every other way of opening a session) now ends with the new session selected **and the cursor in its message box**, and a refresh of the session list can no longer undo that.

- **Focus:** opening a session recreates the chat, and in the same moments `session_shown` can open it a second time. The focus was requested on a chat that was then dropped, or before its box was drawn, so the cursor landed nowhere. `ChatView` now focuses when its box is drawn, and `AppView.focus_lead` carries the request to the chat that stays.
- **Race:** a list read that began before the create returned without the new session and replaced the list, so the old session came back. List reads now carry an epoch (`Epochs`), bumped when a session is added; a read from an older epoch is dropped. The read that follows the add supplies the list.
- **Fake daemon:** it now serves `POST /v1/projects/{p}/sessions` and keeps those sessions; `FAKE_SESSION_DELAY_MS` slows the create so a refresh can land during it.

Rejected: merging a stale list with local additions. It needs rules for deletes and renames; dropping the stale read is simpler, and the add already triggers a fresh one.

## How I checked
- Built the app (debug assertions off, because a GPUI `hover style already set` assertion fires on the unmodified build) and ran it against the fake daemon with lavapipe. Before: Ctrl+T adds and selects "Session 2", but typing does nothing. After: the typed "x" shows in the composer.
- `cargo test -p agentbox-native` (98 pass, including two new `epoch_tests`), `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt`.
- I did not reproduce the stale-refresh race end to end: the fake daemon only has the delay hook, and only the epoch logic is unit-tested. Not tried on a real daemon, Mac or Windows.

Before (Ctrl+T, then typing "x"):

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/880a4999-9545-4ecc-97d7-85dea6812828)

After:

Recordings are in Media: `ctrl-t-new-session-before` and `ctrl-t-new-session-after`.

author: jcschaff
body:
Replaces the per-site webapp images (`vcell-webapp-prod`, `-dev`, `-stage`) with one `vcell-webapp` image.

## Why there were three
The builds differed in two compiled-in values, both equal to the site's origin on every deployment: the Auth0 `audience` (also used as the OpenAPI `basePath`) and the interceptor's `allowedList` origin. In May 2024 the app fetched a runtime `baseuri_config.json` in an `APP_INITIALIZER`, but that runs after the static `AuthModule.forRoot({...})` literal is evaluated, so the Auth0 values could not use it; 694aa15335 ("hard-code apiurl … to make auth work") split the image per site. The fetch was removed in 9103f33770 (April 2025) but the split stayed.

## The change
- `src/app/site-origin.ts`: `environment.siteOrigin ?? window.location.origin`, read **synchronously at module load** — the same way `redirect_uri: window.location.origin` already sat in that `forRoot` literal and worked. Used for the audience, `${origin}/api/*`, and the API base path.
- `environment.prod.ts` has no override; `environment.ts` (`ng serve`) uses stage, `environment.ide.ts` minikube island. The old `ng serve` default mixed a prod audience with a stage allowedList; it is now stage for both.
- Removed: dev/stage/island/remote environment files, their Angular configurations and `build_*` scripts, and the dead `BaseuriConfigService` from the 2024 attempt.
- CI-full builds one `webapp` matrix entry and pushes `vcell-webapp`; `docker/build/build.sh` likewise.

## Rollout
Needs vcell-fluxcd's deploy workflow to use `vcell-webapp:<tag>` — companion PR, which falls back to the per-site name for older releases, so the two can merge in either order. One assumption: each site's Auth0 API identifier equals its origin, as today's baked-in values already do for prod, dev and stage.

## Checked
- `ng build -c configuration_prod` succeeds (only pre-existing warnings). The bundle contains no site hostname except the generated OpenAPI services' fallback `basePath`, which the injected `ApiConfiguration` overrides, as on master.
- The built bundle, served locally and loaded in headless Chrome, bootstraps and renders the nav bar with no console errors, and no longer requests `assets/config/baseuri_config.json`.
- Not checked: a real login round-trip on a deployed site. The first dev deploy of a release with this change is the place to try one.

author: jitsusama
body:
### 💡 TL;DR

The jobs door now holds every heavy Nix start, builds and offloaded runs included, and lets each in only while memory stays available, keeping more through a call. Thirteen starts at once leave a foreground program waking on time.

### 🧩 Problem

When a switch's hold ended, about thirteen agent sessions started their builds within a minute. The door in the jobs slice held only evaluations, and let them in 30 s apart once 16 GiB was free, so builds all came in together. The jobs slice went from 4 to 11 GB of swap in four minutes, the desktop took 785 ms to answer, and a call's microphone went unread for 59 s. The door's sizes were also fixed in GiB, which would hold everything forever on a smaller machine.

### 🔧 Solution

The door now holds every heavy Nix start: evaluations, builds, nix-store realisations and nix-offload there runs. It lets the oldest held one in only while a quarter of memory would stay available once it grows by a sixteenth. Starts let in during the last two minutes count as still growing, so a burst comes in as many as there is room for rather than all at once. A process in a scope already let in is never held, so a run is not frozen midway.

While a call is on, heard through pw-dump as a program recording a microphone, the door keeps three eighths of memory and lets nothing held in. Once no call is on, a start that waited 30 minutes comes in, one per 30 s.

Shares of total memory replace the fixed sizes, which on 64 GiB give the same 16, 24 and 4 GiB. jobs-sorter takes a new `--calls` flag naming pw-dump.

For Joel: nothing to try; a burst of agents' builds no longer stalls a call or the desktop.

### 🔬 Validation

- jobs-sorter's suite, 68 tests in the door, including thirteen_starts_at_once_come_in_only_as_many_as_there_is_room_for; strict clippy clean.
- run-subtests --there vm-apps-come-first heavy starts at once: 5 passed, 15 deselected, at 76839bceb. Its new case starts 13 memory-growing builds at once and holds a foreground program's lateness under 100 ms.
- nix-offload there --changed at 76839bceb: every changed check built but every-script-meets-shellcheck-at-its-strictest, which fails on main the same way over tests/pi-rings-low-and-says-it.sh.
- merge-net needs: no VM test before merging.

Ted narrowed #724 to the wait age only. This pull request adds no daytime drain and no dispatch hold. The nightly deploy from #727 still lands a pending commit.

- `auto-deploy.json` gains `waiting_since`. The first `WAITING` of a wait sets it to that event's `at`.
- Every `WAITING` detail and log line starts with `waiting <H>h<MM>m; `. Hours are not capped. A repeated `WAITING` on the same commit still writes no event, but the state's `detail` and the log line carry the live age.
- `DEPLOYED`, `FAILED` with a commit, and `BLOCKED` with a run-gating line clear `waiting_since`. Every other outcome keeps it, because it pauses the wait and does not end it. Tests cover a failed read and an operator pause. A person-set `kanban.dispatch_profiles` and the gateway lock keep it by the same rule in `record`; no test exercises those two.
- `auto-deploy --status` adds `waiting_seconds`. It is an integer during a wait and `null` otherwise.
- An unreadable `waiting_since` fails the run with `DeployError`. The run first releases anything a crashed run left held, then checks the value before it holds, installs, or records anything. So the value is never reset, on an empty board or a busy one. `--status` fails the same way and names the bad value.
- The **Auto deploy** section of `skills/setup-factory/SKILL.md` names the field and its clear rule. The two `auto-deploy` rows of `docs/rules.md` also name the new tests as enforcers.

## Proof

This probe runs the real `record` with a `waiting_since` seeded 9 h 12 min earlier. It records two `WAITING` results on one commit, then `DEPLOYED`, and reads each state through `auto-deploy --status`:

```text
auto-deploy: WAITING abc1234def: waiting 9h12m; 2 card(s) running; deploying at the next break: t_1 (PAT-1); t_2 (PAT-2)
auto-deploy: WAITING abc1234def again: waiting 9h12m; 1 card(s) running; deploying at the next break: t_1 (PAT-1)
--status: {
  "outcome": "WAITING",
  "detail": "waiting 9h12m; 1 card(s) running; deploying at the next break: t_1 (PAT-1)",
  "waiting_since": "2026-11-09T08:22:32+00:00",
  "waiting_seconds": 33150
}
events: 1 waiting 9h12m; 2 card(s) running; deploying at the next break: t_1 (PAT-1); t_2 (PAT-2)
auto-deploy: DEPLOYED abc1234def
after DEPLOYED: {"outcome": "DEPLOYED", "waiting_since": null, "waiting_seconds": null}
```

The probe above seeds the state file and drives `record` directly, so it is a sketch and not part of the branch. The tests below are the rerunnable proof. Run `python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_auto_deploy` in `skills/setup-factory`. It ran 82 tests and passed: the 69 tests on `main` and 13 new ones. Each new test runs `auto-deploy` as a subprocess against a fake Hermes and checks `auto-deploy.json` or `--status`:

```text

test_a_failure_with_the_commit_ends_the_wait ... ok
test_a_new_commit_waiting_reports_the_age_and_keeps_the_start ... ok
test_a_read_failure_inside_a_wait_does_not_restart_it ... ok

test_a_run_gating_block_ends_the_wait ... ok
```

author: pdcarlson
body:
## Summary

Paul, 2026-11-09: issues only got worked when someone named one. On 2026-11-09, 969 issues were open, 188 of them in `triage` (106 for more than a week). In the 7 days before, 313 were opened and 116 closed. This PR makes two changes:

1. **Your own ask skips triage.**
   - What Paul asks for in his chat goes straight to the Backlog with its priority.
   - So does Shawn's or Winston's ask, when it's ready to build and needs no decision only Paul can make.
   - The `Asked by:` line records whose decision it was. `[human]` items still hold in triage.
2. **A daily pull.** A scheduled task, **Frapp Daily Pull** (14:13 ET), runs `/next` on the top viable P1 or P2 Backlog issue. It opens one PR, never turns on auto-merge, makes no migration, CI or dependency change, and ends once the PR is green.

## Changes

- `AGENTS.md` § Work tracking: the exception and its conditions, stated in one place.
- `.claude/skills/file-follow-up/SKILL.md`, `docs/ci-cd/github-pm.md`: these link to that rule. Their labels, lifecycle, "born with triage" and ownership-boundary lines now allow the skip.
- `docs/ci-cd/routines.md`: the Daily Pull is recorded beside the 2026-09-05 note that turned off the hourly `/next` routine. The note gives its limits, and says it isn't covered by the routines' boundary or the heartbeat.

## Flagged for review

- **The fresh-session mode is unproven.** `routines.md` § Settings records that a fresh-session task failed on 2026-11-08: it got no repository and no connectors. The Daily Pull's prompt attaches the repository itself (`add_repo`), and stops in one line if the GitHub MCP is missing. Its first run, today at 14:13 ET, settles it. If it fails, bind it to a session made for it.
- **Auto-merge merges without Paul.** Branch protection requires no review (`required_pull_request_reviews: null`), so any session that turns auto-merge on merges its own PR once CI is green. The Daily Pull is told never to do that. Whether to require Paul's review in branch protection is his call.

## Docs / Spec impact

- **Docs impact:** Updated (the files above).
- **Spec impact:** None.

## Test plan

- [x] `/diff-review`:
  - Full round with two finders. To save usage I skipped the acceptance-and-tests finder; this is a docs-only change and no script test reads these lines.
  - The round found 8 issues, all fixed in the second commit:
    - restated copies of the rule that dropped its conditions;
    - lifecycle and "born with triage" lines that still contradicted it;
    - `[human]` holds;
    - the ownership boundary;
    - the Daily Pull's missing limits, and its fresh-session risk;
    - a missing blank line.
  - I checked these by reading the files, without verifier agents.
  - The inline round on the fix found nothing new.

## Release label

- [x] `release:patch`

Debt spotted: the auto-merge-without-review gap above (a branch-protection decision for Paul, not filed).

author: montyxace-sys
body:
## Qué arregla

Los ajustes de Misearch **no se guardaban**: al cerrar y volver a abrir, el buscador, el zoom y los interruptores de privacidad volvían a los valores por defecto.

## Causa

`MainWindow` se quedaba con una copia de `AppSettings`:

```csharp
private readonly SettingsStore _settingsStore = new();
private AppSettings _settings = new();
...
_settings = _settingsStore.Load();   // copia nueva, el store conserva la suya
```

La UI modificaba `_settings`, pero `SettingsStore.Save()` serializaba su propia instancia (`Settings`), que nunca cambiaba. El archivo `settings.json` se reescribía siempre con los valores iniciales.

## Arreglo

- `MainWindow` entrega su instancia al store tras cargarla: `_settingsStore.Settings = _settings`. `Save()` escribe ahora exactamente lo que la UI modificó.
- `SettingsStore` acepta una ruta inyectable (`SettingsStore(Func<string> pathProvider)`) para poder probarlo sin tocar `%AppData%`.

### Otros arreglos de la misma pasada

| Archivo | Problema | Arreglo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Core/Models/AppPaths.cs` | `EnsureDirectories()` no creaba `CoreDir`; escribir `version.txt` tras extraer Mihomo podía fallar con `DirectoryNotFoundException` | Se crea `CoreDir` |
| `Core/Vpn/WarpService.cs` | `json[..Math.Min(json.Length, 180)]` con cuerpo vacío lanzaba `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`; `client_id` se buscaba bajo `config` cuando WARP lo envía en la raíz | Truncado seguro y lectura de `client_id` en raíz y `config` |
| `Core/Services/SearchRouter.cs` | Un término sin espacios que no es un host (`c#`, `.net`, `v1.2`) se convertía en una URL rota (`https://c#`) | Se valida la forma del host; si no lo parece, va al buscador |
| `Core/Services/HistoryStore.cs` | Un fallo al escribir historial o marcadores podía tumbar la UI desde un `async void` | La escritura se ignora de forma controlada; las listas en memoria mandan |

## Pruebas

Nuevo proyecto `tests/Misearch.CoreTests` (xUnit), añadido a `Misearch.slnx`:

```
dotnet test tests/Misearch.CoreTests/Misearch.CoreTests.csproj
Correctas! - Con error: 0, Superado: 53, Omitido: 0, Total: 53
```

Cubre ajustes persistentes (incluida la regresión de este bug), enrutado del buscador, listas de bloqueo, perfiles WireGuard, configuración de Mihomo/WARP y la lectura de `client_id`.

`dotnet build Misearch.slnx`: 0 errores, 0 avisos.

## Notas

- No cambia comportamiento visible salvo que los ajustes ahora sí se conservan y que términos como `c#` buscan en vez de fallar.
- Sin cambios en el flujo de release ni en el instalador.

Clean up stale and partial downloads. - Stop with a clear error on exhaustion; explicitly stop PowerVS on download or rendering failure. - Preserve fcct v0.7.0 and existing architecture selection. ### Observed failure An [Azure upgrade run](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results-public/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-ci-5.1-upgrade-from-stable-5.0-e2e-azure-ovn-upgrade/2119665672043630592) failed in `ipi-install-install-stableinitial`. 504 Gateway Time-out

' ``` ## Validation - 37 passing focused regression cases across the 4.12 and 5.0 installer images and the 4.22 upi-installer image. Scenarios include success, 504 recovery, permanent HTTP errors, partial transfers, empty bodies, stale files, timeout recovery, architecture selection and rendering. - Eight baseline runs reproduce the original defect, for 45 expected outcomes in total. The throwaway regression harness is not included in this PR. - Applicable local presubmit-equivalent checks passed, including step-registry shell and metadata validation, configuration validation and repository policy checks. - Full diff reviewed; working tree clean. body:
This PR connects multigraph vertex covers and unit-capacity matching optima to Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsVertexCover` and `SimpleGraph.vertexCoverNum`. Prove the exact effect of simplification on covers, including the extra condition at loop vertices, and give both preimage and image correspondences for `Graph.ofSimpleGraph`. Use the bridge to prove that every unit-capacity matching in a loopless multigraph has size at most its simplification's vertex cover number, and that a bipartition supplies an attaining matching.

Advance [GraphConnectivityAndFlows/README.md, Milestone 6, Target 6.7, “Multiset capacitated Kőnig's theorem”](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/GraphConnectivityAndFlows/README.md#67-multiset-capacitated-kőnigs-theorem), specifically the requirement to transport the unit-capacity result to `SimpleGraph.IsVertexCover` and the extremality interfaces. This is the next independent step because the capacitated Kőnig theorem is on main and the matching-side transport is already in flight in #34514, while no open PR supplies the cover-side bridge or the numerical cover optimum. The matching and cover comparison together serve the simple-graph Kőnig interface. After this PR, Target 6.7 still needs matching-side extremality transport and the explicit bipartite-network flow/cut correspondences; this PR carries no content from any unmerged PR.

Add `Graph/VertexCover/SimpleGraph.lean` (92 lines, five theorems) and `Graph/Matching/VertexCover.lean` (63 lines, two theorems). The structural comparisons assume no finiteness. Weak duality assumes only finitely many actual edges, with no finite-vertex or ambient finiteness assumption. Attainment uses the existing finite bipartition interface, including empty graphs, isolated vertices, and parallel edges.

Follow the required topic-directory layout by moving the existing module unchanged and updating its sole in-repository import:

| Old module | New module |

| `TauCeti.Combinatorics.Graph.VertexCover` | `TauCeti.Combinatorics.Graph.VertexCover.Basic` |

Read the shared protocol and all ten rubrics: scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation, and proof-quality. Self-review confirmed the loop condition is necessary, removed the finite-vertex assumption from weak duality, retained both directions of the characteristic transport API, and found no existing replacements after renewed searches in pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti. author: 0xnullifier
body:
## Rule

In the mobile dApp browser, only the main frame of the dApp page can speak to the wallet bridge. Every bridge message carries the origin of the frame that sent it, and the wallet compares it with the session origin before any parsing.

## Changes

**iOS** (`packages/dapp-browser/ios/.../WKWebViewController.swift`)
- The `messageHandler` branch returns unless `message.frameInfo.isMainFrame`, the same guard the Bread handlers already use.
- Each forwarded message carries `frameOrigin` (formatted as `location.origin`: default and zero ports dropped, IPv6 hosts bracketed, non-http(s) or hostless origins as `"null"`) and `mainFrame: true`.

**Android** (`packages/dapp-browser/android/.../WebViewDialog.java`)
- When `WEB_MESSAGE_LISTENER` is supported, the bridge is a `WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener` that drops non-main-frame and non-string messages and forwards the WebView's `sourceOrigin` as `frameOrigin` with `mainFrame: true`. The listener's allowed-origin list is `"*"` on purpose: the rule applies only to documents loaded after the call and a session can navigate across origins, so the origin check is done in the wallet against the live session origin. `AndroidInterface` stays only for `mobileApp.close` and forwards nothing while the listener is installed.
- WebViews without the feature keep the JavaScript interface; the injected script sends an envelope with `window.location.origin` and `window === window.top`, which native validates for shape (`fallbackBridgeMessage`).
- `androidx.webkit` was already a dependency; no ProGuard rule is needed.

**Wallet** (`src/app/providers/DappBrowserProvider.tsx`)
- Before parsing, a `messageFromWebview` event is dropped unless `mainFrame === true` and `frameOrigin === state.origin`; logged at debug level only. The event type in `packages/dapp-browser/dist/esm/definitions.d.ts` gained the two optional fields.

## Verification

- Jest: both `DappBrowserProvider` suites pass (193 tests) on a fresh `yarn install`; `tsc` and eslint clean.
- Swift: `swiftc -parse` and a full `-typecheck` of the plugin's sources against the iPhone simulator SDK pass.
- Android: `:miden-dapp-browser:compileDebugJavaWithJavac` compiles; `WebViewDialogBridgeMessageTest` (new, 6 cases), `BridgeLogPrivacyTest`, `BreadAuthControllerTest`, `BreadPresentationControllerTest` and `WebViewDialogSnapshotTest` pass.
- iOS simulator (iOS 26.2, E2E harness): a page on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` connected through the bridge; the forwarded `frameOrigin` and the provider's `state.origin` were both `http://127.0.0.1:58753`, equal to the page's `location.origin`, and the connect prompt appeared. Two injected iframes calling the handler directly, one same-origin and one cross-origin, were dropped natively and never reached the provider.
- Not exercised live: a default-port https page, an IPv6 host, and Android on a device or emulator.
- `scripts/check-changelog.sh` passes.

author: qixing-jk
body:
## Summary

Fix history hints that fail to open inside the webpage API testing panel's ShadowRoot, and move type checking off the JavaScript heap limit that failed CI on multiple PRs.

```diff
- document selector -> unresolved ShadowRoot anchor
+ element reference -> positioned hint inside the styled UI scope
- JavaScript-only type check -> heap exhaustion
+ native TS 7 check + supported TS 6 compiler API for tools
```

Keep tooltip anchors stationary during hover/focus, let an expanded combobox handle Escape first, and preserve click/touch, nested focus, accessible descriptions and modal dismissal. Remove the obsolete tooltip dependency and guard namespace, wildcard and dynamic imports that bypass the shared Tooltip.

Use TypeScript 7.0.2 with one checker and the [official TS 6 compatibility setup](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/#running-side-by-side-with-typescript-60). Preserve all project roots, strict options, incremental checks and automatic ambient-type discovery. Upgrade i18next within 25.x and react-i18next within 16.x for TS 6 support. Upgrade ESLint to 10.14.0 and its compatible plugins, migrate the new recommended rules, and remove the unused semantic parser project. Narrow exceptions retain existing credential-redaction and aggregate-error contracts.

Keep language changes from resetting account drafts or reloading announcements with the upgraded i18n runtime. Feedback still retranslates immediately, and later asynchronous operations use the current language. Use a dedicated fixture model for the no-metadata browser scenario so external model-catalog updates cannot change its assumptions. The shared AIMLAPI authentication runner accepts the current signed-out login redirect while checking its origin and return destination, with an isolated client-navigation fixture that keeps both pages under Playwright routing.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a restored webpage history badge has an accessible description but no visible hint. In native UI, opening a hint can move its button between pointerdown and mouseup, breaking reset, model-group and download actions.
  **After:** shadow-root history, mouse/touch/focus interactions, popup Escape priority and stationary reset-button geometry pass their regression checks.
- **Before:** the [quality job](https://github.com/qixing-jk/all-api-hub/actions/runs/42666481293/job/129331378132) aborts at the default JavaScript heap limit.
  **After:** complete cold checks pass with the native compiler. The final TS 6 and TS 7 configurations resolve the same 5,497 project root files.

Same-tree cold checks on Windows with Node 24.14.1:

| Compiler | Wall time | Peak process working set |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| JavaScript TS 6.0.3 | 56.00 s | 4,751.6 MiB |
| Native TS 7.0.2, one checker | 14.11 s | 3,866.6 MiB |

The JavaScript benchmark uses a diagnostic-only 6 GiB heap limit to finish. The production compile command uses the native compiler without a Node heap override.

Validation includes 855 affected tests, 239 wrapper tests and 149 i18n tests; full lint and type checking; Firefox production and Chrome test builds; representative webpage history, font reset at 390/320 px, theme appearance and permission-warning E2E. The original model-group, download, options-layout and DNR recovery failures also passed focused browser reruns.

The upgrade CI's type-check/lint quality job passed. Follow-up validation covers 545 account-workspace, model-data and announcement tests, the complete webpage needle/history workflow, and 67 automatic-sync tests. The added WebDAV regression verifies that a connection failure preserves its cause and stops before remote reads or local/remote writes; transaction line coverage is 100%. All 12 AIMLAPI browser scenarios also pass, including redirect isolation, save/reopen, credential replacement, revoked/denied keys and automatic onboarding.

### Webpage history hint

The same restored history badge is hovered in both views. Chrome, light theme, deterministic local API fixture; cropped from matching 1280×720 captures.

![Before and after: webpage history hint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73d7b307-1dab-4893-bb0f-b7f9b31afe60)

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way; no storage migration or new extension permissions.

**Blast Radius:** Shared. Tooltip behavior affects webpage overlays, extension pages and dialogs; compiler, lint and compatible i18n upgrades affect development checks and the shared translation runtime.

## Related Issues

Follow-up to #1845, which documents the webpage history hint limitation.
