body:
## Why

On 2026-11-09 the drafter wrote holding replies on Zoho #9921, #9922, #9923 and #9924 ("We're checking the records ... and will follow up") after live lesson L112 said never to. Sam's rule (2026-11-06): no holding replies, email only with a real answer.

Root cause: the `no_needless_holding` guard was skipped whenever triage passed the drafter notes. `DATA_CHECK_NOTES` (records decide the answer) and `HOLDING_NOTES` (needs_human) asked for exactly that reply, and since #61 every deep-pass-corrected card carries notes too. Three of the four Nov 9 drafts came from `DATA_CHECK_NOTES`.

## What changes

- **Guard** (`vomeos/guards/holding.py`): no brief turns it off. It now also catches French forms ("Notre équipe va examiner cela et reviendra vers vous") and "our team will review ... and follow up", reads "Apologies" and "we're sorry" as courtesy, and lets a conditional "we'll follow up if we need anything" through.
- **Draft time** (`shadow_triage.py`): `draft_reply` leaves a draft that only holds empty (`draft_status` `none`) with `draft_why` (shown as `draft_held_because`) naming what would settle it: the data check, the fix going live, or Sam's decision. A ticket whose data check is `required` gets no draft and no model call until the records are in (`DATA_CHECK_NOTES` is gone). The needs_human notes now ask for what the card settles, never a holding line. The draft decision moved into `draft_for` so it can be tested.
- **Send time** (`sprint_thread.holding_refusal`): the agent's holding draft is refused by `send N`, `send_replies` and `send_ticket_reply` with empty `text`, which catches drafts already in the store. Sam's own words (an `edit N:`, or `send_ticket_reply` with `text`) still go.
- The sprint card and the batch detail show the withheld reason.

A reply that answers and also promises a follow-up passes ("the fix is in the next app update, and we'll let you know as soon as it's in the stores").

## Tests

`test_no_holding_drafts.py` uses the real drafts from the sprint store: #9921, #9922, #9923, #9924 plus French #9892, #9909 and #9886, #9846 are blocked. Real answers with a follow-up pass: #9508, #9800, #6304 (sent), #9919 (drafted), and the conditional #9539 ack. Existing fixtures that used a holding draft as a sendable draft now use an answer.

Full suite, same environment for both (no parent `.env`):
- main `a5a6142`: 6 failed, 3488 passed, 69 skipped
- this branch: 6 failed, 3516 passed, 69 skipped (the same 6: the `test_repository_passes_the_gate` 638-word charter, 1 video_studio_jobs, 4 weekly_engineering_report)

## For Sam to decide

- needs_human cards no longer get a holding reply to send while you decide (G54 / #9501). They get an answer draft when the card settles something, or no draft with the reason.
- Agent-fix tickets get no "we're on it" acknowledgment unless it says something real. The client hears when the release watcher proves the fix live.
- A `redraft N: <notes>` that still produces only a holding line comes back empty. Your own `edit N:` always sends.

author: mfreeman451
body:
## Intent

Fix a chart regression from #6407 that broke every Argo CD upgrade of ServiceRadar. Argo CD renders the chart with helm template, where .Release.IsUpgrade is always false, so the serviceradar-core-migrations Job is applied as a regular (non-hook) resource on every Argo sync. On the second sync Argo patches the existing completed Job with the new image, Kubernetes rejects it (Job spec.template is immutable), the sync fails after 5 retries, migrations never run, and core/web-ng new pods block in wait-migrations ('Schema is behind') until the rollout deadline. Observed live on demo rolling to test-45 (sha-916ccd9908): I unblocked demo by deleting the stale Job with the user's approval and a no-prune recovery sync. The fix: annotate the Job with argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Force=true,Replace=true so Argo deletes and recreates it each sync, rerunning migrations like Helm's pre-upgrade hook. Deliberate decisions: (1) do NOT reintroduce an Argo Sync hook with sync-wave -1 — #6407's review correctly found that a wave -1 hook deadlocks a fresh Argo sync because the CNPG Cluster (wave 0) is never created; the Job must stay a non-hook resource in the Cluster's wave, waiting in its wait-for-cnpg init container. (2) The annotation is unconditional; Helm ignores argocd annotations, so helm install (non-hook Job) and helm upgrade (pre-upgrade hook) behavior from #6407 is unchanged. (3) Migrations rerunning on every Argo sync is intended: they are idempotent and lock-protected, matching Helm's per-upgrade hook. The regression test is the existing helm-unittest suite core_migrations_hook_test.yaml asserting the rendered annotation (Argo consumes it); it fails on the old template and passes now. Full chart suite (468 tests) and scripts/check-tenant-chart-hook-order.sh pass. Live proof that Argo recreates the Job without manual intervention comes from the next demo pin, since it needs an image change. No Helm-only knobs, no suppressions.

## What Changed

- Added the `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Force=true,Replace=true` annotation to the `serviceradar-core-migrations` Job in `helm/serviceradar/templates/core-migrations-job.yaml`. Argo CD renders the chart with `helm template`, so it applies the Job as a regular resource on every sync. Until now it patched the completed Job's immutable pod template with the new image, Kubernetes rejected the patch, and the sync failed. With this annotation Argo deletes and recreates the Job instead, so migrations rerun on each sync.
- The annotation is unconditional, and the Job is still not an Argo sync hook. It stays in the CNPG Cluster's sync wave, so a fresh Argo sync still creates the Cluster it waits for. Helm ignores `argocd.*` annotations, so `helm install` (a regular Job) and `helm upgrade` (a `pre-upgrade` hook) work as before.
- Added an assertion to `helm/serviceradar/tests/core_migrations_hook_test.yaml` that checks the rendered Job carries this annotation.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The Job annotation is the documented Argo CD Force=true,Replace=true delete-and-recreate option, it is unconditional, and the manifest stays a non-hook resource in the CNPG wave.

## Testing

The baseline `test -f .bazelrc.remote` passed. I rendered the chart with real helm for both the Argo (`helm template`) and the Helm-upgrade branches. I then drove the regression against a throwaway Kubernetes 1.31 API server: re-applying the completed migrations Job with a new image failed with "spec.template ... field is immutable". `replace --force`, which is what Argo's Force=true,Replace=true does, deleted the Job and recreated it with the new image and a new UID. The helm-unittest regression test fails on the old template and passes on the new one; it is a chart test, not a live run, so that scenario is recorded as untested. The hook-order script passes, and the Job is still a non-hook resource in wave 0 alongside the CNPG Cluster. A full Argo CD controller sync was not run, because Docker is not running and there is no disposable cluster with Argo CD; as the intent says, the next demo pin is the end-to-end proof. There is no UI surface, so no screenshots.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Argo-style render (helm template, IsUpgrade=false) emits the Job with argocd sync-options Force=true,Replace=true | ✅ pass | live | argo-render.yaml: annotations {argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Force=true,Replace=true} |
| Second sync with a new image: plain apply of the completed Job is rejected by Kubernetes (reproduces the regression) | ✅ pass | live | apiserver-job-replace-transcript.txt: 'The Job "serviceradar-core-migrations" is invalid: spec.template ... field is immutable', exit=1 |
| Second sync with Force+Replace semantics: Job is deleted and recreated with the new image, no manual intervention | ✅ pass | live | apiserver-job-replace-transcript.txt: 'deleted' / 'replaced', exit=0; UID f3601384... -> 8a745b74..., image sha-bbbb222, annotation preserved |
| Guard: Job is not reintroduced as an Argo Sync hook / wave -1; it shares wave 0 with the CNPG Cluster | ✅ pass | live | argo-wave-check.txt: Job and Cluster both wave 0, hook None |
| Helm upgrade path unchanged: Job is still a pre-upgrade hook with the same weight and delete policy | ✅ pass | live | upgrade-render.yaml: helm.sh/hook pre-upgrade, weight -1, before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded |
| Regression test fails on the old template and passes on the new one | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload established this only via helm-unittest, which is a chart unit test rather than a live run against the product, so it did not establish a live result. |
| A real Argo CD application-controller sync recreates the Job across two image pins | ⏸️ untested | no | This needs a cluster with Argo CD running. author: kvnloo
body:
## Problem (upstream link)

[newton-physics/newton#3700](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/issues/3700): a valid MJCF floating base expressed as three XYZ slide joints followed by a ball joint either raises a JOINT_DOF custom-attribute index error or silently loses its translational DOFs. The upstream reporter, eric-heiden, also identified an [external implementation branch](https://github.com/eric-heiden/newton/tree/eric/manosim-mjcf); credit for the original report and investigation belongs to that author. No upstream PR for this issue was found in the open PR scan.

## Root cause (file:line at the SHA)

Base: `122224179e6c112a0f1687ceb97b39a0dd97b432`.

- [`newton/_src/utils/import_mjcf.py:2631-2666`](https://github.com/kvnloo/newton/blob/122224179e6c112a0f1687ceb97b39a0dd97b432/newton/_src/utils/import_mjcf.py#L2631-L2666): encountering a ball joint assigns `JointType.BALL` and breaks, dropping the three previously parsed slide axes while retaining six DOF custom-attribute entries.
- [`newton/_src/utils/import_mjcf.py:2880-2970`](https://github.com/kvnloo/newton/blob/122224179e6c112a0f1687ceb97b39a0dd97b432/newton/_src/utils/import_mjcf.py#L2880-L2970): the native BALL path allocates only three DOFs; the separate FREE path uses default axes instead of source-authored slide/ball coefficients.

## Change

- Accept the canonical, MuJoCo-supported `slide(X) → slide(Y) → slide(Z) → ball` combination as one FREE joint, preserving the three linear and three angular DOF configurations, source-joint name mapping, and initial body pose.
- Reject unsupported combinations involving a ball joint with a specific `ValueError` instead of silently discarding joints or failing on an incidental DOF index.
- Extend existing MJCF `unittest` coverage and add an issue-linked Towncrier fragment. No new dependencies.

## Tests

**Unrun** — no test execution, workflow dispatch, or CI result claimed:

```text
uv run --extra dev -m newton.tests -k test_import_mjcf
uvx pre-commit run -a
uvx --from towncrier==25.8.0 towncrier build --draft --version 1.8.0 --date 2026-11-09
```

**Expected base RED:** registered MuJoCo per-DOF attributes include entries for slide DOFs 0, 1, 2 and ball DOFs 3, 4, 5. The pre-fix ball branch allocates only 3 DOFs, so attribute index 3 is invalid. Without those custom attributes it silently constructs a 3-DOF BALL. Invalid noncanonical layouts are not consistently rejected.

**Expected head GREEN, verified by code inspection only:** 3 slides × 1 translational DOF = 3, one ball × 3 angular DOFs = 3; total **6 DOFs** and **3 + 4 = 7 position coordinates**. For the authored CPU fixture, damping is `[1,2,3,4,4,4]`, armature `[0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4,0.4,0.4]`, friction `[0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.8,0.8]`, and slide actuator stiffness `[12,13,14]`. FK should preserve the body position `(0.2,-0.3,0.4)`. The two new tests assert those values and reject noncanonical layouts.

## Upstream readiness

**HOLD** until the CPU regression, formatter and CI pass, and potential overlap with the reporter's external branch is coordinated. This is fork-local only; no upstream issue, PR, comment or review was made. A separate MuJoCo solver limitation remains: MuJoCo free joints cannot directly accept the source's per-joint position actuators in the compiled `MjSpec`, so end-to-end solver actuator export is not claimed here.

## Follow-ups

1. Run the CPU `test_import_mjcf` suite and pre-commit on the fork branch; investigate any failures without weakening assertions.
2. Verify the compiled MuJoCo model and map slide/ball source actuators without targeting a native free joint illegally.
3. Compare against the reporter's implementation and request maintainer direction before any upstream proposal.

**Årsaken er ikke funnet i koden.** Det eneste stedet en preset får navn er Øveplan, som bruker et vanlig `<input>` (src/components/oveplan.tsx). author: bradcypert
body: Closes DNO-1336. ## What Answers how a client is configured for setup with Hooks - **Binary:** the first hook event of each UTC day carries three extra headers: - `X-Gram-Device-Fail-Open`: the effective fail-open posture (`failOpenAllowed`). - `X-Gram-Device-Debug-Log`: whether a debug log is on. This is true or false, never the path. - `X-Gram-Device-Spool-Depth`: how many spool entries are waiting to be resent. - The binary writes the day to `snapshot-day` in the hooks state dir, but only after the server accepts that request. A failed send leaves the snapshot for the next event. Two hooks firing at the same moment can each send one, which does no harm. - The snapshot rides a real event, because hooks only run when the coding agent fires one. It carries settings and counts only, never prompt or tool content. - **Server:** the middleware maps the headers to `gram.hook.device.fail_open`, `debug_log` and `spool_depth`. Like the other device attributes, they land on the hook row, and replayed rows skip them. ## Testing - `go test ./hooks/...`, with new tests for: - one snapshot per day, and a new one the next day - no marker written after a 5xx, with the marker set once a send succeeds - spool depth counting only real entries - `go test ./internal/middleware/ -run HookDevice` for the new header mappings. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01L9oYnabm6pTj3cAt683P17)_ --- ## Summary by cubic Closes DNO-1336. The hooks binary now reports its effective fail-open setting, debug log state, and spool depth once a day, so support can see how a client is configured without extra requests. **Details** - The snapshot rides the first hook event of each UTC day and adds three `X-Gram-Device-*` headers, which the server maps to `gram.hook.device.fail_open`, `.debug_log`, and `.spool_depth`. - The day marker is written only after the server accepts a 2xx response, so a failed send retries on the next event. - The marker is keyed by deployment, so a machine reporting to several servers, orgs, or projects sends each its own daily snapshot. - Concurrent hooks at the start of a day may each send a snapshot, which is harmless. - The snapshot carries settings and counts only, never prompt or tool content. Written for commit e8504a71422af444e04a88fa87471dbca3e349f7. Summary will update on new commits.

author: edavis71433
body:
"Send me a test" on Send an update, from the Figma (section 10): see the real email in your own inbox before your list does.

**Needs a functions deploy after merge.** Until then the button says test emails aren't switched on yet. Nothing else waits on it.

## What changes

- **A "Send me a test" button** sits beside "Help me write it". It saves the draft (the same road as Preview), then emails it to **your own sign-in address only**.
  - The subject is marked **[Test]**.
  - The fill-ins read the way the preview shows them ("Hi there").
  - A note confirms where it went: "Test sent to you@… — only you got it."
- **It can't reach anyone else.** The server takes the address from the signed-in person, never from the request.
- **It goes through the one send point** that real updates use, with the same branding, suppression check and one-click unsubscribe.
- **Nothing changes on the update itself:** no send-once claim, no count toward the day's cap, no open counter, nothing in the history.
- **Ten tests an hour per studio,** on the durable limiter the public forms use. Each test is a real email.
- **A team member needs edit for it, not publish,** since it only ever reaches their own inbox. Sending to the list stays publish.
- The real send is unchanged: it still goes through Preview & send and your final press.

author: doemu0992
body:
## Warum

Die Kundenseite im Betreiber-Portal war ein einziges langes Formular und stand immer im Bearbeiten-Modus. Bei Personen und Objekten ist es anders gelöst: eine Ansicht mit Kopf und Reitern, geändert wird auf einer eigenen Seite. Das Mockup dazu wurde freigegeben («Genau so machen»).

## Was neu ist

- **Kundenseite `/betreiber/<id>/`:** Aktenkopf mit Kundennummer, Ansprechperson, Telefon, E-Mail, Anschrift und Statusmarken (Kundenstatus, Stufe, Zahlungsstand). Vier Kennzahlen: offen (mit überfällig), bezahlt, Zahlungsverhalten, nächste Rechnung.
- **Fünf Reiter, nur zum Lesen:** Übersicht (Zu prüfen, Ansprechperson, Zuletzt, Notizen), Stammdaten, Verlauf (mit «+ Eintrag»), Finanzen (Rechnungen, Zahlungen, Summen), Abonnement (Stufe, Module, «Abrechnung ab», Nutzung). Der Reiter lässt sich per `?tab=` öffnen; ein ungültiger Wert fällt auf «Übersicht» zurück.
- **`/betreiber/<id>/bearbeiten/`:** Stammdaten und Ansprechperson als eigene Seite («Speichern» / «Abbrechen»).
- **`/betreiber/<id>/abo/`:** Stufe (mit den Folgen vorab), Module, «Abrechnung ab», Bestandsschutz.
- **Aktionen je Zeile** bleiben auf der Ansicht (PDF, Erneut senden, Erinnerung, Als bezahlt, Stornieren, Eintrag hinzufügen/löschen). Neu im «Mehr»-Menü: Kunde als gekündigt markieren bzw. wieder als Kunde.
- **Verhalten:** Alle Formulare gehen weiter an `/betreiber/<id>/`. Nach einer Aktion landet man auf dem passenden Reiter; bei einem Fehler oder einer Rückfrage auf der Seite, auf der man eingegeben hat (das Formular behält die Werte).

Daten, Logik und Berechtigungen ändern sich nicht. Es ist eine Umstellung der Darstellung; die 4 Hauptaktionen (`stamm`, `plan`, `einstellen`, Rechnungsaktionen) laufen im selben Code wie vorher.

## Geprüft

- Ganze Suite lokal mit `--parallel 4`: 7'132 Tests. Ein Fehler (zwei neue Vorlagen fehlten in der Übersetzungsliste `UEBERSETZT`), behoben; die betroffenen Tests laufen grün.
- 8 neue Tests (`BetreiberKundenseiteTests`): Ansicht ohne Eingabefelder, Reiter aus dem Parameter, Bearbeiten-Seite, Fehler zeigt die Seite mit den Eingaben, Abo-Rückfrage bleibt auf der Abo-Seite, Aktionen landen auf dem passenden Reiter, Status, nur der Betreiber (403) und 404 bei unbekannter Verwaltung.
- Seite im Browser gerendert und geprüft (Übersicht, Finanzen, Bearbeiten); am Telefon kein seitliches Scrollen.
- Isolations-Ausnahmen für die zwei neuen Ansichten eingetragen. Übersetzungen de/en/fr/it für die neuen Texte angehängt.

author: jeongjaesoon
body:
## 왜

検出層の定期 monitor がまだなかった(U15)。Orca plugin worker のタイマー上で orca-monitor・resource-monitor・chat-monitor を回し、event だけを書く。トークンは使わない。launchd・`orca agent launch` は使わない。

## 범위

ラウンド契約(コードより先に固定、`orca-plugin/timer.ts`、決定 0133):

```
startRounds(rounds, clock, { debounceMs }) -> { stats, hint(id), stop }
Round = { id, intervalMs, capMs?, run(at, signal) }
```
- 周期: `intervalMs` ごとのタイマー tick(orca 60 秒・resource 5 分・chat 5 分)
- 単一実行: 実行中の tick・hint は 2 本目を起こさない
- hint: `debounceMs` 内の hint は 1 ラウンドにまとめ、実行中に来た hint は終了後に 1 回だけ回す(`agent.status.changed` → orca)
- 上限: `capMs` を超えると signal を abort し、そのラウンドは event を書かない。次のラウンドは実際に終わるまで待つ

| monitor | 読むもの(Orca はアダプター経由のみ) | 書く event |
|---|---|---|
| orca | `worktree ps --agent-wait`・`worker-list`・`worker-show`・Run ごとの `gate-list --run`・`inbox`(消費しない)・sqlite の `notified`/`decision_*` | `worker_dead`(多数なら `host_restart`)・`worker_stuck`(`lastOutputAt`+`stateStartedAt`、見えなければ 0)・`run_stalled`・`waiting_decision`・`wake_unconfirmed`・`decision_untracked` |
| resource | `sampleLoad`・`diagnostics memory`・`docker ps -a`/`volume ls`・sqlite の `resource` | `pressure_high`/`capacity_free`(`judgeLoad` 1 つ、区間の境界で 1 回)・`resource_leak` |
| chat | `ChatProvider`(既定は null) | `mention_new`(null なら何も書かない) |

T2 の経路: worker の `setInterval`。根拠は U3 の T2 行(15 000 ms ラウンド 23 回、`gapsMs` 15000–15002、エラー 0)。`sangsoe monitor run <name> [--dry-run] [--db]` は同じ `MONITORS` 表を 1 ラウンド回す precheck 入口。

worker はコアを `orca-plugin/core-link.ts` 1 ファイルから実行時に import する(`../dist/core/index.js` → `../core/index.ts`、決定 0132)。

## 트레이드오프

- 承認とコンテンツハッシュはフォルダだけを覆うため、worker が動かすコアは承認範囲の外(0132 の残る隙間)。
- P10: `lastActivityAt` は作業中セッション 6/6 で動かなかったため判定から外した(0133)。
- 初回の resource ラウンドは記録のない Docker 資源を 1 件ずつ `resource_leak` にする(この PC では 268 件、dedupe で 1 回だけ)。
- `run_stalled` は Run ごとの `worker-list --run` で全メンバーを見たときだけ書く。全体の一覧(最新順、終わった Dispatch も含む)は Run を見つけるために 3 ページまでしか読まないため、それより古い未完了ワーカーは見えない。

## 영향 범위

`orca-plugin/`(timer・main・core-link・monitors)、`core/detect/`(新しい置き場)、`core/index.ts` の export、`cli/commands/monitor.ts`、docs(architecture 1 行・test-outcomes T2 2 次/P8/P10/P11・決定 0132/0133)。plugin の能力・コマンド・イベントは変えていないので承認の指紋は変わらない。

## 검증

- VERIFIED: `npm test`(`orch heavy` 経由、main マージ後の 0b790e3) tests 468 · pass 466 · fail 0 · skipped 2
- VERIFIED: `npm run typecheck`・`npm run lint` エラー 0
- VERIFIED: 実 Orca で 1 ラウンド(読みのみ、`--dry-run --db <scratch>`)。orca `planned: []`・`unseen: ["worker-list truncated"]`(全体の履歴が 3 ページを超える。Run ごとの判定は続く)、resource `resource_leak` 268(コンテナ 2・ボリューム 266)・`pressure_high` なし・`unseen: []`、chat `planned: []`
- Orca 内 worker タイマーでの T2 2 次: NOT VERIFIED(動作中のオーナーの plugin を差し替えるのは承認範囲外)
- P8: NOT VERIFIED(idle ワーカーへの `send` が必要)。P11: 未実行 + フィルタは U2 のテストで
- 独立レビュー(review:claude、新しいコンテキストの Claude): 1 回目 fe22f55 で Act-on 5(実際の Orca の形との不一致 4・停止時の競合 1)→ 2e7cf84 で修正。2 回目で Act-on 1(全体一覧のページングで `run_stalled` が止まる)→ 6f49f34 で Run ごとの一覧に変更。3 回目(0b790e3、main マージ込み)で Act-on 0

author: jgoyvaerts
body:
On the J616s (M4 Pro, IMX958), a browser camera test showed a zoomed-in corner of the sensor instead of the 1080p view. Browsers open 640x480 unless the page asks for a size.

`isp_ch_cache_sensor_configs()` appends every firmware sensor config that passes `isp_sensor_config_usable()` as a preset, cropped to its output size at offset 0. On this machine the firmware lists 13 configs, all with output == input, and only config 12 (1536x3024) passes. That config is a window over the right half of the 3072-wide sensor, with the dark lens edge in view. Nothing in the `CH_CAMERA_CONFIG_GET` reply says where a config sits on the sensor, so the driver cannot tell a centred config from an off-centre one.

This causes two problems:
- 1536x3024 is offered as a size of its own, and it is the largest one, so an app that picks the biggest size gets the half view.
- `isp_add_call_sizes()` takes the source with the largest crop for each call size, so 640x480, 1280x960, 960x1280, 1080x1920, 1328x1760 and the square were all cut from that half view.

This change keeps reading the configs for P010 qualification but no longer appends them. Every size then comes from the board's device-tree presets:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| NV12 and P010 sizes | 1920x1080, 1280x720, 1536x3024, 640x480, 1080x1920, 1328x1760, 1280x960, 960x1280, 1536x1536 | 1920x1080, 1280x720, 640x480, 1280x960, 1080x1080 |
| 640x480 / 1280x960 / square | cut from config 12 (right half) | centre of the 1080p view |

The portrait sizes go away because the 1080p view would have to be upscaled to make them. The sensor-config KUnit case now expects only the two board presets.

This removes part of the config discovery from be1528aa9183, and I could only test the J616s. If you'd rather keep the discovered configs, a narrower option is to keep appending them but never use them as sources in `isp_add_call_sizes()`. That fixes 640x480, but the off-centre 1536x3024 stays in the list.

Tested on a J616s with this diff on our 7.3 tree. The module was rebuilt against the running kernel and swapped in live:
- `--list-formats-ext` shows the "after" list for NV12 and P010.
- 640x480, 1920x1080 and 1080x1080 frames show the same centred view.
- Builds with W=1 and no warnings, with and without the KUnit test. The KUnit suite itself has not been run yet.

author: jakechampion
body:
Two slices of bare-metal milestone 6 (#14265), after #14923. The second one is the first "done when" item of the milestone: **the `arm64-linux` compiler, unmodified, compiles a test program on the kernel, and the output is byte-identical to the output on Linux.**

## 1. A layer in memory above the initrd

The compiler writes its cache in `$HOME/.cache/fern` and its output at `-o`, so a read-only root cannot run it. The root of a `std/user_process` process now has a layer in memory above the archive. The kernel answers these calls in that layer:

| Call | What the kernel does |
|---|---|
| `mkdirat` | Makes a directory. `EEXIST` for a path that exists, `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR` for a bad parent |
| `openat` with `O_CREAT`, `O_TRUNC`, `O_EXCL` | Makes or truncates a file, and opens it for writing |
| `write`, `writev` to a descriptor of 3 or more | Writes at the offset of the file |
| `renameat`, `renameat2` | Moves a file, or a directory with each node below it |
| `unlinkat` | Removes a file, or an empty directory with `AT_REMOVEDIR` |
| `fchmod`, `fchmodat` | Sets the mode |
| `fsync`, `fdatasync` | Gives 0 |

- A lookup finds a node of the layer before an entry of the archive, and a directory listing has the nodes of both.
- A file keeps its bytes as a list of chunks, so a long run of writes at the end copies each byte once.
- The archive stays read-only: a write, a rename or a removal there gives `EROFS`.
- `written(path)` gives the kernel the bytes of a file of the layer after the process ends.
- `lookup` moves one step of the walk into `hop`, and `open_found` its checks into `open_errno`, to keep each function under the complexity limit.

## 2. The compiler on the kernel

`TestSelfHostKernelCompilesOnQemu` builds the `arm64-linux` compiler with its stdlib embedded, and puts it with a source file in the initrd.

- On the kernel, the compiler extracts its stdlib into the layer in memory, compiles the file, and writes the output there.
- The kernel prints the size and the FNV-1a hash of the output. The test compares them with the output of the same compiler on Linux, under qemu-user.
- The kernel then runs the output as a second process, which prints `compiled on fernos` and exits with 7.
- The VM runs for about 5 s. Most of the test time is the build of the compiler.

What the compile needed:

- 766 MiB of RAM. qemu-virt puts the initrd 128 MiB above the start of its RAM, so it lies in the frame pool. `std/frames` gains `reserve`, which marks the frames of a range in use, with a case in `tests/stdlib/frames_test.fern`.
- The shared kernel prelude of the process tests now parses the device tree first. It reserves the frames of the initrd, and then moves a heap of the size that each test gives onto frames. `run_to_end`, `release` and `load_image` are shared.
- `bootQemuFor` takes the time limit of the VM, and `bootQemu` keeps 90 s.

## Tests

- `TestSelfHostKernelProcessOnQemu` runs a sixth program, `writer`. It makes a cache tree, writes a file and renames it into place, sets its mode, reads it back and stats it. It lists the tree and removes a scratch file. Each change of the archive fails, and the kernel reads the file it leaves in `/out`.
- `TestSelfHostKernelCompilesOnQemu` is a new step of the `kernel-boot` job.

## Run locally

- Green with `FERN_REQUIRE_QEMU_SYSTEM=1`: `TestSelfHostKernelCompilesOnQemu`, `TestSelfHostKernelProcessOnQemu`, `TestSelfHostKernelSchedulerOnQemu`, `TestSelfHostKernelFramesOnQemu` and `TestSelfHostKernelX86FramesOnQemu`.
- Green: the `std/frames` suite (5 of 5), `TestSelfHostRepoComplexityRatchet`, `fern -fmt -d`, `go vet`, and the pre-push hook.

## What remains of #14265

The second "done when" item: the compiler compiles itself on the kernel. A self-compile uses about 5.7 GB, so it needs a VM with more RAM and more of the time limit.

author: aviadr1
body:
> I'm Claude Opus 5.5, AI can make mistakes. Let the bouncer check the list.

## TLDR

#100 and #108 added lane reuse with this workflow's own `jq`. It set the tests lane to `false` when every job in a hand-written list was proven, and nothing checked that list against the test matrix. Add a matrix cell and forget the list, and the next push that changes nothing the tests read would skip that cell even if it had just failed (review finding F1 on #100 and #108). CI-esta 1.13.0 (ci-esta#176) now owns admission and checks the list. This switches to it.

```text
BEFORE  admit (jq): tests=false when listed jobs proven     ─► nothing checks the list against the matrix
AFTER   resolve-lane-evidence: planned-lanes + lane-keys ─► admitted-lanes
        quality: ci-esta check-workflow (>=1.13) ─► lane-keys must name every job the lane gates, per matrix cell
```

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who decides a lane (tests, contracts) is proven | this workflow's `jq` | CI-esta's tested `admittedLanes` |
| A new matrix cell missing from the list | silently skippable as proven | `quality` fails, naming the cell |
| Manual runs, Publish, `test:full` | plan stands | plan stands (`admitted-lanes \|\| plan`) |

## Evidence

- `ci-esta check-workflow` from CI-esta `main` (with #176) reports "Workflow lane and aggregate-gate contracts passed".
- **Mutation:** dropping `py311-windows` from `lane-keys` fails it with "Lane 'tests' is admitted from lane-keys in select-tests, which omit jobs it gates: ['tests (3.11, windows-latest)']".
- Two evidence steps chain: tests first, then contracts, which plans on the tests step's `admitted-lanes`. The job's `lanes` output is the contract step's result, or the plan when evidence is skipped.
- `actionlint` passes; `tests/test_repository_ci.py`, `tests/test_release_workflow.py` and `tests/testing/test_ci.py`: 131 passed.

## Merge order

Draft until CI-esta 1.13.0 is released (ci-esta#182). Until then `quality` cannot install `ci-esta[selection]>=1.13.0`, and `v1`'s evidence step has no `admitted-lanes`, so the plan stands.

body:
## Launcher option for the native wide scene

As agreed on Discord: the `wide_scene` renderer option (shadGT #16) gets a place in the launcher, so ultrawide players don't have to edit the config, and don't have to re-add the keys after each release overwrites it.

### What changes (Graphics, Display)
- **Screen shape** gets a third choice, **True wide (ultrawide, 21:9 / 32:9)**. It sets `aspect_ratio: auto` and `wide_scene: true`, and turns on what the wide scene needs: the native renderer and "Draw the UI at screen resolution" (their controls update too).
- The other two choices are unchanged and set `wide_scene: false`.
- **Wide scene height:** 1080 (recommended) / 1200 / 1440, saved as `wide_scene_height`. It's only enabled with True wide, and a tip says 1080 runs best.

Only `loader/RyGTLoader.cs` changes (C# 5, as the rest of the launcher).

### Testing
Built with `loader/build.cmd` (.NET Framework csc) and used on a Samsung G9 (5120x1440): the new options save as expected, and Play starts the game wide with True wide.

author: lautaroblasco23
body:
# Simple

**Result:** `apps/mobile` is now a Gradle multi-module Kotlin/Jetpack-Compose Android app; the Expo/RN code is deleted (rollback: git tag `rn-final`). Backend, frontend and `packages/shared` (web) unchanged.

- **Verified:** `gradlew :app:assembleDebug test` green (14 MB APK); unit tests for the auth core (MockWebServer: login/refresh/logout/error envelopes), calendar-week logic, en/es key parity; root `npm test -w @life-tracker/shared` 20/20; `make e2e-mobile` (Maestro smoke) added as pre-push gate.
- **Stack:** AGP 8.10.1 / Gradle 9.3.1 / Kotlin 2.2.21 / KSP 2.2.21-2.0.5 / Hilt 2.57.2 / Compose BOM 2025.09.01; Retrofit over all 13 backend domains (DTOs from Go `json` tags), single-flight refresh-on-401 authenticator, EncryptedSharedPreferences tokens, DataStore settings (api URL/language/theme), i18n from existing messages JSON.
- **Continuity:** same `applicationId com.lifetracker.mobile`, `versionCode 100` (> any RN APK) — installs as an update; **sessions reset once** (token storage backend changed).
- **Deferred to you:** on-device QA — `make mobile`, then walk `kotlin-refactor/qa-checklist.md`; Compose UI instrumentation tests + Maestro E2E require a working emulator.
- **Scope notes:** npm workspaces = `packages/shared` only; Makefile/CI/docs rewritten for Gradle; `make e2e-mobile` needs Maestro (`curl -Ls get.maestro.mobile.dev | bash`) and ANDROID_HOME.
- Details per phase in `plan.md`; API contract in `kotlin-refactor/api-contract.md`.

---

# Original plan summary

## Objective

Replace the Expo/React Native/TypeScript mobile app (`apps/mobile/`) with a native Android app
written in Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, feature-parity with today's app, integrated with the existing
Go backend, Makefile, and CI — via an in-place big-bang rewrite (decisions: in-place, Jetpack
Compose, plain Kotlin module for shared logic, Android-only).

## Phases (all complete)

| Phase | What shipped |
|---|---|
| 0 Baseline | `rn-final` tag (rollback), 201-item QA checklist, 1,091-line API contract from Go DTOs |
| 1 Skeleton | 13 Gradle modules, Compose+Hilt+Navigation, theme tokens, en/es i18n, adaptive icon/splash, CI job |
| 2 Core layer | 13 Retrofit interfaces + DTOs, refresh-on-401 OkHttp authenticator, encrypted token store, DataStore settings, JS-parity lib ports |
| 3 Features | Design system (10 primitives, 1,188 LOC) + 7 feature groups: auth 610, activities+routines+templates+reminders 3,812, time 2,951, notes 1,683, finance ~1,800, social 1,470, profile+backup ~1,900 LOC |
| 4 Tests | Kotlin unit tests (auth MockWebServer semantics, calendar week, i18n parity) |
| 5 Tooling | Makefile `mobile`/`mobile-rebuild`/`api-up`/`e2e-mobile`, single `kotlin-build` CI job, docs rewrite (mobile/tests/README/AGENTS/styles), npm workspaces collapsed to `packages/shared` |
| 6 Cutover | RN deletion (tag `rn-final` for rollback), versionCode continuity, final green gates |

## Key decisions

- Locked toolchain = AGP 8.10.1 + Kotlin 2.2.21 (AGP 9 built-in-Kotlin + KSP2 was systematically broken in this environment; documented).
- Backend DTOs are the single contract; mobile no longer consumes `packages/shared` (web keeps it).
- QA parity checklist + API contract docs included in the branch (`kotlin-refactor/`).

author: guetteman
body:
While resolving the human reviews of one pull request in a private project, three times the owner's question, or a review the owner asked for, led to a design with fewer mechanisms than the agent's proposal. Of two `jsonb` columns, one had that type because of a migration default, and neither needed it. Making both text removed a parser and a rejection the agent had planned around that type. For stores the platform runs as code, the agent proposed a third rule beside a list of forbidden stores and an existing mechanism; the owner chose to let the existing mechanism take over the list instead.

## What changes

- New reference `skills/engineering/strategic-programming/references/second-opinion.md`. When the work chooses between designs, another agent gets the problem, its evidence, and each option in one line, without the author's reasoning or preference, and adds an option of its own. It answers six questions for every option (cause, premise, existing mechanism, why each piece exists, scope, tests) and writes a count: mechanisms, special cases, what each deletes and adds, code touched beyond the problem, and one-way doors. Where another option does better, the author adopts it or names the evidence for the difference.
- `shape` (choosing an option, and the fixes from its gap review), `program-design`, `refine`, `deliver` (changes made after `refine`), and `strategic-programming` point to it. The reference alone says when to skip it.
- `pr-review`'s architecture lens flags a mechanism the change adds beside an existing one, and a piece the change works around that was only a default.

## Decisions

- **The second opinion gets each option and writes a count; it is not asked to find holes.** In the same pull request, a reviewer asked to find holes in the agent's proposal added three pieces to it, each for a real gap, and recommended keeping the rule. A second review got the proposal, the existing mechanism, and an alternative where that mechanism took over the list, and was asked whether the rule was a patch and what each option deletes and adds. It confirmed the alternative. That brief still argued for the alternative, so leaving the author's reasoning out goes further than the evidence; it is a judgment that a reviewer without it is less anchored.
- **A hole that only a new piece closes first questions the earlier choice that left it.** There, the first reviewer closed one hole by adding four entries to the forbidden list, the list the second review let the existing mechanism replace.
- **The comparison counts mechanisms and one-way doors, not lines.** The decisive comparison there was three mechanisms against one.
- **A simpler design still goes through `architect`** for each one-way door it crosses, or to the human during delivery. One of the simpler fixes there was a schema change.

## How to review

Start with the reference, 35 lines. `shape` changes in two steps, `program-design` in its step 3 and its completion criterion, `pr-review`'s lenses gain two sentences, and each other skill gains one sentence or clause. The changelog entry and the version bump to 3.9.0 complete the diff.

## What was tested

This repository has no CI and no tests for skill text. No agent has run the new text yet.

## Not included

`shape`'s spec template has no field for the counts. It can get one once a few runs show what the counts look like in practice.

- **Retrofit and OkHttp.** The `square/retrofit` and `square/okhttp` repositories now redirect to the `lysine-dev` organization. Its published homepage is `lysine.dev`, so citations now use `https://lysine.dev/retrofit/` and the matching OkHttp pages.

author: riponcm
body:
Telemetry from the first hour (see [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md), row 1). Design notes are in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md#telemetry-pull-request-1).

## What
- **API:** OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs over OTLP/HTTP. Export turns on only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set, so tests and fresh clones run without a backend.
- **Every request traced** by the FastAPI instrumentation; the Elasticsearch 9 client traces its own calls as child spans (the contrib instrumentor disables itself on 9.x, so it is not used).
- **Logs** carry trace and span IDs, so a log line links to its trace.
- **`.env` loaded into the process environment** because the OTLP exporters read `OTEL_*` from there, not from app settings.
- **`POST /api/debug/break`** (demo only, off unless `ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINTS=true`): sends Elasticsearch a query it rejects, so Dash0 has a real error to find.
- **Browser:** Dash0 web SDK for page views, web vitals, fetch calls and errors. `/api` calls are same-origin, so the trace header joins the browser and API spans into one trace. The browser token is ingest-only.

## Verified locally
- Browser export to Dash0: `/v1/traces` and `/v1/logs` returned 200.
- API export with the server token: `SUCCESS`; traces for `/api/health` and the failing `/api/debug/break` (with the Elasticsearch `search` span and its exception) visible in Dash0.
- Backend: ruff, 4 tests. Frontend: lint, type check and build.

LLM spans (tokens and cost) arrive with the first LLM call in PR 8.

Correções das consequências da migração de `especialidade` feita direto na `v1` (ver a revisão no PR #30).

A migração apagou as especialidades e a carga as recriou com IDs novos. Fichas confirmadas antes ficaram apontando para IDs inexistentes — fora de qualquer fila, comprovante sem especialidade e reavaliação de cor (RF12) quebrando.

### 2. `api/cadastros` versionado
`GET` e `POST especialidades` existiam só no servidor. Versionados exatamente como publicados (`--dry-run`: "No changes to push"). O `POST` traz o aviso "NÃO PUBLICAR antes da migração aprovada", mas já está no ar — a decisão de mantê-lo fica com a equipe/`add-cadastros-administrador`.

## Ce qui change
- **RG-01, tramage** (`shaders/post.frag`) : le bruit de ±0,5 / 255 était ajouté en lumière **linéaire**, alors que l'écran encode en sRGB (téléphone et banc). Dans un ciel clair, un pas de code vaut alors ≈ 1,6 / 255 en linéaire : le bruit ne cachait plus les marches, d'où les anneaux. Maintenant, un bruit **triangulaire de ±1 code** est ajouté **au code sRGB**, puis ramené en linéaire pour l'écran. Test : marches du dégradé du ciel **0,23 → 0,008 code**.
- **RG-02, ciel de midi** (option A du PO, avis de l'expert réalisme 3D) (`eclairage_unites.h`, `photometrie.json`, `SOURCES.md`) :
  - Le ciel était calé sur 6 000 lx, valeur mesurée **à l'ombre**. Le ciel entier suit maintenant Krochmann et Seidl 1974 : **15 825 lx** à h 70°.
  - Les 6 000 lx restent la valeur de contrôle « point à l'ombre » : au pied d'un mur, le même ciel donne **5 498 lx** (−8 %).
  - Le référentiel gagne l'entrée `lum.ciel_clair.plein_ciel` (±15 %, « à confirmer » : article non ouvert).
  - Le crépuscule et la nuit sont inchangés (raccord au niveau d'avant, `eclairage_physique.cpp`).
- **RG-03, chaussée en Ultra** : rien à corriger dans le rendu. Sur `main`, Ultra et Haute donnent déjà la même chaussée grise (ANO-106 a été corrigée en chemin par un autre ticket). Ajouts : une **preuve au banc** (accroche de 10 lignes dans `bench_passes.cpp` : Ultra puis Haute posés directement, captures `chaussee-*-course`) et la mesure du ΔE.
- **RG-05, vision de nuit loin des lumières** (`post.frag`, `eclairage_exposition.h`, `eclairage_physique.*`, accroche d'une ligne dans `renderer.cpp`) :
  - Le poids de la vision de nuit suit maintenant la **luminance d'adaptation de l'œil**, tirée de l'EV mesuré autour du joueur, ou celle du pixel si elle est plus forte.
  - Avant, il suivait seulement la luminance du pixel : une peinture foncée sous une lampe était traitée comme un paysage sous la lune.
  - Golf sous un lampadaire (15 lx, pire cas EV 3) : **ΔE2000 de 5,6 à 3,1** par rapport à la même image sans vision de nuit (seuil 10).
  - En rase campagne : poids 0,87 au lieu de 0,90, soit ΔE2000 ≤ 1,2 (sous le seuil de perception).
- RG-04 : rien de WFS-208 n'est retiré (nuages, 6 moments).
- **Bancs** (retour du lead dev) : `eclairage_banc.cpp` : l'exposition des moments atteint sa cible avant la capture ; `eclairage_depart_banc.cpp` : départ de jour en Campagne.

## Comment c'est vérifié
- **Tests CPU** : nouveau `test_post_wfs214` (tramage, vision de nuit, constantes identiques au shader). `test_fidelite_lumiere` reçoit 5 vérifications de plus : ciel entier, contrôle à l'ombre, zénith 6 à 8 kcd/m², rapport soleil / ombre 2,5 à 3,2 IL, référentiel. Aucune vérification n'est supprimée ni affaiblie. `test_fidelite` est vert. Les 92 tests passent après synchronisation avec main (`tools/qa/tests_cpu.sh`).
- **Banc `realisme` (mesures)** :

  | Mesure | Avant | Après | Cible |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Zénith à h 70° | 2 667 cd/m² | **7 034 cd/m²** | 6 à 8 kcd/m² |
  | Ciel entier (modèle) | 5 965 lx | **15 732 lx** | 15,8 klx ±15 % |
  | Rapport soleil / ombre rendu | — | **7,76, soit 2,96 IL** | 2,5 à 3,2 IL |
  | Teinte du zénith | x 0,2838 ; y 0,2923 | inchangée | gardée |
  | EV de jour (Ville) | 15 | 15 | l'exposition n'annule pas le gain |

- **Chaussée Ultra / Haute** : ΔE2000 de **0,02 à 0,03** sur la chaussée et de **0,92** sur le trottoir (seuil 3).
- **Banc `depart`** : nuit (Ville, Corniche, Campagne) et jour (Ville, Campagne).
- **Banc `perf`** : voir le point 3 du retour ci-dessous.

## Limites et risques
- **M-03 du banc `realisme`** (rapport soleil / ombre contre le modèle) : écart de 5,5 % pour un seuil de 5 %, donc NON CONFORME, signalé « écart attendu ». La cause : la sonde de la Campagne voit le relief et les arbres, qui cachent environ 10 % du ciel (14 204 lx contre 15 732). Le seuil est gardé tel quel. Le rapport mesuré (2,96 IL) est dans la cible du PO.
- **Pas d'occlusion du ciel sur les objets mobiles** (voiture, plaque du banc) : les ombres de jour sont un peu plus claires partout ; au soleil bas (h 10°), les murs à l'ombre s'éclaircissent nettement. Le décor fixe garde son occlusion précalculée (WFS-269). Si le lead dev ou l'utilisateur trouve les ombres délavées, le PO crée l'US « occlusion du ciel » (P2), comme il l'a prévu.
- **Défaut déjà présent sur `main`, hors de ce ticket** : le banc des passes ne trouve plus le choix « Ultra » dans le panneau à onglets (« introuvable, 21 zones », parcours 2/5 avant comme après). Sa capture `parcours-ultra-course` est donc en Haute ; signalé au PO (ANO-211, WFS-377). Mes captures `chaussee-*` posent Ultra directement.
- **Captures** : elles sont faites selon la méthode de `captures_pr.sh`, mais avec les bancs lancés en parallèle (voir `qa/pr/WFS-214/README.md`). Pas de CI de branche (ce n'est pas une US technique). Rien n'a été essayé sur téléphone.

## Retour du lead dev (revue du commit 75749e6e) : corrections
1. **Moments de jour plus blancs** : la cause est un **défaut du banc**, déjà présent sur main. Le banc des moments fige le temps et ne recrée pas la scène, si bien que l'exposition restait celle de l'aube : EV 8,2 à midi au lieu de 15, soit 7 IL de trop. Les images étaient donc blanches avant comme après, et un ciel plus clair les blanchissait encore. Correction (`eclairage_banc.cpp`) : l'exposition atteint sa cible avant la capture, comme dans le jeu, où le temps avance. Résultat : midi EV 14,98, heure dorée EV 13,2 à 14,6. Avec ce banc corrigé des deux côtés, la luminance moyenne des moments de jour va de 46-84 à 60-130 sur 255. Rien n'est blanc : la colline, l'éolienne et les vaches se voient. L'heure dorée de la Campagne ne change pas (60 → 60) ; l'aube, l'heure bleue et la nuit sont identiques.
2. **Captures ajoutées** : heure dorée (Campagne et circuit), midi (Campagne et circuit), matin du circuit, et `depart-jour-campagne-4`. Pour ce dernier, le banc `depart` fait maintenant aussi un départ de jour en Campagne.
3. **Performance** (banc `perf`, 4 cartes × Haute / Basse, 2 mesures avant, 1 après) : image entière de **−4,1 % à +0,2 %** par rapport à la moyenne d'avant, dans le bruit de mesure (les deux mesures d'avant diffèrent elles-mêmes de 2 à 7 %). La part hors des passes mesurées, qui contient la passe finale, bouge de 2,1 ms au plus sur des images de 420 à 650 ms (lavapipe). Le tramage n'est donc pas simplifié. Limite : lavapipe n'est pas le GPU du téléphone ; le coût ajouté est de 2 `pow(vec3)` et 2 hachages par pixel dans la seule passe finale.
4. **Remarques** :
   - M-03 est noté dans le Suivi de `regles-de-gestion/WFS-214.md`.
   - Le banc des passes qui ne trouve plus « Ultra » est signalé au PO : **ANO-211**, US technique **WFS-377**.
   - La branche est synchronisée avec main (WFS-338 compris).

## Captures pour le lead dev (18 après)

« Avant » des moments et de `depart-jour-campagne-4` : main **avec la même correction du banc** (voir README). Dossier : [`qa/pr/WFS-214`](https://github.com/wlfaleh/waforspeed_mobile/blob/feature/waforspeed-214/qa/pr/WFS-214) — tableau complet avec toutes les images : [`README.md`](https://github.com/wlfaleh/waforspeed_mobile/blob/feature/waforspeed-214/qa/pr/WFS-214/README.md).

author: alexeyshalaev
body:
Срез W2 маршрута подписания (`docs/design/signing-route.md`, разделы 3.1, 3.3, 4.4, 5, 8): экран автора «Отправка на подписание» для точки сдачи.

Адрес `/projects/:id/submit/cp/:profileId/route` (уже задан `signingRouteEditorPath` из W1). Экран отдельным ленивым чанком `SigningRouteEditor-*.js`, бюджет в `.size-limit.json` 12.5 kB (сейчас 10.9 kB: туда же пока попадает `entities/signing-route`, W3 и W4 вынесут его в общий код).

## Что на экране

- **Документы точки**: собран ли каждый документ маршрута (по предпросмотру), «Собрать» (`useStartCompile`), «Открыть». Документ под другим маршрутом помечен.
- **Кто и в каком порядке**: шаги карточками, в шаге люди параллельно. Человек: имя, персона, статус в проекте («участник», «приглашение отправлено», «нет в проекте»), способ («Картинка», «ЭП», «только согласование»), готовность («подпись загружена», «ключ известен» или «укажет при подписании»), число действий из предпросмотра (0: «отправка и есть согласие», 1, 2: «согласовать, затем подписать итоговый PDF»), метка шага L «фиксация после шага». Людей перетаскивают между шагами и в новый шаг, шаги перетаскивают целиком; то же кнопками: стрелки шага, меню человека «В один шаг с предыдущим», «Отдельным шагом», «Убрать» (только у согласующего без слотов).
- **Пригласить**: у человека «нет в проекте» кнопка открывает существующий `InviteDialog` с заготовкой: роль Рецензент и персона шага. Созданное приглашение сразу ставится в шаг (`invitation_id`). Можно взять и ожидающее приглашение с той же персоной. При закрытой регистрации экран это пишет.
- **Добавить согласующего**: руководитель без слотов отдельным последним шагом.
- **Где подписи**: вкладки документов, `PdfStampEditor` только со слотами маршрута, у слота человек, «На стр. N», «Перейти», «Сюда». Необязательные для точки слоты (применимы к документу, но маршрут их не требует): «Добавить подпись: …» (`extra_slots`), у включённого крестик «Убрать». Участника необязательного слота добавляет сервер (как в R5); при выключении слота уходит и его участник, если других подписей у него нет.
- **Ваша подпись**: отправка и есть согласие отправителя первого шага. Картинка: готова или «Загрузить или нарисовать» (`SignatureEditorModal`, загрузка в свои слоты). ЭП: данные плашки готовы или `SignerPlateEditor`; ключ из `sender_key` предпросмотра или ссылка на настройки подписи. Не в первом шаге: «согласуете в свою очередь».
- **Отправка**: срок (дата, в контракт уходит конец дня по местному времени), сообщение (до 2000), фиксация после шага L или при отправке, кто выберет способ сам, список помех по кодам предпросмотра, «Отправить на подписание» («Отправить заново» после остановки, возврата, отмены) и «Отправить и подписать», когда `can_send_and_sign` (пароль, если ключ защищён). `expected` берётся из `docs[].token` предпросмотра. Ошибки `doc_changed`, `route_blocked`, `invalid_transition`, `passphrase_required`, `rate_limited` показаны текстом, предпросмотр перечитывается. После отправки возврат на точку.

Какой маршрут открывается: незавершённый точки; иначе последний отменённый (для «Отправить заново»); иначе новый черновик из пака создаётся при заходе. Завершённый без явного «Новый маршрут» не трогается (новый снял бы его с контроля). `?route=<id>` открывает конкретный. Идущий маршрут показан только для чтения с подсказкой отменить его на точке. Локальная Студия: «работает на сервере Студии», запросов нет.

Правки уходят сразу целиком (PUT), пока запрос идёт, управление видно, но не нажимается. Предпросмотр пересчитывается после правки, сборки и изменения подписей проекта.

## Что ещё поменялось

- `InviteDialog`: необязательный `onCreated` (приглашение создано, до показа ссылки).
- `features/signature-stamper`: наружу `SignatureEditorModal` и `SignerPlateEditor`.
- Моки W1 (`demoRoutes.ts`) как R5: правка добавляет участника необязательного слота отдельным последним шагом с человеком по персоне; предпросмотр называет помеху `sender_not_ready`.
- Тексты: новый словарь `signingRouteEditor` (ru, en).

## Отступления

- «Если таких несколько, автор выбирает одного» (6.5): контракт не отдаёт участников проекта с персонами, поэтому выбор человека из участников не сделан. Человека по персоне назначает сервер в заготовке; на экране можно пригласить или взять ожидающее приглашение. Из этого же: согласующий, добавленный кнопкой, приходит «нет в проекте», даже если человек с этой персоной уже в проекте (R5 не ищет человека для нового участника без `user_id` и `invitation_id`). Если это нужно, проще всего в R5 разрешать такого участника по персоне так же, как в заготовке.
- Карточка «Подписание» на точке с кнопкой «Подготовить и отправить» это W3, поэтому сейчас на экран попадают по адресу.

## Проверки

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint:i18n`, `pnpm test` (`NODE_ENV=test`, весь набор), `pnpm build`, `pnpm bundlesize`. Новые тесты: перестановки шагов и тело PUT (`routeDraft.test.ts`), экран на моках W1 (`SigningRouteEditor.test.tsx`: черновик из пака, необязательный слот и приглашение, согласующий из приглашений, перетаскивание и стрелки, отправка с сообщением, локальный режим). Руками в серверном демо (`VITE_SERVER_DEMO=1`, Playwright): перетаскивание в шаг и в новый шаг, меню, согласующий, окно приглашения, телефон.

body:
The Tree of Sophia's mark (#366) now stands everywhere the earlier one still stood: on the link cards and on the desktop app; and every page names its icons anew so browsers drop the earlier drawing.

## What Changed
- **Link cards** (`access/web/public/og/*.jpg`). The four cards (Zarathustra and Antiquity, en and ru) carry the new mark beside the name, where the constellation tree stood. The rest of each card is unchanged.
- **Desktop app** (`access/web/constructor/desktop/icon.svg`). The local app «Древо Софии — демо» wears the mark on its dark tile.
- **Icon addresses** (`home`, `zarathustra`, `antiquity`, `not-found` pages). The favicon, favicon.ico and touch icon are named with `?v=sophia`, so a browser that keeps a tab icon under its old address takes the new drawing. The not-found page names the touch icon too.

## Why
- After #366 the site serves the new icons, yet browsers keep a page's icon by its address, and the link cards and the desktop app still showed the earlier mark.

## Validation
- Software, in `access/web` on this head (9061466dd): `npx vitest run` passes 156 files, 1315 tests (15 skipped) before the two new tests; `src/public-research/mark.test.mjs` passes 3 tests with them; `npx vite build --mode public-research` builds, and the built pages carry `/__research/favicon.svg?v=sophia` and the rest.
- The four cards were checked by eye: the new mark centred on the name's capitals, the place of the earlier one cleared to the card's own background.

## Boundary / Direction Impact
- No boundary shift.

## Risk / Follow-ups
- Link previews already cached by other services (Telegram and the like) keep the earlier card until they fetch it again.
- An installed copy of the desktop app keeps its icon until it is reinstalled with `--replace`.

author: octobercomms
body:
Three faults. The first two had been in the product all day; the third is why nothing caught them.

---

# 1. The preview could not draw a photograph

`Compositor.jsx` decided image-versus-video with `kind === 'design'`. A photograph is `kind: 'clip'` with `still: true`, so the compositor built a `<video>` element, pointed it at a JPEG, waited for a `readyState` that never arrives, and skipped the layer.

Measured on the shipped build:

```
showroom-01.jpg fetched as: ["img","video","fetch","video","video"]
canvas on a photograph:     0% non-black
```

The render drew the picture correctly the whole time. **So the six camera-move chips that shipped this morning drove a value nobody could see.**

The model has always known the difference — `compositionPlayback.mjs` reads `src.kind === 'clip' && src.still !== true` to decide whether a source has an audio stream. Only that one line did not.

---

# 2. The preview did not repaint when a source finished loading

Measured at 1280x720 *with the fix above in place*:

| | non-black |
|---|---|
| on load | **0%** |
| after one arrow key | 89% |

A source arrives after the frame it belongs to was last drawn, and nothing was asking for a repaint, so the player sat black until the operator moved the playhead or pressed play. This is the one that made the first look like *"the preview cannot draw stills"*, when in fact it could not draw anything that had not arrived yet.

---

# 3. Every media URL in the drive fixture 404'd

```
/api/brand/file/c1/showroom-01.jpg       -> 404
/api/brand/file/c1/atlas-walkthrough.mp4 -> 404
/api/brand/file/c1/space.mp3             -> 404
```

**114 assertions were judging a black rectangle**, and not one of them could tell a broken picture from a missing file. Every claim made about the player today was true about geometry and empty about pixels.

The stub serves `drives/fixtures/media/` now. The photographs carry **distinguishable colour bands** on purpose — a flat fixture makes a pixel assertion vacuous, which this project learned once already with `testsrc2`'s horizontal stripes. The drive asserts the centre of the frame is **green** on a photograph, because the image is red / green / blue across and a cover fit into 9:16 must show the middle third.

---

# What the browser learns is not what the operator did

Serving real media immediately broke two assertions that had been passing: **opening a reel wrote to the database again**, and **undo lit up on a reel nobody had touched**. Both were real. Both were hidden by the 404s.

`onMeta` writes a source's measured duration and frame size into the model when the media loads. That is a correction, not a change of intent: the file is the truth and the row was a guess. It goes through a new `applyDerived` on the history hook, which updates the live state and pushes nothing, and the autosave comparison strips those three fields from both sides. Filling in an item whose length was never known is a different thing — still an edit, still saved.

That distinction cost a round trip of its own: the filter went on the live snapshot and not on the baseline recorded at load, so the two could never match and every load looked like an edit. **A comparison has two sides.**

---

# Verified

Four new drive assertions, none of which could have been written before the fixture served a picture:

```
PASS  the player draws the footage at the start
PASS  and draws a PHOTOGRAPH rather than a black rectangle  — 100% non-black
PASS  and it is the right part of the photograph  — centre pixel {"r":0,"g":129,"b":2}
PASS  and it was loaded as an image, not as a video  — ["img","video","fetch","video","img"]
```

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `drive-studio.mjs` | **118 assertions** |
| Frontend units | 334 |
| Backend steps, as CI runs them | 124 of 124 |
| `lint:hooks`, `vite build` | clean |

Also recorded in the brief, not fixed here: the preview and the render **disagree outside the overscan**. `pos` and `scale` mean "move the already-cropped frame inside the output frame" to the renderer, which produces black bars, and "pan within the source picture" to the preview, which does not. They agree only while `|pos| <= (scale-1)/2`, and all six shipped MOTIONS sit inside that bound — `drift` and `rise` by 5px on a 1080 frame. Any control that lets a person leave the overscan crosses it on the first drag.

---

author: ayhansipahi
body:
## What broke

Since #6 made the service endpoints IAM-only, every signed call from an app to `cart-api` and `orders-api` in prod gets this from Lambda:

> 403 Forbidden — You are not authorized to access this endpoint.

The app turns that into a 502, so signed-in users see "Error / An unexpected error occurred" on `/orders`, `/store/cart` and the mini cart. The `serviceCall` log line added in #7 surfaced this.

## Why

The signature and each app role's own policy are correct. But every stage role carries the `rsc-mfe-boundary-<stage>` permissions boundary, and the boundary never allowed `lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint`. The grant #6 added is cut off by the boundary.

## Change

- `infra/bootstrap.ts`: the boundary allows `lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint` on `web-function/rsc-mfe-<stage>-*/endpoint/*`, so the stage's own endpoints only. Each role's own policy still names the one endpoint it may call.
- `infra/bootstrap.test.ts`: the staging boundary allows the staging cart endpoint and denies prod and other workloads. The test failed before the fix; all 43 infra tests pass now.

## After merge (manual)

The pipeline does not deploy the bootstrap stack. An account admin has to run:

```
npx cdk deploy bootstrap-644789169398
```

This changes IAM only, so no app redeploy is needed. Confirm the CI diff shows only the two boundary policy changes.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Security & Reliability**
  * Stage permissions now allow invocation of web-function endpoints within the matching stage, while blocking access to production endpoints from staging and to endpoints belonging to other workloads.
* **User Experience**

author: dmaffitt
body:
## Description

Concurrent compressed (`.tgz`) uploads can corrupt each other. commons-compress 1.26.0 has a bug, [COMPRESS-666](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/COMPRESS-666): it skips the unread part of a tar entry through a commons-io scratch buffer that every thread shares. A skip on one thread can overwrite inflater output that another thread still needs. Some imports then fail with "Corrupted TAR archive". Others archive files with wrong header values and raise no error.

This PR:
- upgrades commons-compress from 1.26.0 to 1.26.1, which fixes COMPRESS-666. Later versions need a newer commons-lang3 than the one xnat-web forces.
- upgrades commons-io from 2.15.1 to 2.22.0 in the version catalog.
- adds `CompressedTarConcurrencyTest`, a regression test that reads `.tgz` archives the same way `DicomZipImporter.importTgzFile` does, on several threads at once.

<!-- TODO(author): link the ticket or issue. The original commit subject ended with a bare "#". -->

## Release note

<!-- TODO(author): write this yourself. The template asks for it in the author's own words. -->

## Risks and impact

### Input data
The bug is triggered by the importer's normal read pattern. `.txt` sidecars are read only as far as the DICOM parser gets before it gives up, so `getNextTarEntry()` has to skip the rest of the entry. The test reproduces this with pairs of text sidecars and image-like 16-bit data.

### Upgrade and compatibility
Both changes are patch or minor dependency upgrades in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. That file also feeds the published `org.nrg:parent` BOM, so plugins built against the BOM will pick up the new versions.

Without this change, xnat-web's test runtime classpath already resolves commons-io to **2.19.0**, not the 2.15.1 declared in the catalog. The bump to 2.22.0 is therefore a smaller jump than the catalog diff suggests. See the note for reviewers.

### Performance and scale
Only affects concurrent compressed uploads. No change to the single-upload path.

## Testing

### Unit tests
`./gradlew :xnat-web:test --tests "org.nrg.xnat.archive.CompressedTarConcurrencyTest"`

The test reads 6 archives on 4 threads for 6 rounds (144 reads in total). It checks every read against a single-threaded read of the same archive, counting reads that fail and reads that succeed with different bytes. Results on JDK 21.0.11:

| commons-compress | commons-io (resolved) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1.26.0 (current `develop`) | 2.19.0 | **FAILED**: `[reads that failed] Expecting AtomicInteger(144) to have value: 0`. Every concurrent read was unreadable. |
| 1.26.1 | 2.19.0 | passed (1 test, 0 failures) |
| 1.26.1 | 2.22.0 (this PR) | passed (1 test, 0 failures) |

Versions were confirmed with `./gradlew :xnat-web:dependencyInsight --configuration testRuntimeClasspath`.

### REST integration tests
I ran the full [xnat-rest-tests](https://github.com/NrgXnat/xnat-rest-tests) suite (`main` at `b2dcb7f`) against this branch, deployed on a freshly reset local stack: Tomcat 9, PostgreSQL 13 and ActiveMQ, under Docker Desktop. Settings: `xnat.version=1.11.0`, the site settings from `jenkins.sh`, and the suite on JDK 8 as in CI.

**908 tests: 899 passed, 9 failed.** None of the failures come from this change. I reran the three failing classes on their own, on a freshly reset stack, against both this branch and its base (`develop` at `a33e6b7e1`, with commons-compress 1.26.0). All 19 tests had the same outcome on both builds: the same 13 passed and the same 6 failed.

| Failing tests | Same on `develop`? | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `TestDicomDataExtraction` (all 4) | Yes | Already present in `develop`. Multi-valued fields come back with doubled separators, for example `ORIGINAL\\PRIMARY\\AXIAL` where the suite expects `ORIGINAL\PRIMARY\AXIAL` (Image Type, and Operators' Name on the MR session). |
| `TestDicomSCPWhitelist.testWhitelistEnabledWithValidIpAddress`, `testWhitelistEnabledWithValidAEAndValidIp` | Yes | Local environment. Behind Docker Desktop's NAT, XNAT sees every C-STORE peer as `192.168.65.1` (`NOT_WHITELISTED@/192.168.65.1` in `received.log`). That isn't one of the host addresses the test allows. |
| `TestAdvancedSearch.testSubjectSearch`, `testSubjectJoinSearch`, `testScanSearch` | Pass in isolation on both builds | Test order. These assert site-wide counts (`expected:<33> but was:<32>`), and earlier classes in a full run change the totals. |

The suite has no test that uploads compressed archives concurrently, so this run shows that nothing else regressed. It does not exercise the fix itself.

### Manual verification
The build under test was this branch at `12fd28803`, built with `./gradlew :xnat-web:war`. The WAR ships `commons-compress-1.26.1.jar` and `commons-io-2.22.0.jar`, and I confirmed both are in `WEB-INF/lib` of the running container. The REST run above was against that deployment.

**Concurrent `.tgz` uploads, end to end.** I ran the same test against this branch and against `develop` at `a33e6b7e1` (commons-compress 1.26.0), each on a freshly reset stack.
- **Archives:** 25 `.tgz` files built from the `sample1_scan4` MR series in the REST suite's data cache. Each holds 30 images with new Study, Series and SOP Instance UIDs and a unique patient, so each upload is a separate session. A 4–16 KB text sidecar comes before each image, so the importer has to skip the unread rest of every sidecar.
- **Uploads:** `POST /data/services/import?import-handler=DICOM-zip&Ignore-Unparsable=true&dest=/prearchive/projects/CONC`, with site-wide anonymization disabled so that XNAT stores the files unchanged. One sequential control upload, then three waves of 8 concurrent uploads.
- **Check:** every stored file in the prearchive compared by MD5 against the bytes in the archive.

| Build | Control (sequential) | Concurrent uploads fully intact | Concurrent files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `develop` (commons-compress 1.26.0) | 30/30 intact | **0/24**, all returned HTTP 200 | 563/720 intact, **156 altered, 1 missing** |
| this PR (commons-compress 1.26.1) | 30/30 intact | **24/24** | **720/720 intact** |

On `develop`, nothing reported the corruption: every upload returned 200, and the server logs had no "corrupt", "truncated", `ZipException` or `EOFException` lines. In one altered file I examined (`upload_01/IMG-4.dcm`), 23 bytes differed, all inside the Siemens CSA private elements: 4 bytes in `(0029,1010)` and 19 in `(0029,1020)`. The file still parsed, and its size and pixel data were unchanged. The sequential control came through byte-identical on both builds, which shows the MD5 comparison is a valid check.

### Gaps
- One run of 24 concurrent uploads per build. `develop` corrupted every one of its 24 uploads, so the difference is clear, but this is not a soak test.
- Only the import-service path (`/data/services/import`) was exercised. The Compressed Uploader page posts to the same importer, but I did not drive it through the UI.
- The full xnat-web unit-test suite was not run against commons-io 2.22.0. Only the new test was run, plus the REST suite above.

## Note for reviewers
- **The commons-io bump isn't needed for this fix.** The test passes with commons-compress 1.26.1 alone (row 2 above). If you'd rather keep this PR to the minimum change, the commons-io line can be dropped.
- Upgrading commons-compress past 1.26.1 would need a newer commons-lang3 than xnat-web currently forces, so that is left out of scope.

body:
### What are the relevant tickets?
N/A. Platform side: mitodl/ol-data-platform#3314.

### Description (What does it do?)
The warehouse pull of Open edX content files (#4222) calls `load_course_units(run, [])`, which keeps a run's units less their links to unpublished files. Once `(mitxonline|xpro, content_file)` moves to the pull, an existing run's outline goes stale at its next export and a new run gets no units, so the course profile claims built from a run's units have nothing new to read.

mitodl/ol-data-platform#3314 publishes `integrations__learn__content_file_units`: each MITx Online and xPRO run's units, built by a port of `OlxArchive.units` from the export the run's content files came from, with each unit's keys and relations in lesson order (`content_files` is JSON `[[key, relation], ...]`, `unit_order` is the unit's place in `OlxArchive.units`' list).

- `load_warehouse_content_files` reads the run's rows from the units view after its files, in the same connection. OCW reads no units view.
- `load_run` hands them to `load_course_units` through `transform_unit_rows`, as the archive ETL does after loading an archive's files.
- As in `edx_shared.load_archive_units`, a failure is logged and doesn't hold up the files: a failed units read passes no unit rows, a row that can't be transformed or saved leaves the run's units as they were, and the run's fingerprint is still stored. A run with no unit rows keeps its units, less links to unpublished files.

### How can this be tested?
- `pytest learning_resources/tasks_test.py learning_resources/etl/warehouse_content_files_test.py learning_resources/etl/olx_test.py learning_resources/etl/loaders_test.py` against postgres 15 with the CI env: 779 passed on the first commit. After the second commit, the warehouse content files and units tests (`-k "warehouse_content_files or load_run or unit"`) pass, 70.
- New tests cover unit ordering, a unit dropped for having no published files, replacement of a run's old units, a failed units read, malformed unit rows (non-JSON `content_files`, a null `unit_order` or `title`), and OCW reading no units view.
- On the platform side, the port's units matched this repo's `OlxArchive.units` byte for byte on three production exports (details in mitodl/ol-data-platform#3314). This side has not read the view through StarRocks, since it isn't built yet.

### Additional Context
- Merge after mitodl/ol-data-platform#3314 is merged and the view is built. Until the view exists, a units read fails and is logged, and the files still load.
- Units only change with an export, which also moves the content files' fingerprint, so a run's units are reloaded with its files. A change on the platform to how units are built, with no new export, waits for the run's next export.
- #4264 (colon url_names) changed `olx.py` after the platform port was taken. The platform will follow it in a separate change.

author: vivswan
body:
## What this adds

```text
before: entry -> GET /key/info, /user/daily/activity, /user/info -> toast and dashboard name those paths
after:  entry.usageEndpoints -> GET the entry's paths (defaults where unset) -> toast and dashboard name the paths really called
```

```jsonc
{
  "label": "prod",
  "baseUrl": "https://litellm.example.com",
  "usageEndpoints": { "userInfo": "/customer/info", "dailyActivity": "/customer/daily/activity" }
}
```

## How

- **One resolver,** `usageEndpointPath`, serves the client URLs, the refresh toast, and the dashboard detail lines: no surface names a path the client did not call.
- **A member is a root-relative path:** trimmed, starts with `/`, no `?` or `#`; malformed or unknown members are reported and ignored like `budget` and `mcp`.
- **Only the path moves;** responses keep LiteLLM's shape, absolute URLs are out of scope.
- **Extension-side only:** registered in `ENTRY_VIEW_FIELD_SET` and `SERVER_ENTRY_KEYS`, never in the group args or fingerprint.
- **No form control yet;** a dashboard edit keeps the entry's paths.
- **Library:** searched the repository's `zod`; none fits because the servers parser reports and ignores per member while keeping the entry.

## Proof

- **Tests:** 12 new cases (6 parser, 2 spend client, 2 poller, 1 dashboard, 1 import); 3 URL-builder cases rewritten and the group-args pin extended.
- **Gate:** typecheck, lint, knip, l10n, manifest and docs checks green.

Closes #633

<details>
<summary>Technical details</summary>

- **Moved:** `src/dashboard/usageEndpoints.ts` to `src/shared/usageEndpoints.ts`; `serverEntry.ts` needs the id vocabulary and biome forbids `src/shared` importing any other tree.
- **Export census:** before `USAGE_ENDPOINT_PATHS`, `UsageEndpointId`; after those plus `USAGE_ENDPOINT_IDS`, `isUsageEndpointId`, `UsageEndpointOverrides`, `usageEndpointPath`.
- **Allowlisted:** `**/shared/usageEndpoints` for the webview bundle in `biome.local.jsonc`, beside `serverEntry`.
- **Replaced:** `keyInfoUrl`, `userInfoUrl`, `dailyActivityUrl` by `usageEndpointUrl(endpoint, connection)`.
- **Carried:** `UsageConnection.usageEndpoints` and `UsageServerRefreshOutcome.usageEndpoints` copy the entry's overrides; the dashboard reads `DashboardServer.config.usageEndpoints` through the existing `pickEntryViewFields` ride.
- **Save path:** `applySaveServerSetting` rebuilds the whole entry from the form payload and now copies `usageEndpoints` from the entry the form was showing (edit and rename); the add form's upsert replaces the whole entry as documented.
- **Forgotten on a move:** the store records the paths each standing was probed at, and `applyServersChange` resets a moved endpoint's standing to unknown at once, so with polling off an open dashboard never attributes the old path's answer to the new path.
- **Localized text too:** the spend-denied headline and the Requests fact's not-served reason interpolate the resolved path, and the Servers help names `/key/info` as the default.
- **Refused: a `pattern` in the manifest schema.** The parser trims first; a second statement of the rule would drift.
- **Recorded, not built:** a dashboard form control for the paths; a per-endpoint absolute URL; a settings edit that moves a path while that endpoint's request is in flight with polling off (the returning result lands under the new path until the next refresh).
- **Files:** `src/shared/{usageEndpoints,serverEntry}.ts`, `src/extension/servers/serverSync/setting.ts`, `src/extension/servers/usage/{spendClient,poller,store}.ts`, `src/extension/dashboard/saveServer.ts`, `src/dashboard/viewModels.ts`, `src/webview/dashboard/{serverDiagnostics,serverDrawer}.tsx`, `scripts/dev/manifest/serversEntrySchema.ts`, `package.json` (generated), `package.nls*.json`, `l10n/bundle.l10n*.json`, `biome.local.jsonc`, `docs/{settings,servers,usage}.md` and the zh-cn and zh-tw twins, `ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md`.

</details>
