## What was wrong
Benchmark samples (indicator `unnecessary-hypotheses`) in `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Function/`:
- `uhtr4-13664` (`AEStronglyMeasurable.lean`): `aestronglyMeasurable_iInf_of_antitone` assumed `[BorelSpace β]`; its statement mentions no measurable space on `β` at all (`[MeasurableSpace β]` was only a proof device).
- `uhtr4-13668` (`AEStronglyMeasurable.lean`): `AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_prod_sub` assumed `[MeasurableAdd G]`, which follows from `[MeasurableSub₂ G]`.
- `uhtr5-17041` (`EssSup.lean`): `essSup_sub_essInf_mono_measure` assumed `[(ae ν).NeBot]`.
- `uhtr5-17048` (`Jacobian.lean`): `ContinuousAffineMap.setIntegral_comp_of_image_eq` assumed `hs : MeasurableSet s`.
- `uhtr7-13950` (`Campanato.lean`): `setAverage_norm_sub_setAverage_le_of_holderOnWith` carried `[IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]`.
- `uhtr7-13957` (`Campanato.lean`): `tendsto_setAverage_closedBall_preciseRepresentative_of_setAverage_norm_sub_le` assumed `hf : IntegrableOn f (closedBall x ρ) μ`.

## Evidence
All compile; `AEStronglyMeasurable`, `EssSup`, `Jacobian`, `Campanato`, `FullSimplex`, `KernelPotential`, `TailMeasurability`, `Martingale.Convergence` and `Inhomogeneous` build with zero warnings; lint-style, unused-arguments and dot-notation lints are clean. Junk values (Mathlib convention, as agreed for this swarm) are used in the degenerate cases: for `uhtr5-17041`, if `ae ν = ⊥` then `essSup - essInf = limsup f ⊥ - liminf f ⊥ = 0` and the right side is `≥ 0`; for `uhtr7-13957`, if `f` is integrable on no ball of radius `≤ ρ` about `x`, every average is `0` and so is the precise representative. For `uhtr5-17048` the proof now shows that `T` is injective with `|det| = 1`, hence measure preserving and a measurable embedding with `T ⁻¹' s = s`, so no measurability of `s` is needed. Checked (a) the docstrings (updated where they named a removed hypothesis), (b) the roadmaps (no target depends on the removed hypotheses), (d) the standard reviews (none for these declarations).
Not shipped from the same files (settled in Lean): `hμ` and `[ProperSpace X]` of the Hölder oscillation lemma (without `hμ` an empty ball with `r < 0` gives `0 ≤ K (2r)^α` with a negative right side; properness is used for strong measurability), `[CompleteSpace F]` of `bmoSeminorm_const` (the average is the junk value `0` in an incomplete space), `[NormedSpace ℝ F]` of the BMO/VMO lemmas (needed by the definitions).

## The fix
Removes the hypotheses above (for `uhtr4-13664` the two section variables `[MeasurableSpace β] [BorelSpace β]` go and the proofs use `borelize β`; for `uhtr7-13950` the instance is omitted for this lemma only). Review round 2: `MeasurableSub₂.measurableNeg` and `MeasurableSub₂.measurableAdd` are public lemmas in `MeasureTheory/Group/Measure.lean`, cited by `comp_prod_sub`; `ContinuousAffineMap.measurePreserving_of_abs_det_eq_one` is a public lemma in `Jacobian.lean`, cited by `setIntegral_comp_of_image_eq`; `essSup_sub_essInf_mono_measure` uses `Filter.limsup_eq, Filter.liminf_eq` directly (no private helper); the Hölder lemma reuses `ContinuousOn.integrableOn_of_subset_isCompact`; and the `IntegrableOn` hypothesis is dropped from `tendsto_setAverage_closedBall_restrict_preciseRepresentative_of_setAverage_norm_sub_le` itself (the case split lives there, around a private integrable-case lemma), so the `univ` version is a one-line specialization again. The AEStronglyMeasurable module docstring no longer mentions a Borel σ-algebra. Call sites in `FullSimplex.lean` and the file docstring of `Jacobian.lean` are updated. No declaration deleted or renamed.

Built the changed modules, `Campanato`, `AEStronglyMeasurable`, `FullSimplex` and their importers; lints clean.

Review round 4: `ContinuousAffineMap.coe_eq_add_const_comp_contLinear` is now stated for any continuous affine map `V →ᴬ[R] W` between topological modules (proved from Mathlib's `ContinuousAffineMap.decomp`), outside the real normed section; its two uses are unchanged. author: davesnx
body:
Closes #62.

A path through irregular data needed a `?` on every step, and the result had `null` values that could not be traced to a step. Now one `?` on the step that can be absent is enough.

```bash
# users: alice has no metadata; bob's preferences are ["dark_mode", {"notifications": {"email": ...}}]
query-json '.users[].metadata?.preferences[].notifications?.email'
# null                 <- alice: no metadata
# "bob@example.com"
```

- `?` skips the rest of the path when its step gives `null`, like `?.` in JavaScript. `{} | .a?.b.c` gives `null`. The path ends at `|`, `,`, an operator, `??` or a closing bracket, so `(.a?).b` and `.a? | .b` still fail.
- Steps without `?` stay strict: `{"a": {}} | .a?.b` is still `key_not_found`.
- `?` and `try` without `catch` give no output on a type mismatch, as jq does: `"x" | .a?`, `1 | .[]?`, `123 | keys?`. An absent value still gives `null`: a missing key, a key or an index on `null`, an index out of bounds, `first?` on `[]`.
- `?` and `try` without `catch` no longer hide an undefined function: `foo?` reports the error.
- `.[1:2]?` parses without parentheses. A slice on `null` or a number is an error; it used to stop with an OCaml `Assertion failed`.
- `path(.a?.b.c)` and `.a?.b.c |= 9` now work for paths of three or more steps, as the two-step forms already did.

`Optional` in the AST now holds the step and the rest of its path; a plain `?` has `Identity` as the rest. The interpreter runs the rest outside the error handler, so only the marked step is forgiven. `Runtime_error.when_caught` is the one place that maps an error kind to `null`, no output, or propagation.

Differences from jq, on the issue's data:

| Query | `main` (2c08a49) | This branch (fbe6d6f) | jq 1.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.users[].metadata?.preferences?[]?.notifications?.email?` | `null`, `null`, `"bob@example.com"` | `null`, `"bob@example.com"` | `"bob@example.com"` |
| `.users[].metadata?.preferences[].notifications?.email` | error `null_access` | `null`, `"bob@example.com"` | error: cannot iterate over null |
| `... \| values` after either query | | `"bob@example.com"` | |

The proposal in #62 to skip missing values by default is not taken: plain access stays strict, which also covers the proposed `!`.

Checked at fbe6d6f with `dune test --force --root .`: 867 runtime and parser tests and 103 reader tests pass. Each commit's new tests were run against its parent first and failed there.

**Risk:** two-way door for the code; a revert restores the old `?`. It is a breaking language change for users: queries that relied on `?` giving `null` for a type mismatch, or on a `null` flowing into the next step after `?`, give different output. `CHANGES.md` and `docs/JQ_COMPATIBILITY.md` describe it.

Adds a host-clock stereo mixer with bounded ring buffers, drift correction, gain/mute/delay/meters, soft clipping, a timer driver, and AAC-LC encoding with priming-correct timestamps. Synthetic tests cover conversion, ten-second alignment, three 120-second drift/arrival simulations, interruptions, ring wrap, two-source mixing, performance, five-second driving, and AAC decode/phase/frequency/frame-count validation.

Stacked on foundation PR https://github.com/talkaboutdesign/elgato-hdr/pull/3 (rebased onto `893136b`). Base is `main` as requested; merge foundation first. Step 5 is complete: nil-by-default game and microphone taps, including demo mic, with mic start-to-last-sample conversion. Existing playback and recording calls are preserved. No live renderer changes. Temporary package and clock/log stub were removed and never committed. No third-party dependencies, hardware capture, or permission prompts.

Acceptance and limitations:
- Real package `swift build` and `swift test` pass. Default suite skips only the opt-in realtime test; it passed separately and is enabled in the final run below.
- Isolated release suite passes, with two-input rendering at 0.006057 ms/block (<0.2 ms). Full real-package release tests fail to compile in foundation's `ExportTests` because `FixtureProject` is DEBUG-only. Left outside-owned files unchanged; failure excerpt below.
- Bundled demo ran 30 seconds before and after hooks with `--demo-source --demo-camera`; both processes were deliberately terminated with SIGTERM (exit -15). Backlogs remain 130–140 ms; both finish the logged window at 38 cumulative drops. Foundation's four recording/export tests pass. No real-device tests were attempted.
- Driver uses a serial Dispatch queue and DispatchSourceTimer (10 ms / 1 ms leeway). Input locks cover bounded copies and scalar metadata; interpolation and metering happen outside the capture lock. Render/push storage is preallocated. Hooks are configured before capture starts and callbacks must return promptly.

author: kirkmarple-clockgrove
body:
Closes #182

## Cause

`world.advance` builds one environment run per call (`buildRun` → `createEnvironmentRun`) and seeds each source's appearance system and each perishable's spoilage system from the holder contents at the call's start. When a decision (or a routine mover's arrival) consumed from a holder inside the call, `refreshRun` re-seeded only the actors' exposure and wellbeing states. The holder systems kept the stale quantity, so a water source drunk dry mid-call still looked full to its appearance schedule. Its due appearances were skipped until a later call, or a lifecycle change, rebuilt the run. Live steps rebuild the run at every step boundary, so live and fast-forward progressions diverged. Perishable food hid it because it spoils at the next appearance instant anyway.

## Fix

- `EnvironmentReseed` takes optional `holders` (`packages/kernel/src/systems/environment/run.ts:173`). `reseed` replaces the spoilage and appearance states of those holders at the run's position (`run.ts:559`). Growth states are untouched.
- `refreshRun` passes every source and perishable holder's journaled contents, arrival and lifecycle (`packages/kernel/src/world.ts:1348`, helper `ecologyHolders` at `:2906`, shared with `ecologyRunOptions`). `refreshRun` already runs at the instant a consumption is journaled: after a decision's plan (`:2100`) and after an arrival restart (`:1977`). So the appearance schedule sees the change at that instant. Nothing is water-specific: any source whose holder empties, and any perishable consumed to zero, is covered.
- Where nothing was consumed, the journal equals the engine state at those points, so the re-seed changes nothing. No golden changed.
- Contract: `packages/kernel/docs/ecology.md` ("Food and water", and the evidence line under `material-ecology`).

## Acceptance

| Point | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| A source drunk dry by a decision appears at its next due instant inside the same advance call | `worlds/fixture/reference/long-runs/long-run-one-year.json` now walks `fixture.companion` to `garden-edge` (the water bowl) at day 101 (`movement.start`, same step in both runs). Its decisions drink the bowl's 3 units at 8812800000, 8899200000 and 8985600000. The next due time is 9007200000 (`firstAtMs` 8661600000 + 4 × 86400000). New assertions in both runs: `*-bowl-drunk-dry-by-decisions` (3 consumptions in [8661600000, 8985600000]) and `*-bowl-refills-at-next-due` (1 appearance in [8985600000, 9007200000]). **After:** both pass in `main` (live daily steps) and `aggregate` (fast-forward). **Before** (same document against `origin/main`'s kernel): `aggregate-bowl-refills-at-next-due` fails. The aggregate bowl refilled only at 9612000000, 7 days late, then at 10821600000 (full-recording trace of the same document on `origin/main`). |
| Live small steps and one aggregate fast-forward give identical state, and replay matches | The one-year document's `small-step-vs-aggregate` equivalence now also compares `resource.spoiled`, `resource.appeared` and `resource.consumed` events by type, time and payload, beside `finalState`. **After:** `declared-equivalence` passed, along with all 11 long-run checks and every scenario assertion, including `replay-matches` and `aggregate-replay-matches`. **Before:** `small-step-vs-aggregate differs in events, finalState`. |
| The case sits in the equivalence the long-run qualification uses | It is the fixture-hall one-year run of `pnpm run qualify:wave1:long-runs`. Run locally through `qualifyLongRuns` on Node and workerd, the bundles were byte-identical (`sha256:f55ede13…5a8e`) and within budget: Node 67.1 s / 406 MiB of 134.4 s / 760 MiB, workerd 65.2 s / 289 MiB of 127.2 s / 524 MiB. |
| Goldens change only through review, each explained | None changed. Simulator conformance goldens (`test:long-run`, Node and workerd) and the kernel `test:long-run` evidence with its committed ecology and food goldens all match. |
| Version bumps | None. No precondition or invariant check changed behaviour. `ECOLOGY_SYSTEM_VERSION` stays 1 because the systems' own arithmetic is unchanged. Only the advance loop's re-seed points now carry the holders. |

**Why the one-year document, not the 30-day one.** `tests/ci/qualify-wave1-long-runs.test.mjs` (per-PR) cuts the 30-day document by rewriting `steps[0]`, so that document must stay single-step.

**Pre-existing, unrelated failure.** `packages/simulator/test/cli/pack.long-run.test.ts` expects 11 reference scenarios but finds 13. It fails identically on `origin/main`. This PR doesn't touch it.

## Checks run

`pnpm check` (test budget: 0 net test lines vs 39 added production lines), `pnpm format`, kernel `test` and `test:long-run`, simulator `test` and `test:long-run` (apart from the pre-existing failure above), `pnpm test:replay`, and the one-year qualification run on both runtimes as above.

## Design checklist

1. **Authority.** No new command, event, grant or check. `resource.appeared` still comes only from the engine's appearance groups (`world.ts` `emitGroup`), and its guard that the holder is empty at the instant is unchanged.
2. **Growth and retention.** No new state, rows or queues. The re-seed replaces existing in-memory system states one-for-one.
3. **Identity and attribution.** Unchanged. Appearances keep the advance's attribution envelope and their time.
4. **Hot-path cost.** One `ecologyHolders` per `refreshRun`, which runs once per material decision or arrival restart: O(entities + holders) with maps. That is the same order as `refreshRun`'s existing entity scan for movers. Worlds without ecology pay nothing. The one-year run's wall time stayed within its budget.
5. **Test independence.** Expected times come from the pack policy (`firstAtMs`, `periodMs`, the bowl's `quantity` 3) and the live run. Two independent progressions (live daily steps, one fast-forward chain) are compared with each other, and replay is checked in both. The negative control runs the same document on `origin/main`.
6. **Sourced numbers.** 8661600000 is the bowl's `firstAtMs`. 9007200000 is `firstAtMs` + 4 × `periodMs`. 8726400000 is day 101, the clock epoch 8640000000 plus one day. 8985600000 is the third drink, from the recorded run.

## Determinism re-read

The holder list is in policy order (Set of source and perishable ids, as before), and lookups go through maps, so nothing is iterated in Map order for output. No random stream is drawn and no event order changes: the same groups are emitted, and only a stale holder state is replaced. No check is weakened, and the long-run equivalence compares more event types than before.

author: buluoray
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** An app cannot approve its own permissions or turn itself back on after the owner disables it.

Two owner decisions were read from files in the app's own directory, `apps/<name>/`, which code in the app's sandbox can write:

1. `approved-grants.json`: which declared `permissions.api`, `permissions.events` and point-family entries the owner approved. The `approvedGrantsStored` flag that decides how a missing file reads is in `installed.json`, the same tree.
2. `installed.json`'s `enabled` flag, which `is_app_enabled` and every permission check built on it trust (chat control, worker auto-approve, WebSocket events, jobs, notifications, agent tools, app frames).

## Why it matters

A disabled or partly approved app keeps whatever it can write for itself: entries a widening update held back, or its whole surface after the owner turned it off. The owner's disable and approval prompts are the controls for an app that misbehaves.

## Not a goal

- Changing what any permission grants, or the approval UI.
- The `bots` family and the ticked-Bot list from #32983, which keeps its own records under the same store; once both land, its scopes file can become the `bots` family here.
- The app-token cutoff from #34095; it reads `installed.json` and can move into this store as a follow-up.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Both decisions move to `member-records/`, the directory the sandbox masks in every mode and the agent file tools refuse, following #32983's `app-bot-grants` record.

| Part | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/protected_app_state.py` | New store: `app-grants/<app>.json` (the approved set) and `app-disabled/<app>` (the owner's disable), containment-checked. |
| `member_records.py` | Two new record kinds; only the original three are moved from `trust/`. |
| `apps/manager_records.py` | The approved set is read and written only in the store. A one-time import carries each app's existing set over, keeps a record from before sets were stored approving what it declares, then never reads the app tree again; app-tree files are read no-follow, non-blocking, regular files only. The import holds a file lock from its marker check to its marker write, and every store writer runs it first. `_read_installed` reports an app disabled while its disable record exists, and a write that turns an enabled record off creates it. |
| `apps/manager_activation.py` | `disable_app` records the disable first and fails if it cannot; only `enable_app` ends it. |
| `apps/manager_lookup.py` | `app_enabled_state` honours the disable record. |
| `apps/manager_install.py`, `apps/manager_external.py` | A failed update or re-registration restores the stored set and the disable record exactly; a registration with no manifest yet approves what is declared, as before. |
| `apps/manager_uninstall.py`, `apps/manager.py` | Uninstall removes both records and puts them back if the uninstall fails; the facade names the new helpers for type checkers. |
| `apps/manager_install.py`, `apps/manager_builtins.py` | An update that turns an enabled app off records the disable before its tree swap. A new builtin record is stored as approving what it declares. |
| docs | `app-kit-platform.md` §13 and `app-platform-trust-model.md` describe the store, the import and the disable record. |

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: on upgrade the import keeps every app's approvals as they were, including "approve what is declared" for records from before sets were stored, and every enabled app stays enabled. An app disabled on disk stays disabled.

Reader: apps/manager_records.py:staged_app_grants -- app -- reads the store instead of the app tree; `test_app_staged_grants.py`
Reader: apps/manager_lookup.py:is_app_enabled -- app -- reports disabled while the disable record exists; `test_a_rewritten_record_does_not_turn_a_disabled_app_back_on`
Reader: apps/session_consent.py:reconcile_after_ready -- release -- its disable now also writes the record, ended by the owner's consent through `enable_app`; `test_app_session_approval_preconsent.py`

## Tests

- `test/test_protected_app_state.py`: both records sit under the masked `member-records/`; a set the app writes in its tree, or clearing `approvedGrantsStored`, approves nothing; a missing store record approves nothing; the import carries a set over once and ignores a later app-tree file, keeps a legacy record approving what it declares, and reads a lost set as nothing; a FIFO planted as the legacy set neither blocks (30 s bound) nor approves; a rewritten `installed.json` does not turn a disabled app back on; the owner's enable ends the disable; uninstall removes both records; a failed uninstall keeps both; an update held off for consent records the disable; a builtin registered after the import approves what it declares; the import holds its lock until the marker is written; a lost or damaged legacy set imports as nothing in every family; a removal of the two records that stops halfway puts them back. A disable running during a failed uninstall keeps its record; the import carries a disable from before the upgrade over, and leaves a built-in owed its default-on promotion alone.
- Determinism: 20/20 at `-n0`, 10/10 at `-n 4` beside `test_app_staged_grants.py` and `test_member_records.py`, green in a shuffled order.
- `test_app_staged_grants.py`, `test_apps_worker_auto_approve.py` and `test_member_records.py` updated to the store location; `test_member_records.py` pins that the new kinds are never moved from `trust/`.
- Every app manager, staged-grant, enable/disable and facade test file (118 files): 6,054 passed. 2 errors in `test_auto_research_http.py` and `test_auto_research_watchdog.py` error the same way on main.

Proof: not provable -- other: the tests import the new store module, so reverting production hunks fails collection; hand mutations instead: removing the disable check in `_read_installed` fails 2 tests, reading the set from the app tree fails 2 tests

## Manual verification

N/A — the tests drive the real install, enable, disable, update and uninstall paths against an isolated data home.

## Related Issues

Related: #34095 (an app token stops at disable; its cutoff can move into this store), #34107 (app-sent messages are labelled), #32983 (the same protected store for Bot access).

## Sibling sweep

Swept: git grep -nE "is_app_enabled\(|_read_installed\(|approved-grants" -- src/
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/apps/host_exec_grants.py -- not affected -- already keeps its grant in a sealed top-level directory
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/apps/manager_lookup.py -- changed here

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: an authorization decision read from a file under the app's own sandbox-writable directory

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

## Contribution License Agreement

Contributed under the project's Apache-2.0 license.

author: kueda
body:
Main thing here is for observ.ing to just leave along any properties on the occurrence record it doesn't recognize. My specific problem was that it was removing eventID and surveyTargetID which cuanto.bio adds to the record. They're not lexicon properties, but they are DwC terms and they shouldn't do any harm on observ.ing.

Claude's summary:

> Editing an occurrence rebuilt the PDS record from the form, deleting every field observ.ing doesn't model (e.g. cuanto.bio's eventID) and resetting createdAt to the edit time. It also read retained media refs from the pre-#600 `associatedMedia` key, so on current records (`media`) every edit dropped the photos the user kept.
> 
> - Apply the edit on top of the existing record: replace only the fields the form owns, keep everything else and the original createdAt.
> - Read existing media refs from `media`, falling back to `associatedMedia`, and drop the legacy key once `media` is written.
> - Swap putRecord on the fetched CID so a change made mid-edit fails with a 409 instead of being overwritten.
> - Clear taxonID/acceptedIdentificationID when the edit adds an identification for a different taxon.

Fixes #1025

body:
Makes the site easier to use on a phone, since guests open the menus from the table QR code, and brings the menus up to date with the October 2026 printed AYCE menus.

## Menus
- **New AYCE menu:** one All You Can Eat menu in three tiers (Signature, Premium, Supreme), replacing the separate lunch and dinner AYCE menus. Signature (the old lunch list, now all day) is $29.95 at Alki and $27.95 in Kent. Premium and Supreme prices are unchanged. Supreme adds 5 new appetizers.
- **Easier to read:** each section is a text list like the printed menu, with 2 or 3 dish photos beside it (above it on phones). Photos come from the client's Drive folder, cut-outs at 320px WebP (about 1.5MB total).
- **No more bouncing:** the section tabs moved the whole page while you scrolled on phones. Tapping a tab now lands right under the tab bar, and the active tab follows your scroll.
- **Tighter on phones:** smaller header, no Reserve bar (guests are already seated), combo prices stacked as Small / Large, and internal transcriber notes no longer shown to guests.

## Home page
- Video hero from the earlier Vercel version, with the meat-name ticker.
- New "Or Order À La Carte" section (combos, meats by the plate, apps & entrées, lunch & bento) with "from" prices read from the menus.
- The price board, FAQ, location pages and copy now use the three tiers.
- Happy hour uses real photos of the bites and cocktails, and the neon palms from the printed menu.
- Location cards list their hours instead of an "Hours" button.

## Nav
- "Menus" no longer sits higher than the other links on desktop.
- The phone menu was trapped inside the 72px header bar (the header's blur effect contains fixed children). It now sits outside the header and fills the screen.

## Private events
- New "The 2nd Floor Is Yours" section: the Alki second floor for company dinners, birthdays, holiday parties and large groups. Up to 40 guests, 7 days a week. The request form now defaults to "2nd floor".

## Alki winter hours
- Mon–Thu 3–9 PM, Fri 3–10 PM, Sat–Sun 11 AM–10 PM, in `locations.json`.
- **Also update these in the Apnosh portal.** With `APNOSH_SLUG` set, the live site takes Alki's hours from the portal.
- The printed happy hour (2–5 PM) and weekday lunch specials (11 AM–4 PM) don't fit the new weekday opening time. They're left as printed until the menus are updated.

## Not changed
- The happy hour menu, drinks, à la carte, apps & entrées and bento menus keep their current items and prices.
- A few à la carte items still have no photo: spicy pork belly, marinated chicken thigh, head-on prawn, seafood medley.

body:
## Scope

Prepare AlphaCOGANT 1.3.0 as a standalone research-package release. The fixed model remains synthetic; no corporate-performance, learned-coefficient, temporal-authentication or deployment-gating claim is added.

- Preserve small-precision policy mass across overflowing score gaps.
- Standardize overflowing/inexact paired margins without false constant margins, erased subnormal means or premature rounding of the squared statistic.
- Admit integer/list coefficients into canonical float storage while preserving coefficient values, axes, shared-array writeability and detached belief priors.
- Mark wall timing unavailable under detected caller instrumentation without disturbing that instrumentation.
- Reject unrepresentable trajectory aggregates at the first offending cycle, including externally assembled summaries.
- Add a thin contained PDF/HTML producer with source/version/saved-artifact preflight, per-label PNG identity, alt/anchor checks, diagnostic retention and source/runtime/tool/font receipts. This trusted local script adds no agent execution capability.
- Synchronize 1.3.0 package, lock, runtime, citation, CodeMeta, archival and manuscript identities; update modular contracts and remove incidental wording/inventory tests rather than repinning them.

Dependabot PR #3 is integrated by its reviewed commit ancestry, not by replacing its branch. Preserve that ancestry when merging this PR.

## Actually exercised locally

Python 3.15.2 / NumPy 2.5.4, offline qualified execution:

- Locked dev provisioning and Ruff passed.
- Full real-computation suite: **493 passed, one explicitly optional upstream skip; 93.73% coverage**, retaining the >=90% gate.
- Required documentation/render-boundary subset: **24 passed**.
- Independent real API before/after probes verify the five reproduced boundary defects, including exact two-pair arithmetic and preservation of caller tracing.
- Model CLI validation and doctor passed; the demo and all **16** figure producers ran.
- **36** tokens generated/used, **zero** orphans; saved-artifact non-writing validation passed.
- Wheel and sdist built; the wheel installed into a separate environment. The local installed smoke initially had a throwaway caller argument error; its corrected retry was refused before launch during maintenance, not accepted as a pass.
- All 16 fresh registered PNGs and the separate demo were visually inspected. Static documentation checks resolved 131 local links and 16 generated image targets across 44 Markdown sources; 16 external links were not network-certified by that check.

## Merge acceptance still required

- Green supported-minor CI (3.11–3.15), real pinned COGANT coefficient/Bayes/transition integration, and the independently installed wheel console/JSONL/overflow-recovery smoke.
- Actual source-owned PDF/HTML rendering, repeated generated-byte and PDF-page-pixel comparisons, and the unresolved-citation negative scenario without a success receipt.
- Human inspection of actual current-version PDF pages and HTML equations, tables, captions, every figure and bibliography. PNG inspection and successful compilation alone are not publication approval.

Local native render and corrected installed-smoke attempts have been deferred by inherited maintenance admission; no deferred or unrun result is labeled green. The hosted standalone workflow contains the remaining real acceptance paths. Main, annotated tag and release publication remain separate post-acceptance steps.

author: pedrochagasmaster
body:
## Summary

An imported 6-8 range now survives Create custom and an explicit repetition measurement. Pending ranges live in a separate device record keyed by setup draft and slot, bound to the movement identity.

```text
import -> device-only pending ranges + unchanged setup candidate
explicit Reps -> canonical targets, consumed pending hint
activation -> canonical program + exact setup receipt, device hints removed
```

Fixes #669. This addresses revision findings R1 and R2 from `review-pr735-739.md.report`. #735 is accepted and untouched. Base `349054ab156ffe8dc8fc49565cfa427b8ef6be9d`, integration/coach-layer. Assigned revision v716 is retained.

## Acceptance contract

`repforge_import_ranges_v1` holds optional device-only hints with `schemaVersion`, `draftId` and slot-keyed `ranges`. Each entry binds `exerciseId` to bounded integer `min`/`max`. The editor reads only matching import drafts, surviving custom slots and movements without a repetition measurement. Malformed and unrelated hints are ignored without rejecting the setup. Successful setup writes prune consumed, deleted or replaced hints under the existing setup lock. Failed setup writes do not consume them. Setup removal clears the matching device record.

The validated setup-candidate shape is unchanged from the base. Pending hints never enter canonical targets until Reps is chosen, custom movement identity, program data, logs, backups, setup links or telemetry. The exact-byte activation receipt and its crash recovery protocol remain unchanged. They contain no pending hints because the candidate contains none.

| Requirement | Real producer and consumer | Proof in `verifyImportedRepRanges` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1: previous release keeps and resumes the draft | Current import/save -> base release's complete shell and assets -> real Resume control/editor | Pending device record and unchanged control both resume |
| R2: recovery exports exclude pending hints | Duration activation -> damaged IndexedDB -> visible Copy A download | Actual downloaded JSON contains no pending metadata, including receipt bytes |
| Preserve crash recovery | Restore exact captured setup after commit, damage other replica, choose recovery copy | Both replicas retain configured targets; boot removes matching setup and hints |
| Preserve two distinct ranges | Create custom -> explicit Reps -> canonical sets/cycles | Source slots retain 6-8 and 10-14 through save/reload and activation |
| Validate the device boundary | Malformed bounds/shapes, unknown slot, foreign draft/movement -> actual boot/resume/editor | Setup resumes and uses normal 6-10 rather than the invalid hint |
| Keep non-repetition targets separate | Duration selection | No reps target or flat min/max; source pending hint stays separate until activation |
| Mid-setup transfer accepts or drops truthfully | Real transfer builder, client claim/vault and production import hook | Configured 6-8 travels; device-only pending hints are omitted; destination resumes and uses normal 6-10 when Reps is later chosen |
| Publish both replicas and remove hints | Production activation | LocalStorage and IndexedDB contain the configured targets; setup and sidecar removed |

## Evidence

Original red proof: commit `9f675c930`, imported 6-8 became `min:6,max:10`.

Revision red proof: commit `a5ff57c8f`.

## Done, left, next

Implemented R1/R2 and retained the original import correction. Focused proof passed on the recorded clean head. Local proof is composed into the existing import owner; no suite command or inventory changed. Remote ci/ci-full, rendered catalog frames and independent correction review remain coordinator gates. No merge, deployment or CI retry was performed.

Decision: the revision brief supersedes the previous candidate-field design. Install transfer intentionally drops unconfigured device-only hints, which the approved transfer requirement permits. ## What and why

Fixes #14250.

`native_player_logged_out` fires for every way a player leaves but does not say why. Diagnostics and moderation mods need to tell a lost connection, a kick, a timeout, a server stop and a failed connection apart.

- New listen-only hook `player_logged_out_v2(player, name, reason)`, with `reason: NativeQuitReason { Disconnected, Kicked(String), TimedOut, ServerStopping, Error(String) }`. v1 keeps firing unchanged.

body:
Implements plan 11: a dependency-free RTMP/RTMPS publisher for already-encoded H.264 and AAC. It waits for Publish.Start, sends metadata and codec configurations, starts on an IDR, resets timestamps on reconnect, drops video under pressure, and retries transport failures while treating authentication failures as terminal. Statistics use confirmed bytes and a three-second throughput window; errors and logs redact the supplied key.

**Stack dependency:** this PR sits on top of plan 00 PR https://github.com/talkaboutdesign/elgato-hdr/pull/3 (foundation commit 893136b). The requested base is main. Plan 11 itself changes only the ten files under Sources/StudioKit/Streaming/RTMP/ and Tests/StudioKitTests/RTMP/. Foundation changes appear in the main-based diff until plan 00 merges.

Tests cover byte-exact AMF0/connect commands, all chunk header formats, split input, extended timestamps, interleaving and chunk-size changes, FLV payloads, endpoints, loopback handshakes and publish ordering, ping/acknowledgements, stop commands, authentication failure/redaction, socket reconnects, stalled-reader dropping/recovery, and real VideoToolbox H.264 plus AVAudioConverter AAC sent to ffmpeg for five seconds.

Deviations and skips:
- ffprobe does not expose per-stream duration for FLV. The integration test adds -show_packets and -show_format to -show_streams and derives each stream duration from packet timestamps and durations, with the requested 0.3-second tolerance.
- Added defensive malformed-control/Abort handling and extended chunk stream IDs.
- The first connect golden fixture had an incorrect flashVer string length (30 instead of 32); the first test run failed, the fixture was corrected, and subsequent runs pass. The original output is preserved below.
- The integration test is skipped in ordinary swift test because RTMP_FFMPEG_TEST is not set; it ran and passed separately with that flag.
- Removed the uncommitted temporary Package.swift and logging stub before rebasing onto plan 00. No temporary support files are committed.
- No live render path changes; latency comparison is not applicable. RTMPS uses Network.framework TLS with default certificate verification; no live platform credentials or external TLS ingest were used.

body:
Resolves #1552

A Start refused before spawn, such as a Codex Desktop Start whose capability probe refuses the installed build, leaves a record with no process and no `runtimeStart`. `handoffRuntimeCustody` read that record as a legacy seat and refused the whole continuity handoff. The 2026-11-09 FM update therefore exited unclean, and the running seats recovered `stale`.

`verifySeats` now passes over a record that claims no process: no pid, no child handle, not adopted, and no unresolved ownership or cleanup. A seat that does claim a process without a generation-bound Start still refuses, as #1166 pinned.

Evidence: L2 (CI: unit specs drive the real `publishUnavailable` writer and the real handoff) → L3 required (AC-3: an installed FM update). Residual: AC-3, Residual-Owner: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#732.

|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI: `FleetLifecycleService.spec.mjs` › a record that a refused Start left holds no process: the handoff passes it over and seals for the running seat |
| AC-2 | CI: › a seat without a generation-bound Start still refuses the whole handoff, and the refusal revokes nothing (unchanged). The new row › a held seat without a generation-bound Start … keeps a `failed` label from passing a seat over. |

La pagina aperta dal QR mostrava sempre testi italiani. La revisione 0.6.0-beta.3 sceglie italiano o inglese dalle preferenze `Accept-Language` del browser, anche senza JavaScript. Gestisce varianti come it-IT/en-US/en-GB, priorità q e ordine dichiarato; usa inglese quando non trova una lingua supportata e conserva italiano se l’header è assente/vuoto.

Il catalogo in `guest_i18n.py` copre titolo, istruzioni, codice, pulsante, assistenza, conferma ed errori attesi 400/403/404/429/503. La pagina usa testi rivolti all’ospite: «Inserisci il codice di accesso ricevuto dalla struttura» / «Enter the access code provided by the property». Il successo indica «Richiesta inviata» / «Request sent» senza affermare uno sblocco fisico confermato. Nomi delle porte e marchio rimangono invariati; il pannello gestore conserva la lingua attuale.

La lingua viene scelta lato server da un parser con limiti di dimensione/numero voci. Le risposte impostano Content-Language, Vary: Accept-Language e html lang coerenti. Restano no-store, CSP senza script, Referrer-Policy strict-origin, Origin/Fetch Metadata, form CSRF monouso, status HTTP, limiti tentativi e rifiuto dei replay. Gli errori localizzati mantengono il tipo di eccezione e non espongono dettagli interni. Nessun servizio esterno di traduzione, cookie, parametro di form aggiunto o modifica a URL/token/permessi/archivio.

author: joaquin-p-olivera
body:
Dos cosas sobre cómo habla Tox en un grupo, las dos salidas de medir lo que hace y no de suponerlo.

## Dos largos de respuesta en vez de uno

`CLAUDE_MAX_ANSWER_CHARS` (800) se pedía y se cortaba igual en los dos modos, que no son el mismo trabajo. Ahora el modo admin mantiene sus 800 y el modo chat tiene `CLAUDE_PUBLIC_MAX_ANSWER_CHARS` (200), con `answer_limit()` como único lugar que sabe cuál aplica: el número que se le pide al modelo y el número con el que se corta el texto no pueden quedar desfasados.

El prompt del chat pide ahora **una o dos frases** y prohíbe el preámbulo y el resumen de cierre. Un conteo de caracteres es una señal floja para un modelo: la redacción anterior se leía como objetivo y la mediana real quedaba en 250 caracteres.

Un chat puede acortar el suyo con `!config largo`; el límite del modo admin **no** es configurable desde un grupo, a propósito — cuánto puede informar una consulta con acceso a la PC no se decide desde el chat. Hay un test que lo fija.

El comentario que Tox tira por su cuenta es de una sola frase, y se fue la contradicción que arrastraba: el system prompt decía 800 mientras la nota del interject decía "menos de 200".

## Qué cuenta como digno de recordar

En dos semanas el bloque de memoria volvió en 285 respuestas y dijo "nada" en 265, con **cero** fallas de parseo, **cero** respuestas sin el bloque y **cero** notas tiradas por un nombre que no resolvía. O sea: el mecanismo estaba sano y el embudo era la política.

El prompt le decía al modelo, con esas palabras, que no aprender nada *"es lo más común"*. Obedeció. Ese sesgo salió; "durable" pasó a ser una prueba aplicable (si en una semana ya no significa nada, no lo guardes); y ahora dice explícitamente que lo que el grupo dice **sobre** alguien es una nota de ese alguien — que es de lo que trataban casi todas las notas que sí entraron: el que recibe la carga, no el que pregunta.

Las líneas de log `MEMORY` dicen ahora si la respuesta tenía la conversación a la vista o solo la pregunta, porque son apuestas distintas y contarlas juntas es lo que hacía ilegible el rendimiento. Las respuestas sin conversación detrás se siguen pidiendo igual: una pregunta puede traer un dato de quien la hizo, y para un admin —cuyas preguntas son casi todas en el modo de acceso completo— es la única vía por la que se aprende algo de él. Hay un test que lo dice, y es lo que me frenó de "optimizar" eso.

## De paso

El README afirmaba que solo el modo sin acceso aprende. El código nunca hizo eso: el nivel de acceso no tiene nada que ver, como el módulo documentó siempre. Corregido.

## Verificación

- Suite completa: **930 passed** (sin `test_remote_browser.py`, como siempre)
- 3 tests nuevos para los dos largos y el `!config largo`, 1 extendido para la fuente en el log
- `.env` no define ninguno de los dos límites, así que los defaults nuevos aplican al reiniciar

## Phase 4 implementation

- Adds `books-queue/` and a safe Python discovery job that emits a dynamic GitHub Actions `strategy.matrix`.
- Serializes matrix work (`max-parallel: 1`) and bounds artifact retention to 14 days to conserve Actions minutes.
- Adds ImageMagick `identify` pixel-dimension validation for the 300-DPI cover raster proof, derived from each manifest's KDP profile and page count.
- Adds official W3C EPUBCheck 5.4.0 with SHA-256 verification; ERROR/FATAL or a non-zero validator exit blocks publication.
- Adds a gh-pages publish job that runs only on pushes to `main` and depends on all book build and EPUBCheck matrix jobs.
- Adds bounded exponential backoff for transient network failures. The current deterministic swarm has no live model/API client, so no outbound model request is currently wired to it.
- Updates `PROMPT_POLICY.md` with the mandatory GitHub-only/free/low-resource suffix requested for every future ChatGPT prompt prepared for this project.

## Important known limitation

The queue discovery and matrix are dynamic, but the current manuscript adapter and print renderer still use the existing approved 24-page `book.content.PAGES` source and fixed renderer output. The current implementation must therefore be treated as a multi-manifest CI orchestration foundation, **not yet as independent story-content production for arbitrary books**. Parameterizing story loading, content QA and PDF rendering per manifest is required before adding distinct manuscripts.

## Validation

CI will execute from this draft PR. Do not merge until the new matrix workflow passes and the renderer/content-source limitation is resolved or explicitly accepted.

The existing Phase 3 PR remains separate and unchanged.

body:
## What
**Threaded conversations on the to-do list** (rev 7, WP5). As Marc decided, threads are **artist + Blueprint only**.

> Stacked on #70. Merge order: … → #69 → #70 → this. This is the last PR in the rev 7 stack.

## UX
- Open any to-do (BMG Tasks & to-dos, artist workspace, artist phone) and a **Conversation** sits under the edit fields, labelled "You and the artist", "You and Blueprint" or "Blueprint only".
- Comments run in time order with **Reply**, one level deep: a reply to a reply joins the same thread.
- **Remove** your own comment. A BMG admin can remove any. A removed comment stays in place as "Comment removed" so replies still make sense.
- The composer uses the **full emoji picker** from #69, and ⌘/Ctrl+Enter sends.
- The to-do list shows a **💬 count** next to the due date.

## Access
- Anyone who can see the to-do can read and write its thread, via the existing artist-data authz. In practice that's the artist and Blueprint.
- **BMG-only to-dos keep BMG-only threads:** the artist can't open them, and they're never notified.

## Notifications
New `todo.commented` domain event, sent to the API notifier (bell, web push, email, following preferences and quiet hours, throttled per to-do):
- the artist comments → Blueprint people on that artist;
- Blueprint comments → the artist (unless the to-do is BMG-only) plus the rest of Blueprint on that artist;
- the author is never notified. The link opens To-dos (BMG) or To-do (phone).

## API and data
- Routes:
  - `GET /artists/{id}/todos/{todoId}/comments` (thread, nested);
  - `POST /artists/{id}/todos/{todoId}/comments` (`{ text, parentId? }`);
  - `DELETE …/comments/{commentId}`.
- Route count 110 → 113; the API stack is still under the 460 guard.
- Stored next to the to-do as `TODOC#<todoId>#<createdAt>#<id>`. That prefix doesn't match `TODO#`, so to-do list queries are untouched.
- The to-do gets `commentCount` (atomic `ADD`) and `lastCommentAt`.

## Tests
- Thread nesting and ordering, orphaned replies, removed comments hidden, validation, key prefix.
- Notification recipients for an artist author, a BMG author, and BMG-only to-dos.

## Summary
This follows up #212. On the lifting lug, the stresses on the bore stripe along the element edges. The cause is the default stiffness of a `*COMPRESSION ONLY` surface, which is 1e3·E/h. At that stiffness the nine gaps on each quadratic face over-constrain the face.

Results on the lug (2 mm mesh), SXX at the bore:

| default k | corner vs midside node | SXX_max |
|---|---|---|
| 1e3·E/h | up to 3 MPa apart at 12 MPa (stripes) | 31.74 MPa |
| 10·E/h | smooth, monotone | 31.77 MPa |
| 1·E/h | smooth | 32.09 MPa |

A 2×2 rule at the old stiffness made it worse.

- The new default is 10·E/h. Closure is about a tenth of the deformation of one element layer, so the support is still practically rigid.
- The guide and SCHNITTSTELLEN were updated.
- The four `druck-nur-*` fixtures that use the default were re-referenced, and the matrix in FIXTURES.md was regenerated.

author: shuyhere
body:
Part of #2426: the server half. The app half is #2444.

## Problem

Collaboration rooms lived in one process's memory and counted update sequence numbers there, but the server runs as more than one process. Two editors of one document on different processes both wrote the same sequence number; the second insert failed with a duplicate key, that editor was closed with 1011, and its change was neither stored nor shown to the other editor. In a two-editor stress trial this lost one side's text in 5 of 10 runs.

## Change

The stored update log is the shared truth. No migration.

- **Sequence numbers come from the database.** Every append locks the document's `cloud_document_collab` row and takes `max(compacted seq, highest stored seq) + 1`, so writers in different processes cannot collide. This also steps past rows an older server writes during a rolling deploy.
- **Processes relay to each other.** The appending transaction sends `pg_notify('cloud_document_collab', …)`. The existing per-process listener (still one connection) hands it to the room registry, which reads the new rows and passes what the document took to its own sockets. Rooms also catch up on join, when an append finds rows in between, when the listener reconnects, and every 30 seconds.
- **Cursors and presence cross processes** through the same channel, from a bounded queue drained by one task, so a socket never waits on the database to share a cursor. A process that loads a room asks the others for their current awareness.
- **Consistent reads.** Loading and catching up read the compacted state and the later rows in one transaction under `FOR SHARE`; if the rows a room wanted were compacted away, it applies the compacted state.
- **Compaction cannot erase another process's work.** It replaces the stored state only when it covers more than what is stored.
- **A change that cannot be stored is not dropped.** After one retry the room is discarded: every editor is closed with 1013 and reconnects, and y-websocket sends the change again. The registry never hands out a discarded room.
- **A change held back for missing dependencies is stored as received,** so it is not lost when the dependencies arrive from another process.

The wire protocol, tickets, the init grant, the stale flag and close codes 4401/4403/4409 are unchanged. A storage error now closes with 1013 instead of 1011.

## Tests

Run against a local PostgreSQL 17 (`DATABASE_URL` set):

- `cargo test -p kordi-cloud-server collab`: 21 passed
- `cargo test -p kordi-cloud-server --lib document_shares`: 121 passed
- `cargo test -p kordi-cloud-server --lib chat_sync::realtime`: 18 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p kordi-cloud-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

New tests start two server instances on one database, each with its own listener, and connect one editor to each over real sockets:

- both type at once, including the very first edit on both sides, and converge; storage matches; no socket closes
- a writer that finds rows in between catches up with no notification delivered
- a lagging room compacting first, and after another compaction, loses nothing
- catch-up across a compaction applies the compacted state
- a storage failure closes every editor with 1013, the registry hands out a fresh room, and the re-sent change is stored
- awareness set, changed and cleared on one instance reaches the other; an instance ignores its own notifications

Not covered by a test: catch-up on listener reconnect, the awareness queue overflowing, and rows written by an older server during a rolling deploy.

## Rollout

Deployments that were reduced to one API process because of #2426 can go back to several after this ships. During the deploy itself an old and a new process run side by side for a few seconds; the old one still has the bug for that window.

author: kittysoftpaw0510
body:
## Pause the webcam and pipeline while no app uses the virtual camera

**Problem:** once started, vcam captures, mattes and composites every frame even when no app has "OBS Virtual Camera" open, using several cores and keeping the webcam light on all day.

**How it detects use:** every app streaming from the camera holds its own handle to the `OBSVirtualCamVideo` mapping. The OBS DirectShow filter (`virtualcam-filter.cpp`) opens it when capture starts and closes it when the app lets the camera go. So the mapping's handle count, read via `NtQueryObject` (documented in `winternl.h`, a few µs), says whether anyone is watching. No driver changes.

**Behaviour:**
- After Start the webcam runs for 2.5 s, then pauses: webcam off, nothing computed. "OBS Virtual Camera" stays available at the output size, showing black.
- When an app opens the camera, the webcam reopens and the pipeline resumes. It pauses again 2.5 s after the last app lets go.
- While an app waits for the first new frame, the last frame is republished every 100 ms. Otherwise the OBS filter drops and reopens the queue after 10 repeated frames, showing an unwritten picture in between.
- The camera crop editor keeps the webcam on, since it shows the live picture.
- Preview-only mode (no virtual camera) runs as before.
- GUI: "Waiting for your call" and a STANDBY label while paused.

**Tested** on an i7-14700 with ffmpeg as the consumer (`-f dshow -i video="OBS Virtual Camera"`):

| Phase | CPU |
|---|---|
| Paused, no app | 0.0–0.3% of one core |
| App attached | normal pipeline (~30 fps), resumed ~0.2 s after attach |
| App detached | paused again after 2.8 s |

`cargo test` and `cargo clippy` pass with no new warnings.

If the webcam fails while an app wants the output (e.g. Zoom opens the virtual camera before it has released the webcam, giving 0xC00D3704), vcam retries every 500 ms for up to 10 s before failing.

body:
Closes #426.

A part drawing is a single sheet, so projects issuing several sheets together got separate one-page PDFs, each titled **SHEET 1 OF 1**.

## Changes
- **`tertius.drawing.DrawingSet`**: an ordered set of drawings, registered on the compile session (names unique per compile). Drawings join with `Drawing(..., drawing_set=s)` or `s.add(drw)`. A drawing belongs to at most one set.
- **Projection**: each sheet's document carries `set` (`name`, `title`, `number`, `index`, `count`). The title block shows **SHEET n OF m** unless `fields={"sheet_no": ...}` is given. Standalone drawings are unchanged.
- **Drafting build**: stores `drawing_sets` beside `drawings`.
- **PDF**: `render_drawing_set_pdf()` produces one document with a page per sheet, each at its own size (A3 and A4 can be mixed).
- **API**:
  - `GET /api/timus/projects/{name}/drawing-sets`
  - `GET /api/timus/projects/{name}/drawing-sets/{set}.pdf`
  - Same rules as single drawings: 409 on a stale build, 404 for an unknown set (lists the sets), and 422 with the sheet's error if a sheet couldn't be laid out.
  - `/drawings` now reports each drawing's `set`.
- **Docs**: `docs/drafting/part-drawings.md`.

## Testing
- `server/tests/test_part_drawings.py`: 23 passed, 6 of them new:
  - sheet numbering and order
  - one set per drawing, unique set names
  - multi-page PDF with mixed sheet sizes
  - the sandbox records sets
  - set endpoints, including 404/422
  - set endpoints need a current build
- Full backend suite: **1002 passed** (`--ignore=server/tests/gis_cache`, which needs `rasterio` from the GIS image).
- End to end against a real project (`wicking_garden_beds`, three drain auger-hole sheets): one 3-page A3 PDF with title blocks reading 1 OF 3, 2 OF 3 and 3 OF 3.

## Not in this PR
Table entities on sheets. Tables still have to be drawn as geometry.

author: jonataswalker
body:
Agent: claude-opus-5-5 on behalf of Jonatas Walker

Closes #2025. Task T3077, spec #2973.

**In a thread doc, a wheel scroll up from the bottom now finishes, even when lines arrive mid-scroll. Proof: the WebKit stillness check passed 100 of 100 loops with `--trace` at the head ([run 42814636089](https://github.com/kiwi-init/channels/actions/runs/42814636089), artifact `doc-still-trace`).**

## Two causes, one effect

WebKit animates a wheel scroll over about 100-300 ms, and **anything that moves `scrollTop` cancels that animation**, so the view stays near the bottom ("the read never left the bottom: N px below the view").

1. **Our correction write.** An arrival during the animation made `correct()` write `scrollTop`. The arithmetic was right: in the issue's repro it offsets the 52.8 px line and keeps the user's 58 px. The write itself is what cancels the scroll.
2. **The browser's clamp.** The first 100-loop run failed at loop 3. Its trace showed the message window dropping an older row as each new one arrives ("rows +1 −1"). When the dropped row is taller, the list shrinks (24 px in that loop) and the bottom moves above the view. WebKit has no scroll anchoring, so it clamped `scrollTop` to the new bottom ("moved −17 by no write"), which also cancels the animation.

## Fix (`ui/src/chat/stick.ts`)

- **No write in flight:** for 400 ms after a wheel (`WHEEL_MS`), `correct()` in a thread doc re-anchors to where the view is and writes nothing.
- **Room under an upward wheel:** an upward wheel reserves one viewport of spacer below the content (`reserve`, in the same spacer as the existing `room`). A row dropped above can't pull the bottom up under the view, so there is no clamp.
  - Writes to the bottom (`bottom()`) aim above the reserve, so a stuck view never lands in blank space.
  - `toBottom` clears it. A downward wheel drops it at once, so reversing back to the bottom shows no blank space. Once the wheel window is over, `remember()` releases it whole. With no animation left, a clamp to the content's bottom is just the normal bottom.
- The single wheel listener records the time and the reserve, then calls the existing touch handler.

## Tests (`ui/src/chat/stick.test.tsx`)

The harness gains a clock (`setSystemTime`; `later()` moves it), wheel events with a `deltaY`, and `layout()`, which plays the browser's clamp.
- **The issue's repro:** an arrival during the wheel leaves the gap at 100 px or more. After the wheel, the next arrival keeps the doc in place.
- **A row the window drops during an upward wheel:** no clamp. The scroll carries on 193 px further, and after the wheel the spacer is back to empty with still no clamp.
- **The same drop without a reserve clamps the view.** That is the WebKit failure.
- **Reversing a wheel back down to the bottom** leaves no blank space, and arriving lines are followed. **A stopped wheel's reserve** is released once the window is over.
- **A wheel down at the bottom** reserves nothing, and arriving lines are followed.
- 13 of 13 pass. Round 2's `stick.ts` fails both reserve-release tests; main's fails the repro and the drop test.

## CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/ui-doc-still.ts`)

- **New dispatch input `doc_still_loops`** (empty by default, so push and PR runs are unchanged). It runs the WebKit stillness check that many loops with `--trace`, keeps the log as the `doc-still-trace` artifact, and gives the doc job 60 minutes instead of 15.
- **`ui-doc-still.ts`:** prints progress every 10 loops, and its trace logs removed rows next to added ones.

## Gates (local, at 98261d6f)

- Static: every `repo / static` step from ci.yml passes (15 of 15).
- `ci-tests unit`: 4192 pass, 1 fail. The failure is the laptop-only `cursor-agent` harness test; it passes in CI.
- `ci-tests flows`: 297 pass, 0 fail.
- First-load JS: 791,242 bytes of 800,000.
- Local Chromium (at ebecb992): the stillness check passed 10 of 10 loops.
- Dispatched `build,test-flows,doc` with `doc_still_loops=100`: [42814636089](https://github.com/kiwi-init/channels/actions/runs/42814636089). All legs and `ci-ok` passed, and the doc stayed still in all 100 WebKit loops.

No visual change, so there are no screenshots.

author: yasyf
body:
## What changes for you

Your PR cards read the sections from your Nov 9 1:57 PM ruling. Each PR shows a Refresher written for someone who knows the codebase but has not read this code lately, in place of the ELI5, and its Biggest surprise in place of "What changes for you". A stack card's title and opening summary come from a `## The stack` section in the stack's bottom PR. The title no longer strings together cut-off PR titles. A code block in Show me, such as SQL, draws as a syntax-highlighted picture inside that PR's section. Builders are told to write these sections and to put a concrete example in Show me, not a diagram alone.

## Refresher

`drive card` (`lib/drive/card.py`) emits `refresher` (from `## Refresher`, an older `## ELI5`, or the reviewer bot's comment under either heading), `surprise` (from `## Biggest surprise`), the plain PR title, and each row's own `pictures`, which cc-slack 0.19.13 and later place in that PR's section. `render_stack` takes its title and body from `stack_words`, which reads `## The stack` of the bottom PR: first line, then the summary. `cards` refuses a stack card that waits on his tap when that section is missing, the same way it refuses a missing "What you'll hate most". `picture.py` draws any fenced code block tagged with a language through `freeze` (Menlo, GitHub theme), beside the existing `arch` and `dot` diagrams. `landing.md`, `messages.md` and `builder.md` describe the new sections.

## Biggest surprise

A stack card waiting on his tap is refused until its bottom PR has `## The stack`, so a stack opened before this lands draws no card until its builder adds that section; the coordinator hears `EVENT refused` naming it.

## What you'll hate most

The highlighted code pictures need `freeze` (Homebrew `charmbracelet/tap/freeze`) on the Mac running the drive. Without it a code block stays a plain monospace block on the card and the drive logs why.

## Show me

```sql
-- a Show me block like this one now draws as a highlighted picture on his card
INSERT INTO orders (item_id, qty)
SELECT ?, ?
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stock WHERE item_id IS ? AND qty >= ?);
```
